examples.name: FilledTextFieldPlain
examples.title: At its plainest
examples.description:
The least it takes: a `TextFieldState` and a label. The label is inside the box: it rests in the text's place while the field is empty and without the focus. Press the field: the label moves up to its own line above the text and makes room for the text. If the focus leaves the field while it is empty, the label goes back to its place.

The typed text is read from the state: the line below shows `city.text` as it is typed.
examples.code:
val city = rememberTextFieldState()
PantrixFilledTextField(
    state = city,
    modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
    label = "City",
    tagKey = "city"
)
PantrixText(
    text = if (city.text.isEmpty()) "No city typed yet" else "Typed: ${city.text}",
    color = PantrixTheme.colors.textSecondary
)

examples.name: FilledTextFieldLabelAndPlaceholder
examples.title: Label and placeholder
examples.description:
The first field is empty: the label rests in the text's place and the placeholder is not shown. Press the field: the label moves up, and the placeholder appears where the label was. A placeholder is not a label; it gives an example of what to type.

The second field holds a text, so its label is always up. The third has no label: the text stands in the middle of the box, the placeholder shows whenever the field is empty, and `contentDescription` tells a screen reader the field's name.
examples.code:
PantrixFilledTextField(
    state = rememberTextFieldState(),
    modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
    label = "Website",
    placeholder = "https://example.com",
    tagKey = "website"
)
PantrixFilledTextField(
    state = rememberTextFieldState("Kadıköy"),
    modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
    label = "District",
    tagKey = "district"
)
PantrixFilledTextField(
    state = rememberTextFieldState(),
    modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
    placeholder = "Search neighbourhoods",
    contentDescription = "Search neighbourhoods",
    tagKey = "neighbourhood"
)

examples.name: FilledTextFieldSupportingTextAndError
examples.title: Supporting text and error
examples.description:
`supportingText` stands under the box. `error = true` outlines the box in the `danger` colour; the supporting text and the caret turn to that colour too, and a screen reader announces the message as the error. The label keeps its own colour: the outline and the message are what show the error. The fill turns to the surface's colour, as it does with the focus.

The field starts in error. Delete the space: the outline loses the error's colour and the supporting text takes the place of the error message.
examples.code:
val username = rememberTextFieldState("ayşe yılmaz")
val hasSpace = username.text.contains(' ')
PantrixFilledTextField(
    state = username,
    modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
    label = "Username",
    supportingText = if (hasSpace) "A username cannot contain spaces" else "Appears in your profile's address",
    error = hasSpace,
    showClearButton = true,
    tagKey = "username"
)

examples.name: FilledTextFieldSearch
examples.title: Icon, clear button and action key
examples.description:
`leadingIcon` stands before the label and the text. A slot does not size what is put in it; the icon takes the size in the filled field's style: `PantrixTheme.style(FilledTextFieldStyle).iconSize`. While the field is not empty, `showClearButton` shows the button that empties it: the button leaves the caret in the field, and is no stop for Tab.

`keyboardOptions` makes the keyboard's action key "Search"; `onKeyboardAction` is called when that key is pressed. Type something and press the keyboard's "Search" key or Enter: the app's snackbar says what was searched for.
examples.code:
val snackbars = LocalPantrixSnackbars.current
val scope = rememberCoroutineScope()
val query = rememberTextFieldState()
PantrixFilledTextField(
    state = query,
    modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
    label = "Search branches",
    leadingIcon = {
        PantrixIcon(
            imageVector = PantrixIcons.Search,
            contentDescription = null,
            size = PantrixTheme.style(FilledTextFieldStyle).iconSize
        )
    },
    showClearButton = true,
    keyboardOptions = KeyboardOptions(imeAction = ImeAction.Search),
    onKeyboardAction = { scope.launch { snackbars?.show(message = "Branch searched for: ${query.text}") } },
    tagKey = "branch"
)

examples.name: FilledTextFieldTransformations
examples.title: Input and output transformations
examples.description:
`inputTransformation` turns an edit down whole if it holds anything that is not a digit; `maxLength = 4` applies to what it lets through. `outputTransformation` draws a slash between the month and the year: the slash is not part of the text.

Type "1228": the box shows "12/28", while `expiry.text`, which the line below reads, is four digits.

examples.name: FilledTextFieldTransferForm
examples.title: A money transfer form
examples.description:
A money transfer form, with the three overloads together. The first two fields are bound to the form: each takes its value, its error and its name from its field in the form; if the focus leaves one while it is empty, the rule's message shows under the box and the box is outlined in the error colour. The amount field holds its text as a `String` and turns down whatever is not a digit in `onValueChange`: an edit that is turned down is not shown. Its limit is seven digits; its count is hidden with `showCharacterCount = false`.

The note is three lines tall: a text that does not fit scrolls inside the box, and the bar at its end shows how far. Its text is in the state created with `rememberTextFieldState`, and is read from there when the form is sent: the notification reads it with `note.text`.

In the first three fields the keyboard's "Next" key moves the focus to the next field. Leave the fields empty and press "Send": the form is not sent, and the first field in error takes the focus.
examples.code:
val snackbars = LocalPantrixSnackbars.current
val scope = rememberCoroutineScope()
val form = rememberFormState()
var amount by rememberSaveable { mutableStateOf("") }
val note = rememberTextFieldState()
PantrixFilledTextField(
    field = form.field("recipient", initial = "", Rules.notBlank("Enter the recipient's name")),
    modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
    form = form,
    label = "Recipient's full name",
    keyboardOptions = KeyboardOptions(capitalization = KeyboardCapitalization.Words, imeAction = ImeAction.Next)
)
PantrixFilledTextField(
    field = form.field("iban", initial = "", Rules.notBlank("Enter the IBAN")),
    modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
    form = form,
    label = "IBAN",
    placeholder = "TR00 0000 0000 0000 0000 0000 00",
    showClearButton = true,
    keyboardOptions = KeyboardOptions(
        capitalization = KeyboardCapitalization.Characters,
        imeAction = ImeAction.Next
    )
)
PantrixFilledTextField(
    value = amount,
    onValueChange = { if (it.all(Char::isDigit)) amount = it },
    modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
    label = "Amount",
    placeholder = "0",
    supportingText = "Digits only",
    trailingIcon = { PantrixText(text = "TL") },
    maxLength = 7,
    showCharacterCount = false,
    keyboardOptions = KeyboardOptions(keyboardType = KeyboardType.Number, imeAction = ImeAction.Next),
    tagKey = "amount"
)
PantrixFilledTextField(
    state = note,
    modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
    label = "Note",
    placeholder = "Rent, dues, debt…",
    maxLength = 140,
    lineLimits = TextFieldLineLimits.MultiLine(minHeightInLines = 3, maxHeightInLines = 3),
    tagKey = "transfer_note"
)
PantrixButton(
    text = "Send",
    onClick = {
        scope.launch {
            form.submit {
                // The note is read from the state at the moment it is used.
                val sent = if (note.text.isBlank()) "Money sent" else "Money sent: ${note.text}"
                snackbars?.show(message = sent, tagKey = "transfer_sent")
            }
        }
    },
    form = form,
    tagKey = "send_transfer"
)

examples.name: FilledTextFieldFixedHeight
examples.title: A field given a height
examples.description: A height given to the field is the whole field's: `Modifier.height(140.dp)`. The box takes what the supporting text under it leaves of that height; the label and the text stay inside the box, a text that does not fit scrolls there, and the bar at its end shows how far.
examples.code:
PantrixFilledTextField(
    state = rememberTextFieldState(COMPLAINT),
    modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth().height(140.dp),
    label = "Your complaint",
    supportingText = "The field's height is fixed: the text scrolls inside the box",
    lineLimits = TextFieldLineLimits.MultiLine(),
    tagKey = "complaint"
)

private const val COMPLAINT = "The same payment was taken from my card twice.\n" +
    "The first was on the third of the month, the second on the fourth.\n" +
    "Both are for the same amount and from the same merchant.\n" +
    "I have both receipts.\n" +
    "I would like one of them refunded."

examples.name: FilledTextFieldDisabledAndReadOnly
examples.title: Disabled and read-only
examples.description:
`enabled = false` takes the field's fill away: a disabled field is drawn in the theme's disabled text colour on the ground it stands on, takes no focus, and a screen reader is told that it is disabled. This is so whatever `colors` gives: a disabled field looks the same everywhere in an app.

With `readOnly = true` the field keeps its fill and its colours: it can be focused and its text selected and copied; it just cannot be changed.
examples.code:
PantrixFilledTextField(
    state = rememberTextFieldState("TL current account - 1042"),
    modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
    enabled = false,
    label = "Sending account",
    supportingText = "Cannot be changed in this transaction",
    tagKey = "account"
)
PantrixFilledTextField(
    state = rememberTextFieldState("TR33 0006 1005 1978 6457 8413 26"),
    modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
    readOnly = true,
    label = "Your IBAN",
    supportingText = "Read-only: it can be selected and copied",
    tagKey = "own_iban"
)

examples.name: FilledTextFieldOwnColors
examples.title: Its own colours
examples.description:
The colours given with `colors` are used, and the ones left out stay the theme's roles. The first field takes its colours from the theme's `info` role. At rest the fill is the role's soft tone; the label, the text and the icon are in the colour that reads on that tone. With the focus and under a pointer the outline is the role's own colour. The fill with the focus, the placeholder, the supporting text and the error colour are not given: they stay as the theme has them.

The second field does the same with the app's own purple: a colour that is in none of the theme's roles. Press the field: the outline and the caret are purple, and with the focus the fill turns to the theme's surface colour.
examples.code:
val info = PantrixTheme.colors.info
PantrixFilledTextField(
    state = rememberTextFieldState(),
    modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
    label = "Referral code",
    placeholder = "PX-0000",
    supportingText = "The code of the person who invited you, if any",
    showClearButton = true,
    colors = FilledTextFieldColors(
        container = info.container,
        hoveredOutline = info.color,
        focusedOutline = info.color,
        text = info.onContainer,
        label = info.onContainer,
        icon = info.onContainer,
        cursor = info.color
    ),
    tagKey = "reference"
)
val own = ownColors()
PantrixFilledTextField(
    state = rememberTextFieldState(),
    modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
    label = "Promo code",
    colors = FilledTextFieldColors(
        container = own.container,
        hoveredOutline = own.color,
        focusedOutline = own.color,
        text = own.onContainer,
        label = own.onContainer,
        cursor = own.color
    ),
    tagKey = "own_colors"
)

appNames.name: ownColors
appNames.description: The "app's own colour" of the examples: a purple that is in none of the theme's roles. It is there to show what changes when a component is given `colors`; given one of the theme's roles, nobody could tell whether the colour came from the component's tone or from the parameter.

examples.name: FilledTextFieldOwnStyle
examples.title: Its own style
examples.description:
`style` is this call's own style: only the fields it sets change, and the rest comes from the theme's and the platform's style.

The first field's box is fully round: `FilledTextFieldStyle(shape = ShapeRole.Full)`. The second has small corners and, with `borderWidth = 2.dp`, a thick outline. The outline shows with the focus, in error and under a pointer; at rest the box has none.
examples.code:
PantrixFilledTextField(
    state = rememberTextFieldState(),
    modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
    label = "Fully round box",
    style = FilledTextFieldStyle(shape = ShapeRole.Full),
    tagKey = "pill"
)
PantrixFilledTextField(
    state = rememberTextFieldState(),
    modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
    label = "Small corners, thick outline",
    style = FilledTextFieldStyle(shape = ShapeRole.Small, borderWidth = 2.dp),
    tagKey = "small_corners"
)

pages.title: Secure Text Field
pages.summary:
A field for text that is not to be read over a shoulder: a password, a PIN, a card's security code. What is typed is drawn as dots; it cannot be cut, copied or dragged out of the field. The eye button at the box's end shows the text and hides it again.

Its label, its box and its supporting text are those of `PantrixTextField`, and it takes that component's `style` and `colors`: a product that restyles its text fields restyles its password fields with them. The field holds one line. It is built on a `TextFieldState`, and has another overload that takes a form's field; it has none that takes `value` and `onValueChange`.
features: **Hidden text.** The platform is told that the field holds a password, and while the text is hidden it is given dots in place of the text: a screen reader does not read the password out, while a password manager still fills the field and saves it.

**The reveal button.** The eye at the box's end shows the text and hides it again. A press on it with the mouse leaves the caret where it is. With a keyboard it is a Tab stop of its own, after the field, while the keyboard's "Next" key goes past it to the next field. `showRevealButton = false` removes the button.
**That the text was shown is not saved.** When the field is composed anew, as it is when the screen turns, the text is hidden again.

**Obfuscation mode.** `textObfuscationMode` says how the hidden text is drawn: as the platform does it, with the last character typed showing for a moment, or with nothing showing. `textObfuscationCharacter` is the character drawn in place of the dot.

**Keyboard.** What `keyboardOptions` leaves unset is a password's: the password keyboard and no corrections. Naming an action key and nothing else does not bring back a keyboard that learns what is typed. `KeyboardType.NumberPassword` is a PIN's.
**Autofill.** If no `contentType` is given the field holds `ContentType.Password`; `ContentType.NewPassword` is a password that is being chosen.

**Reading the text.** The text is read from the state: `state.text` at the moment it is used, `snapshotFlow` to follow it as it is typed. A caller that keeps the text as a `String` is handed each change that way.

**Form.** The overload that takes a `field` gets its value, its error and its name from its field in the form. The field is checked when the focus leaves the field and its buttons; if `form` is given, the keyboard's action key submits the form.

**What comes from the text field.** `label`, `placeholder`, `supportingText`, `error`, `leadingIcon`, `showClearButton` and `maxLength` are as they are in the text field. `trailingIcon` stands after the clear button and the reveal button.

**Automation.** With `tagKey` the field is named `SecureTextField_<tagKey>`, the clear button `SecureTextFieldClear_<tagKey>` and the reveal button `SecureTextFieldReveal_<tagKey>`. The field reports that it took the focus, that it was cleared and that its text was shown or hidden; never its text.
api: com.pantrixui.components.inputs.securetextfield.PantrixSecureTextField(TextFieldState, Modifier, Boolean, Boolean, String?, String?, String?, Boolean, (@Composable () -> Unit)?, (@Composable () -> Unit)?, Boolean, Boolean, Int?, Boolean, TextObfuscationMode, Char, KeyboardOptions, KeyboardActionHandler?, InputTransformation?, ContentType?, TextFieldStyle?, TextFieldColors?, String?, String?, MutableInteractionSource?)

com.pantrixui.components.inputs.securetextfield.PantrixSecureTextField(FormField<String>, Modifier, FormState?, Boolean, Boolean, String?, String?, String?, (@Composable () -> Unit)?, (@Composable () -> Unit)?, Boolean, Boolean, Int?, Boolean, TextObfuscationMode, Char, KeyboardOptions, KeyboardActionHandler?, InputTransformation?, ContentType?, TextFieldStyle?, TextFieldColors?, String?, MutableInteractionSource?)

examples.name: SecureTextFieldPlain
examples.title: At its plainest
examples.description:
The least there is to write: a `TextFieldState` and a label. What is typed is drawn as dots; it cannot be cut or copied. The text is in the state: the line below reads only the length of `password.text`.

The eye button at the box's end shows the text and hides it again. A press on it with the mouse does not take the caret out of the field. With a keyboard, Tab stops at the button after the field, while the keyboard's "Next" key skips the button. That the text was shown is not saved: when the field is composed anew it is hidden again.
examples.code:
val password = remember { TextFieldState() }
PantrixSecureTextField(
    state = password,
    modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
    label = "Wi-Fi password",
    tagKey = "wifi_password"
)
PantrixText(text = "Characters typed: ${password.text.length}", color = PantrixTheme.colors.textSecondary)

examples.name: SecureTextFieldObfuscation
examples.title: Obfuscation mode and character
examples.description:
`textObfuscationMode` says how the text is drawn while it is hidden. The default, `System`, does as the platform does: on Android the last character typed shows for a moment where the system's own setting says so, and nowhere else does anything show. `RevealLastTyped` shows the last character typed for a moment on every platform, and `Hidden` shows it on none. Type something into the first two fields and see the difference.

`textObfuscationCharacter` is what is drawn in place of a hidden character: in the third field, stars instead of dots.
examples.code:
PantrixSecureTextField(
    state = remember { TextFieldState() },
    modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
    label = "The last character typed shows",
    textObfuscationMode = TextObfuscationMode.RevealLastTyped,
    tagKey = "reveal_last"
)
PantrixSecureTextField(
    state = remember { TextFieldState() },
    modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
    label = "Nothing shows",
    textObfuscationMode = TextObfuscationMode.Hidden,
    tagKey = "hidden"
)
PantrixSecureTextField(
    state = remember { TextFieldState("stars") },
    modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
    label = "Stars instead of dots",
    textObfuscationCharacter = '*',
    tagKey = "stars"
)

examples.name: SecureTextFieldSupportingTextAndError
examples.title: Supporting text and error
examples.description:
`supportingText` stands under the box. `error = true` turns the border, the label, the supporting text and the caret to the `danger` role, and the message is announced to a screen reader as the error. Type different things into the two fields: the second one goes into error and says what is wrong.

Each field's text is in its own state; the comparison reads both from there. The first field was given only an action key: the keyboard's "Next" key does not stop at the eye button, and goes on to the second field. The rest of the keyboard was not given, so it is a password's: the password keyboard and no corrections.
examples.code:
val password = remember { TextFieldState() }
val repeated = remember { TextFieldState() }
val differs = repeated.text.isNotEmpty() && repeated.text.toString() != password.text.toString()
PantrixSecureTextField(
    state = password,
    modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
    label = "Account password",
    supportingText = "Include letters and digits",
    keyboardOptions = KeyboardOptions(imeAction = ImeAction.Next),
    contentType = ContentType.NewPassword,
    tagKey = "chosen_password"
)
PantrixSecureTextField(
    state = repeated,
    modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
    label = "Account password (again)",
    supportingText = if (differs) "The two passwords do not match" else "Type the same password once more",
    error = differs,
    contentType = ContentType.NewPassword,
    tagKey = "repeated_password"
)

examples.name: SecureTextFieldButtonsAndIcon
examples.title: Clear button, count and icon
examples.description:
Three things can stand side by side at the box's end, always in the same order: the clear button, the button that shows the text, and `trailingIcon`. The icon here says whether the password is long enough; it is not decoration, so it has a `contentDescription`.

The clear button of `showClearButton` shows while the field is not empty, and leaves the caret in the field. `maxLength = 32` does not take a longer password; the count is written under the box, opposite the supporting text. `placeholder` shows only while the field is empty.
examples.code:
val password = remember { TextFieldState() }
val longEnough = password.text.length >= 12
PantrixSecureTextField(
    state = password,
    modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
    label = "Master password",
    placeholder = "It can be a sentence too",
    supportingText = "At least 12 characters",
    trailingIcon = {
        PantrixIcon(
            imageVector = if (longEnough) PantrixIcons.Success else PantrixIcons.Warning,
            contentDescription = if (longEnough) "Long enough" else "Still too short",
            size = PantrixTheme.style(TextFieldStyle).iconSize
        )
    },
    showClearButton = true,
    maxLength = 32,
    tagKey = "master_password"
)

examples.name: SecureTextFieldLoginForm
examples.title: A sign-in bound to a form
examples.description:
The `PantrixSecureTextField` that takes a `field` gets its value, its error and its name from its field in the form: if the field is left with the password too short, the rule's message takes the place of the supporting text. When the focus moves to the eye button the field does not count as left, so the error does not show then. The text of a field bound to a form is the value of the form's field: it does not have to be taken separately.

In a field given `form`, the keyboard's action key submits the form through the "Sign in" button; in the email field the "Next" key moves the focus to the password. The email field is a `PantrixTextField`: the two components draw the same label and the same box.
examples.code:
val snackbars = LocalPantrixSnackbars.current
val scope = rememberCoroutineScope()
val form = rememberFormState()
PantrixTextField(
    field = form.field("login_email", initial = "", Rules.matches(EMAIL, "Enter a valid email address")),
    modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
    form = form,
    label = "Email",
    placeholder = "name@example.com",
    keyboardOptions = KeyboardOptions(keyboardType = KeyboardType.Email, imeAction = ImeAction.Next),
    contentType = ContentType.EmailAddress
)
PantrixSecureTextField(
    field = form.field("login_password", initial = "", Rules.minLength(8, "The password must be at least 8 characters long")),
    modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
    form = form,
    label = "Password",
    supportingText = "At least 8 characters",
    showClearButton = true
)
PantrixButton(
    text = "Sign in",
    onClick = {
        scope.launch { form.submit { snackbars?.show(message = "Signed in", tagKey = "signed_in") } }
    },
    form = form,
    tagKey = "sign_in"
)

private val EMAIL = Regex("""\S+@\S+\.\S+""")

examples.name: SecureTextFieldAccountForm
examples.title: A form that carries its text to a ViewModel
examples.description:
It builds the username's state with `rememberTextFieldState` and the password's with `remember { TextFieldState(…) }`, from the value the ViewModel holds at that moment: the password does not go into the saved state. It follows the text in the state with `snapshotFlow` and reports each change to the ViewModel. This is how the text is taken from a field's state: the same way in a plain text field and in a secure one.

The first value in the ViewModel is read once. From then on it is one way: the text flows from the field to the ViewModel, and a change made in the ViewModel does not come back to the field. When the screen is composed anew the ViewModel is still there, and the fields start from its value.

The line below shows what the ViewModel holds: the username, and the length of the password rather than the password itself. The button reads from it too: it cannot be pressed until there is a username and a long enough password.

examples.name: SecureTextFieldPin
examples.title: A PIN that gives its text as a String
examples.description:
The secure field has no overload that takes `value` and `onValueChange`; for a caller that keeps its text as a `String`, one is built on top of the state. `PinInput` starts the field with `value`, follows the text in the state with `snapshotFlow` and reports each change through `onValueChange`. The flow is one way: `value` is the first value, and if it is changed from outside later, the field does not show the change. The supporting text is made from the `String` the caller holds, and says how many digits are missing.

This is a PIN: with `showRevealButton = false` it has no button to show its text, and with `TextObfuscationMode.Hidden` the last digit typed is not shown either. Its keyboard is the number keyboard (`KeyboardType.NumberPassword`); an input transformation turns down whatever is not a digit.

examples.name: SecureTextFieldDisabledAndReadOnly
examples.title: Disabled and read-only
examples.description:
A field with `enabled = false` takes no focus, is drawn in the theme's disabled colours and has no button to show its text.

A field with `readOnly = true` can be focused and its text can be shown with the button, but it cannot be changed: like a recovery code that is given once.
examples.code:
PantrixSecureTextField(
    state = remember { TextFieldState("unchanging") },
    modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
    enabled = false,
    label = "Disabled",
    supportingText = "It has no button to show its text",
    tagKey = "locked_password"
)
PantrixSecureTextField(
    state = remember { TextFieldState("PX-4821-9930") },
    modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
    readOnly = true,
    label = "Recovery code",
    supportingText = "Read-only: it can be shown but not changed",
    tagKey = "recovery_code"
)

examples.name: SecureTextFieldOwnColorsAndStyle
examples.title: Its own colours and style
examples.description:
The secure field has no style class or colour class of its own: it takes the `TextFieldColors` and the `TextFieldStyle` of `PantrixTextField`. A product that restyles its text fields in the theme restyles its password fields with them.

In the first field the focused border, the caret and the icon colour are the app's own purple: the eye button is drawn in the icon colour too. The colours that are not given keep their role in the theme. The second field's box is fully round: `TextFieldStyle(shape = ShapeRole.Full)`.
examples.code:
val own = ownColors()
PantrixSecureTextField(
    state = remember { TextFieldState() },
    modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
    label = "Wallet password",
    colors = TextFieldColors(focusedBorder = own.color, icon = own.color, cursor = own.color),
    tagKey = "own_colors"
)
PantrixSecureTextField(
    state = remember { TextFieldState() },
    modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
    label = "Vault password",
    style = TextFieldStyle(shape = ShapeRole.Full),
    tagKey = "pill"
)

appNames.name: ownColors
appNames.description: The "app's own colour" of the examples: a purple that is in none of the theme's roles. It is there to show what changes when a component is given `colors`; given one of the theme's roles, nobody could tell whether the colour came from the component's tone or from the parameter.

pages.title: Filled Secure Text Field
pages.summary:
A secure text field whose label is inside its box: a password, a PIN or a card's security code, in the filled text field's box. What is typed is drawn as dots, and cannot be cut, copied or dragged out of the field. The eye button at the box's end shows the text and hides it again.

The secure field underneath is `PantrixSecureTextField`'s, and its box `PantrixFilledTextField`'s. It takes the filled field's `style` and `colors`: the two filled fields are restyled together, and the two secure fields can stand in for each other. The field holds one line; it is built on a `TextFieldState`, and has an overload that takes a form's field.
features: **The label inside the box.** `label` rests in the text's place while the field is empty and without the focus; with the focus, or while the field holds a text, it moves up to its own line above the text. `placeholder` shows while the label is out of its place: while the field is empty and has the focus.
**Fill and outline.** At rest the box is filled and has no outline; it is outlined with the focus and in error. A disabled field has no fill.

**Hidden text.** The platform is told that the field holds a password, and while the text is hidden it is given dots in place of the text: a screen reader does not read the password out, while a password manager still fills the field and saves it.

**The reveal button.** A press on the eye button with a mouse leaves the caret where it is. With a keyboard it is a Tab stop of its own, after the field; the keyboard's "Next" key goes past it. That the text was shown is not saved. `showRevealButton = false` takes the button away.
**Obfuscation mode.** `textObfuscationMode` says how the hidden text is drawn, and `textObfuscationCharacter` which character is drawn in place of the dot.
**Keyboard and autofill.** What `keyboardOptions` leaves unset is a password's: the password keyboard and no corrections. Without a `contentType` the field holds `ContentType.Password`.
**Reading the text.** The text is read from the state: `state.text` when it is used, `snapshotFlow` to follow it as it is typed. There is no overload that takes a `value` and an `onValueChange`.
**Form.** The overload that takes a `field` gets its value, its error and its name from its field in the form; given `form`, the keyboard's action key submits the form.

**What comes from the filled field.** `supportingText`, `error`, `leadingIcon`, `showClearButton` and `maxLength` are as they are in the filled text field. `trailingIcon` stands after the clear button and the reveal button.

**Automation.** With `tagKey` the field is named `FilledSecureTextField_<tagKey>`, the clear button `FilledSecureTextFieldClear_<tagKey>` and the reveal button `FilledSecureTextFieldReveal_<tagKey>`. The field never reports its text.

examples.name: FilledSecureTextFieldPlain
examples.title: At its plainest
examples.description:
The least there is to write: a `TextFieldState` and a label. The label is inside the box: it rests in the text's place while the field is empty, and moves up to its own line above the text when the field is pressed. What is typed is drawn as dots, and cannot be cut or copied.

Type something and press the eye button at the end of the box: the text shows, and another press hides it again. A press with a mouse does not take the caret out of the field; with a keyboard, Tab stops at the button after the field. That the text was shown is not saved.
examples.code:
PantrixFilledSecureTextField(
    state = remember { TextFieldState() },
    modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
    label = "Vault password",
    tagKey = "safe_password"
)

examples.name: FilledSecureTextFieldSupportingTextAndError
examples.title: Supporting text and error
examples.description:
`supportingText` stands under the box. `error = true` outlines the box in the `danger` colour; the supporting text and the caret turn to that colour too, and a screen reader announces the message as the error. The label keeps its own colour.

The field starts in error: there is a space in its text. Press the eye button to see the text, and delete the space: the error goes. It is the caller, not the field, that works out the error; here by reading `password.text`.
examples.code:
val password = remember { TextFieldState("secret password") }
val hasSpace = password.text.contains(' ')
PantrixFilledSecureTextField(
    state = password,
    modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
    label = "App lock",
    supportingText = if (hasSpace) "A password cannot contain a space" else "A password without spaces",
    error = hasSpace,
    showClearButton = true,
    tagKey = "app_lock"
)

examples.name: FilledSecureTextFieldIconAndButtons
examples.title: Icon, clear button and count
examples.description:
`leadingIcon` stands before the label and the text. A slot does not size what is put in it: the example itself gives this icon the size in the filled field's style, `PantrixTheme.style(FilledTextFieldStyle).iconSize`. What is at the box's end is always in the same order: first the clear button, then the button that shows the text, and last `trailingIcon`, where one is given.

The clear button shows while the field is not empty, leaves the caret in the field and is no stop for Tab; the eye button is a Tab stop. `maxLength = 16` turns down a longer password, and writes the count under the box.
examples.code:
PantrixFilledSecureTextField(
    state = remember { TextFieldState() },
    modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
    label = "Admin password",
    leadingIcon = {
        PantrixIcon(
            imageVector = PantrixIcons.Person,
            contentDescription = null,
            size = PantrixTheme.style(FilledTextFieldStyle).iconSize
        )
    },
    showClearButton = true,
    maxLength = 16,
    tagKey = "admin_password"
)

examples.name: FilledSecureTextFieldChangePasswordForm
examples.title: A password change bound to a form
examples.description:
Both fields get their value, their error and their name from their field in the form. In the current password the keyboard's "Next" key moves the focus to the new password; in the new password the action key submits the form through the "Change password" button. Leave both fields empty and press the button: the form is not submitted, and the first field in error takes the focus.

The platform is told that the new password is one that is being chosen (`ContentType.NewPassword`): a password manager offers to suggest a new one here, not to fill in the saved one. The current password was given no `contentType`: the field holds `ContentType.Password`.
examples.code:
val snackbars = LocalPantrixSnackbars.current
val scope = rememberCoroutineScope()
val form = rememberFormState()
PantrixFilledSecureTextField(
    field = form.field("current_password", initial = "", Rules.notBlank("Enter your current password")),
    modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
    form = form,
    label = "Current password",
    keyboardOptions = KeyboardOptions(imeAction = ImeAction.Next)
)
PantrixFilledSecureTextField(
    field = form.field("new_password", initial = "", Rules.minLength(8, "The new password must be at least 8 characters")),
    modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
    form = form,
    label = "New password",
    supportingText = "At least 8 characters",
    showClearButton = true,
    contentType = ContentType.NewPassword
)
PantrixButton(
    text = "Change password",
    onClick = {
        scope.launch {
            form.submit { snackbars?.show(message = "Password changed", tagKey = "password_changed") }
        }
    },
    form = form,
    tagKey = "change_password"
)

examples.name: FilledSecureTextFieldCardCode
examples.title: A security code read when it is used
examples.description:
The three-digit security code on the back of a card: its keyboard is the number keyboard, an input transformation turns down what is not a digit, and its count is not shown. The eye button stays, so that the user can compare the code they typed with the one on the card.

The text is read from the state when it is used: `code.text`, when the button is pressed. It is carried nowhere in between; the field's state is its only source. The notification says how many digits were received, not the code itself.

examples.name: FilledSecureTextFieldFollowed
examples.title: A text followed as it is typed
examples.description:
A caller that wants the text as it is typed follows it from the state: `snapshotFlow { state.text.toString() }` gives every change, here to a `String` the caller holds. The supporting text is made from that `String`, and says what the password still lacks.

The flow goes one way: the text flows from the field to the caller. Carrying it to a ViewModel is written the same way: each change is reported to the ViewModel inside `collect`.

examples.name: FilledSecureTextFieldPin
examples.title: A PIN that is never shown
examples.description:
`showRevealButton = false` takes away the eye button: the text stays as `textObfuscationMode` draws it. With `TextObfuscationMode.Hidden` the last digit typed shows on no platform; the default, `System`, would show the last character typed for a moment on Android, where the system's own setting says so. `textObfuscationCharacter` draws an asterisk in place of the dot.

Its keyboard is a PIN's: `KeyboardType.NumberPassword`. `maxLength = 4` takes no fifth digit, and writes the count under the box.
examples.code:
PantrixFilledSecureTextField(
    state = remember { TextFieldState() },
    modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
    label = "Card PIN",
    supportingText = "Four digits",
    showRevealButton = false,
    maxLength = 4,
    textObfuscationMode = TextObfuscationMode.Hidden,
    textObfuscationCharacter = '*',
    keyboardOptions = KeyboardOptions(keyboardType = KeyboardType.NumberPassword),
    inputTransformation = DigitsOnly,
    tagKey = "card_pin"
)

private val DigitsOnly = InputTransformation {
    if (!asCharSequence().all(Char::isDigit)) revertAllChanges()
}

examples.name: FilledSecureTextFieldDisabledAndReadOnly
examples.title: Disabled and read-only
examples.description:
`enabled = false` takes the field's fill away: the field is drawn in the theme's disabled text colour, takes no focus and has no button to show its text.

With `readOnly = true` the field keeps its fill: it can be focused, and its text shown with the eye button, but it cannot be changed.
examples.code:
PantrixFilledSecureTextField(
    state = remember { TextFieldState("unchanging") },
    modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
    enabled = false,
    label = "App password",
    supportingText = "Set by your organisation",
    tagKey = "managed_password"
)
PantrixFilledSecureTextField(
    state = remember { TextFieldState("PX-7730-1184") },
    modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
    readOnly = true,
    label = "Backup code",
    supportingText = "Shown with the eye button, cannot be changed",
    tagKey = "backup_code"
)

examples.name: FilledSecureTextFieldOwnColorsAndStyle
examples.title: Its own colours and style
examples.description:
The filled secure field takes the filled text field's `FilledTextFieldColors` and `FilledTextFieldStyle`: the two filled fields are restyled together.

The first field's fill, label, text, icon, outline and caret are from the app's own purple; the eye button is drawn in the icon colour. What is not given, such as the fill with the focus, stays the theme's role. The second's box is fully round: `FilledTextFieldStyle(shape = ShapeRole.Full)`.
examples.code:
val own = ownColors()
PantrixFilledSecureTextField(
    state = remember { TextFieldState() },
    modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
    label = "Membership password",
    colors = FilledTextFieldColors(
        container = own.container,
        focusedOutline = own.color,
        text = own.onContainer,
        label = own.onContainer,
        icon = own.onContainer,
        cursor = own.color
    ),
    tagKey = "own_colors"
)
PantrixFilledSecureTextField(
    state = remember { TextFieldState() },
    modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
    label = "Archive password",
    style = FilledTextFieldStyle(shape = ShapeRole.Full),
    tagKey = "pill"
)

appNames.name: ownColors
appNames.description: The "app's own colour" of the examples: a purple that is in none of the theme's roles. It is there to show what changes when a component is given `colors`; given one of the theme's roles, nobody could tell whether the colour came from the component's tone or from the parameter.

pages.title: Auto Resize Text Field
pages.summary:
A text field whose text gets smaller to stay in view: an amount, a card number, a short note; anything that is read whole. The text is as large as its style says while it fits the box; when it does not, it gets as small as it takes to fit, and it grows back as it is deleted. The box does not grow wider with its text.

Its label, its box and its supporting text are those of `PantrixTextField`, and it takes that component's `style` and `colors`. It is built on a `TextFieldState`; it has an overload that takes a `value` and an `onValueChange`, and one that takes a form's field.
features: **A box that does not change.** The box's width is its style's least width or the one its caller gave it; a text that grows longer does not widen it, but gets as small as it takes to fit.

**The largest size.** `textStyle` is the style of the text at its largest: a role of the theme's typography, such as `headline` for an amount. It is `body` unless given. A box too short for the style grows to hold a line of it.

**The smallest size.** `minFontSize` is the smallest the text gets: a size in sp, or one in em, which is a share of the style's size. It is the theme's `footnote` size unless given. A text that still does not fit at that size scrolls, as the text of any field does.

**Several lines.** With `lineLimits = TextFieldLineLimits.MultiLine(...)` the text wraps, and the box grows with it from the least of its lines to the most. From there the box keeps its height, and the text is set smaller, its line spacing with it.
**A given height.** A height the field is given comes before its lines: the box fills it, and the text is fitted to that height.

**What is fitted is the text as it is shown.** The thousands separators that an `outputTransformation` adds only for display count too, and so does what the keyboard is still composing. The placeholder is in the text's style, and where it is long it shrinks too.
**It is the text's size that gets smaller.** Nothing is drawn smaller than it is: the caret, a selection and its handles are those of the size the text is in.

**Three overloads.** In the one that takes a `state` the text is read from the state. The one that takes a `value` and an `onValueChange` keeps the text with its caller, and takes its lines as `singleLine`, `minLines` and `maxLines`. The one that takes a `field` is bound to a form's field.

**What comes from the text field.** `label`, `placeholder`, `supportingText`, `error`, the icons, `showClearButton`, `maxLength`, the keyboard and the transformations are as they are in the text field.

**Automation.** With `tagKey` the field is named `AutoResizeTextField_<tagKey>`, and its clear button `AutoResizeTextFieldClear_<tagKey>`. The field reports that it took the focus and that it was cleared, and never its text.
api: com.pantrixui.components.inputs.autoresizetextfield.PantrixAutoResizeTextField(TextFieldState, Modifier, Boolean, Boolean, String?, String?, String?, Boolean, (@Composable () -> Unit)?, (@Composable () -> Unit)?, Boolean, Int?, Boolean, TextStyle?, TextUnit, TextFieldLineLimits, KeyboardOptions, KeyboardActionHandler?, InputTransformation?, OutputTransformation?, ContentType?, TextFieldStyle?, TextFieldColors?, String?, String?, MutableInteractionSource?)

examples.name: AutoResizeTextFieldPlain
examples.title: At its plainest
examples.description:
The least it takes: a `TextFieldState` and a label. The field is given no width: the box has its style's least width, and does not grow wider with its text. The address is too long for that box, so it is drawn in a smaller size.

Keep typing: the text shrinks down to its smallest size, the theme's `footnote` size; there it stops shrinking and scrolls, as the text of any field does. Delete: the text grows back, but not past its style's size, here `body`.
examples.code:
PantrixAutoResizeTextField(
    state = rememberTextFieldState("Atatürk Bulvarı No: 125, Daire 14, Çankaya"),
    label = "Address",
    tagKey = "plain_address"
)

examples.name: AutoResizeTextFieldAmount
examples.title: An amount set large
examples.description:
The amount of a money transfer, in the theme's largest style: `textStyle = PantrixTheme.typography.display`. A few digits fill the box; with the ones that follow, the digits get as small as it takes to fit, and the box keeps both its width and its height. The box is tall enough to hold a line of this style.

Its keyboard is the decimal one, an input transformation turns down what is not an amount, and an output transformation puts in the dots between the thousands only for display. What is fitted is the text as it is drawn: the dots count too.

The text is read from the state at the moment it is used: `amount.text` when the button is pressed. What is read is the text that was typed; the dots added for display are no part of it.

examples.name: AutoResizeTextFieldSmallestSize
examples.title: The smallest size
examples.description:
All three fields hold the same address in the `title` style. The address fits none of their boxes, so each is down to its own smallest size. The first is given no `minFontSize`: the text shrinks down to the theme's `footnote` size. In the second the smallest size is 14 sp. In the third it is given in em: `0.8.em`, eight tenths of the style's own size.

A text that still does not fit at its smallest size stops shrinking and scrolls, as the text of any field does. With a `minFontSize` at the style's own size or above it, the text never shrinks.
examples.code:
val address = "Atatürk Bulvarı No: 125, Daire 14, Kızılay Mahallesi, Çankaya, Ankara"
PantrixAutoResizeTextField(
    state = rememberTextFieldState(address),
    label = "Not given: footnote size",
    textStyle = PantrixTheme.typography.title,
    tagKey = "smallest_default"
)
PantrixAutoResizeTextField(
    state = rememberTextFieldState(address),
    label = "Smallest 14 sp",
    textStyle = PantrixTheme.typography.title,
    minFontSize = 14.sp,
    tagKey = "smallest_sp"
)
PantrixAutoResizeTextField(
    state = rememberTextFieldState(address),
    label = "Smallest 0.8 em",
    textStyle = PantrixTheme.typography.title,
    minFontSize = 0.8.em,
    tagKey = "smallest_em"
)

examples.name: AutoResizeTextFieldCardNumber
examples.title: A field whose text is held as a String
examples.description:
A card number of sixteen digits. The caller holds the number as a `String`: the field shows it and asks for every change, and since a change that is not all digits is not taken, it is not shown either. The supporting text is made from that `String`. This overload takes its lines as `singleLine`, `minLines` and `maxLines`.

The text is in the `title` style, and shrinks in a box it does not fit. Its smallest size is the label size (`minFontSize = PantrixTheme.typography.label.fontSize`): the number is never set smaller than that. The placeholder is in the text's style too.
examples.code:
var number by rememberSaveable { mutableStateOf("") }
val missing = 16 - number.length
PantrixAutoResizeTextField(
    value = number,
    onValueChange = { if (it.all(Char::isDigit)) number = it },
    modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
    label = "Card number",
    placeholder = "0000000000000000",
    supportingText = if (missing == 0) "Number complete" else "Digits to go: $missing",
    maxLength = 16,
    showCharacterCount = false,
    textStyle = PantrixTheme.typography.title,
    minFontSize = PantrixTheme.typography.label.fontSize,
    keyboardOptions = KeyboardOptions(keyboardType = KeyboardType.Number),
    contentType = ContentType.CreditCardNumber,
    tagKey = "card_number"
)

examples.name: AutoResizeTextFieldIbanForm
examples.title: An IBAN bound to a form
examples.description:
The overload that takes a `field` gets its value, its error and its name from its field in the form: if the focus leaves while the IBAN is incomplete, the rule's message takes the place of the supporting text. In a field that is given `form`, the keyboard's action key submits the form through the "Save IBAN" button. The text of a field bound to a form is the value of the form's field: it does not have to be read separately.

Twenty-six characters in the `callout` style do not fit a narrow box: the text shrinks, and the whole IBAN stays in view.
examples.code:
val snackbars = LocalPantrixSnackbars.current
val scope = rememberCoroutineScope()
val form = rememberFormState()
PantrixAutoResizeTextField(
    field = form.field("iban", initial = "", Rules.matches(IBAN, "Enter a 26-character IBAN that starts with TR")),
    modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
    form = form,
    label = "IBAN",
    placeholder = "TR000000000000000000000000",
    supportingText = "Long as it is, all of it stays in view",
    showClearButton = true,
    maxLength = 26,
    textStyle = PantrixTheme.typography.callout,
    keyboardOptions = KeyboardOptions(capitalization = KeyboardCapitalization.Characters)
)
PantrixButton(
    text = "Save IBAN",
    onClick = {
        scope.launch { form.submit { snackbars?.show(message = "IBAN saved", tagKey = "iban_saved") } }
    },
    form = form,
    tagKey = "save_iban"
)

private val IBAN = Regex("""TR\d{24}""")

examples.name: AutoResizeTextFieldCourierNote
examples.title: A note of several lines
examples.description:
With `lineLimits = TextFieldLineLimits.MultiLine(minHeightInLines = 2, maxHeightInLines = 4)` the text wraps: the box is two lines tall, and grows with the text to four lines. Once the note passes four lines the box stays as it is, and the text gets as small as it takes to fit, its line spacing with it. Enter starts a new line.

The text is read from the state at the moment it is used: `note.text` when the button is pressed.
examples.code:
val snackbars = LocalPantrixSnackbars.current
val scope = rememberCoroutineScope()
val note = rememberTextFieldState()
PantrixAutoResizeTextField(
    state = note,
    modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
    label = "Note for the courier",
    placeholder = "Don't ring the bell, leave it at the door",
    supportingText = "Grows to four lines, then the text shrinks",
    showClearButton = true,
    maxLength = 280,
    lineLimits = TextFieldLineLimits.MultiLine(minHeightInLines = 2, maxHeightInLines = 4),
    tagKey = "courier_note"
)
PantrixButton(
    text = "Save note",
    onClick = {
        val written = note.text.toString()
        val message = if (written.isBlank()) "Write a note" else "Note saved. Characters: ${written.length}"
        scope.launch { snackbars?.show(message = message, tagKey = "note_saved") }
    },
    tagKey = "save_note"
)

examples.name: AutoResizeTextFieldCardMessage
examples.title: A field given a height
examples.description:
A message written on a gift card, in a field that is given a height: `Modifier.height(180.dp)`. The height is the whole field's: the box fills what the label and the supporting text leave of it, and is just as tall while the message is short. The text starts in the `title` style; when it does not fit the box it goes down to the largest size in which all of it is in view, and it grows back as it is deleted.

No line limit is given (`TextFieldLineLimits.MultiLine()`): the room the text is fitted to is the field's height.
examples.code:
PantrixAutoResizeTextField(
    state = rememberTextFieldState(CARD_MESSAGE),
    modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth().height(180.dp),
    label = "Card message",
    supportingText = "The field's height is fixed: the text shrinks to fit",
    showClearButton = true,
    maxLength = 280,
    textStyle = PantrixTheme.typography.title,
    lineLimits = TextFieldLineLimits.MultiLine(),
    tagKey = "card_message"
)

private const val CARD_MESSAGE = "Happy birthday! May the year ahead bring you health, happiness and plenty of joy. " +
    "Here's to many more good years together."

examples.name: AutoResizeTextFieldSupportingTextAndError
examples.title: Supporting text and error
examples.description:
`supportingText` stands under the box. `error = true` turns the border, the label, the supporting text and the caret to the `danger` role, and the message is announced to a screen reader as an error. The field starts in error: 75.000 is over the daily limit. Delete a digit: the error goes.

It is the caller that works out the error, not the field; here by reading `amount.text`. What is read is the digits that were typed: the dots between the thousands are only drawn.

examples.name: AutoResizeTextFieldReadOnlyAndDisabled
examples.title: Read-only and disabled
examples.description:
A field with `readOnly = true` cannot be changed, but it can be focused, and its text selected and copied. The balance is in the `headline` style and is shown with the dots between its thousands; in a box it does not fit, it shrinks as it does in a field that can be typed into.

A field with `enabled = false` is drawn in the theme's disabled colours and takes no focus. Its text is still fitted to its box.
examples.code:
PantrixAutoResizeTextField(
    state = rememberTextFieldState("125000000000000,00"),
    modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
    readOnly = true,
    label = "Balance",
    supportingText = "Read-only: in the headline style, shrunk to fit",
    trailingIcon = { PantrixText(text = "TL") },
    textStyle = PantrixTheme.typography.headline,
    outputTransformation = GroupedInThousands,
    tagKey = "balance"
)
PantrixAutoResizeTextField(
    state = rememberTextFieldState("4543 60** **** 0719"),
    modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
    enabled = false,
    label = "Saved card",
    supportingText = "Disabled: cannot be changed for this payment",
    textStyle = PantrixTheme.typography.title,
    tagKey = "saved_card"
)

private val GroupedInThousands = OutputTransformation {
    val whole = asCharSequence().indexOf(',').let { comma -> if (comma < 0) length else comma }
    // From right to left: each dot added later lies to the left of those added before it, and does not shift them.
    var at = whole - 3
    while (at > 0) {
        insert(at, ".")
        at -= 3
    }
}

examples.name: AutoResizeTextFieldOwnColorsAndStyle
examples.title: Its own colours and style
examples.description:
This field has no style or colour class of its own: it takes the `TextFieldColors` and the `TextFieldStyle` of `PantrixTextField`. A product that restyles its text fields restyles this one with them.

In the first field the text, the focused border and the caret are the app's own purple. The second field's box is fully round: `TextFieldStyle(shape = ShapeRole.Full)`. `textStyle` and `style` are two different things: the first is the text's style, the second the box's.
examples.code:
val own = ownColors()
PantrixAutoResizeTextField(
    state = rememberTextFieldState("2026 Spring Campaign"),
    modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
    label = "Campaign name",
    textStyle = PantrixTheme.typography.title,
    colors = TextFieldColors(focusedBorder = own.color, text = own.color, cursor = own.color),
    tagKey = "own_colors"
)
PantrixAutoResizeTextField(
    state = rememberTextFieldState("PX-2026-0914"),
    modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
    label = "Tracking number",
    textStyle = PantrixTheme.typography.title,
    style = TextFieldStyle(shape = ShapeRole.Full),
    tagKey = "pill"
)

appNames.name: ownColors
appNames.description: The "app's own colour" of the examples: a purple that is in none of the theme's roles. It is there to show what changes when a component is given `colors`; given one of the theme's roles, nobody could tell whether the colour came from the component's tone or from the parameter.

pages.title: Filled Auto Resize Text Field
pages.summary:
A text field whose label is inside its box and whose text gets smaller to stay in view: an amount, a card number, a short note, in the filled text field's box. The text is as large as its style says while it fits the box; when it does not, it is set as small as it takes to fit, and it grows back as it is deleted.

Its box is `PantrixFilledTextField`'s, and its shrinking text `PantrixAutoResizeTextField`'s. It takes the filled field's `style` and `colors`: the filled fields are restyled together, and the two fields that shrink their text can stand in for each other. It is built on a `TextFieldState`, and has an overload that takes a `value` and an `onValueChange`, and one that takes a form's field.
features: **The label inside the box.** At rest `label` stands in the text's place: in the `body` size, whatever the text's style. With the focus, or while the field holds a text, it moves up to its own line above the text.

**A box that does not change.** The box's width is its style's least or the one its caller gave it; a text that grows longer does not widen it: it is set as small as it takes to fit, and grows back when it is shortened.

**The largest size.** `textStyle` is the style of the text at its largest: a role of the theme's typography, such as `title` for an amount. A large style makes the box taller only by what its label and one line of that style need.

**The smallest size.** `minFontSize` is the smallest the text gets: a size in sp, or one in em, which is a share of the style's size. It is the theme's `footnote` size unless given. A text that still does not fit at that size scrolls, as the text of any field does.

**Several lines.** In a field of several lines the box grows with its text from the least of its lines to the most; from there the box keeps its height, and the text is set smaller, its line spacing with it.
**A given height.** A height the field is given comes before its lines: the box fills what the supporting text leaves of it, and the text is fitted to that height.
**Placeholder.** `placeholder` shows while the label is out of its place: while the field is empty and has the focus. It is in the text's style, and where it is long it shrinks too.
**Fill, outline and error.** At rest the box is filled and has no outline; it is outlined with the focus and in error. `error` does not change the label's colour. A disabled field has no fill.

**Three overloads.** In the one that takes a `state` the text is read from the state. The one that takes a `value` and an `onValueChange` keeps the text with its caller, and takes its lines as `singleLine`, `minLines` and `maxLines`. The one that takes a `field` is bound to a form's field.

**Automation key.** With `tagKey` the field is named `FilledAutoResizeTextField_<tagKey>`, and its clear button `FilledAutoResizeTextFieldClear_<tagKey>`. The field reports that it took the focus and that it was cleared, and never its text.

examples.name: FilledAutoResizeTextFieldPlain
examples.title: At its plainest
examples.description:
The least there is to write: a `TextFieldState` and a label. The field was given no width: the box is at its style's least width and does not grow wider with its text. The account name is too long for that box, so it is drawn smaller; and since the field holds a text, the label is on its own line above the text.

Delete the text: what is left grows back. Once the field is empty and loses the focus, the label comes down to the text's place.
examples.code:
PantrixFilledAutoResizeTextField(
    state = rememberTextFieldState("Yılmaz Mimarlık ve Mühendislik Limited Şirketi"),
    label = "Account name",
    tagKey = "account_name"
)

examples.name: FilledAutoResizeTextFieldTextStyle
examples.title: The text style and the box's height
examples.description:
`textStyle` is the style of the text at its largest; without it the text is in the `body` size. A large style makes the box taller only by what its label and one line of that style need: compare the first two fields.

The third field is empty and in the `display` style. Whatever the text's style, the label rests in the text's place in the `body` size. Press the field: the label moves up, and the placeholder appears in the text's style.
examples.code:
PantrixFilledAutoResizeTextField(
    state = rememberTextFieldState("1250"),
    modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
    label = "No style given",
    tagKey = "style_body"
)
PantrixFilledAutoResizeTextField(
    state = rememberTextFieldState("1250"),
    modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
    label = "In the title style",
    textStyle = PantrixTheme.typography.title,
    tagKey = "style_title"
)
PantrixFilledAutoResizeTextField(
    state = rememberTextFieldState(),
    modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
    label = "In the display style, empty",
    placeholder = "0",
    textStyle = PantrixTheme.typography.display,
    tagKey = "style_display"
)

examples.name: FilledAutoResizeTextFieldSmallestSize
examples.title: The smallest size
examples.description:
Both fields hold the same name in the `title` style, and the name fits neither box. The first was given no `minFontSize`: the text shrinks as far as the theme's `footnote` size. In the second it is never set smaller than 16 sp. `minFontSize` can also be given in em: it is then a share of the style's own size.

A text that still does not fit at its smallest size stops shrinking and scrolls, as the text of any field does.
examples.code:
val company = "Yılmaz Mimarlık, Mühendislik ve Danışmanlık Limited Şirketi"
PantrixFilledAutoResizeTextField(
    state = rememberTextFieldState(company),
    label = "Not given: footnote size",
    textStyle = PantrixTheme.typography.title,
    tagKey = "smallest_default"
)
PantrixFilledAutoResizeTextField(
    state = rememberTextFieldState(company),
    label = "Smallest 16 sp",
    textStyle = PantrixTheme.typography.title,
    minFontSize = 16.sp,
    tagKey = "smallest_sp"
)

examples.name: FilledAutoResizeTextFieldPayment
examples.title: An amount that carries its text to a ViewModel
examples.description:
A payment amount, in the `headline` style. The field's state is created with `rememberTextFieldState`, from the value the ViewModel holds at that moment; the text in the state is followed with `snapshotFlow`, and every change is reported to the ViewModel. This is how the text is taken from the field's state.

The first value in the ViewModel is read once. From then on it goes one way: the text flows from the field to the ViewModel. When the screen is composed anew the ViewModel is still there, and the field starts with its value.

The line below shows what the ViewModel holds, and the button reads from it too: it cannot be pressed until an amount has arrived.

examples.name: FilledAutoResizeTextFieldCustomerNumber
examples.title: A field whose text is held as a String
examples.description:
A customer number of twelve digits. The caller holds the number as a `String`: the field shows it and asks for every change, and since a change that is not all digits is not taken, it is not shown either. The supporting text is made from that `String`.

The text that is asked for has to come back as `value` by the next frame, or the field shows the old text and the caret jumps: keep the text in state that the callback writes at once, and choose the overload that takes a `state` when the text lives in a flow.
examples.code:
var number by rememberSaveable { mutableStateOf("") }
val missing = 12 - number.length
PantrixFilledAutoResizeTextField(
    value = number,
    onValueChange = { if (it.all(Char::isDigit)) number = it },
    modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
    label = "Customer number",
    supportingText = if (missing == 0) "Number complete" else "Digits to go: $missing",
    maxLength = 12,
    showCharacterCount = false,
    textStyle = PantrixTheme.typography.title,
    keyboardOptions = KeyboardOptions(keyboardType = KeyboardType.Number),
    tagKey = "customer_number"
)

examples.name: FilledAutoResizeTextFieldReferenceForm
examples.title: A reference code bound to a form
examples.description:
The overload that takes a `field` gets its value, its error and its name from its field in the form: leave the code empty and move on, and the rule's message takes the place of the supporting text. In a field that is given `form`, the keyboard's action key submits the form through the "Save reference" button.

The text of a field bound to a form is the value of the form's field: it does not have to be taken separately.

examples.name: FilledAutoResizeTextFieldDeliveryAddress
examples.title: An address of several lines
examples.description:
A delivery address of several lines. The caller holds the address as a `String`; in this overload the field takes its lines as `singleLine`, `minLines` and `maxLines`. The box is two lines tall and grows to three; once the address passes three lines the box stays as it is, and the text is set as small as it takes to fit, its line spacing with it.

The supporting text is made from the `String` the caller holds. Its limit is 240 characters; its count is hidden with `showCharacterCount = false`.
examples.code:
var address by rememberSaveable { mutableStateOf("") }
PantrixFilledAutoResizeTextField(
    value = address,
    onValueChange = { address = it },
    modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
    label = "Delivery address",
    supportingText = if (address.isBlank()) "Neighbourhood, street, house number" else "Characters: ${address.length}",
    showClearButton = true,
    maxLength = 240,
    showCharacterCount = false,
    singleLine = false,
    minLines = 2,
    maxLines = 3,
    keyboardOptions = KeyboardOptions(capitalization = KeyboardCapitalization.Sentences),
    tagKey = "delivery_address"
)

examples.name: FilledAutoResizeTextFieldSupportingTextAndError
examples.title: Supporting text and error
examples.description:
`supportingText` stands under the box. `error = true` outlines the box in the `danger` colour; the supporting text and the caret turn to that colour too, and a screen reader announces the message as the error. The label keeps its own colour.

The field starts in error: the plate has lowercase letters. Type them again in capitals: the error goes. It is the caller, not the field, that works out the error; here by reading `plate.text`.
examples.code:
val plate = rememberTextFieldState("34 abc 1903")
val lowercase = plate.text.any(Char::isLowerCase)
PantrixFilledAutoResizeTextField(
    state = plate,
    modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
    label = "Licence plate",
    supportingText = if (lowercase) "Type the plate in capitals" else "As written on the registration document",
    error = lowercase,
    showClearButton = true,
    maxLength = 12,
    showCharacterCount = false,
    textStyle = PantrixTheme.typography.title,
    keyboardOptions = KeyboardOptions(capitalization = KeyboardCapitalization.Characters),
    tagKey = "plate"
)

examples.name: FilledAutoResizeTextFieldDisabledAndReadOnly
examples.title: Disabled and read-only
examples.description:
`enabled = false` takes the field's fill away: the field is drawn in the theme's disabled text colour and takes no focus. Its text is still fitted to its box: the IBAN is in the `title` style, and is set smaller in a box it does not fit.

With `readOnly = true` the field keeps its fill: it can be focused, and its text selected and copied; it just cannot be changed.
examples.code:
PantrixFilledAutoResizeTextField(
    state = rememberTextFieldState("TR330006100519786457841326"),
    modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
    enabled = false,
    label = "Saved IBAN",
    supportingText = "Disabled: in the title style, shrunk to fit",
    textStyle = PantrixTheme.typography.title,
    tagKey = "saved_iban"
)
PantrixFilledAutoResizeTextField(
    state = rememberTextFieldState("PX-2026-0914-TR-000187"),
    modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
    readOnly = true,
    label = "Contract number",
    supportingText = "Read-only: it can be selected and copied",
    textStyle = PantrixTheme.typography.title,
    tagKey = "contract_no"
)

examples.name: FilledAutoResizeTextFieldOwnColorsAndStyle
examples.title: Its own colours and style
examples.description:
This field takes the filled text field's `FilledTextFieldColors` and `FilledTextFieldStyle`: the filled fields are restyled together.

The first field's fill, label, text, outline and caret are from the app's own purple; the fill with the focus was not given, and is the theme's surface colour. The second's box is fully round: `FilledTextFieldStyle(shape = ShapeRole.Full)`. `textStyle` is the style of the text, `style` that of the box.
examples.code:
val own = ownColors()
PantrixFilledAutoResizeTextField(
    state = rememberTextFieldState("Summer 2026 Collection"),
    modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
    label = "List name",
    textStyle = PantrixTheme.typography.title,
    colors = FilledTextFieldColors(
        container = own.container,
        focusedOutline = own.color,
        text = own.onContainer,
        label = own.onContainer,
        cursor = own.color
    ),
    tagKey = "own_colors"
)
PantrixFilledAutoResizeTextField(
    state = rememberTextFieldState("KP-48213"),
    modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
    label = "Coupon",
    textStyle = PantrixTheme.typography.title,
    style = FilledTextFieldStyle(shape = ShapeRole.Full),
    tagKey = "pill"
)

appNames.name: ownColors
appNames.description: The "app's own colour" of the examples: a purple that is in none of the theme's roles. It is there to show what changes when a component is given `colors`; given one of the theme's roles, nobody could tell whether the colour came from the component's tone or from the parameter.

pages.title: Text Area
pages.summary: Text of several lines: a comment, a message, a note. While it is empty the box is its least lines tall; it grows a line at a time as it is typed in, at its most lines the text scrolls inside the box, and the thin bar at the box's end shows how far. Its label, box and supporting text are `PantrixTextField`'s, and it takes that field's style and colours.
features: **Three overloads.** The one that takes a `state` keeps the text in a `TextFieldState`. The one that takes a `value` and an `onValueChange` keeps the text in its caller; the text field underneath does not tell how far it is scrolled, so its box has no bar. The one that takes a `field` takes its value, its error and its name from the form's field.

**Lines.** `minLines` (3 by default) says how many lines the box is at the least, and `maxLines` (8 by default) at the most. A `Modifier.height` given to the field takes the place of the lines, and the text scrolls inside the box.

**Enter is a new line.** The keyboard's action key is always the new line: on Android another action would take the place of the key for a new line. Sending is `onSubmit`'s: Ctrl+Enter or Cmd+Enter on a hardware keyboard. A software keyboard has no such keys; the screen gives a send button as well. Tab moves the focus on and types no tab.

**A soft limit.** `maxLength` can be passed (`TextLimit.Allow`): past it the count says how far past in words ("12 over the limit"), and the count and the border turn to the error's colour. A paste that does not fit is taken whole, and the user cuts it where they choose. A form is not submitted with a bound field's text past the limit. `TextLimit.Block` turns an edit past the limit down whole, as a text field's limit does.

**The count and a screen reader.** Up to the limit the count writes "120/500". A screen reader is told it once typing stops, at the limit and past it: told at every key, it would talk over the keyboard's own echo of each letter.
**Icons and the clear button.** `leadingIcon`, `trailingIcon` and `showClearButton` stand at the first line, not in the middle of the box.

**The handle that resizes.** On the platforms used with a pointer, a desktop and the web, the handle in the box's bottom corner drags the box taller and shorter. A dragged box does not grow with its text, and is never shorter than its least lines. A phone has no handle: a finger on the box scrolls the text. `resizable = false` takes the handle away.

**Putting the keyboard away.** On iOS the keyboard of a field of several lines has no key that puts it away. `Modifier.clearFocusOnTap()` on the screen's root clears the focus on a tap outside the field, and the keyboard goes; this catalogue does so too.

**Style, colours and direction.** `style` (`TextFieldStyle`) and `colors` (`TextFieldColors`) are the text field's; the handle takes the icon's colour and the bar the `scrollBar` colour. In a right-to-left layout the handle is in the bottom corner at the left.
