examples.name: TextAreaComment
examples.title: A comment that grows
examples.description:
A comment field: three lines while it is empty, it grows a line at a time as it is typed in, and at eight lines the text scrolls inside the box. The thin bar at the box's end shows how far the text is scrolled. A sentence starts with a capital: the keyboard opens that way.

`maxLength = 500` writes the count under the box. The line below reads `comment.text` as it is typed.
examples.code:
val comment = rememberTextFieldState()
PantrixTextArea(
    state = comment,
    modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
    label = "Comment",
    placeholder = "What did you think of the product?",
    supportingText = "Your comment is public",
    maxLength = 500,
    tagKey = "comment"
)
PantrixText(
    text = "Lines: ${comment.text.lines().size}",
    color = PantrixTheme.colors.textSecondary
)

examples.name: TextAreaFixedHeight
examples.title: A field given a height
examples.description:
A height given to the field is the whole field's: `Modifier.height(200.dp)`. The box fills what the label and the count leave of it; that height takes the place of the lines, and a text that does not fit scrolls inside the box.

The second field is given `heightIn`: the handle drags the box only within that range. A fixed height leaves the handle nothing to move.
examples.code:
PantrixTextArea(
    state = rememberTextFieldState(DELIVERY_NOTES),
    modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth().height(200.dp),
    label = "Delivery instructions",
    showClearButton = true,
    maxLength = 400,
    tagKey = "instructions"
)
PantrixTextArea(
    state = rememberTextFieldState(),
    modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth().heightIn(max = 320.dp),
    label = "Extra note",
    supportingText = "The handle makes it 320dp tall at the most",
    tagKey = "extra_note"
)

private const val DELIVERY_NOTES =
    "Use the back door of the building; the bell on the front door does not work. The lift is serviced on Fridays, " +
        "take the stairs to the third floor. If I am out, leave the parcel with the porter, Mr Hasan. Thank you!"

examples.name: TextAreaSoftLimit
examples.title: A soft limit and the count
examples.description:
The limit is soft: the text may pass 140 characters. Past it the count says how far past in words ("6 over the limit"), the count and the border turn to the error's colour, and a screen reader is told the field's error, "Too long". Paste a long text: it is taken whole, and you can cut it where you choose.

Type and stop with a screen reader on: the count is told once, after typing stops.
examples.code:
PantrixTextArea(
    state = rememberTextFieldState(ALMOST_A_POST),
    modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
    label = "Post",
    supportingText = "140 characters at the most",
    minLines = 2,
    maxLength = 140,
    // The default: the text may pass the limit.
    overLimit = TextLimit.Allow,
    tagKey = "post"
)

private const val ALMOST_A_POST =
    "The new version is out! A dark theme, faster search and an offline mode are here. Tell us what you think; " +
        "your comments guide us."

examples.name: TextAreaBlockedLimit
examples.title: A limit that blocks, on a field whose text is a String
examples.description:
`overLimit = TextLimit.Block` turns down an edit past the limit whole: typing stops at the limit, and a paste that does not fit is not put in at all.

This field holds its text as a `String`: `value` and `onValueChange`. An edit past the limit is never asked of `onValueChange`. The text field underneath does not tell how far it is scrolled, so this overload's box has no bar.
examples.code:
var reason by remember { mutableStateOf("") }
PantrixTextArea(
    value = reason,
    onValueChange = { reason = it },
    modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
    label = "Reason for the return",
    placeholder = "In a few words",
    minLines = 2,
    maxLines = 4,
    maxLength = 80,
    overLimit = TextLimit.Block,
    tagKey = "return_reason"
)

examples.name: TextAreaSubmit
examples.title: Sending with Ctrl/Cmd+Enter
examples.description:
`onSubmit` is called by Ctrl+Enter or Cmd+Enter on a hardware keyboard; Enter alone starts a new line. A software keyboard has no such keys, so a "Send" button stands beside it as well. Type a message and press Ctrl+Enter: the app's snackbar says the message was sent, and the field is emptied.

The send is reported as an event (`submit`); what was typed never is.

examples.name: TextAreaForm
examples.title: Bound to a form's field
examples.description:
The `PantrixTextArea` that takes a `field` takes its value, its error and its name from the form's field: no `tagKey` is given, the field's `id` is the automation key (`TextArea_<id>`). With `form` given, Ctrl+Enter or Cmd+Enter submits the form through the "Save" button.

The limit is soft, but the form is not submitted with a text past it: the field is in error with "Too long", the count says how far past, and the focus goes to the field. Leave the field empty, or go past 160 characters, and press "Save".
examples.code:
val snackbars = LocalPantrixSnackbars.current
val scope = rememberCoroutineScope()
val form = rememberFormState()
PantrixTextArea(
    field = form.field("bio", initial = "", Rules.notBlank("Tell us about yourself in a few sentences")),
    modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
    form = form,
    label = "About me",
    supportingText = "Shown on your profile",
    maxLength = 160
)
PantrixButton(
    text = "Save",
    onClick = {
        scope.launch { form.submit { snackbars?.show(message = "Profile saved", tagKey = "bio_saved") } }
    },
    form = form,
    tagKey = "save_bio"
)

examples.name: TextAreaDisabledAndReadOnly
examples.title: Disabled and read-only
examples.description:
`enabled = false` draws the field in the theme's disabled colours: it takes no focus, cannot be typed into, has no handle, and a screen reader is told it is disabled.

`readOnly = true` only stops changes: the field is focused, its text selected, copied and scrolled; it can be made taller with the handle and read.
examples.code:
PantrixTextArea(
    state = rememberTextFieldState("Your order has shipped; no note can be added."),
    modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
    enabled = false,
    label = "Shipping note",
    minLines = 2,
    tagKey = "shipping_note"
)
PantrixTextArea(
    state = rememberTextFieldState(RETURN_POLICY),
    modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
    readOnly = true,
    label = "Return policy",
    maxLines = 4,
    tagKey = "return_policy"
)

private const val RETURN_POLICY =
    "You can return the product within 14 days of the day you received it. It must be unused, with its labels " +
        "still on and in its original packaging. We pay for the return shipping. Your money goes back to the card you " +
        "paid with within 3 working days of the product reaching our warehouse."

examples.name: TextAreaOwnColorsAndStyle
examples.title: Its own colours and style
examples.description:
`colors` and `style` are the text field's: `TextFieldColors` and `TextFieldStyle`. The colours that are given are used, and the rest stay the theme's roles. The first field's border, caret and scroll bar are the app's own purple; the handle and the clear button take the icon's colour.

The second field's style draws the box rounder with `ShapeRole.Large` and gives it more padding.
examples.code:
val own = ownColors()
PantrixTextArea(
    state = rememberTextFieldState(DELIVERY_NOTES),
    modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
    label = "Note",
    showClearButton = true,
    maxLines = 4,
    colors = TextFieldColors(
        focusedBorder = own.color,
        cursor = own.color,
        icon = own.color,
        scrollBar = own.color
    ),
    tagKey = "own_colors"
)
PantrixTextArea(
    state = rememberTextFieldState(),
    modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
    label = "Description",
    style = TextFieldStyle(shape = ShapeRole.Large, horizontalPadding = 20.dp, verticalPadding = 16.dp),
    tagKey = "own_style"
)

private const val DELIVERY_NOTES =
    "Use the back door of the building; the bell on the front door does not work. The lift is serviced on Fridays, " +
        "take the stairs to the third floor. If I am out, leave the parcel with the porter, Mr Hasan. Thank you!"

appNames.name: ownColors
appNames.description: The "app's own colour" of the examples: a purple that is in none of the theme's roles. It is there to show what changes when a component is given `colors`; given one of the theme's roles, nobody could tell whether the colour came from the component's tone or from the parameter.

examples.name: TextAreaResize
examples.title: The handle that resizes
examples.description:
On a desktop and on the web, drag the handle in the box's bottom corner: the box gets taller or shorter, and the pointer turns to an up-and-down resize arrow. A dragged box keeps that height and does not grow with its text; nor is it ever shorter than its least lines. A phone has no handle.

The second field has `resizable = false`: no handle, and the box grows with its text alone.
examples.code:
PantrixTextArea(
    state = rememberTextFieldState(),
    modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
    label = "Meeting notes",
    supportingText = "Make it taller with the handle in the bottom corner",
    tagKey = "meeting_notes"
)
PantrixTextArea(
    state = rememberTextFieldState(),
    modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
    label = "Short note",
    minLines = 2,
    maxLines = 4,
    resizable = false,
    tagKey = "short_note"
)

examples.name: TextAreaRightToLeft
examples.title: Right to left
examples.description: In a right-to-left layout the icon and the clear button swap places, the handle moves to the bottom corner at the left, and the scroll bar stands at the box's left: that is where a line ends. Each paragraph takes its direction from its own first letter.

examples.name: TextAreaTapOutside
examples.title: A tap outside puts the keyboard away
examples.description:
On iOS the keyboard of a field of several lines has no key that puts it away. `Modifier.clearFocusOnTap()` clears the focus when an empty part of this column is tapped, and the keyboard goes. A tap on the field or on a button is theirs: the caret moves, the button does its work. A scroll is no tap.

The app's root does the same: in this catalogue a tap on any empty part of the page puts the keyboard away.

pages.title: Filled Text Area
pages.summary: Text of several lines in a filled box: a comment, a message, a note. The label is inside the box: it rests in the first line's place while the field is empty and without the focus, and rises above the text when the field takes the focus or holds text. While it is empty the box is its least lines tall; it grows a line at a time as it is typed in, at its most lines the text scrolls inside the box, and the thin bar at the box's end shows how far. Its box and supporting text are `PantrixFilledTextField`'s, and it takes that field's style and colours.
features: **Three overloads.** The one that takes a `state` keeps the text in a `TextFieldState`. The one that takes a `value` and an `onValueChange` keeps the text in its caller; the text field underneath does not tell how far it is scrolled, so its box has no bar. The one that takes a `field` takes its value, its error and its name from the form's field.

**Lines.** `minLines` (3 by default) says how many lines the box is at the least, and `maxLines` (8 by default) at the most. A `Modifier.height` given to the field takes the place of the lines, and the text scrolls inside the box.
**Enter is a new line.** The keyboard's action key is always the new line. Sending is `onSubmit`'s: Ctrl+Enter or Cmd+Enter on a hardware keyboard. Tab moves the focus on and types no tab.

**A soft limit.** `maxLength` can be passed (`TextLimit.Allow`): past it the count says how far past in words ("12 over the limit"), and the count and the outline turn to the error's colour. A form is not submitted with a bound field's text past the limit. `TextLimit.Block` turns an edit past the limit down whole. A screen reader is told the count once typing stops, at the limit and past it.
**Icons and the clear button.** `leadingIcon`, `trailingIcon` and `showClearButton` stand at the first line.
**The handle that resizes.** On a desktop and on the web the handle in the box's bottom corner drags the box taller and shorter; a phone has no handle. `resizable = false` takes the handle away.

**Style, colours and direction.** `style` (`FilledTextFieldStyle`) and `colors` (`FilledTextFieldColors`) are the filled text field's. In a right-to-left layout the handle is in the bottom corner at the left.

examples.name: FilledTextAreaComment
examples.title: A comment that grows
examples.description:
A comment field: three lines while it is empty, with its label resting in the first line's place; a press on the field raises the label above the text, and the placeholder shows. As it is typed in the box grows a line at a time, and at eight lines the text scrolls inside the box. A sentence starts with a capital: the keyboard opens that way.

`maxLength = 500` writes the count under the box. The line below reads `comment.text` as it is typed.
examples.code:
val comment = rememberTextFieldState()
PantrixFilledTextArea(
    state = comment,
    modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
    label = "Comment",
    placeholder = "What did you think of the product?",
    supportingText = "Your comment is public",
    maxLength = 500,
    tagKey = "filled_comment"
)
PantrixText(
    text = "Lines: ${comment.text.lines().size}",
    color = PantrixTheme.colors.textSecondary
)

examples.name: FilledTextAreaFixedHeight
examples.title: A field given a height
examples.description:
A height given to the field is the whole field's: `Modifier.height(200.dp)`. The box fills what the count leaves of it; that height takes the place of the lines, and a text that does not fit scrolls inside the box.

The second field is given `heightIn`: the handle drags the box only within that range. A fixed height leaves the handle nothing to move.
examples.code:
PantrixFilledTextArea(
    state = rememberTextFieldState(DELIVERY_NOTES),
    modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth().height(200.dp),
    label = "Delivery instructions",
    showClearButton = true,
    maxLength = 400,
    tagKey = "filled_instructions"
)
PantrixFilledTextArea(
    state = rememberTextFieldState(),
    modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth().heightIn(max = 320.dp),
    label = "Extra note",
    supportingText = "The handle makes it 320dp tall at the most",
    tagKey = "filled_extra_note"
)

private const val DELIVERY_NOTES =
    "Use the back door of the building; the bell on the front door does not work. The lift is serviced on Fridays, " +
        "take the stairs to the third floor. If I am out, leave the parcel with the porter, Mr Hasan. Thank you!"

examples.name: FilledTextAreaSoftLimit
examples.title: A soft limit and the count
examples.description:
The limit is soft: the text may pass 140 characters. Past it the count says how far past in words ("6 over the limit"), the count and the outline turn to the error's colour, and a screen reader is told the field's error, "Too long". Paste a long text: it is taken whole, and you can cut it where you choose.

Type and stop with a screen reader on: the count is told once, after typing stops.
examples.code:
PantrixFilledTextArea(
    state = rememberTextFieldState(ALMOST_A_POST),
    modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
    label = "Post",
    supportingText = "140 characters at the most",
    minLines = 2,
    maxLength = 140,
    // The default: the text may pass the limit.
    overLimit = TextLimit.Allow,
    tagKey = "filled_post"
)

private const val ALMOST_A_POST =
    "The new version is out! A dark theme, faster search and an offline mode are here. Tell us what you think; " +
        "your comments guide us."

examples.name: FilledTextAreaBlockedLimit
examples.title: A limit that blocks, on a field whose text is a String
examples.description:
`overLimit = TextLimit.Block` turns down an edit past the limit whole: typing stops at the limit, and a paste that does not fit is not put in at all.

This field holds its text as a `String`: `value` and `onValueChange`. An edit past the limit is never asked of `onValueChange`. The text field underneath does not tell how far it is scrolled, so this overload's box has no bar.
examples.code:
var reason by remember { mutableStateOf("") }
PantrixFilledTextArea(
    value = reason,
    onValueChange = { reason = it },
    modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
    label = "Reason for the return",
    placeholder = "In a few words",
    minLines = 2,
    maxLines = 4,
    maxLength = 80,
    overLimit = TextLimit.Block,
    tagKey = "filled_return_reason"
)

examples.name: FilledTextAreaSubmit
examples.title: Sending with Ctrl/Cmd+Enter
examples.description:
`onSubmit` is called by Ctrl+Enter or Cmd+Enter on a hardware keyboard; Enter alone starts a new line. A software keyboard has no such keys, so a "Send" button stands beside it as well. Type a message and press Ctrl+Enter: the app's snackbar says the message was sent, and the field is emptied.

The send is reported as an event (`submit`); what was typed never is.

examples.name: FilledTextAreaForm
examples.title: Bound to a form's field
examples.description:
The `PantrixFilledTextArea` that takes a `field` takes its value, its error and its name from the form's field: no `tagKey` is given, the field's `id` is the automation key (`FilledTextArea_<id>`). With `form` given, Ctrl+Enter or Cmd+Enter submits the form through the "Save" button.

The limit is soft, but the form is not submitted with a text past it: the field is in error with "Too long", the count says how far past, and the focus goes to the field. Leave the field empty, or go past 160 characters, and press "Save".
examples.code:
val snackbars = LocalPantrixSnackbars.current
val scope = rememberCoroutineScope()
val form = rememberFormState()
PantrixFilledTextArea(
    field = form.field("filled_bio", initial = "", Rules.notBlank("Tell us about yourself in a few sentences")),
    modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
    form = form,
    label = "About me",
    supportingText = "Shown on your profile",
    maxLength = 160
)
PantrixButton(
    text = "Save",
    onClick = {
        scope.launch { form.submit { snackbars?.show(message = "Profile saved", tagKey = "filled_bio_saved") } }
    },
    form = form,
    tagKey = "filled_save_bio"
)

examples.name: FilledTextAreaDisabledAndReadOnly
examples.title: Disabled and read-only
examples.description:
`enabled = false` draws the field in the theme's disabled colours: it takes no focus, cannot be typed into, has no handle, and a screen reader is told it is disabled.

`readOnly = true` only stops changes: the field is focused, its text selected, copied and scrolled; it can be made taller with the handle and read.
examples.code:
PantrixFilledTextArea(
    state = rememberTextFieldState("Your order has shipped; no note can be added."),
    modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
    enabled = false,
    label = "Shipping note",
    minLines = 2,
    tagKey = "filled_shipping_note"
)
PantrixFilledTextArea(
    state = rememberTextFieldState(RETURN_POLICY),
    modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
    readOnly = true,
    label = "Return policy",
    maxLines = 4,
    tagKey = "filled_return_policy"
)

private const val RETURN_POLICY =
    "You can return the product within 14 days of the day you received it. It must be unused, with its labels " +
        "still on and in its original packaging. We pay for the return shipping. Your money goes back to the card you " +
        "paid with within 3 working days of the product reaching our warehouse."

examples.name: FilledTextAreaOwnColorsAndStyle
examples.title: Its own colours and style
examples.description:
`colors` and `style` are the filled text field's: `FilledTextFieldColors` and `FilledTextFieldStyle`. The colours that are given are used, and the rest stay the theme's roles. The first field's outline with the focus, its caret and its scroll bar are the app's own purple; the handle and the clear button take the icon's colour.

The second field's style draws the box rounder with `ShapeRole.Large` and gives it more padding.
examples.code:
val own = ownColors()
PantrixFilledTextArea(
    state = rememberTextFieldState(DELIVERY_NOTES),
    modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
    label = "Note",
    showClearButton = true,
    maxLines = 4,
    colors = FilledTextFieldColors(
        focusedOutline = own.color,
        cursor = own.color,
        icon = own.color,
        scrollBar = own.color
    ),
    tagKey = "filled_own_colors"
)
PantrixFilledTextArea(
    state = rememberTextFieldState(),
    modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
    label = "Description",
    style = FilledTextFieldStyle(shape = ShapeRole.Large, horizontalPadding = 20.dp, verticalPadding = 16.dp),
    tagKey = "filled_own_style"
)

private const val DELIVERY_NOTES =
    "Use the back door of the building; the bell on the front door does not work. The lift is serviced on Fridays, " +
        "take the stairs to the third floor. If I am out, leave the parcel with the porter, Mr Hasan. Thank you!"

appNames.name: ownColors
appNames.description: The "app's own colour" of the examples: a purple that is in none of the theme's roles. It is there to show what changes when a component is given `colors`; given one of the theme's roles, nobody could tell whether the colour came from the component's tone or from the parameter.

examples.name: FilledTextAreaResize
examples.title: The handle that resizes
examples.description:
On a desktop and on the web, drag the handle in the box's bottom corner: the box gets taller or shorter, and the pointer turns to an up-and-down resize arrow. A dragged box keeps that height and does not grow with its text; nor is it ever shorter than its least lines. A phone has no handle.

The second field has `resizable = false`: no handle, and the box grows with its text alone.
examples.code:
PantrixFilledTextArea(
    state = rememberTextFieldState(),
    modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
    label = "Meeting notes",
    supportingText = "Make it taller with the handle in the bottom corner",
    tagKey = "filled_meeting_notes"
)
PantrixFilledTextArea(
    state = rememberTextFieldState(),
    modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
    label = "Short note",
    minLines = 2,
    maxLines = 4,
    resizable = false,
    tagKey = "filled_short_note"
)

examples.name: FilledTextAreaRightToLeft
examples.title: Right to left
examples.description: In a right-to-left layout the icon and the clear button swap places, the handle moves to the bottom corner at the left, and the scroll bar stands at the box's left: that is where a line ends. Each paragraph takes its direction from its own first letter.

pages.title: Checkbox
pages.summary:
A box that is checked or not, and the label beside it. It is for options that are independent of each other: subscribing to a newsletter, accepting a condition, selecting a few rows of a list. `PantrixTriStateCheckbox` shows a third state too: the "select all" box, which is neither checked nor unchecked while some of the rows under it are selected.

The box changes nothing by itself: it is whatever `checked` says. A press reports the value that is asked for with `onCheckedChange`; the caller keeps the state.
features: **One target.** The box, the label and the supporting text are one target: a press on the text changes the box too. However small the box is, the row takes as much room as the platform's touch target.
**Label and supporting text.** `label` stands beside the box, and `supportingText` under it in smaller text. The box is on the label's first line, however many lines the text runs to.

**Three states.** `PantrixTriStateCheckbox` takes a `ToggleableState`: checked, unchecked or indeterminate. An indeterminate box draws a dash, and is read to a screen reader as indeterminate, not as unchecked. What a press leads to is the caller's to say.
**Error.** `error` turns the box and the supporting text to the theme's `danger` role; a screen reader is told the input is invalid.

**Form.** The `PantrixCheckbox` that takes a `field` gets its value, its error and its name from the form's field. The rule's message shows after the first change or on an attempt to submit the form, and takes the place of the supporting text.

**Read-only and disabled.** If `onCheckedChange` is null the box is read-only: it takes no press and no focus, and still says its name and its state. `enabled = false` draws the box in the disabled colours.

**Colours of its own.** `CheckboxColors` takes the fill, the tick and the edge separately; one that is left out stays in the theme's role. A disabled box and a box in error are drawn in the theme's colours even when colours are given.
**Style.** `CheckboxStyle` changes the box's size, its corners and the thickness of its lines. The box is 18dp, and 22dp on iOS; its corners are the small step of the shape scale.
**The box at the end.** `controlPosition = ControlPosition.End` puts the box at the end of the label: given a width, the row has the box at its end.
**Screen reader.** One checkbox is read: its name is its label, and its state is said in the theme's language. A box without a label gets its name from `contentDescription`.
**Motion.** The tick is drawn on and off, and the fill fades in and out with it. Where the theme's motion is reduced, both happen at once.
api: com.pantrixui.components.elements.checkbox.PantrixCheckbox(Boolean, ((Boolean) -> Unit)?, Modifier, Boolean, String?, String?, Boolean, CheckboxStyle?, CheckboxColors?, String?, String?, MutableInteractionSource?, ControlPosition)
com.pantrixui.components.elements.checkbox.PantrixCheckbox(FormField<Boolean>, Modifier, Boolean, String?, String?, CheckboxStyle?, CheckboxColors?, String?, ControlPosition)

examples.name: CheckboxLabelled
examples.title: Label and supporting text
examples.description: Its plainest form: `checked` reads the state, and `onCheckedChange` reports the value that is asked for. `label` stands beside the box and `supportingText` under it, and the three are one target. Press the text: the box still changes.
examples.code:
var newsletter by rememberSaveable { mutableStateOf(true) }
PantrixCheckbox(
    checked = newsletter,
    onCheckedChange = { newsletter = it },
    label = "Weekly newsletter",
    supportingText = "One email a week; you can unsubscribe at any time",
    tagKey = "newsletter"
)

examples.name: CheckboxSelectAll
examples.title: Three states: select all
examples.description:
`PantrixTriStateCheckbox` draws a third state. While some of the boxes under it are selected, "All notifications" is neither checked nor unchecked: it shows a dash, and that is how a screen reader reads it.

The caller works out the state, not the box: `On` if all are selected, `Off` if none is selected, `Indeterminate` in between. `onClick` only reports that it was pressed; here it selects them all, and when all are selected it clears them all.

examples.name: CheckboxError
examples.title: Error
examples.description:
`error` turns the box and the supporting text to the theme's `danger` role, and a screen reader is told the input is invalid. While the error lasts, the supporting text is the message itself: it says what to put right.

Here the example works out the error itself: `error` is true while the box is unchecked. Check the box: the colour and the text go back to what they were.
examples.code:
var read by rememberSaveable { mutableStateOf(false) }
PantrixCheckbox(
    checked = read,
    onCheckedChange = { read = it },
    label = "I have read the privacy notice",
    supportingText = if (read) "Thank you" else "Check this box to continue",
    error = !read,
    tagKey = "privacy"
)

examples.name: CheckboxInAForm
examples.title: Consent bound to a form
examples.description:
The `PantrixCheckbox` that takes a `field` is bound to a field of a form: it gets its value, its error and its name from the field; `checked` and `onCheckedChange` are not given. The field's id is the automation key: this box is `Checkbox_terms`.

Press "Send" without checking the box: the message of the `Rules.mustBeTrue` rule takes the place of the supporting text, and the focus goes to the box. When the box is checked the message goes away; when the form is submitted, the app's snackbar lets you know.

examples.name: CheckboxDisabledAndReadOnly
examples.title: Disabled and read-only
examples.description:
`enabled = false` draws the box in the disabled colours: the box takes no press, and a screen reader is told it is disabled.

With `onCheckedChange = null` the box is read-only: it takes no press and no focus, its colours do not change, and it still says its name and its state. It is only for showing what was selected.
examples.code:
PantrixCheckbox(checked = true, onCheckedChange = {}, enabled = false, label = "Disabled", tagKey = "off")
PantrixCheckbox(
    checked = true,
    onCheckedChange = null,
    label = "Read-only",
    supportingText = "Cannot be pressed; it only shows its state",
    tagKey = "read_only"
)

examples.name: CheckboxWithoutALabel
examples.title: Without a label: in a row of a list
examples.description:
A box without a label: in a row of a table or a list, the text is already in the row. `contentDescription` tells a screen reader the box's name: "Select order 1042".

The text in the row is no part of the box: what is pressed is the box and the touch target reserved around it.

examples.name: CheckboxOwnColors
examples.title: Its own colours
examples.description:
`colors` changes only the fields that are given: the fill of the "Gift wrap" box is in the app's own purple, and its tick in the colour that reads on that purple; its edge stays in the theme's colour. Uncheck the box: its edge is the same as the other boxes'.

These are the colours of a box that can be pressed and is not in error. The second box was given the same colours too, but it is disabled: it is drawn in the theme's disabled colours. A box in error stays in the theme's `danger` role as well.
examples.code:
val own = ownColors()
var giftWrap by rememberSaveable { mutableStateOf(true) }
PantrixCheckbox(
    checked = giftWrap,
    onCheckedChange = { giftWrap = it },
    label = "Gift wrap",
    supportingText = "The box's fill and tick were given by the caller",
    colors = CheckboxColors(checked = own.color, checkmark = own.onColor),
    tagKey = "gift_wrap"
)
PantrixCheckbox(
    checked = true,
    onCheckedChange = {},
    enabled = false,
    label = "Gift note",
    supportingText = "The same colours were given; a disabled box stays in the theme's colour",
    colors = CheckboxColors(checked = own.color, checkmark = own.onColor),
    tagKey = "gift_note"
)

appNames.name: ownColors
appNames.description: The "app's own colour" of the examples: a purple that is in none of the theme's roles. It is there to show what changes when a component is given `colors`; given one of the theme's roles, nobody could tell whether the colour came from the component's tone or from the parameter.

examples.name: CheckboxOwnStyle
examples.title: Style
examples.description:
`style` changes the geometry of one box: `size` is the box's size, `shape` its corners, and `strokeWidth` the thickness of the lines of the edge and the tick. Only the fields that are given change; the rest comes from the theme's and the platform's style.

The first box is 24dp and its line is 3dp; the second has square corners. The box's colour is no part of the style: it comes from the state and from `colors`.
examples.code:
var large by rememberSaveable { mutableStateOf(true) }
var square by rememberSaveable { mutableStateOf(true) }
PantrixCheckbox(
    checked = large,
    onCheckedChange = { large = it },
    label = "Large box, thick line",
    style = CheckboxStyle(size = 24.dp, strokeWidth = 3.dp),
    tagKey = "large"
)
PantrixCheckbox(
    checked = square,
    onCheckedChange = { square = it },
    label = "Square box",
    style = CheckboxStyle(shape = ShapeSpec.Fixed(RectangleShape)),
    tagKey = "square"
)

examples.name: CheckboxAtTheEnd
examples.title: The box at the end
examples.description: The box at the end of the label (`controlPosition = ControlPosition.End`): a list's options, the boxes one under another at the column's end. The rows take the column's width (`Modifier.fillMaxWidth()`).

pages.title: Radio Button
pages.summary:
One of several options: a ring and the label beside it. It is almost always used through `PantrixRadioGroup`: the group lays the options out, moves the selection with the arrow keys and binds to a form's field. On its own, `PantrixRadioButton` is for a layout a group cannot make, such as a list where each option is a card.

The group selects nothing by itself: whichever value `selected` says is the one selected. A press and the arrow keys report, through `onSelect`, the value of the option that is wanted; the caller holds the selection.
features: **Options.** An option is a `RadioOption`: its value, its label, the text under the label that says what it is, whether it can be selected, and its automation key.

**One under another or side by side.** `orientation` lays the options out one under another (`Orientation.Vertical`, the default) or side by side (`Orientation.Horizontal`): as many on a line as the width takes, and the rest on the next line.

**Keyboard.** The group is one stop for Tab: the focus comes to the selected option, or to the first option that can be selected while none is. The arrow keys select the next and the previous option, wrap around from the last to the first and skip one that cannot be selected; in a right-to-left layout left and right change places.
**One target.** The ring, the label and the text under it are one target: a press on the words selects too. However small the ring is, the row takes up the platform's touch target.
**Error.** `error` turns the rings and the text under the group to the theme's `danger` role; the group tells a screen reader of the error, once.

**Form.** The `PantrixRadioGroup` that takes a `field` gets its selection, its error and its name from the form's field. A choice that has to be made is built with a field that starts at null and `Rules.required`.

**Disabled and read-only.** `RadioOption(enabled = false)` disables a single option, and the group's `enabled = false` all of them. A `PantrixRadioButton` whose `onClick` is null is read-only: it takes no press and no focus, and says whether it is selected.

**Its own colours and style.** `RadioColors` gives the colour of the selected ring and of the unselected one; `RadioStyle` gives the size of the ring, the size of the dot in it and the thickness of the line. The ring is 20dp and its dot 10dp; on iOS, 22dp and 12dp.

**The ring at the end.** `controlPosition = ControlPosition.End` puts the ring at the end of the label; in a group one under another, the options take the group's width and the rings stand in a column.

**Screen reader.** Each option is a radio button that says whether it is selected; the group's name is `label`. Buttons used on their own are wrapped in `Modifier.selectableGroup()`, so that they are heard as one choice.
**Motion.** The dot of a ring that is selected grows, and the ring turns to the `primary` colour with it. In a theme with reduced motion both happen at once.
api: com.pantrixui.components.elements.radiobutton.PantrixRadioGroup(List<RadioOption<T>>, T?, (T) -> Unit, Modifier, Orientation, Boolean, String?, String?, Boolean, RadioStyle?, RadioColors?, String?, ControlPosition)
com.pantrixui.components.elements.radiobutton.PantrixRadioGroup(FormField<T>, List<RadioOption<T>>, Modifier, Orientation, Boolean, String?, String?, RadioStyle?, RadioColors?, ControlPosition)

examples.name: RadioButtonGroupOfOptions
examples.title: A group and its options
examples.description:
`PantrixRadioGroup` lays the options out one under another below `label`, and writes `supportingText` at the very bottom. Each option is a `RadioOption`; here what each one means is written under it. "Store pickup" cannot be selected (`enabled = false`): a press on it does nothing and the arrow keys skip it.

Try it with the keyboard: Tab enters the group once and stops on the selected option. The down and up arrows move the selection and the focus together, and wrap around from the last option to the first.
examples.code:
var delivery by rememberSaveable { mutableStateOf("standard") }
PantrixRadioGroup(
    options = DELIVERIES,
    selected = delivery,
    onSelect = { delivery = it },
    label = "Delivery",
    supportingText = "You can change it until the order ships",
    tagKey = "delivery"
)

private val DELIVERIES = listOf(
    RadioOption("standard", "Standard", supportingText = "Three to five working days", tagKey = "standard"),
    RadioOption("express", "Express", supportingText = "Next working day", tagKey = "express"),
    RadioOption(
        value = "pickup",
        label = "Store pickup",
        supportingText = "Not available in your city yet",
        enabled = false,
        tagKey = "pickup"
    )
)

examples.name: RadioButtonSideBySide
examples.title: Side by side
examples.description:
`orientation = Orientation.Horizontal` lays the options out side by side: as many on a line as the width takes, and the rest on the next line. The rings are aligned on the first line of their labels, whether or not something is written under a label.

The left and right arrows move the selection too; in a right-to-left layout they swap directions. The down and up arrows are the next and the previous option in both orientations.
examples.code:
var digest by rememberSaveable { mutableStateOf("weekly") }
PantrixRadioGroup(
    options = listOf(
        RadioOption("daily", "Every day", tagKey = "daily"),
        RadioOption("weekly", "Once a week", tagKey = "weekly"),
        RadioOption("monthly", "Once a month", tagKey = "monthly"),
        RadioOption("never", "Never", tagKey = "never")
    ),
    selected = digest,
    onSelect = { digest = it },
    orientation = Orientation.Horizontal,
    label = "Digest email",
    tagKey = "digest"
)

examples.name: RadioButtonInAForm
examples.title: A choice of size bound to a form
examples.description:
The `PantrixRadioGroup` that takes a `field` is bound to a form's field: it gets its selection, its error and its name from the field. This is how a choice that has to be made is built: the field starts at null and carries `Rules.required`. The field's id is the automation key: the group is `RadioGroup_size`, and its options are named inside it.

Press "Add to cart" without picking a size: the rule's message takes the place of the supporting text, the rings turn to the error colour and the focus goes to the group. The sizes are laid out side by side; "XL" is sold out and cannot be selected.
examples.code:
val snackbars = LocalPantrixSnackbars.current
val scope = rememberCoroutineScope()
val form = rememberFormState()
PantrixRadioGroup(
    field = form.field<String?>("size", initial = null, Rules.required("Choose a size to continue")),
    options = SIZES,
    orientation = Orientation.Horizontal,
    label = "Size",
    supportingText = "Runs small; if you are between sizes, choose the larger one"
)
PantrixButton(
    text = "Add to cart",
    onClick = {
        scope.launch { form.submit { snackbars?.show(message = "Added to cart", tagKey = "added_to_cart") } }
    },
    form = form,
    tagKey = "add_to_cart"
)

private val SIZES = listOf("XS", "S", "M", "L", "XL", "XXL").map { size ->
    RadioOption(value = size.lowercase(), label = size, enabled = size != "XL", tagKey = size.lowercase())
}

examples.name: RadioButtonError
examples.title: Error
examples.description:
`error` turns the rings and the text under the group to the theme's `danger` role; the group tells a screen reader that the input is invalid, once. The texts under the options keep their colour: they say what an option is, not what is wrong.

Here the example works out the error itself: `error` is true while none is selected. Pick one: the rings and the text below go back to how they were.
examples.code:
var invoice by rememberSaveable { mutableStateOf<String?>(null) }
PantrixRadioGroup(
    options = listOf(
        RadioOption("personal", "Personal", supportingText = "The invoice is issued in your name", tagKey = "personal"),
        RadioOption("company", "Company", supportingText = "A tax number is required", tagKey = "company")
    ),
    selected = invoice,
    onSelect = { invoice = it },
    label = "Invoice type",
    supportingText = if (invoice == null) "Choose a type to continue" else "You can change it later",
    error = invoice == null,
    tagKey = "invoice"
)

examples.name: RadioButtonDisabledAndReadOnly
examples.title: Disabled and read-only
examples.description:
The group's `enabled = false` disables every option; the label and the supporting text are written in the disabled text colour too. Which option is selected can still be seen.

A `PantrixRadioButton` given `onClick = null` is read-only: it takes no press and no focus, its colours do not change, and it still says its name and that it is selected.
examples.code:
PantrixRadioGroup(
    options = listOf(
        RadioOption("card", "Card", tagKey = "card"),
        RadioOption("transfer", "Bank transfer", tagKey = "transfer")
    ),
    selected = "card",
    onSelect = {},
    orientation = Orientation.Horizontal,
    enabled = false,
    label = "Payment",
    supportingText = "Disabled: your saved card will be charged",
    tagKey = "payment"
)
PantrixRadioButton(
    selected = true,
    onClick = null,
    label = "Read-only",
    supportingText = "Cannot be pressed; it only shows what was chosen",
    tagKey = "read_only"
)

examples.name: RadioButtonInCards
examples.title: On its own: inside cards
examples.description:
On its own, `PantrixRadioButton` is for a layout a group cannot make: here each option is inside a card. The caller holds the selection: each button is told whether it is selected through `selected`, and asks through `onClick` when it is pressed.

The buttons are in a column that carries `Modifier.selectableGroup()`: a screen reader hears them as one choice. Moving with the arrow keys is the group's work, and there is none of it here: each button is a separate stop for Tab.

examples.name: RadioButtonOwnColors
examples.title: Its own colours
examples.description:
`colors` paints every option of the group. Here only the selected ring's colour was given (`RadioColors(selected = …)`): the selected ring and its dot are in the app's own purple, and the others stay in the theme's colour.

These are the colours of a ring that can be selected and is not in error. A disabled option and a group in error are drawn in the theme's colours, even when colours are given.
examples.code:
var wrapping by rememberSaveable { mutableStateOf("gift") }
PantrixRadioGroup(
    options = listOf(
        RadioOption("plain", "Plain", tagKey = "plain"),
        RadioOption("gift", "Gift wrap", tagKey = "gift")
    ),
    selected = wrapping,
    onSelect = { wrapping = it },
    orientation = Orientation.Horizontal,
    label = "Wrapping",
    supportingText = "The selected ring's colour was passed in; the others are in the theme's colour",
    colors = RadioColors(selected = ownColors().color),
    tagKey = "wrapping"
)

appNames.name: ownColors
appNames.description: The "app's own colour" of the examples: a purple that is in none of the theme's roles. It is there to show what changes when a component is given `colors`; given one of the theme's roles, nobody could tell whether the colour came from the component's tone or from the parameter.

examples.name: RadioButtonOwnStyle
examples.title: Style
examples.description:
`style` changes the ring of every option of the group: `size` is the size of the ring, `dotSize` that of the dot in it, and `strokeWidth` how thick the ring's line is. Only the fields that are given change; the rest comes from the theme's and the platform's style.

The ring here is 28dp, its dot 14dp and its line 3dp. The ring's colour is not part of the style: it comes from the state and from `colors`.
examples.code:
var seat by rememberSaveable { mutableStateOf("window") }
PantrixRadioGroup(
    options = listOf(
        RadioOption("window", "Window", tagKey = "window"),
        RadioOption("aisle", "Aisle", tagKey = "aisle")
    ),
    selected = seat,
    onSelect = { seat = it },
    orientation = Orientation.Horizontal,
    label = "Seat",
    style = RadioStyle(size = 28.dp, dotSize = 14.dp, strokeWidth = 3.dp),
    tagKey = "seat"
)

examples.name: RadioButtonAtTheEnd
examples.title: The rings at the end
examples.description: The rings at the end of the options (`controlPosition = ControlPosition.End`): options one under another take the group's width, and their rings stand in a column at the group's end.
examples.code:
var delivery by rememberSaveable { mutableStateOf("standard") }
PantrixRadioGroup(
    options = DELIVERIES,
    selected = delivery,
    onSelect = { delivery = it },
    modifier = Modifier.widthIn(max = 360.dp),
    label = "Delivery",
    tagKey = "delivery_end",
    controlPosition = ControlPosition.End
)

private val DELIVERIES = listOf(
    RadioOption("standard", "Standard", supportingText = "Three to five working days", tagKey = "standard"),
    RadioOption("express", "Express", supportingText = "Next working day", tagKey = "express"),
    RadioOption(
        value = "pickup",
        label = "Store pickup",
        supportingText = "Not available in your city yet",
        enabled = false,
        tagKey = "pickup"
    )
)

pages.title: Switch Button
pages.summary:
A setting that is on or off and takes effect at once: a track, a thumb that slides on it, and the label beside it. Notifications, Wi-Fi, battery saver and the like. An answer that can be wrong is for a checkbox: a switch is a setting.

The switch changes nothing by itself: it is what `checked` says. A press, a key and a drag report the value asked for through `onCheckedChange`; the caller holds the state.
features: **One target.** The track, the label and the supporting text are one target: a press on the words turns the switch too. The row takes the platform's touch target, small as the track is.

**Dragging the thumb.** Let go past the middle of the track, the thumb turns the switch on, and short of the middle it turns it off; let go on the side it started from, it settles back and nothing is reported. The drag runs with the reading direction: in a right-to-left layout the on end is on the left.

**Platform.** On Android the thumb grows from off to on, and further while it is held. On iOS, the desktop and the web it is one size; on iOS it is always white, there is a shadow under it, and the track has no edge.
**Screen reader.** One switch is read: its name is its label, and whether it is on or off is said in the theme's language. A switch with no label gets its name from `contentDescription`.
**Error.** `error` turns only the supporting text to the theme's `danger` role, and a screen reader is told. The switch itself keeps its colours.

**Form.** The `PantrixSwitchButton` that takes a `field` gets its value, its error and its name from the form's field. The rule's message shows after the first change or on an attempt to submit the form, and takes the place of the supporting text.

**Read-only and disabled.** With a null `onCheckedChange` the switch is read-only: it takes no press, no drag and no focus, and still says its name and its state. `enabled = false` draws the switch in the disabled colours.

**Its own colours.** `SwitchColors` takes the colour of the track on and off, of the thumb on and off, and of the edge, each on its own; one that is left out stays the theme's role. A disabled switch is drawn in the theme's colours even when it is given colours.

**Style.** `SwitchStyle` gives the track's width and height, the thumb's size off, on and pressed, the edge's width and the thumb's shadow. `labelStyle` gives the label's type; the track stands on its first line.

**The switch at the end.** `controlPosition = ControlPosition.End` puts the track at the end of the label, as a settings screen has it: given a width, the row has the track at its end, and the label wraps in the room left.
**Motion.** The thumb slides, and the track turns to the `primary` colour with it. In a theme with reduced motion both happen at once.
api: com.pantrixui.components.elements.switchbutton.PantrixSwitchButton(Boolean, ((Boolean) -> Unit)?, Modifier, Boolean, String?, String?, Boolean, SwitchStyle?, SwitchColors?, String?, String?, MutableInteractionSource?, TextStyle, ControlPosition)
com.pantrixui.components.elements.switchbutton.PantrixSwitchButton(FormField<Boolean>, Modifier, Boolean, String?, String?, SwitchStyle?, SwitchColors?, String?, TextStyle, ControlPosition)

examples.name: SwitchButtonLabelled
examples.title: Label and supporting text
examples.description:
At its plainest: the state is read from `checked`, and `onCheckedChange` reports the value asked for. The track, the label and the supporting text are one target: a press on the words turns the switch too.

Drag the thumb: let go of it past the middle of the track and the switch turns. Let go short of the middle and it settles back, and nothing is reported.
examples.code:
var notifications by rememberSaveable { mutableStateOf(true) }
PantrixSwitchButton(
    checked = notifications,
    onCheckedChange = { notifications = it },
    label = "Notifications",
    supportingText = "Order updates and reminders",
    tagKey = "notifications"
)

examples.name: SwitchButtonWithoutALabel
examples.title: Without a label: in a row of the app's own
examples.description:
A row with the words at its start and the switch at its end is a row of the app's own: the words are a `PantrixText` of their own, and the switch has no label. `contentDescription` tells a screen reader the switch's name.

In this layout the words are no part of the target: what is pressed is the switch and the touch target kept around it.

examples.name: SwitchButtonError
examples.title: Error
examples.description:
`error` turns the supporting text to the theme's `danger` role, and a screen reader is told the input is invalid. The switch itself keeps its colours: a switch is a setting, and an answer that can be wrong belongs to a checkbox.

Here the example works the error out itself: `error` is true while the switch is off. Turn the switch on: the text goes back to the colour it had.
examples.code:
var location by rememberSaveable { mutableStateOf(false) }
PantrixSwitchButton(
    checked = location,
    onCheckedChange = { location = it },
    label = "Location",
    supportingText = if (location) "Stores near you are shown" else "Stores cannot be searched while location is off",
    error = !location,
    tagKey = "location"
)

examples.name: SwitchButtonInAForm
examples.title: A setting bound to a form
examples.description:
The `PantrixSwitchButton` that takes a `field` is bound to a form's field: its value, its error and its name come from the field; `checked` and `onCheckedChange` are not given. The field's id is the automation key: the test tag is `SwitchButton_two_step`.

Press "Save" while two-step sign-in is off: the message of the `Rules.mustBeTrue` rule takes the place of the supporting text, and the focus goes to the switch. Turn the switch on and try again: the app's snackbar says the settings were saved.

examples.name: SwitchButtonDisabledAndReadOnly
examples.title: Disabled and read-only
examples.description:
`enabled = false` draws the switch in the disabled colours: it takes no press and no drag, and a screen reader is told it is disabled. The thumb's place still shows whether it is on or off.

With `onCheckedChange = null` the switch is read-only: it takes no press, no drag and no focus, its colours do not change, and it still says its name and its state.
examples.code:
PantrixSwitchButton(checked = true, onCheckedChange = {}, enabled = false, label = "Disabled", tagKey = "off")
PantrixSwitchButton(
    checked = true,
    onCheckedChange = null,
    label = "Read-only",
    supportingText = "Cannot be turned; it only shows its state",
    tagKey = "read_only"
)

examples.name: SwitchButtonOwnColors
examples.title: Its own colours
examples.description:
`colors` changes only the fields it is given: here the colours of the track and of the thumb while the switch is on. Turn the switch off: the track, the thumb and the edge are in the theme's colours. In between, the track and the thumb turn from one colour to the other as the thumb slides.

The app's purple is in none of the theme's roles; the colour of the thumb on such a track is the caller's to give as well. A disabled switch is drawn in the theme's colours even when it is given colours.
examples.code:
val own = ownColors()
var batterySaver by rememberSaveable { mutableStateOf(true) }
PantrixSwitchButton(
    checked = batterySaver,
    onCheckedChange = { batterySaver = it },
    label = "Battery saver",
    supportingText = "When on, the track's and the thumb's colours are given from outside; when off, they are the theme's",
    colors = SwitchColors(checkedTrack = own.color, checkedThumb = own.onColor),
    tagKey = "battery_saver"
)

appNames.name: ownColors
appNames.description: The "app's own colour" of the examples: a purple that is in none of the theme's roles. It is there to show what changes when a component is given `colors`; given one of the theme's roles, nobody could tell whether the colour came from the component's tone or from the parameter.

examples.name: SwitchButtonOwnStyle
examples.title: Style
examples.description:
`style` changes the geometry of one switch. Only the fields that are given change; the rest comes from the theme's and the platform's style.

The first switch is given three fields of the iOS style and is drawn so on every platform: the thumb is always white (`thumbAlwaysLight`), with a shadow under it (`thumbShadow`), and the track has no edge when it is off (`strokeWidth = 0.dp`). The second is a larger track: the track's width and height and the thumb's size in its three states are given together. Its label is set by `labelStyle` in the theme's `callout`, in bold; the track stands on that type's first line.
examples.code:
var lightThumb by rememberSaveable { mutableStateOf(true) }
var largeTrack by rememberSaveable { mutableStateOf(false) }
PantrixSwitchButton(
    checked = lightThumb,
    onCheckedChange = { lightThumb = it },
    label = "White thumb, with a shadow and no edge",
    style = SwitchStyle(strokeWidth = 0.dp, thumbAlwaysLight = true, thumbShadow = 2.dp),
    tagKey = "light_thumb"
)
PantrixSwitchButton(
    checked = largeTrack,
    onCheckedChange = { largeTrack = it },
    label = "Large track",
    style = SwitchStyle(
        trackWidth = 64.dp,
        trackHeight = 36.dp,
        thumbSizeOff = 28.dp,
        thumbSizeOn = 28.dp,
        thumbSizePressed = 28.dp
    ),
    tagKey = "large_track",
    labelStyle = PantrixTheme.typography.callout.copy(fontWeight = FontWeight.Bold)
)

examples.name: SwitchButtonAtTheEnd
examples.title: The switch at the end
examples.description: A settings screen: the track at the end of the label (`controlPosition = ControlPosition.End`). The rows take the column's width (`Modifier.fillMaxWidth()`), the tracks stand one under another at the column's end, and a long label wraps in the room left.
examples.code:
var wifi by rememberSaveable { mutableStateOf(true) }
var saver by rememberSaveable { mutableStateOf(false) }
Column(Modifier.widthIn(max = 360.dp)) {
    PantrixSwitchButton(
        checked = wifi,
        onCheckedChange = { wifi = it },
        modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
        label = "Wi-Fi",
        tagKey = "wifi_end",
        controlPosition = ControlPosition.End
    )
    PantrixSwitchButton(
        checked = saver,
        onCheckedChange = { saver = it },
        modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
        label = "Battery saver",
        supportingText = "Cuts back refreshing in the background and some visual effects",
        tagKey = "saver_end",
        controlPosition = ControlPosition.End
    )
}

pages.title: Segment Button
pages.summary:
A few options side by side in one control, one of them selected. It is a radio group drawn as one control, and a choice changes the screen around it at once: a list's order, a chart's span, a map's layer.

It is for two to five options of a word or two. For more options, or longer ones, a radio group is used; for actions rather than a choice, buttons. The control selects nothing by itself: whichever value `selected` says is the one selected; a press and the arrow keys report the wanted value through `onSelect`.
features: **The sliding pill.** The pill slides under the segment that is selected, and that segment's label is written in the `primary` colour. Pressing the selected segment again does nothing.

**Width.** `fullWidth` (the default) spans the control across the width it is given and gives the segments equal shares: the segments stay where they are whatever their labels say in another language. `fullWidth = false` makes each segment as wide as its label.
**Icons.** `SegmentOption(icon = …)` puts an icon before the label, in the label's colour; a screen reader passes over it.

**A segment that cannot be selected.** `SegmentOption(enabled = false)` disables a single segment: a press on it does nothing and the arrow keys skip it. The control's `enabled = false` disables them all; the pill stays where it is and the selection can still be read.
**With none selected.** If `selected` is not the value of any option, and null is such a value, no segment is selected and no pill is drawn.

**Keyboard.** The control is one stop for Tab, on the selected segment. The arrow keys select the next or the previous segment, go round from the last to the first and skip one that cannot be selected; in a right-to-left layout the directions swap.
**Screen reader.** It is read as a group of radio buttons: each segment is named by its label, and one of them is selected.
**Platform.** On Android it is a fully round pill 40dp tall. On iOS it is 32dp tall, on desktop 30dp and on the web 34dp: a rectangle with medium rounded corners.

**Its own colours and style.** `SegmentButtonColors` gives the colour of the track, of the pill, and of the selected and the unselected labels; `SegmentButtonStyle` gives the track's shape, its height and its paddings. `labelStyle` changes the labels' type; their colours come from the segment's state.

**Font scale.** The track is as tall as the style says, and the platform's touch target is reserved around it. When the system's font size is made larger, a label taller than the track makes the track taller too.

examples.name: SegmentButtonFullWidth
examples.title: Segments that share the width equally
examples.description:
At its plainest: the options, the selected value and `onSelect`. The control spans the width it is given and the three segments share it equally (`fullWidth`, the default). The choice is applied at once: the line under the control changes with what is chosen.

The pill slides under the segment that is selected, and that segment's label is written in the `primary` colour. With a keyboard the control is one Tab stop; the arrow keys move the selection to the next segment or to the previous one.
examples.code:
var sort by rememberSaveable { mutableStateOf("newest") }
PantrixSegmentButton(
    options = SORTS,
    selected = sort,
    onSelect = { sort = it },
    modifier = Modifier.widthIn(max = 480.dp),
    tagKey = "sort"
)
PantrixText(
    text = "Sort order: ${SORTS.first { it.value == sort }.label}",
    style = PantrixTheme.typography.footnote,
    color = PantrixTheme.colors.textSecondary,
    tagKey = "sort_result"
)

private val SORTS = listOf(
    SegmentOption("newest", "Newest", tagKey = "newest"),
    SegmentOption("cheapest", "Cheapest", tagKey = "cheapest"),
    SegmentOption("nearest", "Nearest", tagKey = "nearest")
)

examples.name: SegmentButtonAsWideAsItsLabels
examples.title: As wide as its labels
examples.description:
`fullWidth = false` makes each segment as wide as its label: in a toolbar or beside a heading the control takes only the room it needs. If there is not room for them all, the short labels stay whole and the long ones share what is left.

Both controls are like this: a time span with four options and a choice of platform with three.
examples.code:
var span by rememberSaveable { mutableStateOf("week") }
var platform by rememberSaveable { mutableStateOf("web") }
PantrixSegmentButton(
    options = SPANS,
    selected = span,
    onSelect = { span = it },
    fullWidth = false,
    tagKey = "span"
)
PantrixText(
    text = "Showing: the last ${SPANS.first { it.value == span }.label.lowercase()}",
    style = PantrixTheme.typography.footnote,
    color = PantrixTheme.colors.textSecondary,
    tagKey = "span_result"
)
PantrixSegmentButton(
    options = PLATFORMS,
    selected = platform,
    onSelect = { platform = it },
    fullWidth = false,
    tagKey = "platform"
)

private val SPANS = listOf(
    SegmentOption("day", "Day", tagKey = "day"),
    SegmentOption("week", "Week", tagKey = "week"),
    SegmentOption("month", "Month", tagKey = "month"),
    SegmentOption("year", "Year", tagKey = "year")
)

private val PLATFORMS = listOf(
    SegmentOption("android", "Android", tagKey = "android"),
    SegmentOption("ios", "iOS", tagKey = "ios"),
    SegmentOption("web", "Web", tagKey = "web")
)

examples.name: SegmentButtonIcons
examples.title: Icons and a segment that cannot be selected
examples.description:
`SegmentOption(icon = …)` puts an icon before the label: the icon is in the label's colour, and a screen reader passes over it.

"Folders" is not open yet (`enabled = false`): it is written in the disabled colour, a press on it does nothing and the arrow keys skip it.
examples.code:
var view by rememberSaveable { mutableStateOf("list") }
PantrixSegmentButton(
    options = listOf(
        SegmentOption("list", "List", icon = PantrixIcons.Menu, tagKey = "list"),
        SegmentOption("search", "Search", icon = PantrixIcons.Search, tagKey = "search"),
        SegmentOption("folders", "Folders", icon = PantrixIcons.Folder, enabled = false, tagKey = "folders")
    ),
    selected = view,
    onSelect = { view = it },
    modifier = Modifier.widthIn(max = 480.dp),
    tagKey = "view"
)

examples.name: SegmentButtonNothingSelected
examples.title: With none selected
examples.description:
If `selected` is not the value of any option, no segment is selected and no pill is drawn; null is such a value too. It is used where an answer must not be chosen in advance.

Press one: the pill appears there. From then on the selection slides between the two segments; the control does not clear the selection by itself.
examples.code:
var helpful by rememberSaveable { mutableStateOf<String?>(null) }
PantrixText(text = if (helpful == null) "Was this page helpful?" else "Your answer was saved")
PantrixSegmentButton(
    options = listOf(
        SegmentOption("yes", "Yes", tagKey = "yes"),
        SegmentOption("no", "No", tagKey = "no")
    ),
    selected = helpful,
    onSelect = { helpful = it },
    fullWidth = false,
    tagKey = "helpful"
)

examples.name: SegmentButtonOwnColors
examples.title: Its own colours
examples.description:
`colors` changes only the fields that are given: here the pill is in the app's own purple (`pill`), and the label on it in the colour that reads on that purple (`selectedContent`); the track and the unselected labels stay in the theme's colour.

The app's purple is in none of the theme's roles: the colour that reads on such a pill is the caller's to give too. A disabled control's track and a segment that cannot be selected are drawn in the theme's colours, even when colours are given.
examples.code:
val own = ownColors()
var span by rememberSaveable { mutableStateOf("week") }
PantrixSegmentButton(
    options = SPANS,
    selected = span,
    onSelect = { span = it },
    modifier = Modifier.widthIn(max = 480.dp),
    colors = SegmentButtonColors(pill = own.color, selectedContent = own.onColor),
    tagKey = "span_own"
)

private val SPANS = listOf(
    SegmentOption("day", "Day", tagKey = "day"),
    SegmentOption("week", "Week", tagKey = "week"),
    SegmentOption("month", "Month", tagKey = "month"),
    SegmentOption("year", "Year", tagKey = "year")
)

appNames.name: ownColors
appNames.description: The "app's own colour" of the examples: a purple that is in none of the theme's roles. It is there to show what changes when a component is given `colors`; given one of the theme's roles, nobody could tell whether the colour came from the component's tone or from the parameter.

examples.name: SegmentButtonDisabled
examples.title: Disabled
examples.description:
`enabled = false` disables every segment: the track and the labels are drawn in the disabled colours, and the control takes no press and no focus. The pill stays where it is: which option is selected can still be read.

This control's options are the same as those of the first example. The segments are named inside the control's test tag, so they do not clash: the one there is `SegmentButton_sort.Segment_newest`, and the one here `SegmentButton_locked.Segment_newest`.
examples.code:
PantrixSegmentButton(
    options = SORTS,
    selected = "newest",
    onSelect = {},
    modifier = Modifier.widthIn(max = 480.dp),
    enabled = false,
    tagKey = "locked"
)

private val SORTS = listOf(
    SegmentOption("newest", "Newest", tagKey = "newest"),
    SegmentOption("cheapest", "Cheapest", tagKey = "cheapest"),
    SegmentOption("nearest", "Nearest", tagKey = "nearest")
)

examples.name: SegmentButtonOwnStyle
examples.title: Style
examples.description:
`style` changes the geometry of a single control: the track's shape (`shape`) and its height (`height`), the room between the track's edge and the pill (`trackPadding`), and the room on each side of a label (`segmentPadding`). Only the fields that are given change; the rest comes from the theme's and the platform's style.

The pill has no shape of its own: it is the track's shape, with each corner made smaller by `trackPadding`. That way the corners of the two curve around the same centre.
examples.code:

pages.title: Select
pages.summary:
One choice out of a list: a country, a currency, a plan. Its box is a text field's box: its label above, its supporting or error text below, a chevron at its end. A press on the box opens the list under the box, as wide as the box.

The choice is the caller's and not the component's: `selected` is given, and `onSelect` asks for a new one. A press on an option chooses it and closes the list; a press outside it, the back key and Escape only close it.

It is for a list short enough to read, or one worth searching. For two or three options that should all be in view at once, a radio group or a segment button is used; for actions, a menu; for more than one value, `PantrixMultiSelect`.
features: **A field's box.** `label`, `placeholder`, `supportingText` and `error` are as they are in a text field. While the list is open the box is drawn as a field with the focus.
**The selected row.** The selected option is marked by its row's fill and the tick at its end: not by a colour alone. The list opens with the selected row in view.

**Where the list goes.** The list opens under the box and stays there: if it does not fit the room below, it is only as tall as that room and scrolls inside it. If there is not room for three of its rows below, it opens above the box. Once it is open it stays where it is as long as there is room for one of its rows, even when the keyboard comes up and leaves less room.
**Search.** `searchable` puts a search field in the list that narrows the options by their labels; the list gets as short as the rows that are left.
**Options.** A `SelectOption` carries a value, a label and, if wanted, an icon. An option with `enabled = false` stays in the list and is read, but cannot be chosen.

**Keyboard.** Enter or the space bar opens the list, and the focus comes to the selected row. The arrows move through the rows and go round from the last to the first, Home and End go to the first and the last row, and Enter and the space bar choose. Once the list has closed the focus is on the box again.
**Form.** The `PantrixSelect` that takes a `field` gets its choice, its error and its name from the form's field.

**Colours and style.** The list's colours are given with `colors` (`SelectColors`) and the box's with `fieldColors` (`TextFieldColors`); the list's style with `style` (`SelectStyle`) and the box's with `fieldStyle` (`TextFieldStyle`).
**Screen reader.** The box is a drop-down list, collapsed or expanded; its label and its supporting text are read with it. `contentDescription` gives the name of a select that has no label.

**Automation.** `tagKey` tags the box `Select_<tagKey>`, its list `SelectList_<tagKey>` and its search field `SelectSearch_<tagKey>`. The options are named inside the box: `Select_country.SelectOption_tr`.

examples.description:
This is not a `PantrixSelect`. The options of `PantrixSelect` are a one-line label and an icon; when an avatar, a second line of text and an action row at the bottom are needed, the switcher is built with `PantrixPopover` and these are written as the popover's content: with `PantrixTextField`, `PantrixAvatar` and `PantrixDivider`.

The panel that opens has a search field, a heading, rows with an avatar and a second line of text, a tick at the end of the selected row and, at the bottom, a row that creates a new workspace. examples.name: SelectWidths
examples.title: Width
examples.description:
A select given no width is as wide as a text field's least width: the first box is like this. In a row, with `Modifier.weight(1f)`, it is as wide as its share of the row: the two boxes in the middle share the row.

The box at the bottom is given `Modifier.width(IntrinsicSize.Max)`: the select is asked how wide it would be, and answers with what its options need. The box is as wide as its longest option and no wider, and stays so whichever is chosen. A select in a toolbar or in a table's foot is built this way: the select of `PantrixPageSize` is one too. Choose another currency: the box stands still.

The list is always as wide as its box. A label that does not fit the box is cut off on one line; in the box that is as wide as its options no option is cut, nor in its row of the list.

var from by rememberSaveable { mutableStateOf<String?>("try") }
var to by rememberSaveable { mutableStateOf<String?>("eur") }

    options = CURRENCIES,
    selected = alone,
    onSelect = { code ->
        alone = code
        report("Currency: ${CURRENCIES.first { it.value == code }.label}")
    },
    label = "Currency",
    tagKey = "currency"
)
Row(
    modifier = Modifier.widthIn(max = 480.dp).fillMaxWidth(),
    horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(PantrixTheme.spacing.sm)
) {
    PantrixSelect(
        options = CURRENCIES,
        selected = from,
        onSelect = { code ->
            from = code
            report("Source currency: ${CURRENCIES.first { it.value == code }.label}")
        },
        modifier = Modifier.weight(1f),
        label = "Source",
        tagKey = "currency_from"
    )
    PantrixSelect(
        options = CURRENCIES,
        selected = to,
        onSelect = { code ->
            to = code
            report("Target currency: ${CURRENCIES.first { it.value == code }.label}")
        },
        modifier = Modifier.weight(1f),
        label = "Target",
        tagKey = "currency_to"
    )
}
PantrixSelect(
    options = CURRENCIES,
    selected = fitted,
    onSelect = { code ->
        fitted = code
        report("In the box as wide as its options: ${CURRENCIES.first { it.value == code }.label}")
    },
    modifier = Modifier.width(IntrinsicSize.Max),
    contentDescription = "Currency",
    tagKey = "currency_fitted"
)

pages.title: Multi Select
pages.summary:
Several choices out of a list: the projects a page is narrowed to, the days a shop is open. It is a select's box and list; the difference is in its rows: every option is a check box, a press ticks it or clears it, and the list stays open for the next choice. A press outside it, back and Escape close the list.

What is chosen is the caller's and not the component's: it is given the set in `selected`, and `onSelectionChange` asks for the whole of the new set.
features: **The text in the box.** The box shows the labels of what is ticked, in the options' order and with a comma between them, and cuts what does not fit at one line. With nothing ticked, `placeholder` shows.
**Summary.** Given `valueText`, the box shows it in place of the labels while something is ticked: a count, or one word for all of them.

**Search.** `searchable` puts a search field in the list that narrows the options by their labels. The focus stays in that field: the arrows move among the rows that match, and the keyboard's action key ticks or clears the row the arrows are on.
**Options.** The options are a select's `SelectOption`: a value, a label and, if wanted, an icon. An option with `enabled = false` stays in the list and is read, but cannot be ticked.

**Keyboard.** It is a select's: Enter or the space bar opens the list, the arrows move among the rows and go round from the last to the first, and Home and End go to the first and the last row. Enter and the space bar tick or clear.
**Form.** A `PantrixMultiSelect` that takes `field` gets its choices, its error and its name from the form's field: the field's value is the set of what is ticked.

**Error and disabled.** `error` and `enabled` work as in a select: an error turns the box's border, its label and the text under it to the `danger` role; a disabled box takes no focus and its list does not open.

**Colours and style.** It shares a select's style and colours: `SelectStyle` and `SelectColors`, and `TextFieldStyle` and `TextFieldColors` for its box. A product that restyles its selects restyles these with them. The check boxes stay in the theme's colour.

**Automation.** `tagKey` tags the box `MultiSelect_<tagKey>`, its list `MultiSelectList_<tagKey>` and the search field `MultiSelectSearch_<tagKey>`. The options are named inside the box: `MultiSelect_projects.MultiSelectOption_compose`.

pages.title: File Drop
pages.summary: Where the user gives the app a file: a zone with a dashed edge that opens the platform's picker when pressed and takes the files dropped on it. Choosing and reading are the same on every platform, with foundation's file API.
features: **Pressing works everywhere.** Pressing the zone (or Enter or Space while it has the focus) opens the platform's picker: the documents on Android, Files on iOS, the system's window on the desktop, the browser's on the web. Where only pictures are taken, Android and iOS open the photo picker. None of them asks for a permission.

**Dropping is a pointer's work.** On the desktop and the web files are dragged over the zone and dropped; on Android and the iPad from an app beside it too. While something is dragged over it the zone turns the primary role's colour and says "Drop to add". Its words follow suit: on the desktop and the web they put dropping first, on a phone choosing.

**Screening.** `accept` sets the kinds taken, `maxSize` the largest size, `multiple` more than one file. Files that do not fit go to `onRejected` with their reasons (kind, size, number), the rest to `onFiles`; what to say is the app's.

**The zone keeps no state.** The app keeps the files taken and lists them under the zone as `PantrixFileItem` rows: the name (its middle cut when long), the size in the language's way, the remove button, an optional progress and an error.

**Reading.** A `PantrixFile` carries its name, size and type, and reads its bytes when `readBytes()` asks. The platform's own file is there too: `uri` on Android, `url` on iOS, `file` on the desktop, `domFile` on the web.
**Screen reader.** The whole zone is one button. How many files were taken and how many were not is announced politely; with `error` the supporting text is read as the error.
**Platform.** The zone is 140dp tall on a phone and 120dp on the desktop and the web; the rows are 56dp on a phone and 44dp under a pointer.
