A chart of one series has no legend: what the one line is belongs in the words around the chart. `always` gives it one all the same.

An entry is a switch for its series. Pressed, it takes the series out of the chart, and the chart is drawn for the series that are left; pressed again, it brings the series back. The entry stays, drawn faint, so that what was taken out can be brought back. A screen reader hears each entry as a switch, with the series' name and whether it is on.

parameters.name: position
parameters.description: Which side of the chart the legend stands on. Above and under it the entries stand in a row, on as many lines as they need; beside it they stand under each other.

parameters.name: alignment
parameters.description: Where in the room it has the legend stands: along the chart's width above and under it, and from the chart's top beside it.

parameters.name: toggles
parameters.description: Whether pressing an entry takes its series out of the chart and brings it back.

parameters.name: always
parameters.description: Whether a chart of one series has a legend too.

declarations.name: ChartLegendPosition
declarations.signature: enum class ChartLegendPosition
declarations.description: Which side of a chart its legend stands on.

entries.name: Top
entries.description: Over the chart.

entries.name: Bottom
entries.description: Under the chart: where a legend stands unless told.

entries.name: Start
entries.description: Where lines start: the left of the chart, and the right in a language read from the right.

entries.name: End
entries.description: Where lines end.

declarations.name: ChartLegendAlignment
declarations.signature: enum class ChartLegendAlignment
declarations.description: Where a legend stands in the room it has along its side of the chart.

entries.name: Start
entries.description: At the start of its side: the left, and the right in a language read from the right.

entries.name: Center
entries.description: In the middle of its side: where it stands unless told.

entries.name: End
entries.description: At the end of its side.

declarations.name: ChartPattern
declarations.signature: enum class ChartPattern
declarations.description:
A texture a chart's fill is drawn with besides its colour: what tells two series apart for a reader who cannot tell their colours apart, on a screen, in the legend, in the tooltip and in a file the chart is exported as.

The texture is cut into the fill in the colour of what the chart stands on, as grooves are: a bar stays its colour, with lines or dots across it.

Where a chart's style turns patterns on (`ChartStyle.patterns`), each series, slice or tile that names none takes one in turn: the first none, and the next ones in the order these are declared, from `Diagonal`. One that names a pattern has it, whether the chart's patterns are on or off; `None` keeps a fill plain.

entries.name: None
entries.description: No texture: the fill is its colour alone.

entries.name: Diagonal
entries.description: Lines that rise from the left, a slash's way.

entries.name: Dots
entries.description: Dots in rows, every other row set half a step along.

entries.name: HorizontalLines
entries.description: Lines across.

entries.name: Crosshatch
entries.description: Lines that rise from the left and lines that fall, crossing.

entries.name: DiagonalReverse
entries.description: Lines that fall from the left, a backslash's way.

entries.name: VerticalLines
entries.description: Lines up and down.

entries.name: Grid
entries.description: Lines across and lines up and down.

entries.name: Zigzag
entries.description: Rows of zigzags.

declarations.name: ChartState
declarations.signature: class ChartState(hidden: Set<String> = emptySet())
declarations.description:
What a reader has done to a chart: the series they have put out of sight from its legend, and the place a pointer, a finger or the keys are on.

A chart keeps one for itself. A screen that wants to know either, or to say them, makes its own with `rememberChartState` and gives it to the chart. Two charts given the same state are one to their reader: a series hidden in the one is hidden in the other, and the place pointed at in the one is marked in both, where both have it.

A chart with axes that is given a `zoom` keeps the part of its places that is in view here too, as `window`: two such charts given the same state are looked at closer together. A Gantt chart keeps the part of its time there, and a scatter chart the part of its values across in `window` and up its side in `valueWindow`.

To a pie its slices are what its series are to a chart with axes: a slice is put out of sight by its key, and the slice that is pointed at is the selection whose `x` is that key.

In a scatter chart the point that is pointed at is the selection whose `series` is the key of its series and whose `x` is its place among that series' rows, counted from nought.

parameters.name: hidden
parameters.description: the keys of the series that are out of sight to begin with.

members.name: hidden
members.description: The keys of the series that are not drawn: what the legend's entries turn on and off.

members.name: selection
members.description: The place that is pointed at, and the tooltip is shown for: null while none is. A pointer over the chart, a finger on it and the arrow keys set it; a pointer that leaves, and Escape, clear it.

members.name: window
members.signature:
var window: ClosedFloatingPointRange<Float> by mutableStateOf(-1)
    private set
members.description: The part of the chart's places that is in view, from a share of the way along them to another: `0f..1f`, the whole of them, unless the chart is looked at closer. A chart with axes that is given a `zoom` lets its reader change it; a screen changes it with `zoomTo` and `resetZoom`.

members.name: zoomed
members.description: Whether a part of the chart's places, or of its values, is in view, and not all of them.

members.name: toggle
members.description: Puts the series with the key `series` out of sight where it is drawn, and back where it is not.

members.name: zoomTo
members.signature:
fun zoomTo(
    start: Float,
    end: Float
)
members.description: Brings the part of the places from `start` to `end` into view, each a share of the way along them from nought to one: `zoomTo(0.5f, 1f)` shows the later half. The two are taken in order and kept within the whole, and a part narrower than a thousandth of it is widened to that.

members.name: resetZoom
members.description: Shows all the places, and all the values, again.

members.name: valueWindow
members.signature:
var valueWindow: ClosedFloatingPointRange<Float> by mutableStateOf(-1)
    private set
members.description: The part of the chart's values that is in view up its side, from a share of the way up them to another: `0f..1f`, all of them, unless the chart is looked at closer. Only a scatter chart given a `zoom` looks closer at its values up its side; a screen changes the part with `zoomValuesTo` and `resetZoom`.

members.name: zoomValuesTo
members.signature:
fun zoomValuesTo(
    start: Float,
    end: Float
)
members.description: Brings the part of the values up the chart's side from `start` to `end` into view, each a share of the way up them from nought to one: `zoomValuesTo(0f, 0.5f)` shows the lower half. The two are taken as `zoomTo` takes its two.

declarations.name: rememberChartState
declarations.signature:
@Composable
fun rememberChartState(hidden: Set<String> = emptySet()): ChartState
declarations.description: A chart's state, kept while the screen is, and its hidden series as long as the screen's saved state is.

parameters.name: hidden
parameters.description: the keys of the series that are out of sight to begin with.

declarations.name: ChartSelection
declarations.description: A place on a chart that is pointed at.

parameters.name: x
parameters.description: The place, as the series' rows name it: what their `x` gave. In a pie, the key of the slice. In a scatter chart, the point's place among its series' rows, counted from nought. In a heatmap, the place among the chart's data of the datum that fills the cell, counted from nought. In a treemap, the key of the tile.

parameters.name: series
parameters.description: The key of the series that is pointed at there, where the chart tells them apart, and null where every series at the place is pointed at together, and in a pie.

declarations.name: ChartPoint
declarations.description:
A value of a chart, as it is handed to what a screen does with one: a press on it, a tooltip of the screen's own.

A slice of a pie is handed over as one too: its key is its `series` and its `x`, its name its `name` and its `label`, and its `text` its value with its share of the whole after it.

So is a point of a scatter chart: its `x` is its place among its series' rows, counted from nought, its `label` what the point is called, or its series' name where it is called nothing, and its `value` its value up the chart.

So is a cell of a heatmap: its `x` is its datum's place among the chart's data, counted from nought, its `label` its column as the chart writes it and its `name` its row; it is of no series, and its `series` is empty.

And a tile of a treemap: its key is its `series` and its `x`, its name its `name` and its `label`, and its `text` its value with its share of the whole after it.

A range is handed over as its higher value, with its lower as `from`, and its `text` is the two with a dash between them. A step of a waterfall is what the step adds, with the level it starts from as `from`; its `text` has the step's sign. A total of a waterfall is what it comes to. A candle is handed over as its close, with its opening as `from` and the two ends of its wick as `high` and `low`; its `text` is the four, each called by what it is.

What a stack comes to at a place, which a tooltip of the place writes after the stack's values, is handed to the tooltip's own content as one too: it is of no series, and its `series` is empty; its name is the theme's word for a total, its `value` the sum of the stack's values and its colour unspecified. In a stack that stands as shares, a value's `text` has its share after it.

parameters.name: series
parameters.description: The key of the series the value is of.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The name of that series.

parameters.name: x
parameters.description: Where the value stands, as the series' rows name it.

parameters.name: label
parameters.description: That place as the chart writes it.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: The value.

parameters.name: text
parameters.description: The value as the chart writes it.

parameters.name: color
parameters.description: The colour the series is drawn in, and for a step of a waterfall the colour of the way it goes.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Where the value's mark starts, for a value that is drawn neither from nought nor on a stack: the lower value of a range, the level a step of a waterfall starts from, and the opening of a candle. Null for any other value.

parameters.name: high
parameters.description: The highest a candle reached. Null for any other value.

parameters.name: low
parameters.description: The lowest a candle reached. Null for any other value.

declarations.name: ChartStyle
declarations.description:
A chart's geometry: how tall it is where nothing says, how thick its lines and how large its marks are, and the room between its parts; and whether its fills have textures besides their colours.

A chart is as tall on a phone as leaves room for what is around it, and taller in a window with room to spare. Under a finger its values' lines stand a little further apart than under a pointer.

The rooms between the parts follow the density, the gaps between bars and between slices among them. The height, the widths of the lines, the sizes of the marks and of the bubbles, a bar's width and corners, how far a pointed slice stands out, how thick a gauge's arc is, how tall a meter's bar, a tracker's blocks and a navigator's strip are, and the tooltip's corners and shadow do not: a chart's lines are as thick in a dense layout as in a roomy one.

parameters.name: height
parameters.description: How tall a chart's plot is, with its axes, where the chart's modifier gives it no height. A legend above or under the plot adds its own.

parameters.name: lineWidth
parameters.description: The width of a series' line.

parameters.name: markerSize
parameters.description: The width and height of the mark on a point.

parameters.name: selectedMarkerSize
parameters.description: The same of the mark on the point that is pointed at.

parameters.name: gridWidth
parameters.description: The width of the grid's lines, of the lines along the axes and of the line that marks the place pointed at. Zero draws none.

parameters.name: labelGap
parameters.description: Between the plot and what is written beside it and under it, and between that and an axis' title.

parameters.name: tickSpacing
parameters.description: The least room between two values marked along the axis of values: what decides how many are marked where the axis does not say.

parameters.name: legendGap
parameters.description: Between the legend and the chart it stands beside.

parameters.name: legendItemGap
parameters.description: Between one entry of the legend and the next.

parameters.name: swatchSize
parameters.description: How wide the sample of a series is in the legend and in the tooltip: a short run of its line, or a patch of its fill.

parameters.name: swatchGap
parameters.description: Between that sample and the name after it.

parameters.name: tooltipShape
parameters.description: The tooltip's corners: a step of the brand's shape scale, or a fixed shape.

parameters.name: tooltipHorizontalPadding
parameters.description: Between the tooltip's sides and what it holds.

parameters.name: tooltipVerticalPadding
parameters.description: Between its top and bottom and what it holds, and between its heading and rows.

parameters.name: tooltipGap
parameters.description: Between the place pointed at and the tooltip beside it.

parameters.name: tooltipElevation
parameters.description: The tooltip's shadow.

parameters.name: barGap
parameters.description: Between two bars that stand side by side at a place. Bars too thin for it stand closer.

parameters.name: barMaxWidth
parameters.description: The widest a bar is, however much room its place has: a chart of three places is not three slabs.

parameters.name: barRadius
parameters.description: How round the corners of a bar's end are, the end away from nought.

parameters.name: sliceGap
parameters.description: Between two slices of a pie that lie side by side, the same from the pie's middle to its rim.

parameters.name: selectedSliceOffset
parameters.description: How far the slice of a pie that is pointed at stands out past the pie's rim. The pie keeps this much room about itself, so that the slice has where to stand.

parameters.name: gaugeWidth
parameters.description: How thick the arc of a gauge is. An arc is no thicker than half its radius.

parameters.name: meterHeight
parameters.description: How tall the bar of a meter group is.

parameters.name: trackerHeight
parameters.description: How tall the blocks of a status tracker are.

parameters.name: bubbleMinSize
parameters.description: How far across the smallest bubble of a scatter chart is: a point whose size is nothing, or too little to be seen as an area, is still a point.

parameters.name: bubbleMaxSize
parameters.description: How far across its largest bubble is: the one whose size is the most of the chart's.

parameters.name: navigatorHeight
parameters.description: How tall the strip under a chart's plot is, on which the part of the chart that is in view is marked and moved, in a chart whose zoom has one: how wide, beside a plot whose places go down its side.

parameters.name: barBandShare
parameters.description: How much of a place's band its bars take, more than nought and one at the most: the rest is the room between one place's bars and the next's. Bars are no wider than `barMaxWidth` all the same.

parameters.name: markLineWidth
parameters.description: The width of a mark's line: a target, a limit, a day. Zero draws none, and the mark's words are written all the same.

parameters.name: markBandAlpha
parameters.description: How much of its colour a mark's band is drawn in, from nought to one: a band lies behind the series, and is a tint.

parameters.name: patterns
parameters.description: Whether the fills of a chart's series, slices and tiles are drawn with textures besides their colours, and its lines broken in turn (`ChartPattern`): what tells them apart for a reader who cannot tell the colours apart. Left out, as the system is set: on where it is set to tell things apart without colour, iOS's "Differentiate Without Color" and Android's colour correction, and off otherwise.

parameters.name: nodeWidth
parameters.description: How wide a node of a sankey is.

parameters.name: nodeGap
parameters.description: Between two nodes of a column of a sankey.

declarations.name: ChartColors
declarations.description:
What a chart is painted with, for a chart that does not take the theme's colours: a colour that is set is used, and one that is left out stays the theme's.

```
// A chart in the brand's two colours, whatever the theme's chart colours are:
PantrixChart(series = series, colors = ChartColors(series = listOf(brand, accent)))
```

A chart has no fill of its own: it is drawn on what it stands on. On the theme's own grounds its lines and its words are the theme's. On a fill, which gives what stands on it a colour, the theme's are not known to read: the words are written in that colour and the lines drawn in a share of it. The colours of the series are drawn as they are given wherever the chart stands, and on a fill it is the caller who knows which read there.

parameters.name: series
parameters.description: The colours the series are drawn in, in the order they are handed out, for the series that name none of their own. Empty, they are the theme's chart colours.

parameters.name: grid
parameters.description: The lines drawn across the chart at the marks of an axis. The theme's `divider`.

parameters.name: axis
parameters.description: The line along an axis. The theme's `border`.

parameters.name: label
parameters.description: What is written beside the axes: the values, the places and the axes' titles, and the names in the legend. The theme's `textSecondary`.

parameters.name: crosshair
parameters.description: The line that marks the place pointed at. The theme's `borderHover`: stronger than the grid it crosses, and quieter than the series it stands behind.

parameters.name: tooltipContainer
parameters.description: The tooltip's fill. The theme's `surface`.

parameters.name: tooltipBorder
parameters.description: The tooltip's edge. The theme's `border`.

parameters.name: tooltipText
parameters.description: The tooltip's heading and its values. The theme's `textPrimary`.

parameters.name: tooltipLabel
parameters.description: The names of the series in the tooltip. The theme's `textSecondary`.

parameters.name: rising
parameters.description: What a value that goes up is drawn in: a step of a waterfall that adds. The theme's `success`.

parameters.name: falling
parameters.description: What a value that goes down is drawn in: a step of a waterfall that takes away. The theme's `danger`.

declarations.name: ChartTooltip
declarations.description:
A chart's tooltip: the values at the place that is pointed at, on a small card beside it.

It comes up under a pointer, where a finger touches the chart or is drawn along it, and at the place the arrow keys have gone to. It goes when the pointer leaves, at a second touch on the place, and at Escape. It stands inside the chart, beside the place and on the side that has room for it. In a chart too narrow to have room on either side it stands over the place, at the end of the plot that the place's values are not at. It takes no press: what is under it is pressed as if it were not there.

`null` in its place shows none. The place pointed at is still marked, and still told to the chart's state.

parameters.name: shared
parameters.description: Whether the tooltip is of the place, with the value every series has there, or of the one series nearest the pointer. Together is how a chart is read at a place, and under a finger it asks for no aim; apart suits a chart whose series are read each on its own.

parameters.name: crosshair
parameters.description: Whether the place is marked across the chart: by a line through it, and in a chart with bars by a shade over its band.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: How a value is written in the tooltip and to a screen reader, where that is not how the axis writes it: a chart with no axis of values says here what its numbers are. Left out, the axis' `format` writes them, and the theme's language where the axis has none.

parameters.name: content
parameters.description: The card's own content, in the place of the heading and the rows: given the values at the place, the one pointed at where the series are told apart. The card around it stays the chart's.

declarations.name: ChartZoom
declarations.description:
What lets a reader look closer at a part of a chart: given to a chart as its `zoom`, it lets them bring a part of the chart's places into view, as wide as the chart, and move along the rest.

The part in view is kept in the chart's `ChartState`, as its `window`: a screen reads it there, and sets it with `zoomTo` and `resetZoom`. Two charts given one state show the same part of their places, so that the one is looked at closer as the other is. A Gantt chart given a zoom looks closer at its time the same way, and a scatter chart at its two values, the part up its side kept as the state's `valueWindow`; neither has a navigator.

- With a mouse: a wheel turned while Ctrl, or a Mac's Command, is held looks closer about the place under the pointer, and a wheel turned along the places moves along them: sideways, or up and down a chart whose places go down its side; so does a drag, while a part of them is in view. Any other turn is left to the page, and so is one that moves the part in view no further, at an end of the places.

- With fingers: two moved apart look closer about the point between them, and two moved along the chart take the places with them. One finger points at a place, as in any chart.

- With the keyboard, on the chart: plus looks closer and minus further off, about the place that is pointed at, nought shows all the places again, and the arrows bring the place they go to into view.

- With the `buttons`, for whoever has none of those, or would rather not drag: back and on along the places, further off, closer, and all the places again.

- With the `navigator`, a strip under the chart, or beside one whose places go down its side, that all the places lie on: the part in view is marked on it, dragged along it, and made wider and narrower by its two ends.

The axes of values stay as all the values have them, so that they hold still while the reader moves along the places; where the chart is to `fitValues`, they are made again for the values in view as it is looked at closer, and a stretch that changes little fills the plot. The navigator's lines stay on the axes of all the values.

```
PantrixLineChart(data = days, x = { it.day }, values = visits, zoom = ChartZoom(navigator = true))
```

parameters.name: closest
parameters.description: How many times closer than all its places the chart may be looked at, at the most: twenty shows a twentieth of them. One or more.

parameters.name: buttons
parameters.description: Whether the chart has its row of buttons, above its plot at the side lines end at.

parameters.name: navigator
parameters.description: Whether the chart has the strip under its plot, or beside it where its places go down its side. It is as tall, or as wide, as the chart's style says, its `navigatorHeight`.

parameters.name: fitValues
parameters.description: Whether the axes of values are made for the values of the places in view, and the marks, while a part of the places is in view: as an axis is made for all of them, from nought where it takes nought in and between the ends it is given where it has them.

declarations.name: ChartCurve
declarations.signature: enum class ChartCurve
declarations.description: How a line goes from one point to the next.

entries.name: Linear
entries.description: Straight from point to point.

entries.name: Smooth
entries.description: Rounded through the points, and never past them: between two points the line stays between their values, so it shows no peak and no dip that the values do not have.

entries.name: Step
entries.description: Level at each point's value, and stepping to the next halfway between the two.

entries.name: StepBefore
entries.description: Stepping to a point's value at the point before it: level before each point.

entries.name: StepAfter
entries.description: Level after each point, until the next: a value that holds until it changes.

declarations.name: ChartFill
declarations.signature: enum class ChartFill
declarations.description: What the room between a line and nought is filled with.

entries.name: None
entries.description: Nothing: a line.

entries.name: Solid
entries.description: A soft tint of the series' colour, the same from the line down.

entries.name: Gradient
entries.description: The series' colour, fading from the line down to nothing at nought.

declarations.name: ChartDash
declarations.signature: enum class ChartDash
declarations.description: Whether a line is drawn whole or broken.

entries.name: Solid
entries.description: A whole line.

entries.name: Dashed
entries.description: A line of dashes.

entries.name: Dotted
entries.description: A line of dots.

declarations.name: ChartMarker
declarations.signature: enum class ChartMarker
declarations.description: What marks a point of a line. Shapes tell series apart where colours alone would not.

entries.name: None
entries.description: No mark, but for a point that stands alone.

entries.name: Circle
entries.description: A round mark.

entries.name: Square
entries.description: A square mark.

entries.name: Diamond
entries.description: A square mark stood on one of its corners.

entries.name: Triangle
entries.description: A triangular mark.

declarations.name: ChartMissing
declarations.signature: enum class ChartMissing
declarations.description: What a line does at a row that has no value.

entries.name: Gap
entries.description: The line stops before it and starts again after it.

entries.name: Connect
entries.description: The line goes on from the point before it to the point after it.

entries.name: Zero
entries.description: The row is taken to have the value nought.

declarations.name: ChartExportFormat
declarations.signature: enum class ChartExportFormat
declarations.description: A kind of file a chart is taken out of the app as.

entries.name: Png
entries.description: A picture of pixels: what every app shows, and no sharper than it was made.

entries.name: Svg
entries.description: A picture of lines and shapes, sharp at any size: what a browser and a drawing program open.

entries.name: Pdf
entries.description: A page of lines and shapes, sharp at any size: what is printed and put into a report.

declarations.name: ChartExport
declarations.description:
What lets a reader take a chart out of the app as a file: given to a chart as its `export`, it puts a button among the chart's own, which makes the file and hands it to `onExport`. A chart that is given none has no such button, and nothing of this is there.

The chart makes the file and does nothing with it: where a file goes is the app's to say, and is another thing on every platform. A phone shares it, a window asks where to save it, a browser downloads it. What `onExport` is handed has the file's name, its type and its bytes, which is what each of those ways takes.

The file shows the chart as it is on the screen, with what the reader has done to it: the series they have taken out are out, and of a chart that is looked at closer it shows the part in view. The place that is pointed at and its tooltip are not in it, nor are the chart's buttons; the legend stands under the plot.

```
PantrixLineChart(
    data = months,
    x = { it.name },
    values = revenue,
    export = ChartExport(fileName = "revenue") { file -> share(file.name, file.mimeType, file.bytes) }
)
```

parameters.name: formats
parameters.description: The kinds of file the reader chooses from, in the order they are offered. One kind alone is made at the press of the button, with no choice to make.

parameters.name: fileName
parameters.description: What the file is called, without the ending its kind adds.

parameters.name: scale
parameters.description: How many pixels a PNG has to each dp of the chart: two is twice as sharp as a screen that has one. An SVG and a PDF are as large as the chart is in dp, and sharp at any size.

parameters.name: background
parameters.description: What the file's picture stands on. Unspecified, the theme's `background`: a chart has no fill of its own, and its words are written to be read on the theme's grounds. `Color.Transparent` leaves the picture with nothing under it.

parameters.name: padding
parameters.description: The room the picture leaves around the chart on every side, in its `background`: a chart's own box ends where its words do, and a picture cut there has them at its very edge. 12dp unless given.

parameters.name: onExport
parameters.description: Handed the file once it is made.

declarations.name: ChartExportFile
declarations.description: A chart as a file.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The file's name, with the ending of its kind: `revenue.svg`.

parameters.name: mimeType
parameters.description: Its type as the web names types: `image/png`, `image/svg+xml` or `application/pdf`.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Its kind.

parameters.name: bytes
parameters.description: What is in it. An SVG is text, in UTF-8.

declarations.name: FunnelStage
declarations.description:
One stage of a `PantrixFunnelChart`: a step of what is followed, and how many reached it.

```
FunnelStage("signups", "Sign-ups", 1240)
```

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: What tells the stage from the others of its funnel, and stays the same while its value changes: what a selection names, and what an event reports. Written as a test tag's key is, in small letters and digits.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: What the stage is called: at the stage, in the tooltip and to a screen reader.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: How many reached the stage. One that is no number, has no end or is under nought counts for nothing.

parameters.name: color
parameters.description: The colour the stage is drawn in. Left out, it is the theme's chart colour for its place among the stages.

parameters.name: pattern
parameters.description: The texture the stage is drawn with besides its colour. Left out, none, and where the chart's patterns are on (`ChartStyle.patterns`), its turn by its place among the stages: none for the first.

declarations.name: FunnelShape
declarations.signature: enum class FunnelShape
declarations.description: How the stages of a `PantrixFunnelChart` are drawn.

entries.name: Funnel
entries.description: As one funnel: each stage narrows or widens to the size of the stage after it.

entries.name: Bars
entries.description: As bars, each as large as it counts for all along its row.

declarations.name: FunnelRate
declarations.signature: enum class FunnelRate
declarations.description: Which shares a stage's value is written with in a `PantrixFunnelChart`.

entries.name: First
entries.description: Of the first stage: how much of all that was followed reached it.

entries.name: Previous
entries.description: Of the stage before it: how much of those that reached that one went on to it. The first stage has none.

entries.name: Both
entries.description: Of the first stage and of the stage before it.

declarations.name: PantrixFunnelChart
declarations.signature:
@Composable
fun PantrixFunnelChart(
    stages: List<FunnelStage>,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    labels: ChartDataLabels? = ChartDataLabels(),
    tooltip: ChartTooltip? = ChartTooltip(),
    empty: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null,
    state: ChartState = rememberChartState(),
    description: String? = null,
    onSelect: ((ChartPoint) -> Unit)? = null,
    style: ChartStyle? = null,
    colors: ChartColors? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null,
    shape: FunnelShape = FunnelShape.Funnel,
    horizontal: Boolean = false,
    rate: FunnelRate = FunnelRate.First,
    export: ChartExport? = null
)
declarations.description:
A funnel: the stages of something that fewer and fewer get through, one under another, each as wide as the number that reached it. It shows where the others were lost: the visitors who signed up, the sign-ups who tried, the trials who paid.

The chart is given its `stages`, in the order they follow one another. The largest is as wide as the chart, and each narrows down to the width of the one after it, so that the stages make one funnel; the last keeps its width. A stage that is larger than the one before it widens instead: the funnel draws what it is given. Drawn as `FunnelShape.Bars`, each stage is a bar as wide as it counts for. A `horizontal` funnel lays its stages side by side from where lines start, each as tall as it counts for.

A stage has its name and its value written in it, the value with its shares after it as `rate` says, in the one of black and white that reads better on its colour. A stage too small for them has them beside it, or under it in a horizontal funnel, the name over the value where its column is too narrow for one line; where they have room in none of these places its name is written by itself, and a stage with no room for that has nothing. The `tooltip` and a screen reader always have both.

**Pointing at a stage.** A pointer over a stage's row points at it; a finger does by a tap, and a tap on the stage it points at lets go of it. With the keyboard the chart is one stop for Tab: the arrows go from stage to stage, up and down, or right and left in a horizontal funnel; Home and End go to the first and the last, and Escape lets go. The stage is ringed, the tooltip shown for it, and it is told to `state`, as a selection whose `x` is the stage's key. A press, Enter or Space on it calls `onSelect`.

**To a screen reader** the chart is its `description`, then each stage with its name, its value and its shares, in their order: a share says which stage it is of, but where the funnel writes the first stage's alone.

**Its size.** The chart is as wide as it is given room, and as tall as its modifier says or, given no height, as the chart's style says.

```
PantrixFunnelChart(
    stages = listOf(
        FunnelStage("visits", "Visits", 3000),
        FunnelStage("signups", "Sign-ups", 1240),
        FunnelStage("paid", "Paid", 310)
    ),
    description = "From a visit to a payment",
    tagKey = "sales"
)
```

parameters.name: stages
parameters.description: the stages, in the order they follow one another. Their keys tell them apart, and two with one key are refused.

parameters.name: modifier
parameters.description: the chart's modifier. A height here is the chart's.

parameters.name: labels
parameters.description: what is written at the stages: each stage's name and its value, written as `format` says or in the theme's language where it says nothing, with its shares. `null` writes nothing at them.

parameters.name: tooltip
parameters.description: what is shown for the stage that is pointed at: its name and its value with its shares. With both shares the value stands alone on the stage's row and each share on a row of its own under it, which a tooltip of the caller's own is handed as a point of the stage named by the share, with the share as its value and no text. A stage has no place to share and no line through it: `shared` and `crosshair` are not read. `null` shows none.

parameters.name: empty
parameters.description: what the chart shows while it has no value to draw, in the place of the theme's words for it ("No data"), which a screen reader is then not told either. `null` writes the words.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: what the reader points at: the chart's own where none is given.

parameters.name: description
parameters.description: what the chart shows, in a few words, for a screen reader: the first thing it says of the chart. Left out, the chart is announced by the names of its stages.

parameters.name: onSelect
parameters.description: called with the stage that is pressed: its key is its `series` and its `x`, its name its `name` and its `label`, and its `text` its value with its shares after it.

parameters.name: style
parameters.description: this chart's own geometry: the fields set here, with the theme's for the rest. Two stages are a `sliceGap` apart.

parameters.name: colors
parameters.description: this chart's own colours, where they are not the theme's.

parameters.name: tagKey
parameters.description: the chart's automation key: the chart is `Funnel_<tagKey>`, its stages together `Funnel_<tagKey>.Plot`, a stage `Funnel_<tagKey>.Stage_<number>`, counted from one, and the tooltip `Funnel_<tagKey>.Tooltip`. A press on a stage is reported as a `Funnel` `select` event with the stage's key. Nothing of the values is reported.

parameters.name: shape
parameters.description: how the stages are drawn: as one funnel, or as bars.

parameters.name: horizontal
parameters.description: whether the stages stand side by side, from where lines start, and not one under another.

parameters.name: rate
parameters.description: which shares a stage's value is written with: of the first stage, of the stage before it, or both. At a stage they stand in brackets after the value, two of them apart by a dot; to a tooltip and a screen reader one of the stage before it, and each of two, says which it is (`PantrixStrings.shareOfFirst` and `shareOfPrevious`).

parameters.name: export
parameters.description: what lets the reader take the chart out of the app as a PNG, an SVG or a PDF: a button over the chart makes the file of it as it is and hands it over (see `ChartExport`). `null`, the chart has no such button.

declarations.name: GanttTask
declarations.description:
One task of a `PantrixGanttChart`: something that takes from a moment to another, and how much of it is done.

```
GanttTask("design", "Design", start = kickoff, end = kickoff + 14.days, progress = 0.6f)
```

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: What tells the task from the others of its chart, and stays the same while its moments change: what a selection names, and what an event reports. Written as a test tag's key is, in small letters and digits.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: What the task is called: beside its row, in the tooltip and to a screen reader.

parameters.name: start
parameters.description: The moment the task starts.

parameters.name: end
parameters.description: The moment it ends: for a task that takes the whole of its last day, the midnight after it. A task that ends when it starts is a moment, a milestone, and is drawn as a diamond. One that ends before it starts is taken the other way about.

parameters.name: progress
parameters.description: How much of the task is done, from nought to one: that much of its bar, from where it starts, is drawn in full colour and the rest fainter. Left out, the whole bar is in full colour and nothing is said of how far the task is.

parameters.name: color
parameters.description: The colour the task is drawn in. Left out, it is the first of the chart's colours: the tasks of a chart are one series, and a colour of its own is what sets a task or a group of them apart.

parameters.name: pattern
parameters.description: The texture the task is drawn with besides its colour. Left out, none, and where the chart's patterns are on (`ChartStyle.patterns`), the turn of its colour among the colours of the chart's tasks, in the order they first come: a group set apart by a colour is set apart by a texture too, and the first colour has none.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: The keys of the tasks this one follows: each is drawn with an arrow from where it ends to where this one starts. A key the chart has no task for, or the task's own, is refused, and so are tasks that follow one another round: a task that follows one that follows it.

parameters.name: group
parameters.description: The name of the group the task lies in. The tasks that name the same group stand together under a row of the group's own, in the place of the first of them, with a bar from the start of the earliest of them to the end of the latest. Null, the task is in no group.

parameters.name: row
parameters.description: The name of the row the task stands in. The tasks that name the same row share it, side by side along its time, and the row is called by it: a person's tasks in a row of their own. Those whose times overlap stand one under another in it, and the row is as tall as a row for each. Null, the task has a row of its own, called by the task's name.

declarations.name: PantrixGanttChart
declarations.signature:
@Composable
fun PantrixGanttChart(
    tasks: List<GanttTask>,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    time: ChartTime? = null,
    today: Instant? = null,
    names: Boolean = true,
    tooltip: ChartTooltip? = ChartTooltip(),
    empty: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null,
    state: ChartState = rememberChartState(),
    description: String? = null,
    onSelect: ((ChartPoint) -> Unit)? = null,
    style: ChartStyle? = null,
    colors: ChartColors? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null,
    weekends: Boolean = false,
    export: ChartExport? = null,
    zoom: ChartZoom? = null
)
declarations.description:
A Gantt chart: the tasks of a plan, a row each, every one a bar from the moment it starts to the moment it ends along one axis of time. It shows what runs when, what overlaps, and how far each task is.

The chart is given its `tasks`, in the order of their rows. Time runs from the start of the first task to the end of the last, along the chart, and its axis is marked at round moments, days, weeks, months, as many as have room, with a line up the rows at each. The tasks' names stand in a column where lines start, no wider than two fifths of the chart; a name too long for it is cut short, and the tooltip and a screen reader have it whole.

A task that says how much of it is done has that much of its bar in full colour and the rest fainter. A task that ends when it starts is a milestone, a diamond at its moment. Where `today` is given and lies in the chart's time, a line is drawn over the bars at it, what is to its left is past, and the word for today is written over it, on a line of its own over the rows.

**Groups, rows and what follows what.** Tasks that name a `group` stand together under a row of the group's own, whose bar runs from the earliest of them to the latest, with a point down at each end; their names stand a gap in from the group's. Tasks that name a `row` share it, side by side along its time, and the row is called by that name: a person's tasks in a lane of their own; those whose times overlap stand one under another. A task that names others in `after` follows them: an arrow leads from where each ends to where it starts, turning at a right angle, and round below or above where it starts too soon. With `weekends` the Saturdays and Sundays are shaded faint under all, where a day is wide enough to show.

Moments are read by the screen's clock (`LocalPantrixClock`) and written in the theme's language, unless `time` says otherwise: see `ChartTime`. The chart takes no clock of its own: the moment it is read at is the caller's to give.

**Pointing at a task.** A pointer over a task's row points at it, its name's part of the row too; a finger does by a tap, and a tap on the task it points at lets go of it. With the keyboard the chart is one stop for Tab: the arrows up and down go from task to task, Home and End to the first and the last, and Escape lets go. The task's bar is ringed, the tooltip shown for it, and it is told to `state`, as a selection whose `x` is the task's key. A press, Enter or Space on it calls `onSelect`.

**To a screen reader** the chart is its `description`, and where the line at `today` is drawn, the word for today and its day; then each task with its group and its row where it has them, its name, when it starts and ends, and how much of it is done, in the order of the tasks.

**Its size.** The chart is as wide as it is given room, and as tall as its modifier says; given no height, it is as tall as its rows need: thirty-two dp a lane, a group's header among them, under them a line of writing for the marks of time, and over them one for the word for today where it is written.

```
PantrixGanttChart(
    tasks = listOf(
        GanttTask("design", "Design", start = monday, end = monday + 5.days, progress = 1f),
        GanttTask("build", "Build", start = monday + 5.days, end = monday + 19.days, progress = 0.4f),
        GanttTask("launch", "Launch", start = monday + 21.days, end = monday + 21.days)
    ),
    today = now,
    description = "The plan of the spring release",
    tagKey = "release"
)
```

parameters.name: tasks
parameters.description: the tasks, in the order of their rows. Their keys tell them apart, and two with one key are refused.

parameters.name: modifier
parameters.description: the chart's modifier. A height here is the chart's.

parameters.name: time
parameters.description: how the chart's moments are written and by which clock. Left out, in the theme's language and by the screen's clock (`LocalPantrixClock`).

parameters.name: today
parameters.description: the moment the chart is read at: a line is drawn at it where it lies between the start of the first task and the end of the last. `null` draws none.

parameters.name: names
parameters.description: whether the tasks' names are written beside their rows. Without them the bars have the whole width, and the names stay in the tooltip and for a screen reader.

parameters.name: tooltip
parameters.description: what is shown for the task that is pointed at: its group and its row as the heading, where it has them, and under it its name, when it starts and ends, and how much of it is done. A task has no place to share and no line through it: `shared`, `crosshair` and `format` are not read. `null` shows none.

parameters.name: empty
parameters.description: what the chart shows while it has no value to draw, in the place of the theme's words for it ("No data"), which a screen reader is then not told either. `null` writes the words.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: what the reader points at: the chart's own where none is given.

parameters.name: description
parameters.description: what the chart shows, in a few words, for a screen reader: the first thing it says of the chart. Left out, the chart is announced by the names of its tasks.

parameters.name: onSelect
parameters.description: called with the task that is pressed: its key is its `series` and its `x`, its name its `name` and its `label`, its `value` how many days it takes, and its `text` when it starts and ends as the chart writes it.

parameters.name: style
parameters.description: this chart's own geometry: the fields set here, with the theme's for the rest. A bar's corners are as round as `barRadius` says, and the lines at the marks of time as wide as `gridWidth`.

parameters.name: colors
parameters.description: this chart's own colours, where they are not the theme's.

parameters.name: tagKey
parameters.description: the chart's automation key: the chart is `Gantt_<tagKey>`, its rows together `Gantt_<tagKey>.Plot`, a task `Gantt_<tagKey>.Task_<number>`, counted from one, and the tooltip `Gantt_<tagKey>.Tooltip`. A press on a task is reported as a `Gantt` `select` event with the task's key. Nothing of its moments is reported.

parameters.name: weekends
parameters.description: whether the Saturdays and Sundays of the chart's time, by its clock, are shaded. None are where a day is narrower than two pixels.

parameters.name: export
parameters.description: what lets the reader take the chart out of the app as a PNG, an SVG or a PDF: a button over the chart makes the file of it as it is and hands it over (see `ChartExport`). `null`, the chart has no such button.

parameters.name: zoom
parameters.description: what lets the reader look closer at a part of the chart's time, as a chart with axes is looked at closer along its places (see `ChartZoom`): a wheel with Ctrl or Command, two fingers, plus and minus on the chart, and its buttons bring a part of the time into view, as wide as the chart; a drag of the mouse and the buttons move along it, and the arrows bring the task they go to into view. What lies past the part in view is cut off at the time's two ends; the names stay. The part is kept in `state`, as its `window`. A Gantt chart has no navigator: its `navigator` is not read, nor is its `fitValues`. `null`, the chart shows all its time.

declarations.name: GaugeSegment
declarations.description:
A stretch of a `PantrixGauge`'s scale that has a colour and a name of its own: the range in which a reading is fine, the one in which it is high.

```
GaugeSegment(upTo = 60, name = "Normal")
```

The segments of a gauge are given in the order they lie along its scale: the first begins where the scale does, and each of the others where the one before it ends.

Two are the same segment where everything they were built from is the same; a whole number and the same number with a fraction of nought are one value.

parameters.name: upTo
parameters.description: Where the segment ends: a reading up to this value, the value itself with it, is the segment's.

parameters.name: color
parameters.description: The colour the segment is drawn in. Left out, it is the theme's chart colour for its place among the gauge's segments.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: What a reading in the segment is called, which a screen reader says after the reading: "Normal", "High". Left out, the reading is said by itself.

parameters.name: pattern
parameters.description: The texture the segment is drawn with besides its colour, and the filled arc while it reaches into the segment. Left out, none, and where the gauge's patterns are on (`ChartStyle.patterns`), its turn by its place among the segments: none for the first.

declarations.name: PantrixGauge
declarations.signature:
@Composable
fun PantrixGauge(
    value: Number?,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    min: Number = 0,
    max: Number = 100,
    segments: List<GaugeSegment> = emptyList(),
    needle: Boolean = false,
    format: ((Double) -> String)? = null,
    center: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null,
    description: String? = null,
    style: ChartStyle? = null,
    colors: ChartColors? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null,
    export: ChartExport? = null
)
declarations.description:
A gauge: one reading on a scale, as how far round an arc it reaches. A speed, a load, a share of a quota: a value that is read against the least and the most it can be.

The scale runs clockwise round three quarters of a turn, from `min` at the lower left to `max` at the lower right, with both written under its ends. The `value` fills the arc from where the scale begins up to itself, and is written in the middle of the gauge; a value past an end of the scale stands at that end, and is written as it is.

**Segments.** `segments` give stretches of the scale a colour and a name: the range that is fine, the range that is too much. The arc is then drawn in the colour of the segment the value has reached, over the segments themselves in a faint shade of their own colours.

**A needle.** With `needle` a hand points at the value from the middle of the gauge, as on a dial, and the value is written under it, between the arc's two ends. A gauge with a needle and segments shows the segments in their full colours and no filled arc: the hand is read against them.

**To a screen reader** the gauge is one thing: its `description`, then the value as it is written, and the name of the segment it is in where the segment has one.

**Its size.** The gauge is as wide as it is given room, and as tall as the chart's style says unless its modifier gives it a height; the arc is the largest that has room in that, in the middle of it. A change of the value moves the arc and the hand to it, unless the system asks for reduced motion.

The scale runs the same way in a language read from the right: a dial is no line of text.

```
PantrixGauge(
    value = 72,
    segments = listOf(
        GaugeSegment(upTo = 60, name = "Normal"),
        GaugeSegment(upTo = 85, name = "High"),
        GaugeSegment(upTo = 100, name = "Critical")
    ),
    format = { "${it.toInt()}%" },
    description = "Processor load",
    tagKey = "load"
)
```

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: the reading. `null`, and what is no number, is no reading: the gauge shows its scale and nothing on it.

parameters.name: modifier
parameters.description: the gauge's modifier. A height here is the gauge's.

parameters.name: min
parameters.description: where the scale begins.

parameters.name: max
parameters.description: where the scale ends: more than `min`.

parameters.name: segments
parameters.description: the stretches of the scale that have a colour and a name, in the order they lie along it; each ends past where the one before it does. None, and the arc is drawn in the first of the chart's colours.

parameters.name: needle
parameters.description: whether a hand points at the value.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: how a value is written: the reading, and the two ends of the scale. Left out, they are written as numbers in the theme's language.

parameters.name: center
parameters.description: what stands in the gauge in place of the reading as it is written: the reading with a unit under it, an icon. It has the room the arc leaves in its middle, or the room between the arc's two ends where the gauge has a needle.

parameters.name: description
parameters.description: what the gauge measures, in a few words, for a screen reader: the first thing it says of the gauge.

parameters.name: style
parameters.description: this gauge's own geometry: the fields set here, with the theme's for the rest.

parameters.name: colors
parameters.description: this gauge's own colours, where they are not the theme's.

parameters.name: tagKey
parameters.description: the gauge's automation key: the gauge is `Gauge_<tagKey>`.

parameters.name: export
parameters.description: what lets the reader take the chart out of the app as a PNG, an SVG or a PDF: a button over the chart makes the file of it as it is and hands it over (see `ChartExport`). `null`, the chart has no such button. What stands in the middle, `center`, is not in the file; the reading the gauge writes there of itself is.

declarations.name: HeatmapScale
declarations.description:
How a `PantrixHeatmap` turns a value into a shade: the two ends of its scale, how many shades it has, and its colours. A PantrixTreemap given one shades its tiles by it.

```
HeatmapScale(min = 0.0, max = 100.0, steps = 5)
HeatmapScale(low = Color(0xFFFFF3B0), color = Color(0xFFB3261E))
```

A cell is drawn in `color`, the more of it the further its value is along the scale: a little of it for the least, and all of it for the most. The colour lies on what the chart stands on, so that a scale reads in a light theme and in a dark one. Given a `low` colour, the scale goes from it to `color` instead: the two are mixed in Oklab, where each step along looks as large as the next, and the least is drawn in `low` itself. Such a scale is the same in a light theme and a dark one: the two colours are the caller's to choose for both. A value under `min` is drawn as the least, and one over `max` as the most.

Two scales are the same where all five are.

parameters.name: min
parameters.description: The value the lightest shade stands for. Left out, it is the least of the chart's values.

parameters.name: max
parameters.description: The value the full colour stands for. Left out, it is the most of them.

parameters.name: steps
parameters.description: How many shades the scale has: with five, the scale is cut into five even ranges and every value of a range has that range's shade. Nought, every value has a shade of its own.

parameters.name: color
parameters.description: The colour of the most. Left out, it is the first of the theme's chart colours.

parameters.name: low
parameters.description: The colour of the least. Left out, the least is a little of `color` on what the chart stands on.

declarations.name: PantrixHeatmap
declarations.signature:
@Composable
fun <T> PantrixHeatmap(
    data: List<T>,
    x: (T) -> Any,
    y: (T) -> Any,
    value: (T) -> Number?,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    xAxis: ChartAxis? = ChartAxis(),
    yAxis: ChartAxis? = ChartAxis(),
    scale: HeatmapScale = HeatmapScale(),
    labels: ChartDataLabels? = null,
    legend: ChartLegend? = ChartLegend(),
    tooltip: ChartTooltip? = ChartTooltip(),
    empty: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null,
    state: ChartState = rememberChartState(),
    description: String? = null,
    onSelect: ((ChartPoint) -> Unit)? = null,
    style: ChartStyle? = null,
    colors: ChartColors? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null,
    export: ChartExport? = null
)
declarations.description:
A heatmap: a grid of cells, each in a shade that says how much its value is. It suits what has two names and a number: the hours of the days of a week, the months of several years, one list set against another. What is much and what is little is seen at a glance, where a table of the same numbers would have to be read.

The chart is given its `data` and three ways to read a datum: the column it stands in (`x`), its row (`y`) and its `value`. The columns and the rows are those the data name, each once, in the order it is first named. A datum whose value is no number fills no cell, and a cell that no datum fills is drawn faint; of two that name the same cell, the later is the cell's.

Around the cells stand the parts a chart has, each given by what describes it and taken away by `null`: the names of the columns and of the rows, the `legend`, which here is the scale of shades with its least and its most, and the `tooltip`, which shows the value of the cell that is pointed at.

**Pointing at a cell.** A pointer over a cell points at it; a finger does by a tap, and a tap on the cell it points at lets go of it. With the keyboard the chart is one stop for Tab: the arrows go from cell to cell, past the cells that nothing fills, Home and End to the first cell and the last, and Escape lets go. The cell is ringed, the tooltip shown for it, and it is told to `state`, as a selection whose `x` is the datum's place among `data`, counted from nought. A press, Enter or Space on it calls `onSelect`.

**To a screen reader** the chart is its `description`, then each cell with its column, its row and its value, row after row. A chart of more than two hundred cells is told by its description alone.

**Its size.** The chart is as wide as it is given room. A height on its modifier is the whole chart's, the scale's with it; given none, the cells are as tall as the chart's style says and a scale above or under them adds its own. Every column is as wide as the next and every row as tall. A name that has no room to be written is left out by a rule, every second, every third.

In a language read from the right the columns run from the right, and the rows' names are written at the right.

```
PantrixHeatmap(
    data = visits,
    x = { it.hour },
    y = { it.day },
    value = { it.count },
    description = "Visits by day and hour",
    tagKey = "visits"
)
```

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: the data, a datum for each cell that has a value.

parameters.name: x
parameters.description: the column a datum stands in: a name, an hour, anything that is equal to itself.

parameters.name: y
parameters.description: its row, in the same way.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: its value, or null where it has none.

parameters.name: modifier
parameters.description: the chart's modifier. A height here is the chart's, the scale's with it.

parameters.name: xAxis
parameters.description: the columns: whether their names are written under the cells (`labels`) and how a name is written (`label`). Nothing else of it is read. `null` writes none.

parameters.name: yAxis
parameters.description: the rows: whether their names are written beside the cells, and how. `null` writes none.

parameters.name: scale
parameters.description: how a value becomes a shade.

parameters.name: labels
parameters.description: the values written in the cells, each in the one of black and white that reads better on its shade, where the cell has room for it. `null` writes none.

parameters.name: legend
parameters.description: where the scale of shades stands. `null` shows none. A scale has nothing to take out of the chart: only where it stands is read.

parameters.name: tooltip
parameters.description: what is shown for the cell that is pointed at: its column as the heading, and under it its row and its value, written as `format` says. A cell has no place to share and no line through it: `shared` and `crosshair` are not read. `null` shows none.

parameters.name: empty
parameters.description: what the chart shows while it has no value to draw, in the place of the theme's words for it ("No data"), which a screen reader is then not told either. `null` writes the words.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: what the reader points at: the chart's own where none is given.

parameters.name: description
parameters.description: what the chart shows, in a few words, for a screen reader: the first thing it says of the chart. Left out, the chart is announced by the names of its rows.

parameters.name: onSelect
parameters.description: called with the cell that is pressed: its `x` is the datum's place among `data`, counted from nought, its `label` its column, its `name` its row, and its `value` its value.

parameters.name: style
parameters.description: this chart's own geometry: the fields set here, with the theme's for the rest. Two cells are a `sliceGap` apart, and their corners as round as `barRadius` says.

parameters.name: colors
parameters.description: this chart's own colours, where they are not the theme's.

parameters.name: tagKey
parameters.description: the chart's automation key: the chart is `Heatmap_<tagKey>`, its cells together `Heatmap_<tagKey>.Plot`, a cell `Heatmap_<tagKey>.Cell_<number>`, counted from one row after row among the cells that are filled, the scale `Heatmap_<tagKey>.Legend` and the tooltip `Heatmap_<tagKey>.Tooltip`. A press on a cell is reported as a `Heatmap` `select` event with the datum's number. Nothing of the values is reported.

parameters.name: export
parameters.description: what lets the reader take the chart out of the app as a PNG, an SVG or a PDF: a button over the chart makes the file of it as it is and hands it over (see `ChartExport`). `null`, the chart has no such button. The scale of shades stands under the cells in the file.

declarations.name: PantrixLineChart
declarations.signature:
@Composable
fun <T> PantrixLineChart(
    data: List<T>,
    x: (T) -> Any,
    values: List<ChartValue<T>>,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    curve: ChartCurve = ChartCurve.Linear,
    missing: ChartMissing = ChartMissing.Gap,
    labels: ChartDataLabels? = null,
    xAxis: ChartAxis? = ChartAxis(),
    yAxis: ChartAxis? = ChartAxis(),
    secondYAxis: ChartAxis? = ChartAxis(),
    marks: List<ChartMark> = emptyList(),
    legend: ChartLegend? = ChartLegend(),
    tooltip: ChartTooltip? = ChartTooltip(),
    zoom: ChartZoom? = null,
    decimation: ChartDecimation? = ChartDecimation(),
    export: ChartExport? = null,
    empty: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null,
    state: ChartState = rememberChartState(),
    description: String? = null,
    onSelect: ((ChartPoint) -> Unit)? = null,
    style: ChartStyle? = null,
    colors: ChartColors? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null
)
declarations.description:
A line chart of rows that are given once: a line for each of the `values` read from them, along the places `x` reads from them.

It is a `PantrixChart` whose series are all lines and all read from the same rows, written shorter: everything a chart does, it does. A chart whose series come from different lists, or are of different kinds, is a `PantrixChart` with a `LineSeries` for each.

```
PantrixLineChart(
    data = months,
    x = { it.name },
    values = listOf(
        ChartValue("desktop", "Desktop") { it.desktop },
        ChartValue("mobile", "Mobile") { it.mobile }
    ),
    tagKey = "visits"
)
```

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: the rows, in the order the lines go through them.

parameters.name: x
parameters.description: where a row stands along the chart: a name, a day, anything that is equal to itself.

parameters.name: values
parameters.description: the series: what each reads from a row, and how it is called and drawn.

parameters.name: modifier
parameters.description: the chart's modifier. A height here is the chart's, the legend's with it.

parameters.name: curve
parameters.description: how each line goes from a point to the next.

parameters.name: missing
parameters.description: what a line does at a row that has no value.

parameters.name: labels
parameters.description: the values written over the points of every line, where they have room. `null` writes none.

parameters.name: xAxis
parameters.description: the axis of the places, under the chart. `null` draws nothing of it.

parameters.name: yAxis
parameters.description: the axis of the values, beside the chart. `null` draws nothing of it.

parameters.name: secondYAxis
parameters.description: the second axis of the values, at the chart's other side: drawn where a value is read by it (`ChartValue.axis`), and not otherwise. `null` draws nothing of it.

parameters.name: marks
parameters.description: the lines and the bands drawn in the plot besides the series: a target, a limit, a stretch of places.

parameters.name: legend
parameters.description: where the names of the series stand. `null` shows none.

parameters.name: tooltip
parameters.description: what is shown for the place that is pointed at. `null` shows none.

parameters.name: zoom
parameters.description: what lets the reader look closer at a part of the places and move along the rest. `null`, which it is unless the chart is given one, shows all the places and no more.

parameters.name: decimation
parameters.description: how a line with more points in view than the plot has room for is drawn through fewer of them. `null` draws every point, as many as there are.

parameters.name: export
parameters.description: what lets the reader take the chart out of the app as a file: a picture, or a drawing that is sharp at any size. `null`, which it is unless the chart is given one, and the chart has no such button.

parameters.name: empty
parameters.description: what the chart shows in its plot while it has no value to draw, in the place of the theme's words for it ("No data"), which a screen reader is then not told either. `null` writes the words. A file the chart is exported as says them.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: what the reader has hidden and what they point at: the chart's own where none is given.

parameters.name: description
parameters.description: what the chart shows, in a few words, for a screen reader.

parameters.name: onSelect
parameters.description: called with the value that is pressed.

parameters.name: style
parameters.description: this chart's own geometry.

parameters.name: colors
parameters.description: this chart's own colours, where they are not the theme's.

parameters.name: tagKey
parameters.description: the chart's automation key. The chart is tagged as the `PantrixChart` it is, `Chart_<tagKey>`, and its parts and events are that chart's.

declarations.name: MeterItem
declarations.description:
One of the amounts a `PantrixMeterGroup` sets side by side on its bar.

```
MeterItem("photos", "Photos", 24)
```

Two are the same item where everything they were built from is the same; a whole number and the same number with a fraction of nought are one value.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: What tells the item from the others of its group, and stays the same while its value changes. Written as a test tag's key is, in small letters and digits.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: What the item is called, in the legend and to a screen reader.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: How much of the bar the item takes, counted in what the bar's `max` is counted in. An item whose value is no number, or is not over nought, takes none of it, and keeps its name in the legend.

parameters.name: color
parameters.description: The colour the item is drawn in. Left out, it is the theme's chart colour for its place among the group's items.

parameters.name: pattern
parameters.description: The texture the item is drawn with besides its colour. Left out, none, and where the group's patterns are on (`ChartStyle.patterns`), its turn by its place among the items: none for the first.

declarations.name: PantrixMeterGroup
declarations.signature:
@Composable
fun PantrixMeterGroup(
    items: List<MeterItem>,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    max: Number = 100,
    format: ((Double) -> String)? = null,
    legend: ChartLegend? = ChartLegend(),
    description: String? = null,
    style: ChartStyle? = null,
    colors: ChartColors? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null,
    export: ChartExport? = null
)
declarations.description:
A meter group: several amounts of one whole, side by side on one bar. What a storage is filled with, how a budget is spent: the parts are read against each other and against what is left.

The bar is as long as `max`. Each of the `items` takes as much of it as its value, one after the other from where lines start, in the theme's chart colour for its place unless it names its own; what no item takes shows the bar's track. What the items come to past `max` is cut off at the bar's end.

The `legend` writes each item's name with its value after it, beside a patch of its colour. It stands above the bar or under it: a legend at the start is above, and one at the end under. Its entries are no switches here: a meter group shows what it is given.

**To a screen reader** the bar is a picture with its `description`, and the legend's entries say the items. A group with no legend says the items with the bar.

In a language read from the right the first item stands at the right.

```
PantrixMeterGroup(
    items = listOf(
        MeterItem("apps", "Apps", 16),
        MeterItem("photos", "Photos", 24),
        MeterItem("system", "System", 10)
    ),
    max = 64,
    format = { "${it.toInt()} GB" },
    description = "Storage",
    tagKey = "storage"
)
```

parameters.name: items
parameters.description: the amounts, in the order they lie on the bar. Their keys tell them apart, and two with one key are refused.

parameters.name: modifier
parameters.description: the group's modifier.

parameters.name: max
parameters.description: how much the whole bar is: more than nought.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: how a value is written in the legend. Left out, it is written as a number in the theme's language.

parameters.name: legend
parameters.description: where the names of the items stand, above the bar or under it. `null` shows none.

parameters.name: description
parameters.description: what the bar measures, in a few words, for a screen reader.

parameters.name: style
parameters.description: this group's own geometry: the fields set here, with the theme's for the rest.

parameters.name: colors
parameters.description: this group's own colours, where they are not the theme's.

parameters.name: tagKey
parameters.description: the group's automation key: the group is `MeterGroup_<tagKey>`, its bar `MeterGroup_<tagKey>.Bar` and the legend's entry of an item `MeterGroup_<tagKey>.Legend_<item's key>`.

parameters.name: export
parameters.description: what lets the reader take the chart out of the app as a PNG, an SVG or a PDF: a button over the chart makes the file of it as it is and hands it over (see `ChartExport`). `null`, the chart has no such button. The legend stands under the bar in the file.

declarations.name: PieSlice
declarations.description:
A slice of a `PantrixPieChart`: one of the parts of the whole the pie shows.

```
PieSlice("search", "Search", 310)
```

Two are the same slice where everything they were built from is the same; a whole number and the same number with a fraction of nought are one value.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: What tells the slice from the others of its pie, and stays the same while its value changes: what the legend keeps a hidden slice by, what a selection names, and what an event reports. Written as a test tag's key is, in small letters and digits.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: What the slice is called: in the legend, in the tooltip and to a screen reader.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: How much the slice is of the whole. A slice whose value is no number, or is not over nought, has no part of the pie: a share of a whole is no less than nothing.

parameters.name: color
parameters.description: The colour the slice is drawn in. Left out, it is the theme's chart colour for its place among the slices of the pie: the first of them for the first.

parameters.name: pattern
parameters.description: The texture the slice is drawn with besides its colour. Left out, none, and where the chart's patterns are on (`ChartStyle.patterns`), its turn by its place among the slices: none for the first.

declarations.name: PieSort
declarations.signature: enum class PieSort
declarations.description: The order a pie's slices lie in, from where they begin.

entries.name: Given
entries.description: As they are given.

entries.name: Descending
entries.description: The largest first.

entries.name: Ascending
entries.description: The smallest first.

declarations.name: PieOthers
declarations.description:
How a pie gathers its smallest slices into one, so that a crowd of slivers is read as one slice: every slice that is less of the whole than `share` goes into a slice after all the others, which the tooltip and a screen reader open into the slices it holds. A single slice that small keeps its own place.

```
PieOthers(share = 0.05f)
```

The gathered slice's key is `others`: a pie that gathers keeps that key for it, and refuses a slice of its own with it. Its legend's entry takes the gathered slices out together.

parameters.name: share
parameters.description: How much of the whole a slice is at the least to stand on its own: three hundredths, and from nought, where none is gathered, to one.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: What the gathered slice is called. Left out, it is the theme's word for it (`PantrixStrings.others`, "Other").
