declarations.name: PantrixPieChart
declarations.signature:
@Composable
fun PantrixPieChart(
    slices: List<PieSlice>,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    hole: Float = 0f,
    center: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null,
    labels: ChartDataLabels? = null,
    legend: ChartLegend? = ChartLegend(),
    tooltip: ChartTooltip? = ChartTooltip(),
    empty: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null,
    state: ChartState = rememberChartState(),
    description: String? = null,
    onSelect: ((ChartPoint) -> Unit)? = null,
    style: ChartStyle? = null,
    colors: ChartColors? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null,
    startAngle: Float = 0f,
    sweepAngle: Float = 360f,
    sort: PieSort = PieSort.Given,
    others: PieOthers? = null,
    export: ChartExport? = null
)
declarations.description:
A pie chart: the parts of a whole as the slices of a disc, each as much of the turn as its value is of their sum. With a `hole` in its middle it is a ring, a donut, which has room in the hole for a total or a title.

The pie is given its `slices`, each with a key, a name and a value. They lie in the order they are given, or the order `sort` says, clockwise from `startAngle`, and take a whole turn or the `sweepAngle` it is given: half of one for a half pie. Each is in the theme's chart colour for its place unless it names its own. A slice whose value is no number, or is not over nought, has no part of the pie, and keeps its place in the legend. Where the pie is given `others`, its smallest slices are gathered into one, last.

Around the pie stand the parts a chart with axes has, each given by what describes it and taken away by `null`: the `legend`, which lists the slices and takes one out of the pie when its entry is pressed, and the `tooltip`, which shows the value of the slice that is pointed at and its share of the whole.

**Pointing at a slice.** A pointer over a slice points at it; a finger does by a tap, and a tap on the slice it points at lets go of it. With the keyboard the pie is one stop for Tab: the arrows go from slice to slice round the pie, and past the last to the first again, Home and End to the first and the last, and Escape lets go. The slice stands out past the pie's rim, the tooltip is shown for it, and it is told to `state`. A press, Enter or Space on it calls `onSelect`. In a window and in a browser a press on the pie takes the focus, as a press on a button does, so that the arrows after it go through this pie.

**To a screen reader** the pie is its `description`, then each slice with its value and its share, in the slices' order; the legend's entries are switches.

**Its size.** The chart is as wide as it is given room. A height on its modifier is the whole chart's, the legend's with it; given none, it is as tall as the chart's style says and a legend above or under it adds its own. The pie is the largest that has room in what the legend leaves, in the middle of it: of a half pie, the half that is drawn. Where its labels are written outside it, it keeps room for them at its sides, and where that room would leave it less than half as large, it writes on its slices only.

The pie turns the same way in a language read from the right; its legend and its tooltip follow the reading direction.

```
PantrixPieChart(
    slices = listOf(
        PieSlice("direct", "Direct", 420),
        PieSlice("search", "Search", 310),
        PieSlice("social", "Social", 150)
    ),
    hole = 0.6f,
    description = "Visits by where they came from",
    tagKey = "sources"
)
```

parameters.name: slices
parameters.description: the slices, in the order they lie in the pie where `sort` keeps it, clockwise from `startAngle`. Their keys tell them apart, and two with one key are refused.

parameters.name: modifier
parameters.description: the chart's modifier. A height here is the chart's, the legend's with it.

parameters.name: hole
parameters.description: how much of the pie's radius is cut out of its middle: nought for a whole pie, and six tenths for a ring with room to write in. No more than nine tenths.

parameters.name: center
parameters.description: what stands in the hole of a ring: a total, a title. It has the largest box the hole holds, of a half ring in the half that is drawn. A whole pie has no place for it.

parameters.name: labels
parameters.description: what is written about the slices: each slice's share of the whole, or its value as the labels' `format` writes it. On a slice it is written in black or white, whichever reads on the slice; outside it, the slice's name comes before it, with a line in the slice's colour leading to it. Their `position` says where: `Outside` outside every slice, `Auto` on each slice that holds its words and outside the others, and any other on the slices only, where a slice too small to hold its words has none. Words outside stand in a column at each side; where a side has no room for all of them, one under another, the smallest slices there have none. `null` writes nothing about them.

parameters.name: legend
parameters.description: where the names of the slices stand. `null` shows none.

parameters.name: tooltip
parameters.description: what is shown for the slice that is pointed at: its value, as the tooltip's `format` writes it or in the theme's language, and its share of the whole. `null` shows none. Whether a tooltip is `shared` and whether it has a `crosshair` say nothing to a pie.

parameters.name: empty
parameters.description: what the chart shows while it has no value to draw, in the place of the theme's words for it ("No data"), which a screen reader is then not told either. `null` writes the words.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: what the reader has hidden and what they point at: the chart's own where none is given. A slice is hidden by its key, and pointed at by a selection whose `x` is its key.

parameters.name: description
parameters.description: what the pie shows, in a few words, for a screen reader: the first thing it says of the chart. Left out, the chart is announced by the names of its slices.

parameters.name: onSelect
parameters.description: called with the slice that is pressed: its key as the point's `series` and its `x`, its name, its value, and what the pie writes for it.

parameters.name: style
parameters.description: this chart's own geometry: the fields set here, with the theme's for the rest.

parameters.name: colors
parameters.description: this chart's own colours, where they are not the theme's.

parameters.name: tagKey
parameters.description: the chart's automation key: the chart is `PieChart_<tagKey>`, the pie `PieChart_<tagKey>.Plot`, a slice `PieChart_<tagKey>.Slice_<number>` counted from one, the legend's entry of a slice `PieChart_<tagKey>.Legend_<slice's key>` and the tooltip `PieChart_<tagKey>.Tooltip`. A press on a slice is reported as a `PieChart` `select` event with the slice's key, and a press on a legend's entry as a `toggle` event with the key and whether the slice is shown. Nothing of the values is reported.

parameters.name: startAngle
parameters.description: where the first slice begins, in degrees clockwise from twelve o'clock: 270 begins at nine o'clock.

parameters.name: sweepAngle
parameters.description: how many degrees the slices take together: a whole turn, 360, or 180 for a half pie, from over nought up to a whole turn.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: the order the slices lie in: as given, the largest first or the smallest first.

parameters.name: others
parameters.description: how the smallest slices are gathered into one. `null` gathers none.

parameters.name: export
parameters.description: what lets the reader take the chart out of the app as a PNG, an SVG or a PDF: a button over the chart makes the file of it as it is and hands it over (see `ChartExport`). `null`, the chart has no such button. What stands in the hole, `center`, is not in the file.

declarations.name: PolarSeries
declarations.description:
One series of bars in a `PantrixPolarChart`: the rows it is read from, the sector each of them stands in and its value there.

```
PolarSeries("north", "North", months, x = { it.name }, y = { it.north })
```

`x` says which sector a row stands in: a name, a month, anything that is equal to itself; the chart writes it with its axis' `label`, and as it writes itself where that is left out. `y` is the row's value, and null where it has none: a row with no value has no bar. A value that is no number, or has no end, is taken as none.

Two series are the same series where everything they were built from is the same, the two functions among them.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: What tells the series from the others of its chart, and stays the same while its values change: what the legend keeps a hidden series by, what a selection names, and what an event reports. Written as a test tag's key is, in small letters and digits.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: What the series is called: in the legend, in the tooltip and to a screen reader.

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: The rows.

parameters.name: x
parameters.description: The sector a row stands in.

parameters.name: y
parameters.description: A row's value, or null where it has none.

parameters.name: color
parameters.description: The colour the series is drawn in. Left out, it is the theme's chart colour for its place among the series of the chart: the first of them for the first.

parameters.name: stack
parameters.description: What the series is stacked with. The series that name the same stack share one bar in each sector, each further out than the one before it. Null, a series has a bar of its own beside the others'.

parameters.name: pattern
parameters.description: The texture its bars are drawn with besides its colour. Null, none, and where the chart's patterns are on (`ChartStyle.patterns`), its turn by its place among the chart's series.

parameters.name: fillAlpha
parameters.description: How much of its colour its bars are filled with: nought to one, all of it by default. Less lets the rings behind its bars show through them; the legend and the tooltip keep the whole colour.

declarations.name: PantrixPolarChart
declarations.signature:
@Composable
fun PantrixPolarChart(
    series: List<PolarSeries<*>>,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    hole: Float = 0f,
    xAxis: ChartAxis? = ChartAxis(),
    yAxis: ChartAxis? = ChartAxis(),
    legend: ChartLegend? = ChartLegend(),
    tooltip: ChartTooltip? = ChartTooltip(),
    empty: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null,
    state: ChartState = rememberChartState(),
    description: String? = null,
    onSelect: ((ChartPoint) -> Unit)? = null,
    style: ChartStyle? = null,
    colors: ChartColors? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null,
    grid: RadarGrid = RadarGrid.Circle,
    export: ChartExport? = null
)
declarations.description:
A polar chart: bars set out round a middle, each as long from the middle out as its value: a rose. It suits what comes round again, the hours of a day, the months of a year, the points of a compass, and what is to be compared at a glance by how far each reaches.

The chart is given its `series`, and each of them carries its own rows: the sector a row stands in and its value there. The chart sets out every sector any of them names, in the order they are first named, clockwise from twelve o'clock, each an equal part of the turn. The bars of several series stand side by side in a sector, and the series that name the same `stack` share one bar there. One axis of values goes out from the middle: from nought, unless the axis says otherwise, to a round number over the most of the values. Its rings are round, as the ends of the bars are that are read against them; with a `grid` of polygons they are straight from one sector's side to the next, and so are the bars' ends. With a `hole` the bars start from a ring, and the shortest of them still shows.

Around the bars stand the parts a chart with places has, each given by what describes it and taken away by `null`: the two axes, the `legend`, which lists the series and takes one out of the chart when its entry is pressed, and the `tooltip`, which shows the values in the sector that is pointed at.

**Pointing at a sector.** A pointer over a sector points at it; a finger does by a tap, and a tap on the sector it points at lets go of it. With the keyboard the chart is one stop for Tab: the arrows go from sector to sector round the chart, and past the last to the first again, Home and End to the first and the last, and Escape lets go. Where the tooltip tells the series apart, the arrows up and down go from one series' bar to the next. The sector is shaded, the tooltip shown for it, and it is told to `state`. A press, Enter or Space on it calls `onSelect`.

**To a screen reader** the chart is its `description`, then each sector with the values the series have there, in the sectors' order; the legend's entries are switches.

**Its size.** The chart is as wide as it is given room. A height on its modifier is the whole chart's, the legend's with it; given none, it is as tall as the chart's style says and a legend above or under it adds its own. The rose is the largest that has room in what the legend leaves, with the sectors' names about it.

The chart turns the same way in a language read from the right; its legend and its tooltip follow the reading direction.

```
PantrixPolarChart(
    series = listOf(PolarSeries("visits", "Visits", hours, x = { it.hour }, y = { it.visits })),
    hole = 0.3f,
    description = "Visits by the hour of the day",
    tagKey = "hours"
)
```

parameters.name: modifier

parameters.name: hole
parameters.description: how much of the chart's radius is cut out of its middle: nought for bars that start at the middle. No more than nine tenths.

parameters.name: xAxis
parameters.description: the sectors: whether their names are written about the chart (`labels`), how a name is written (`label`), and whether a line is drawn between one sector and the next (`line`). `null` draws nothing of them.

parameters.name: yAxis
parameters.description: the axis of the values, out from the chart's middle: its ends, about how many values it marks, how a value is written, whether the marked values are written (`labels`) and whether a ring is drawn at each (`grid`). It starts at nought unless `startFromZero` or `min` says otherwise. `null` draws nothing of it.

parameters.name: legend
parameters.description: where the names of the series stand. `null` shows none.

parameters.name: tooltip
parameters.description: what is shown for the sector that is pointed at. `null` shows none.

parameters.name: empty
parameters.description: what the chart shows while it has no value to draw, in the place of the theme's words for it ("No data"), which a screen reader is then not told either. `null` writes the words.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: what the reader has hidden and what they point at: the chart's own where none is given.

parameters.name: description
parameters.description: what the chart shows, in a few words, for a screen reader: the first thing it says of the chart. Left out, the chart is announced by the names of its series.

parameters.name: onSelect
parameters.description: called with the value that is pressed: the one pointed at, or of the series whose bar is nearest the press where the sector's values are pointed at together.

parameters.name: style
parameters.description: this chart's own geometry: the fields set here, with the theme's for the rest.

parameters.name: colors
parameters.description: this chart's own colours, where they are not the theme's.

parameters.name: tagKey
parameters.description: the chart's automation key: the chart is `PolarChart_<tagKey>`, its plot `PolarChart_<tagKey>.Plot`, a sector of it `PolarChart_<tagKey>.Point_<number>` counted from one, the legend's entry of a series `PolarChart_<tagKey>.Legend_<series' key>` and the tooltip `PolarChart_<tagKey>.Tooltip`. A press on a value is reported as a `PolarChart` `select` event with the series' key, and a press on a legend's entry as a `toggle` event with the key and whether the series is shown. Nothing of the values is reported.

parameters.name: grid
parameters.description: how the rings are drawn: round, or straight from one side of a sector to the next, a web, whose bars end straight on its lines and are read against them. A chart of fewer than three sectors has round rings either way.

parameters.name: export
parameters.description: what lets the reader take the chart out of the app as a PNG, an SVG or a PDF: a button over the chart makes the file of it as it is and hands it over (see `ChartExport`). `null`, the chart has no such button.

declarations.name: PantrixProgressCircle
declarations.signature:
@Composable
fun PantrixProgressCircle(
    value: Number,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    max: Number = 100,
    color: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    trackColor: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    contentDescription: String? = null,
    style: ProgressCircleStyle? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null,
    export: ChartExport? = null,
    content: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null
)
declarations.description:
A ring that fills as something gets done: how much of an upload has gone, how many steps of a set-up are behind, how much of a quota is used. It shows a share of a whole that is known; for work whose end is not known there is the spinner.

The ring fills clockwise from twelve o'clock, `value` of `max` of the way round, over a faint ring that shows the whole. A value under nought is nought, and one over `max` is the whole. What is given as `content` stands in the middle of the ring: the share as a number, an icon.

It is drawn in `color`, or else the content colour of where it stands, as on a filled card, or the primary colour; its track is a faint share of the same colour unless `trackColor` says otherwise. A change of the value moves the ring to it, unless the system asks for reduced motion.

**To a screen reader** it is a progress bar with `contentDescription` for its name and the share it has reached. What stands in its middle is read too, as whatever it is: a number written there is better hidden from the screen reader, which has the share already.

The ring fills the same way in a language read from the right, as a clock's hand goes.

```
PantrixProgressCircle(value = 72, contentDescription = "Uploaded") {
    PantrixText(text = "72%", style = PantrixTheme.typography.caption)
}
```

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: how much is done, between nought and `max`. What is no number counts as nought.

parameters.name: modifier
parameters.description: the circle's modifier. A size here is the circle's.

parameters.name: max
parameters.description: how much the whole is: more than nought.

parameters.name: color
parameters.description: the colour of the ring.

parameters.name: trackColor
parameters.description: the colour of the ring's track, the whole it fills.

parameters.name: contentDescription
parameters.description: what is progressing, in a word or two, for a screen reader.

parameters.name: style
parameters.description: this circle's own geometry: its size and how thick its ring is.

parameters.name: tagKey
parameters.description: the circle's automation key: the circle is `ProgressCircle_<tagKey>`.

parameters.name: export
parameters.description: what lets the reader take the circle out of the app as a PNG, an SVG or a PDF: a button over it makes the file of it as it is and hands it over (see `ChartExport`). `null`, it has no such button. What stands in the circle, `content`, is not in the file. It comes before `content`, which stays last.

parameters.name: content
parameters.description: what stands in the middle of the ring. It has the room inside the ring.

declarations.name: ProgressCircleStyle
declarations.description:
`PantrixProgressCircle`'s geometry.

The circle is a mark and not room between things: neither of its sizes follows the density.

parameters.name: size
parameters.description: The circle's width and height: 56dp on every platform, unless a brand or a theme sets another.

parameters.name: strokeWidth
parameters.description: How thick the ring is: 6dp. A ring is no thicker than a quarter of its circle.

declarations.description:
One web of a `PantrixRadarChart`: the rows it is read from, the spoke each of them stands on and its value there.

```
RadarSeries("ada", "Ada", skills, x = { it.skill }, y = { it.ada })

A value that is no number, or has no end, is taken as none.

parameters.description: What the series is called: in the legend, in the tooltip and to a screen reader.

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: The rows.

parameters.name: x

parameters.description: The colour the series is drawn in. Left out, it is the theme's chart colour for its place among the series of the chart: the first of them for the first.
