@Composable
fun <T> PantrixRangeChart(
    data: List<T>,
    x: (T) -> Any,
    low: (T) -> Number?,
    high: (T) -> Number?,
    name: String,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    kind: RangeKind = RangeKind.Area,
    curve: ChartCurve = ChartCurve.Linear,
    lines: Boolean = true,
    dash: ChartDash? = null,
    marker: ChartMarker = ChartMarker.None,
    fillAlpha: Float = 0.16f,
    pattern: ChartPattern? = null,
    color: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    horizontal: Boolean = false,
    labels: ChartDataLabels? = null,
    xAxis: ChartAxis? = ChartAxis(),
    yAxis: ChartAxis? = ChartAxis(),
    marks: List<ChartMark> = emptyList(),
    tooltip: ChartTooltip? = ChartTooltip(),
    zoom: ChartZoom? = null,
    export: ChartExport? = null,
    empty: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null,
    state: ChartState = rememberChartState(),
    description: String? = null,
    onSelect: ((ChartPoint) -> Unit)? = null,
    style: ChartStyle? = null,
    colors: ChartColors? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null
)
declarations.description:
A chart of what lies between two values at each place: the coldest and the warmest of a day, the least and the most a price went to, the hours a shift starts and ends at.

It is a `PantrixChart` with one `RangeSeries`, written shorter: it does everything a chart does. As an Area the range is a band from place to place between two lines; as a Bar it is a bar at each place, from the one value to the other. A band with a line over it, a forecast within the bounds it is trusted within, or two ranges in one chart, is a `PantrixChart` given the series for it. `horizontal`, the places go down the chart's side, one under the other, and the ranges along it: the shifts of a timetable.

Its axis of values does not start at nought unless the axis says so: nothing of a range stands on nought, and what is read is how far apart its two values are and where they lie. A row with no `low` or no `high` has neither.

The tooltip and a screen reader are given both values with a dash between them. A press is handed the higher as the point's `value` and the lower as its `from`.

```
PantrixRangeChart(
    data = days,
    x = { it.name },
    low = { it.coldest },
    high = { it.warmest },
    name = "Temperature",
    tagKey = "temperature"
)
```

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: the rows.

parameters.name: x
parameters.description: where a row stands along the chart: a name, a day, anything that is equal to itself.

parameters.name: low
parameters.description: a row's lower value, or null where it has none.

parameters.name: high
parameters.description: a row's higher value, or null where it has none.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: what the two values are of: what the tooltip calls them, and a screen reader the chart where it has no `description`.

parameters.name: modifier
parameters.description: the chart's modifier. A height here is the chart's.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: whether the range is a band from place to place or a bar at each place.

parameters.name: curve
parameters.description: how the two lines of a band go from a point to the next. A bar has no line.

parameters.name: lines
parameters.description: whether the two lines of a band are drawn, or the tint between them alone.

parameters.name: dash
parameters.description: whether the two lines are drawn whole, in dashes or in dots. `null` draws them whole, and dashed where the chart's patterns are on (`ChartStyle.patterns`).

parameters.name: marker
parameters.description: the mark drawn on each point of the two lines. None by default.

parameters.name: fillAlpha
parameters.description: how much of the range's colour the tint between the lines has, from none to all of it. Left out, about a sixth.

parameters.name: pattern
parameters.description: the texture the band or the bars are drawn with besides their colour. `null` draws none, and where the chart's patterns are on, none too: a chart of one range has nothing to tell it from.

parameters.name: color
parameters.description: the colour the range is drawn in. Left out, it is the first of the chart's colours.

parameters.name: horizontal
parameters.description: whether the places go down the chart's side and the range along it, and not along its foot and up.

parameters.name: labels
parameters.description: the two values written at the range's ends, the higher over it and the lower under it, where they have room. `null` writes none.

parameters.name: xAxis
parameters.description: the axis of the places, under the chart, or beside it where it is `horizontal`. `null` draws nothing of it.

parameters.name: yAxis
parameters.description: the axis of the values, beside the chart, or under it where it is `horizontal`. `null` draws nothing of it.

parameters.name: marks
parameters.description: the lines and the bands drawn in the plot besides the range: a limit, a stretch of places.

parameters.name: tooltip
parameters.description: what is shown for the place that is pointed at. `null` shows none.

parameters.name: zoom
parameters.description: what lets the reader look closer at a part of the places and move along the rest. `null`, which it is unless the chart is given one, shows all the places and no more.

parameters.name: export
parameters.description: what lets the reader take the chart out of the app as a file: a picture, or a drawing that is sharp at any size. `null`, which it is unless the chart is given one, and the chart has no such button.

parameters.name: empty
parameters.description: what the chart shows in its plot while it has no value to draw, in the place of the theme's words for it ("No data"), which a screen reader is then not told either. `null` writes the words. A file the chart is exported as says them.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: what the reader points at: the chart's own where none is given.

parameters.name: description
parameters.description: what the chart shows, in a few words, for a screen reader.

parameters.name: onSelect
parameters.description: called with the range that is pressed.

parameters.name: style
parameters.description: this chart's own geometry.

parameters.name: colors
parameters.description: this chart's own colours, where they are not the theme's.

parameters.name: tagKey
parameters.description: the chart's automation key. The chart is tagged as the `PantrixChart` it is, `Chart_<tagKey>`, and its parts and events are that chart's; its one series has the key `range`.

declarations.name: SankeyNode
declarations.description:
One node of a `PantrixSankeyChart`: something that what the chart follows flows out of, into, or through.

```
SankeyNode("search", "Search")
```

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: What tells the node from the others of its chart: what a link names it by, what a selection names, and what an event reports. Written as a test tag's key is, in small letters and digits.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: What the node is called: beside it, in the tooltip and to a screen reader.

parameters.name: color
parameters.description: The colour the node is drawn in, and the flows that leave it. Left out, it is the theme's chart colour for its place among the nodes.

parameters.name: pattern
parameters.description: The texture the node is drawn with besides its colour. Left out, none, and where the chart's patterns are on (`ChartStyle.patterns`), its turn by its place among the nodes: none for the first.

declarations.name: SankeyLink
declarations.description:
One link of a `PantrixSankeyChart`: how much flows from one node to another.

```
SankeyLink(from = "search", to = "signup", value = 420)
```

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: The key of the node it leaves.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: The key of the node it reaches: another node than the one it leaves.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: How much flows. One that is no number, has no end or is not over nought is no flow.

declarations.name: SankeyAlign
declarations.signature: enum class SankeyAlign
declarations.description: Which column each node of a `PantrixSankeyChart` stands in. Every node stands a column past the nodes that flow into it; the four differ in where a node stands that could stand in more than one.

entries.name: Justify
entries.description: A column past the last of the nodes that flow into it, and a node nothing flows out of in the last column.

entries.name: Left
entries.description: A column past the last of the nodes that flow into it: a node nothing flows out of too.

entries.name: Right
entries.description: A column before the first of the nodes it flows into, and a node nothing flows into as late as it can be.

entries.name: Center
entries.description: A column past the last of the nodes that flow into it, and a node nothing flows into a column before the first of those it flows into.

declarations.name: SankeyOrder
declarations.signature: enum class SankeyOrder
declarations.description: The order the nodes of a column of a `PantrixSankeyChart` stand in, from the top down.

entries.name: Untangled
entries.description: The order that keeps their flows from crossing where that can be helped.

entries.name: Given
entries.description: The order the nodes are given in.

declarations.name: PantrixSankeyChart
declarations.signature:
@Composable
fun PantrixSankeyChart(
    nodes: List<SankeyNode>,
    links: List<SankeyLink>,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    names: Boolean = true,
    tooltip: ChartTooltip? = ChartTooltip(),
    empty: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null,
    state: ChartState = rememberChartState(),
    description: String? = null,
    onSelect: ((ChartPoint) -> Unit)? = null,
    style: ChartStyle? = null,
    colors: ChartColors? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null,
    align: SankeyAlign = SankeyAlign.Justify,
    order: SankeyOrder = SankeyOrder.Untangled,
    export: ChartExport? = null
)
declarations.description:
A sankey chart: what flows from where to where, and how much. Nodes stand in columns, and between them lie the flows as bands, each as wide as what flows: where the visitors of a site come from and what they go on to, what a budget is made of and what it is spent on, where the energy of a plant ends up.

The chart is given its `nodes` and the `links` between them, each link by the keys of its two nodes. The columns come from the links: a node nothing flows into stands in the first, every other a column past the last of the nodes that flow into it, and a node nothing flows out of in the last, as `align` has it by default. In a column the nodes are put in the order that keeps their flows from crossing where that can be helped, or the order they are given in where `order` says so. A node is as tall as the greater of what flows into it and what flows out of it; one that no link names has no place in the chart.

Two links between the same two nodes are one flow, of what they come to together. The links have to lead one way: a link from a node to itself, links that lead back to where they started, and a link that names a node the chart does not have are refused.

**Pointing at a node.** A pointer over a node points at it; a finger does by a tap, and a tap on the node it points at lets go of it. With the keyboard the chart is one stop for Tab: an arrow goes to the nearest node the way it points, Home and End to the first node and the last, and Escape lets go. The node is ringed, its flows are drawn stronger and the others fainter, the tooltip is shown for it, and it is told to `state`, as a selection whose `x` is the node's key. A press, Enter or Space on it calls `onSelect`.

**Pointing at a flow.** A pointer over a flow, off the nodes, points at the flow, and a finger does by a tap: the flow is drawn stronger and the others fainter, and the tooltip names its two nodes, the way it flows, with how much flows. It is told to `state` as a selection whose `series` is the key of the node it leaves and whose `x` is the key of the node it reaches, and a press on it calls `onSelect`. The keys go from node to node, and leave the flows to the nodes' tooltips.

**To a screen reader** the chart is its `description`, then each node with what it counts for and, after it, each of its flows: where it comes from or goes to, and how much.

**Its size.** The chart is as wide as it is given room, and as tall as its modifier says or, given no height, as the chart's style says. In a language read from the right the first column stands at the right.

```
PantrixSankeyChart(
    nodes = listOf(SankeyNode("search", "Search"), SankeyNode("signup", "Sign-up"), SankeyNode("left", "Left")),
    links = listOf(SankeyLink("search", "signup", 420), SankeyLink("search", "left", 580)),
    description = "Where the visitors from search go",
    tagKey = "visitors"
)
```

parameters.name: nodes
parameters.description: the nodes. Their keys tell them apart, and two with one key are refused.

parameters.name: links
parameters.description: what flows between the nodes: each from one node to another, by their keys.

parameters.name: modifier
parameters.description: the chart's modifier. A height here is the chart's.

parameters.name: names
parameters.description: whether each node's name is written beside it, where it has room.

parameters.name: tooltip
parameters.description: what is shown for the node that is pointed at: its name and what it counts for, and under them each flow into it and out of it, with the node at its other end. Its `format` writes the values; `shared` and `crosshair` are not read. `null` shows none.

parameters.name: empty
parameters.description: what the chart shows while it has no value to draw, in the place of the theme's words for it ("No data"), which a screen reader is then not told either. `null` writes the words.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: what the reader points at: the chart's own where none is given.

parameters.name: description
parameters.description: what the chart shows, in a few words, for a screen reader: the first thing it says of the chart. Left out, the chart is announced by the names of its nodes.

parameters.name: onSelect
parameters.description: called with the node that is pressed: its key is its `series` and its `x`, its name its `name` and its `label`, and its `value` what it counts for; and with the flow that is pressed: the key of the node it leaves is its `series` and of the node it reaches its `x`, its `name` the two nodes' names, and its `value` how much flows.

parameters.name: style
parameters.description: this chart's own geometry: the fields set here, with the theme's for the rest. A node is `nodeWidth` wide, two nodes of a column are a `nodeGap` apart, and a node's corners are as round as `barRadius` says.

parameters.name: colors
parameters.description: this chart's own colours, where they are not the theme's.

parameters.name: tagKey
parameters.description: the chart's automation key: the chart is `Sankey_<tagKey>`, its nodes and flows together `Sankey_<tagKey>.Plot`, a node `Sankey_<tagKey>.Node_<number>`, counted from one, column by column and in each from the top down, and the tooltip `Sankey_<tagKey>.Tooltip`. A press on a node is reported as a `Sankey` `select` event with the node's key, and a press on a flow with the keys of its two nodes, `from>to`. Nothing of the values is reported.

parameters.name: align
parameters.description: which column each node stands in, of those it could stand in.

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: the order the nodes of a column stand in: the one that keeps the flows from crossing, or as given.

parameters.name: export
parameters.description: what lets the reader take the chart out of the app as a PNG, an SVG or a PDF: a button over the chart makes the file of it as it is and hands it over (see `ChartExport`). `null`, the chart has no such button.

declarations.name: ScatterSeries
declarations.description:
One group of points in a `PantrixScatterChart`: the rows it is read from, where each of them stands along the chart and up it, and, for bubbles, how large each is.

```
ScatterSeries("europe", "Europe", countries, x = { it.income }, y = { it.lifeExpectancy })
```

`x` and `y` are numbers, and a row stands where the two put it. A row that has no number for either, or one with no end, has no point. With `size` each point is a bubble: its area is as much of the largest bubble's as its size is of the largest size in the chart, so that a value twice another's is twice its area. `label` is what a point is called, a country, a product: the heading of its tooltip, and what a screen reader says of it.

Two series are the same series where everything they were built from is the same, the functions among them: a chart whose caller builds its series anew each time is not drawn anew for it.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: What tells the series from the others of its chart, and stays the same while its rows change: what the legend keeps a hidden series by, what a selection names, and what an event reports. Written as a test tag's key is, in small letters and digits.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: What the series is called: in the legend, in the tooltip and to a screen reader.

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: The rows.

parameters.name: x
parameters.description: Where a row stands along the chart.

parameters.name: y
parameters.description: Where it stands up the chart.

parameters.name: size
parameters.description: How large a row's point is, for a chart of bubbles. Left out, the series' points are marks of one size. A row whose size is no number, or is not over nought, is the smallest bubble.

parameters.name: label
parameters.description: What a row's point is called. Left out, a point goes by its series' name.

parameters.name: color
parameters.description: The colour the series is drawn in. Left out, it is the theme's chart colour for its place among the series of the chart: the first of them for the first.

parameters.name: marker
parameters.description: What a point of the series is drawn as. Shapes tell series apart where colours alone would not. A bubble is a circle whatever this says. Null, a circle, and where the chart's patterns are on (`ChartStyle.patterns`), a circle, a square, a diamond or a triangle by its place among the chart's series.

parameters.name: pattern
parameters.description: The texture its bubbles are drawn with besides their colour. Null, none, and where the chart's patterns are on, its turn by its place among the chart's series. A point that is a mark has none.

declarations.name: PantrixScatterChart
declarations.signature:
@Composable
fun PantrixScatterChart(
    series: List<ScatterSeries<*>>,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    xAxis: ChartAxis? = ChartAxis(),
    yAxis: ChartAxis? = ChartAxis(),
    sizeAxis: ChartAxis? = null,
    marks: List<ChartMark> = emptyList(),
    legend: ChartLegend? = ChartLegend(),
    tooltip: ChartTooltip? = ChartTooltip(),
    empty: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null,
    state: ChartState = rememberChartState(),
    description: String? = null,
    onSelect: ((ChartPoint) -> Unit)? = null,
    style: ChartStyle? = null,
    colors: ChartColors? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null,
    export: ChartExport? = null,
    zoom: ChartZoom? = null
)
declarations.description:
A scatter chart: points set out by two values, one along the chart and one up it, to show how the two go together. With a third value for the size of each point it is a bubble chart.

The chart is given its `series`, and each of them carries its own rows: where a row stands along the chart, where up it, and, for bubbles, how large it is. Both of its axes are of values: each goes from a round number under the least of its values to one over the most, and marks round values between. A chart with bubbles keeps room at the ends of its axes for the largest of them, so that none is cut by the plot's edge.

Around the points stand the parts a chart with places has, each given by what describes it and taken away by `null`: the two axes, the `legend`, which lists the series and takes one out of the chart when its entry is pressed, and the `tooltip`, which shows the values of the point that is pointed at.

**Marks.** A line at a value of either axis, and a band between two, are drawn with the points for them to be read by: an average, a limit, the quarter of the chart that matters. A mark's `x` is here a value of the axis along the chart. See `ChartMark`.

**Pointing at a point.** A pointer over a point, or near it, points at it; a finger does by a tap, and a tap on the point it points at lets go of it. Where points lie on one another, the smallest under the pointer is the one pointed at. With the keyboard the chart is one stop for Tab: the arrows along the chart go from point to point of a series, as they stand along the chart, the arrows up and down go to the series before and after, Home and End to the series' first point and its last, and Escape lets go. The point is marked, the tooltip shown for it, and it is told to `state`, as a selection whose `x` is its place among its series' rows, counted from nought, and whose `series` is its series' key. A press, Enter or Space on it calls `onSelect`.

**To a screen reader** the chart is its `description`, then each point with what it is called and its values, series by series; the legend's entries are switches. A chart of more than two hundred points is told by its description alone.

**Its size.** The chart is as wide as it is given room. A height on its modifier is the whole chart's, the legend's with it; given none, the plot is as tall as the chart's style says and a legend above or under it adds its own.

In a language read from the right the values along the chart run from the right, and those up it are written at the right.

```
PantrixScatterChart(
    series = listOf(
        ScatterSeries("europe", "Europe", europe, x = { it.income }, y = { it.lifeExpectancy }),
        ScatterSeries("asia", "Asia", asia, x = { it.income }, y = { it.lifeExpectancy })
    ),
    xAxis = ChartAxis(title = "Income"),
    yAxis = ChartAxis(title = "Life expectancy"),
    description = "Life expectancy by income",
    tagKey = "countries"
)
```

parameters.name: series
parameters.description: the series, in the order they are listed. Their keys tell them apart, and two with one key are refused.

parameters.name: modifier
parameters.description: the chart's modifier. A height here is the chart's, the legend's with it.

parameters.name: xAxis
parameters.description: the axis of the values along the chart, under it. Its title is what those values are called in the tooltip and to a screen reader. `null` draws nothing of it.

parameters.name: yAxis
parameters.description: the axis of the values up the chart, beside it. `null` draws nothing of it.

parameters.name: sizeAxis
parameters.description: what the bubbles' sizes measure: its `title` is what a size is called in the tooltip and to a screen reader, its `format` how one is written, and its `max` the size the largest bubble stands for, where that is not the largest in the chart. Nothing of it is drawn, and nothing else of it is read.

parameters.name: marks
parameters.description: the lines and the bands drawn in the plot besides the points.

parameters.name: legend
parameters.description: where the names of the series stand. `null` shows none.

parameters.name: tooltip
parameters.description: what is shown for the point that is pointed at: its heading is what the point is called, and under it a row for each of its values. Its `crosshair` is a line across the plot and one up it through the point, and its `format` writes the value up the chart; a point has no place to share, and `shared` is not read. A tooltip's own `content` is given the point's values, the one along the chart first. `null` shows none.

parameters.name: empty
parameters.description: what the chart shows while it has no value to draw, in the place of the theme's words for it ("No data"), which a screen reader is then not told either. `null` writes the words.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: what the reader has hidden and what they point at: the chart's own where none is given.

parameters.name: description
parameters.description: what the chart shows, in a few words, for a screen reader: the first thing it says of the chart. Left out, the chart is announced by the names of its series.

parameters.name: onSelect
parameters.description: called with the point that is pressed: its `x` is its place among its series' rows, counted from nought, its `label` what it is called, and its `value` its value up the chart.

parameters.name: style
parameters.description: this chart's own geometry: the fields set here, with the theme's for the rest.

parameters.name: colors
parameters.description: this chart's own colours, where they are not the theme's.

parameters.name: tagKey
parameters.description: the chart's automation key: the chart is `ScatterChart_<tagKey>`, its plot `ScatterChart_<tagKey>.Plot`, a point `ScatterChart_<tagKey>.Point_<series' key>_<number>`, the number being its row's counted from one, the legend's entry of a series `ScatterChart_<tagKey>.Legend_<series' key>` and the tooltip `ScatterChart_<tagKey>.Tooltip`. A press on a point is reported as a `ScatterChart` `select` event with the series' key, and a press on a legend's entry as a `toggle` event with the key and whether the series is shown. Nothing of the values is reported.

parameters.name: export
parameters.description: what lets the reader take the chart out of the app as a PNG, an SVG or a PDF: a button over the chart makes the file of it as it is and hands it over (see `ChartExport`). `null`, the chart has no such button.

parameters.name: zoom
parameters.description: what lets the reader look closer at a part of the chart's values, across it and up it alike (see `ChartZoom`): a wheel with Ctrl or Command and two fingers look closer about the point between them, plus and minus on the chart about the point that is pointed at, and the buttons about the middle; a drag of the mouse moves what is in view every way, the buttons along it, and the arrows bring the point they go to into view. Both axes are marked anew for the values in view, and what lies past the plot's edges is cut off. The parts are kept in `state`, as its `window` and its `valueWindow`. A scatter chart has no navigator: its `navigator` is not read, nor is its `fitValues`. `null`, the chart shows all its values.

declarations.name: SparklineKind
declarations.signature: enum class SparklineKind
declarations.description: How a `PantrixSparkline` draws its values.

entries.name: Line
entries.description: A line through the values.

entries.name: Area
entries.description: A line through the values, with what is under it filled in a faint share of its colour.

entries.name: Bar
entries.description: A bar for each value, up from nought or down from it.

declarations.name: PantrixSparkline
declarations.signature:
@Composable
fun PantrixSparkline(
    values: List<Number?>,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    kind: SparklineKind = SparklineKind.Line,
    color: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    contentDescription: String? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null,
    export: ChartExport? = null,
    style: ChartStyle? = null,
    curve: ChartCurve = ChartCurve.Linear,
    markLast: Boolean = false,
    reference: Number? = null,
    min: Number? = null,
    max: Number? = null
)
declarations.description:
A sparkline: the run of a number in the room of a word, beside the number it belongs to. It has no axes, no legend and nothing to point at: it shows which way the number has gone, and a chart shows the rest.

The `values` are set out at even steps from where lines start to where they end. Its height goes from `min` up to `max`; where they are not given, a line and an area go from the least of the values to the most, so that the run fills the height it has, and bars from nought, or from the least of them where it is under nought. A `reference` line is taken in too. A value past an end that is given is cut off at the box's edge. A value that is `null`, or no number, is a gap in a line and a place with no bar.

It is 96dp wide and 32dp tall unless its modifier says otherwise, and is drawn in `color` or in the first of the theme's chart colours, as thick as the `style`'s `lineWidth`. In a language read from the right its first value stands at the right.

**To a screen reader** it is a picture with `contentDescription` for its name; with none it is not there at all, which suits a sparkline beside a number that says the same.

```
PantrixSparkline(values = visits, contentDescription = "Visits, last thirty days")
PantrixSparkline(values = temperature, curve = ChartCurve.Smooth, markLast = true, reference = 20)
```

parameters.name: values
parameters.description: the values, in the order they are read.

parameters.name: modifier
parameters.description: the sparkline's modifier. A size here is the sparkline's.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: whether the values are a line, an area or bars.

parameters.name: color
parameters.description: the colour it is drawn in.

parameters.name: contentDescription
parameters.description: what the run is of, in a few words, for a screen reader. `null` leaves it out of what a screen reader reads.

parameters.name: tagKey
parameters.description: the sparkline's automation key: the sparkline is `Sparkline_<tagKey>`.

parameters.name: export
parameters.description: what lets the reader take the chart out of the app as a PNG, an SVG or a PDF: a button over the chart makes the file of it as it is and hands it over (see `ChartExport`). `null`, the chart has no such button.

parameters.name: style
parameters.description: the sizes it is drawn in over the theme's: the line's width (`lineWidth`), the gap between two bars (`barGap`), the mark of the last value (`markerSize`) and the reference line's width (`markLineWidth`).

parameters.name: curve
parameters.description: how a line or an area goes from one value to the next. Bars have none.

parameters.name: markLast
parameters.description: whether the last value is marked: a dot on a line or an area, as large as the style's `markerSize`, and on bars the last one in `color` and the rest in a quieter share of it. The last value is the last that is a number.

parameters.name: reference
parameters.description: a value a dashed line is drawn across the sparkline at, behind its values, in the colour charts write in: a target, or where the run began. `null` draws none.

parameters.name: min
parameters.description: the value at the sparkline's foot, or `null` for the least of its values. A number, and less than `max`.

parameters.name: max
parameters.description: the value at its top, or `null` for the most of them.

declarations.name: StatusBlock
declarations.description:
One block of a `PantrixStatusTracker`: what was the case at one step of a run, as a colour and a few words.

```
StatusBlock("12 October: operational", color = PantrixTheme.colors.success.color)
```

Two are the same block where their names and their colours are.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: What the block stands for, in words: its step and what was the case at it. Written under the row when the block is pointed at, and said to a screen reader.

parameters.name: color
parameters.description: The colour of the block. Left out, the block is in the colour of a chart's grid: a step of which nothing is known.

parameters.name: pattern
parameters.description: The texture the block is drawn with besides its colour. Left out, none, and where the tracker's patterns are on (`ChartStyle.patterns`), the turn of its colour among the row's colours, in the order they first come: a status is one texture, as it is one colour, and the first status none.

declarations.name: PantrixStatusTracker
declarations.signature:
@Composable
fun PantrixStatusTracker(
    blocks: List<StatusBlock>,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    caption: Boolean = true,
    state: ChartState = rememberChartState(),
    description: String? = null,
    onSelect: ((Int) -> Unit)? = null,
    style: ChartStyle? = null,
    colors: ChartColors? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null,
    export: ChartExport? = null
)
declarations.description:
A status tracker: a run of steps as a row of blocks, each in the colour of what was the case at it. The days a service was up, the builds that passed: where the bad ones are is seen at a glance, and which they were is read by pointing at them.

The `blocks` stand side by side from where lines start, each as wide as an even share of the row. The name of the block that is pointed at is written under the row, beside a patch of its colour, unless `caption` says otherwise; with a block pointed at, the others are drawn faint.

**Pointing at a block.** A pointer over a block points at it; a finger does by a tap, and a tap on the block it points at lets go of it. With the keyboard the row is one stop for Tab: the arrows go from block to block, Home and End to the first and the last, and Escape lets go. The block is told to `state`, as a selection whose `x` is its place counted from nought. A press, Enter or Space on it calls `onSelect`.

**To a screen reader** the row is its `description`, then each block by its name, in the blocks' order. A row of more than two hundred blocks is told by its description alone.

In a language read from the right the first block stands at the right, and the arrows go the way they point.

```
PantrixStatusTracker(
    blocks = days.map { StatusBlock("${it.date}: ${it.status}", colorOf(it.status)) },
    description = "Uptime, last thirty days",
    tagKey = "uptime"
)
```

parameters.name: blocks
parameters.description: the blocks, in the order they are read.

parameters.name: modifier
parameters.description: the tracker's modifier.

parameters.name: caption
parameters.description: whether the name of the block that is pointed at is written under the row. The line's room is kept whether a block is pointed at or not, so that the row does not move.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: what the reader points at: the tracker's own where none is given.

parameters.name: description
parameters.description: what the row shows, in a few words, for a screen reader.

parameters.name: onSelect
parameters.description: called with the place of the block that is pressed, counted from nought.

parameters.name: style
parameters.description: this tracker's own geometry: the fields set here, with the theme's for the rest.

parameters.name: colors
parameters.description: this tracker's own colours, where they are not the theme's.

parameters.name: tagKey
parameters.description: the tracker's automation key: the tracker is `StatusTracker_<tagKey>`, its row `StatusTracker_<tagKey>.Blocks`, a block `StatusTracker_<tagKey>.Block_<number>` counted from one and the line under the row `StatusTracker_<tagKey>.Caption`. A press on a block is reported as a `StatusTracker` `select` event with the block's number. Nothing of the names is reported.

parameters.name: export
parameters.description: what lets the reader take the chart out of the app as a PNG, an SVG or a PDF: a button over the chart makes the file of it as it is and hands it over (see `ChartExport`). `null`, the chart has no such button. The line under the row is not in it.

declarations.name: TreemapItem
declarations.description:
One item of a `PantrixTreemap`: a tile with a value, or a group of tiles.

```
TreemapItem("docs", "Documents", 12)
TreemapItem(
    key = "design",
    name = "Design",
    children = listOf(TreemapItem("ui", "Interface", 42), TreemapItem("brand", "Brand", 18))
)
```

An item with no `children` is a tile, as large as its `value` is of all the values. An item with children is a group: its tiles are its children, they lie together under its name, and what it counts for is what they count for together; a value given to a group is not read. A child that has children of its own is one tile, which counts for all of them.

Two items are the same item where everything they were built from is the same.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: What tells the item from the others, and stays the same while its value changes: what a selection names and what an event reports. Written as a test tag's key is, in small letters and digits.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: What it is called: in its tile, over its group, in the tooltip and to a screen reader.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: How much it counts for. An item whose value is no number, or is not over nought, has no tile.

parameters.name: color
parameters.description: The colour it is drawn in. Left out, a tile has its group's colour, and an item the treemap was given the theme's chart colour for its place among them: the first of them for the first.

parameters.name: children
parameters.description: The tiles of a group.

parameters.name: pattern
parameters.description: The texture it is drawn with besides its colour. Left out, a tile has its group's, and an item the treemap was given none, or where the chart's patterns are on (`ChartStyle.patterns`), its turn by its place among them: none for the first.

declarations.name: PantrixTreemap
declarations.signature:
@Composable
fun PantrixTreemap(
    items: List<TreemapItem>,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    labels: ChartDataLabels? = ChartDataLabels(),
    tooltip: ChartTooltip? = ChartTooltip(),
    empty: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null,
    state: ChartState = rememberChartState(),
    description: String? = null,
    onSelect: ((ChartPoint) -> Unit)? = null,
    style: ChartStyle? = null,
    colors: ChartColors? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null,
    scale: HeatmapScale? = null,
    legend: ChartLegend? = ChartLegend(),
    export: ChartExport? = null
)
declarations.description:
A treemap: a box cut into tiles, each as large as its value is of the whole. It suits a whole of many parts, where a pie would have too many slices to read: the folders of a disk, a budget by its lines, a market by its companies. What is large is seen at once, and the small parts still have their place.

The chart is given its `items`. Each of them is a tile, or a group whose own items are its tiles: a group's tiles lie together in a block, in the group's colour, with the group's name over them where the block has room for it. The blocks are set out the largest first from where lines start, and in each block its tiles the largest first, every tile as near a square as the cutting lets it be. An item that counts for nothing has no tile.

A tile has its name and its value written in it where it has room for them, in the one of black and white that reads better on its colour; a tile too small for its name has neither, and the `tooltip` and a screen reader still have both.

**Shaded by value.** Given a `scale`, every tile is drawn in the shade of its value along it, as a heatmap's cells are, whatever colour its item or its group names: the larger a tile, the further along the scale, so that two tiles of nearly one size, or of two blocks far apart, are still told apart at a glance. The blocks still lie together under their groups' names, a tile keeps its group's texture, and the `legend` shows the scale with its least and its most.

**Pointing at a tile.** A pointer over a tile points at it; a finger does by a tap, and a tap on the tile it points at lets go of it. With the keyboard the chart is one stop for Tab: an arrow goes to the nearest tile the way it points, Home and End to the largest tile and the last, and Escape lets go. The tile is ringed, the tooltip shown for it, and it is told to `state`, as a selection whose `x` is the item's key. A press, Enter or Space on it calls `onSelect`.

**To a screen reader** the chart is its `description`, then each tile with its group, its name, its value and its share of the whole, the largest block first. A chart of more than two hundred tiles is told by its description alone.

**Its size.** The chart is as wide as it is given room, and as tall as its modifier says or, given no height, as the chart's style says.

In a language read from the right the largest tile lies at the right.

```
PantrixTreemap(
    items = listOf(TreemapItem("photos", "Photos", 48), TreemapItem("video", "Video", 31)),
    description = "What fills the disk",
    tagKey = "disk"
)
```

parameters.name: items
parameters.description: the tiles and the groups of tiles. Their keys tell the tiles apart, and two tiles with one key are refused.

parameters.name: modifier
parameters.description: the chart's modifier. A height here is the chart's.

parameters.name: labels
parameters.description: what is written in the tiles: each tile's name, and under it its value, written as `format` says or short where it says nothing. `null` writes nothing in them.

parameters.name: tooltip
parameters.description: what is shown for the tile that is pointed at: its group as the heading, where it lies in one, and under it its name and its value with its share of the whole. A tile has no place to share and no line through it: `shared` and `crosshair` are not read. `null` shows none.

parameters.name: empty
parameters.description: what the chart shows while it has no value to draw, in the place of the theme's words for it ("No data"), which a screen reader is then not told either. `null` writes the words.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: what the reader points at: the chart's own where none is given.

parameters.name: description
parameters.description: what the chart shows, in a few words, for a screen reader: the first thing it says of the chart. Left out, the chart is announced by the names of the items it was given.

parameters.name: onSelect
parameters.description: called with the tile that is pressed: its key is its `series` and its `x`, its name its `name` and its `label`, and its `text` its value with its share of the whole after it.

parameters.name: style
parameters.description: this chart's own geometry: the fields set here, with the theme's for the rest. Two tiles are a `sliceGap` apart, and their corners as round as `barRadius` says.

parameters.name: colors
parameters.description: this chart's own colours, where they are not the theme's.

parameters.name: tagKey
parameters.description: the chart's automation key: the chart is `Treemap_<tagKey>`, its tiles together `Treemap_<tagKey>.Plot`, a tile `Treemap_<tagKey>.Tile_<number>`, counted from one as the tiles are laid out, the scale `Treemap_<tagKey>.Legend` and the tooltip `Treemap_<tagKey>.Tooltip`. A press on a tile is reported as a `Treemap` `select` event with the item's key. Nothing of the values is reported.

parameters.name: scale
parameters.description: what shades the tiles by their values, as a heatmap's scale does its cells: where it names no ends, they are the least and the most of the tiles' values. `null`, each tile has its own colour or its group's.

parameters.name: legend
parameters.description: where the scale of shades stands, where the treemap has a `scale`: without one there is nothing for it to show. `null` shows none.

parameters.name: export
parameters.description: what lets the reader take the chart out of the app as a PNG, an SVG or a PDF: a button over the chart makes the file of it as it is and hands it over (see `ChartExport`). `null`, the chart has no such button. The scale of shades stands under the tiles in the file.

declarations.name: PantrixWaterfallChart
declarations.signature:
@Composable
fun <T> PantrixWaterfallChart(
    data: List<T>,
    x: (T) -> Any,
    y: (T) -> Number?,
    name: String,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    total: ((T) -> Boolean)? = null,
    connectors: Boolean = true,
    color: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    horizontal: Boolean = false,
    labels: ChartDataLabels? = null,
    xAxis: ChartAxis? = ChartAxis(),
    yAxis: ChartAxis? = ChartAxis(),
    marks: List<ChartMark> = emptyList(),
    tooltip: ChartTooltip? = ChartTooltip(),
    zoom: ChartZoom? = null,
    export: ChartExport? = null,
    empty: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null,
    state: ChartState = rememberChartState(),
    description: String? = null,
    onSelect: ((ChartPoint) -> Unit)? = null,
    style: ChartStyle? = null,
    colors: ChartColors? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null
)
declarations.description:
A waterfall chart: how an amount comes about, step by step. Each bar starts where the one before it ended, going up for what a row adds and down for what it takes away, and a total stands on nought and shows what the steps before it come to.

It is a `PantrixChart` with one `WaterfallSeries`, written shorter: it does everything a chart does. A step that adds is drawn in the chart's `rising` colour and one that takes away in its `falling` colour, the theme's `success` and `danger` unless `colors` says otherwise; a total is drawn in `color`. A thin line leads from the end of each bar to where the next begins. `horizontal`, the places go down the chart's side, one under the other, and the bars along it, each starting where the one over it ended.

**Totals.** A row that `total` says is a total needs no value: it shows the count so far. A total that does have a value is where the count starts again, as an opening amount before the first step is. A row that is no total and has no value is a step of nothing, and has no bar.

In the tooltip and to a screen reader a step is what it adds, with its sign, and a total what it comes to. A press is handed the step as the point's `value` and the level it starts from as its `from`.

```
PantrixWaterfallChart(
    data = moves,
    x = { it.name },
    y = { it.amount },
    name = "Cash",
    total = { it.isTotal },
    tagKey = "cash"
)
```

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: the rows, in the order their steps are counted.

parameters.name: x
parameters.description: where a row stands along the chart: a name, a day, anything that is equal to itself.

parameters.name: y
parameters.description: what a row adds, under nought what it takes away, or null where it has no value. For a total, the amount the count starts again from, or null for what the steps before it come to.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: what the amounts are of: what the tooltip calls them, and a screen reader the chart where it has no `description`.

parameters.name: modifier
parameters.description: the chart's modifier. A height here is the chart's.

parameters.name: total
parameters.description: whether a row is a total. `null`, the chart has none.

parameters.name: connectors
parameters.description: whether a line leads from the end of each bar to the next.

parameters.name: color
parameters.description: the colour the totals are drawn in. Left out, it is the first of the chart's colours.

parameters.name: horizontal
parameters.description: whether the places go down the chart's side and the bars along it, and not along its foot and up.

parameters.name: labels
parameters.description: what each bar stands for written at its end, a step with its sign and a total as it is, where it has room. `null` writes none.

parameters.name: xAxis
parameters.description: the axis of the places, under the chart, or beside it where it is `horizontal`. `null` draws nothing of it.

parameters.name: yAxis
parameters.description: the axis of the values, beside the chart, or under it where it is `horizontal`. `null` draws nothing of it.

parameters.name: marks
parameters.description: the lines and the bands drawn in the plot besides the steps: a target, a limit.

parameters.name: tooltip
parameters.description: what is shown for the place that is pointed at. `null` shows none.

parameters.name: zoom
parameters.description: what lets the reader look closer at a part of the places and move along the rest. `null`, which it is unless the chart is given one, shows all the places and no more.

parameters.name: export
parameters.description: what lets the reader take the chart out of the app as a file: a picture, or a drawing that is sharp at any size. `null`, which it is unless the chart is given one, and the chart has no such button.

parameters.name: empty
parameters.description: what the chart shows in its plot while it has no value to draw, in the place of the theme's words for it ("No data"), which a screen reader is then not told either. `null` writes the words. A file the chart is exported as says them.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: what the reader points at: the chart's own where none is given.

parameters.name: description
parameters.description: what the chart shows, in a few words, for a screen reader.

parameters.name: onSelect
parameters.description: called with the step or the total that is pressed.

parameters.name: style
parameters.description: this chart's own geometry.

parameters.name: colors
parameters.description: this chart's own colours, where they are not the theme's: `rising` and `falling` among them.

parameters.name: tagKey
parameters.description: the chart's automation key. The chart is tagged as the `PantrixChart` it is, `Chart_<tagKey>`, and its parts and events are that chart's; its one series has the key `steps`.

declarations.name: PantrixAccordion
declarations.signature:
@Composable
fun PantrixAccordion(
    sections: List<AccordionSection>,
    expanded: Set<String>,
    onExpandedChange: (Set<String>) -> Unit,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    variant: AccordionVariant = AccordionVariant.Plain,
    singleExpanded: Boolean = false,
    enabled: Boolean = true,
    style: AccordionStyle? = null,
    colors: AccordionColors? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null
)

parameters.name: sections
parameters.description: the sections, in the order they are shown. No two of them have one key.

parameters.name: expanded
parameters.description: the keys of the sections that are open.

parameters.name: onExpandedChange
parameters.description: called with the keys that are to be open after a header was pressed. The accordion changes nothing by itself.

parameters.name: modifier
parameters.description: the accordion's modifier. The accordion is as wide as the room it is given and as tall as its headers and what the open ones show.

parameters.name: variant
parameters.description: how the sections are told apart: by a line between them, by an edge around the set, or each as a card of its own.

parameters.name: singleExpanded
parameters.description: whether opening a section closes whichever was open: for a page where two open sections would push the rest off the screen.

parameters.name: enabled
parameters.description: whether the headers can be pressed. False holds every section as it is, and a section says the same of itself alone.

parameters.name: style
parameters.description: this call's own style: over every enclosing one and under the density. Only the fields it sets change, on every platform.

parameters.name: colors
parameters.description: this accordion's own colours, where they are not the theme's: the ones set here, with the theme's for the rest.

parameters.name: tagKey
parameters.description: the accordion's automation key: the accordion is `Accordion_<tagKey>`, a header in it `Accordion_<tagKey>.Header_<key>` and what it opens `Accordion_<tagKey>.Content_<key>`. A press is reported as an `Accordion` event: `expand` and `collapse`, with the section's key.

declarations.name: AccordionVariant
declarations.signature: enum class AccordionVariant
declarations.description: How the sections of a `PantrixAccordion` are told apart.

entries.name: Plain
entries.description: A line between one section and the next, and nothing around the set: for a page's own column.

entries.name: Bordered
entries.description: One edge around the whole set, with a line between the sections inside it.

entries.name: Separated
entries.description: Each section a card of its own, with a gap between one and the next.

declarations.name: AccordionSection

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: What the accordion's `expanded` holds for this section. It is the same in every language, so a translated screen opens the same section, and no two sections of an accordion have one key.

parameters.name: title
parameters.description: The header's text, and the section's name for a screen reader.

parameters.name: subtitle
parameters.description: A second line under the title, or null for none.

parameters.name: icon
parameters.description: Drawn before the title, in the title's colour, or null for none. A screen reader passes over it.

parameters.name: enabled
parameters.description: Whether the header can be pressed. One that cannot is written in the disabled text's colour, and its section stays open or closed as the accordion's `expanded` has it.

parameters.name: tagKey
parameters.description: The section's automation key, the same in every language, where it is to be another than `key`: the header is `Header_<tagKey>` and what it opens `Content_<tagKey>`, inside the tag of an accordion that has a key, as `Accordion_faq.Header_delivery`.

parameters.name: trailing
parameters.description: What stands between the title and the chevron, or null for nothing: a count, a badge. It is a part of the header's button and is read with it: a control of its own does not belong there.

parameters.name: content
parameters.description: What the section shows while it is open, one thing under another with the theme's small spacing between them, as in a card. A closed section composes none of it.

declarations.name: AccordionStyle
declarations.description:
`PantrixAccordion`'s geometry: the room in a section's header and around what the header opens, and the edge.

A header is a row of a list. On Android it is Material 3's one-line list item, 56dp tall with 16dp at its sides. On iOS it is a row of 44pt, the least a finger is given there. Desktop and the web are tighter, for a pointer, and the web's header is no lower than 44dp: a browser may be a touch screen's.

The corners are the card's on each platform, since a section of `AccordionVariant.Separated` is a card: medium on Android, large on iOS, small on desktop and the web.

The header's height, the paddings and the gaps follow the density, since they are the room around the words. The icon's size, the edge's width and the shape do not.

parameters.name: shape
parameters.description: The corners of the edge around the set in `AccordionVariant.Bordered`, and around each section in `AccordionVariant.Separated`: a step of the brand's shape scale, or a fixed shape.

parameters.name: headerMinHeight
parameters.description: The least height of a header. A title on two lines, a subtitle or a larger type makes it taller, and the platform's touch target is its floor.

parameters.name: horizontalPadding
parameters.description: The room between a header's sides and what it holds.

parameters.name: verticalPadding
parameters.description: The room over and under a header's lines, where they need more than the least height.

parameters.name: contentPadding
parameters.description: The room at the sides of what an open section shows, and under it.

parameters.name: iconGap
parameters.description: Between a header's icon, its title, what it has at its end and its chevron.

parameters.name: iconSize
parameters.description: The width and height of a header's icon and of its chevron.

parameters.name: borderWidth
parameters.description: The width of the lines between sections, and of the edges. Zero draws none.

parameters.name: sectionGap
parameters.description: Between one section and the next in `AccordionVariant.Separated`.

declarations.name: AccordionColors
declarations.description:
What a `PantrixAccordion` is painted with, for an accordion that does not take the theme's colours: a colour that is set is used, and one that is left out stays the theme's.

```
// Each section a card in the primary role's soft fill, written in what the theme pairs with it.
PantrixAccordion(…, colors = AccordionColors(container = PantrixTheme.colors.primary.container))
```

A `container` given here that is one of the theme's role colours brings the colour the theme pairs with it, unless `content` is given too. A fill no role has does not: what reads on it is the caller's to give.

parameters.name: container
parameters.description: The fill behind the sections. None in `AccordionVariant.Plain` and `AccordionVariant.Bordered`, which stand on what is behind them, and the theme's `surface` under each section of `AccordionVariant.Separated`.

parameters.name: content
parameters.description: A header's title and its icon, and what a section shows where that gives no colour of its own. The theme's `textPrimary`, or on a fill that is not the accordion's, the colour that fill gives what stands on it. A subtitle and a chevron are the theme's `textSecondary` on the theme's own grounds, and this colour elsewhere and where it is given.

parameters.name: divider
parameters.description: The lines between sections, and the edges. The theme's `divider` on the theme's own grounds. On a fill, where that line would not read, a share of `content`: the edge a subtle button has.

declarations.name: AlertTone
declarations.signature: enum class AlertTone
declarations.description:
What an alert is telling the user: one of the theme's colour roles, which also decides its icon and how it is announced.

The semantic tones, `Info`, `Success`, `Warning` and `Danger`, say how something went, and reach the user as a colour and as an icon, because a colour alone fails whoever cannot see it. `Primary` and `Neutral` say nothing of that, and have no icon of their own: an alert in one of them is a note set apart from the text around it.

entries.name: Info
entries.description: Something worth knowing that is neither good nor bad.

entries.name: Success
entries.description: Something that worked.

entries.name: Warning
entries.description: Something to look at before it becomes a problem.

entries.name: Danger
entries.description: Something that failed. The one tone announced assertively: it interrupts what a screen reader is saying.

entries.name: Primary
entries.description: Something the app wants noticed, in the brand's colour, without an icon: a feature to try, an offer.

entries.name: Neutral
entries.description: A note with no hue of its own, in the theme's grey, without an icon: what does not ask for the eye.

declarations.name: AlertVariant
declarations.signature: enum class AlertVariant
declarations.description: How an alert is drawn, so that it can be seen on whatever it stands on.

entries.name: Soft
entries.description: The tone's pale fill. The default, and what a page wants.

entries.name: Outline
entries.description: An edge in the tone's colour and no fill: for a card or a dialog, whose own fill a pale one would be lost on.

entries.name: Accent
entries.description: The pale fill with a bar down its leading edge: for alerts one under another, told apart at a glance.

declarations.id: com.pantrixui.components.container.alert.PantrixAlert(String, Modifier, AlertTone, AlertVariant, String?, ImageVector?, (@Composable RowScope.() -> Unit)?, (() -> Unit)?, Boolean, AlertStyle?, AlertColors?, String?, TextStyle)
declarations.name: PantrixAlert
declarations.signature:
@Composable
fun PantrixAlert(
    message: String,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    tone: AlertTone = AlertTone.Info,
    variant: AlertVariant = AlertVariant.Soft,
    title: String? = null,
    icon: ImageVector? = tone.icon(),
    action: (@Composable RowScope.() -> Unit)? = null,
    onDismiss: (() -> Unit)? = null,
    announce: Boolean = true,
    style: AlertStyle? = null,
    colors: AlertColors? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null,
    textStyle: TextStyle = PantrixTheme.typography.body
)
declarations.description:
A message about what the user is doing, shown beside the thing it is about: the form that was just sent, the row about to be deleted, the one field that needs a second look.

It stands in the content, next to that thing, and is as wide as what holds it. It stays until the screen takes it away: what the app has just done, said for a few seconds over the whole screen, is a snackbar.

A semantic tone reaches the user three ways, as a colour, as an icon and as the way a screen reader is told, because a colour alone fails whoever cannot see it. A screen reader hears the title and the message as one, and the action and the close button after them.

The icon and the close button stand on the text's first line, as a bullet does, however large the type is set. That line is as tall as an icon with one beside it or without, so alerts one under another are as tall as each other. The close button is as large as its cross where it is laid out, so the alert is no taller for it, and its touch target reaches past it into the room around.

parameters.name: message
parameters.description: what happened, or what to know: a sentence or two.

parameters.name: modifier
parameters.description: the alert's modifier. The alert fills the width it is given.

parameters.name: tone
parameters.description: what the alert is telling: its colours, its icon and the way it is announced.

parameters.name: variant
parameters.description: how it is drawn: a pale fill, an edge alone, or the fill with a bar.

parameters.name: title
parameters.description: a line above the message, in a heavier type: what it is about, in a few words.

parameters.name: icon
parameters.defaultNote: `icon`: The tone's own icon; a primary and a neutral alert have none.
parameters.description: the mark before the text: the tone's own unless another is given, and none when null. A primary and a neutral alert have none of their own. It is never read out: the message says what it stands for.

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: what the user can do about it, under the message at the end: one or two small buttons. A text button's own colour is the brand's: `PantrixTheme.colors.warning.buttonColors(ButtonVariant.Text)` draws it in the tone's, which reads on the tone's fill. A button there takes the room it is drawn in: the room a finger needs around it reaches into the alert's padding, and the alert is no taller for it.

parameters.name: onDismiss
parameters.description: called when the close button is pressed, or a screen reader's dismiss action is used. Null leaves the button out. The alert stays until the caller stops showing it.

parameters.name: announce
parameters.description: whether a screen reader is told when the alert appears or changes: assertively for `AlertTone.Danger`, politely for the rest. Turn it off for an alert that was there before the user came, as a note that a record cannot be changed: a screen reader gets to it in its own time.

parameters.name: style
parameters.description: this call's own style: over every enclosing one and under the density. Only the fields it sets change, on every platform.

parameters.name: colors
parameters.description: this alert's own colours, where they are not its tone's: the ones set here, with the tone's for the rest.

parameters.name: tagKey
parameters.description: the alert's automation key: the alert is `Alert_<tagKey>` and its close button `AlertClose_<tagKey>`. A dismissal is reported as an `Alert` event, `dismiss`, with the tone and the variant and never the message.

parameters.name: textStyle
parameters.description: the type the message is set in, and the title in its bold: the theme's `body` unless given. A colour in it is not the text's, which is the alert's.
