declarations.name: TabBadge
declarations.description:
A badge on a tab of `PantrixTabs`: a count, or a dot where there is nothing to count.

The badge comes after the tab's label, and takes its room from the label where the tab is narrow: a long label is cut, and the badge is whole. It is a `PantrixBadge`, as large as that is and in its colours, on a tab of any state.

A screen reader hears `contentDescription` after the tab's label, as a part of the tab: "Inbox, 3 unread". A number alone would say nothing of what it counts, so the badge is silent without one, which is right only where the label says it already. It has no default for that reason: null is a decision.

parameters.name: contentDescription
parameters.description: What a screen reader says of the badge, after the tab's label, or null to say nothing.

parameters.name: count
parameters.description: The number to show, or null for a dot. It is capped as a badge's is: `99+`.

parameters.name: tone
parameters.description: The colour role the badge is filled from.

parameters.name: colors
parameters.description: The badge's own colours, in place of its tone's: the ones it sets, with the tone's for the rest.

declarations.name: TabItem
declarations.description: One tab of `PantrixTabs`: its label, an icon before it, a badge after it, and a key for automation.

parameters.name: label
parameters.description: The visible text, and the tab's name for a screen reader.

parameters.name: icon
parameters.description: Drawn before the label, in the label's colour, or null for none.

parameters.name: enabled
parameters.description: Whether the tab can be selected. A press does nothing on one that cannot, and the arrow keys skip it.

parameters.name: tagKey
parameters.description: The tab's automation key, the same in every language: the tab is `Tab_<tagKey>`, or `Tab_<index>` without one, inside the tag of a row that has a key: `Tabs_mail.Tab_inbox`.

parameters.name: badge
parameters.description: A count or a dot after the label, or null for none.

declarations.name: PantrixTabs
declarations.signature:
@Composable
fun PantrixTabs(
    tabs: List<TabItem>,
    selectedIndex: Int,
    onSelect: (index: Int) -> Unit,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    scrollable: Boolean = false,
    style: TabsStyle? = null,
    colors: TabsColors? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null
)
declarations.description:
A row of tabs that switches between views of the same content: one is selected, and a mark slides to the one selected next.

What marks the selected tab is the style's `TabsStyle.indicator`: a line under it, a line over it, a pill behind it, or its colour alone. The mark is where its tab is. It follows the tab when the row changes size, and slides only when the selection changes: at once under reduced motion.

The row is one stop for Tab, on the selected tab, as the WAI-ARIA tabs pattern has it. The arrow keys select the next or the previous tab, the other way round in a right-to-left layout, and Home and End the first and the last; a tab that is disabled is skipped. While a tab has the focus, the focus goes with the selection, whoever makes it: a key, a press, or the app, as when a pager is swiped to the next view. A press on a tab asks for it, and the focus goes to the row's one stop, the selected tab, where a press can take the focus. For a screen reader each tab is a tab that says whether it is selected, in one group.

A tab may carry a badge after its label, a count or a dot: `TabItem.badge`. A screen reader hears the badge's description after the label, as a part of the tab.

With `scrollable`, each tab is as wide as its label and the row scrolls sideways. It opens on the selected tab, and brings the one selected next to its middle, so that the tabs on both sides of it can be seen and pressed.

A tab is at least as tall as the platform's touch target, whatever the style's height and the density say. The row has no fill of its own: it sits on the page or on a surface, and its labels read on both. The tabs are only the row: the view that `selectedIndex` stands for is the app's, below it.

parameters.name: tabs
parameters.description: the tabs, in order.

parameters.name: selectedIndex
parameters.description: the selected tab's index. Outside `tabs`, no tab is selected and no mark is drawn.

parameters.name: onSelect
parameters.description: called with the index of the tab the user chose, by a press or by the keys, whether or not it is selected already. The row selects nothing by itself: a tab is selected when `selectedIndex` says so.

parameters.name: modifier
parameters.description: the row's modifier. The row fills the width it is given.

parameters.name: scrollable
parameters.description: false shares the row's width between the tabs. True makes each as wide as its label, at least the style's `minTabWidth`, in a row that scrolls sideways and keeps the selected tab in its middle.

parameters.name: style
parameters.description: this call's own style: over every enclosing one and under the density. Only the fields it sets change, on every platform.

parameters.name: colors
parameters.description: this row's own colours: the ones it sets, with the theme's for the rest. A disabled tab keeps the theme's.

parameters.name: tagKey
parameters.description: the row's automation key: the row is `Tabs_<tagKey>`, and its tabs are named inside it, `Tabs_<tagKey>.Tab_<key>`, so that two rows with the same tabs are told apart. A selection is reported as a `Tabs` event that carries the tab's index and whether a press or a key chose it, and never its label.

declarations.name: TabIndicator
declarations.signature: enum class TabIndicator
declarations.description: How `PantrixTabs` marks the selected tab.

entries.name: Underline
entries.description: A line along the selected tab's bottom edge, over the hairline under the row. The default on every platform.

entries.name: Top
entries.description: The same line along the tab's top edge, for a row that sits below what it switches.

entries.name: Pill
entries.description: A pill in the primary role's container behind the selected tab, inset by the style's `indicatorPadding`. A row of pills draws no hairline: it is a control of its own, not a heading over the content.

entries.name: None
entries.description: No indicator: the selected tab is marked by its colour alone.

declarations.name: TabsStyle
declarations.description:
`PantrixTabs`' geometry, and how it marks the selected tab.

Fixed tabs share the row's width. Scrollable tabs are as wide as their labels, at least `minTabWidth`, with `edgePadding` before the first and after the last. The air follows the density: `height`, `horizontalPadding`, `edgePadding`, `iconGap` and `indicatorPadding`. The indicator's thickness, the icon's size and the least a tab is wide do not. The tabs' colours are not part of the style: they come from the theme, and from `TabsColors` where a row has its own.

Android follows Material 3's primary tabs, with the icon before the label. iOS has no tab row of its own, since a segmented control does that job there, which `TabIndicator.Pill` draws; its values and the desktop's are Pantrix's own.

parameters.name: height
parameters.description: The least a tab is tall: 48dp on Android, 44dp on iOS, 40dp on desktop and the web. A tab is never shorter than the platform's touch target, whatever this says.

parameters.name: horizontalPadding
parameters.description: Inside a tab, before its icon or label and after its label.

parameters.name: indicatorHeight
parameters.description: How thick a `TabIndicator.Underline` or a `TabIndicator.Top` line is.

parameters.name: minTabWidth
parameters.description: The least a scrollable tab is wide.

parameters.name: edgePadding
parameters.description: Before the first scrollable tab and after the last.

parameters.name: iconSize
parameters.description: The size of a tab's icon.

parameters.name: iconGap
parameters.description: Between a tab's icon and its label, and between its label and its badge.

parameters.name: indicator
parameters.description: What marks the selected tab.

parameters.name: indicatorPadding
parameters.description: Between a `TabIndicator.Pill` and the edges of the tab it marks.

declarations.name: TabsColors
declarations.description:
What `PantrixTabs` is painted with, for a row that does not take the theme's: a colour that is set is used, and one that is left out stays the theme's role.

```
PantrixTabs(
    tabs = views,
    selectedIndex = view,
    onSelect = { view = it },
    colors = TabsColors(selectedContent = brand, indicator = brand)
)
```

They are the colours of tabs that can be selected. A disabled tab is drawn in the theme's disabled text colour whatever is given here.

parameters.name: selectedContent
parameters.description: The label and the icon of the selected tab. The theme's `primary`, and on a pill the primary role's `onContainer`, the colour paired with the pill's fill. A pill given an `indicator` that is one of the theme's own colours brings the colour the theme pairs with it; for one no role has, give this with it.

parameters.name: unselectedContent
parameters.description: The label and the icon of the other tabs. The theme's `textSecondary`.

parameters.name: indicator
parameters.description: What marks the selected tab: the line under or over it, or the pill behind it. The theme's `primary`, and for a pill the primary role's `container`.

parameters.name: divider
parameters.description: The hairline under the row, which a row of pills does not draw. The theme's `divider` on the theme's own grounds. A row of tabs has no fill of its own: on a fill, where that line would not read, a share of what is written there.

declarations.name: TabletopControls
declarations.signature: enum class TabletopControls
declarations.description: Where a `PantrixTabletopLayout`'s controls are while no fold divides its room.

entries.name: Below
entries.description: Under the content, as tall as they are: the content takes the rest of the room.

entries.name: Overlay
entries.description: Over the content, at its bottom, as tall as they are: the content takes the whole room, as a video's does.

declarations.name: TabletopArrangement
declarations.signature: enum class TabletopArrangement
declarations.description: How a `PantrixTabletopLayout` lays out its two parts, as the fold of its room has it.

entries.name: Flat
entries.description: No fold divides the room: the controls are below the content, or over it.

entries.name: Tabletop
entries.description: A foldable laid on a table: the content fills the half above the fold, the controls the half below.

entries.name: Book
entries.description: A foldable held like a book: the content at the start of the fold, the controls past it.

declarations.name: TabletopScope
declarations.signature: interface TabletopScope
declarations.description: What both parts of a `PantrixTabletopLayout` are told of the layout they are in.

members.name: arrangement
members.description: How the layout lays its parts out: controls drawn larger on a table, where they have half the screen, or a video that knows the controls are over it.

declarations.name: PantrixTabletopLayout
declarations.signature:
@Composable
fun PantrixTabletopLayout(
    content: @Composable TabletopScope.() -> Unit,
    controls: @Composable TabletopScope.() -> Unit,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    flatControls: TabletopControls = TabletopControls.Below,
    tagKey: String? = null
)
declarations.description:
Content that is looked at and the controls that are touched, laid out for how a foldable is held: on a table, half open with the fold lying across, the content fills the half above the fold and the controls the half below, where the hands are; held like a book, the two stand at each side of the fold; and on a screen that does not fold, the controls are below the content or over it, as `flatControls` says. A video and its player's buttons, a video call and its buttons, a camera's view and its shutter.

- **Its own room.** The layout looks for the fold where it crosses its own room, not the window: a layout that lies wholly on one side of the fold is laid out flat.

- **The fold's strip.** On a table and like a book, nothing is laid on the strip the fold keeps clear, and a strip in the middle of the room leaves both halves as large as each other.

- **Kept state.** The two parts stay where they are in the composition as the posture changes, at once and with no motion: a video goes on playing, and what the controls remember is kept.

- **Each part a window.** What a part holds is told the part's room as its window: `PantrixTheme.window`, its classes and `PantrixTheme.layout` answer for the part. The posture stays the window's.

- **Screen reader.** Each part is read as one group, the content first and the controls after it.

- **Reading direction.** Held like a book, the content is at the start of the fold: on the right where the language is read from right to left.

- **Automation.** The layout is tagged `TabletopLayout_<tagKey>`, its parts `TabletopContent_<tagKey>` and `TabletopControls_<tagKey>`.

The layout takes the room it is given, which is to be bounded both ways: `Modifier.fillMaxSize()` on a screen.

parameters.name: content
parameters.description: what is looked at: a video, the people of a call, a camera's view.

parameters.name: controls
parameters.description: what is touched: a player's buttons and its progress, a call's buttons, a shutter.

parameters.name: modifier
parameters.description: the room the two parts have.

parameters.name: flatControls
parameters.description: where the controls are while no fold divides the room.

parameters.name: tagKey
parameters.description: the key of the layout's automation tags.

declarations.name: PantrixTopBarState
declarations.signature: class PantrixTopBarState(collapsedFraction: Float = 0f)
declarations.description:
How far a `PantrixTopBar` with a collapsing title has collapsed, and the scroll that collapses it.

A bar given a state is `TopBarStyle.expandedHeight` tall, with its title in a large type in a band under the navigation icon and the actions. As the content under it scrolls up the band closes, the title comes into the row, and the bar is `TopBarStyle.height` tall. The content hands the bar its scroll with `topBarScroll`: the bar collapses before the content moves, and opens again only once the content is back at its top, so the large title does not come back in the middle of a list. A finger that leaves the bar between its two heights is followed by the bar going on to the nearer, and a mouse wheel by the bar going on the way the wheel was last turned.

The state is the app's, as a scroll state is: keep it with `rememberPantrixTopBarState`, which survives a configuration change, and read `collapsedFraction` for anything else that follows the bar.

parameters.name: collapsedFraction
parameters.description: how far the bar is collapsed to begin with: 0, all open, unless it is told.

members.name: collapsedFraction
members.description: 0 while the bar is all open, 1 once it has collapsed. Set, it is kept between the two: set to 0, as a screen that has just gone back to its top does, it opens the bar.

companion.name: Saver
companion.description: Keeps how far the bar had collapsed across a configuration change.

declarations.name: rememberPantrixTopBarState
declarations.signature:
@Composable
fun rememberPantrixTopBarState(): PantrixTopBarState
declarations.description: A `PantrixTopBarState` that survives a configuration change, for a `PantrixTopBar` with a collapsing title.

declarations.name: topBarScroll
declarations.signature: fun Modifier.topBarScroll(state: PantrixTopBarState): Modifier
declarations.description:
Hands the scroll of the content this is on to `state`, so that the top bar over it collapses as the content scrolls up, and opens again once the content is back at its top. It watches a mouse wheel over the content too: a wheel says nothing of when its scroll is over, and content at its top has no use for a wheel turned up.

```
val topBar = rememberPantrixTopBarState()
LazyColumn(modifier = Modifier.topBarScroll(topBar), contentPadding = padding) { ... }
```

declarations.name: PantrixTopBar
declarations.signature:
@Composable
fun PantrixTopBar(
    title: String,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    subtitle: String? = null,
    titleStyle: TextStyle = PantrixTheme.typography.title,
    subtitleStyle: TextStyle = PantrixTheme.typography.footnote,
    navigationIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null,
    actions: (@Composable RowScope.() -> Unit)? = null,
    scrolled: Boolean = false,
    state: PantrixTopBarState? = null,
    style: TopBarStyle? = null,
    colors: TopBarColors? = null,
    insets: PaddingValues = PaddingValues(),
    tagKey: String? = null
)
declarations.description:
The bar at the top of a screen: the screen's title, with a navigation icon before it and actions after it.

Where the title stands follows the platform (`TopBarStyle.titleAlignment`): at the start on Android, the desktop and the web, in the middle of the bar on iOS. A title in the middle is in the middle of the bar, whatever is beside it, while it fits there; one too wide for that moves over, away from the wider side. Neither kind runs under the navigation icon or the actions: a title that is too long for the room between them is cut short, and so is the `subtitle` under it. The title is the screen's heading for a screen reader.

The bar is as wide as what holds it, and as tall as its style says under the `insets` it keeps clear. It is taller only where what it holds needs it, as a title in a larger type does: the title's lines keep a little clear of its top and its bottom.

```
val list = rememberLazyListState()
PantrixScaffold(
    topBar = { insets ->
        PantrixTopBar(
            title = stringResource(Res.string.conversation),
            navigationIcon = { PantrixBackButton(onClick = onBack, tagKey = "back") },
            scrolled = list.canScrollBackward,
            insets = insets,
            tagKey = "conversation"
        )
    }
) { padding -> Messages(list, padding) }
```

With a `state` the bar has a collapsing title. It starts `TopBarStyle.expandedHeight` tall, with the title in a large type, and the subtitle under it, in a band of their own under the navigation icon and the actions, at the bar's start on every platform. As the content under the bar scrolls up the band closes and the bar comes down to `TopBarStyle.height`, the title in the row coming in as the one in the band goes. The content hands the bar its scroll with `Modifier.topBarScroll(state)`. A screen reader reads the title in the row, which is there all the time, and never meets the title twice.

A screen reader and the Tab key go through the bar in the order it reads: the navigation icon, the title and the subtitle under it, the actions.

**In the system's vertical bar.** Inside a `PantrixScaffold` that holds the column the iPhone Duo's outer screen keeps along its side, the bar hands its navigation icon and its actions over to it: they stand at the column's top, under the status bar, the navigation icon in a capsule of the bar's fill and the actions one above another in another, as UIKit puts a navigation bar's buttons there. The bar keeps its title, which then has the bar's width. Of two bars handing buttons over at once, as while one page slides over another, the column shows the one that came last.

parameters.name: title
parameters.description: the screen's name, on one line.

parameters.name: modifier
parameters.description: the bar's modifier.

parameters.name: subtitle
parameters.description: a line under the title in a smaller type, a count or a state, or null for none.

parameters.name: titleStyle
parameters.description: the type the title is set in, in the row: the theme's `title` unless given. A larger one makes the bar as tall as its line needs. Its colour is the bar's unless the style has one of its own. The large title of a collapsing bar is the theme's `headline`, whatever this is.

parameters.name: subtitleStyle
parameters.description: the type the subtitle is set in, in the row and in a collapsing bar's band: the theme's `footnote` unless given. Its colour is the bar's unless the style has one of its own.

parameters.name: navigationIcon
parameters.description: what stands before the title: a `PantrixBackButton`, or a button that opens a drawer. Null for none, and the title then starts at the bar's own inset.

parameters.name: actions
parameters.description: what stands after the title, in a row: icon buttons for what the screen can do, the most used first. A button draws in its own colours, the brand's unless it is given others: on a bar with a fill of its own, give each the colour that reads there.

parameters.name: scrolled
parameters.description: whether a line is drawn along the bar's bottom edge, to part it from what is scrolled under it: pass whether the content can scroll back, as `listState.canScrollBackward`. The line is inside the bar's height, and nothing moves as it comes and goes.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: gives the bar a collapsing title: kept with `rememberPantrixTopBarState`, and handed the content's scroll with `Modifier.topBarScroll`. Null is a bar of one height.

parameters.name: style
parameters.description: this bar's own geometry, which a `PantrixBackButton` in `navigationIcon` draws with too. Only the fields it sets change, on every platform.

parameters.name: colors
parameters.description: this bar's own colours, or null for the theme's: its `surface`, with the title in `textPrimary` and the subtitle in `textSecondary`.

parameters.name: insets
parameters.description: the room the bar keeps clear at its edges, the status bar's and a cutout's, as a `PantrixScaffold` hands its top bar. The bar's fill runs behind them.

parameters.name: tagKey
parameters.description: the bar's automation key, the same in every language: the bar is tagged `TopBar_<tagKey>`, and the large title of a collapsing one `TopBar_<tagKey>.Title_large`.

declarations.name: PantrixBackButton
declarations.signature:
@Composable
fun PantrixBackButton(
    onClick: () -> Unit,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    enabled: Boolean = true,
    tagKey: String? = null
)
declarations.description:
A button that goes back to the screen before, for a `PantrixTopBar`'s navigation icon: an icon button a screen reader calls "Back" in the theme's language.

It draws the platform's own icon (`TopBarStyle.backIcon`): an arrow on Android, the desktop and the web, a chevron on iOS. Both turn round in a right-to-left layout. In a top bar's `navigationIcon` it takes the style that bar was given.

It is a `PantrixIconButton`, and on the theme's grounds it is drawn as one: in the brand's colour. On a fill, and in a bar that was given a colour for what it holds, it is drawn in that colour. It is tagged `IconButton_<tagKey>` and reports an `IconButton` `click`.

parameters.name: onClick
parameters.description: called at a press: go back to the screen before.

parameters.name: modifier
parameters.description: the button's modifier.

parameters.name: enabled
parameters.description: whether the button can be pressed.

parameters.name: tagKey
parameters.description: the button's automation key, the same in every language.

declarations.name: TopBarTitleAlignment
declarations.signature: enum class TopBarTitleAlignment
declarations.description: Where a `PantrixTopBar` puts its title.

entries.name: Start
entries.description: At the start, after the navigation icon: the top bars of Android, the desktop and the web.

entries.name: Center
entries.description: In the middle of the bar, whatever stands beside it, while it fits there: the navigation bar of iOS.

declarations.name: BackButtonIcon
declarations.signature: enum class BackButtonIcon
declarations.description: The icon a `PantrixBackButton` draws.

entries.name: Arrow
entries.description: An arrow: the back button of Android, the desktop and the web.

entries.name: Chevron
entries.description: A chevron: the back button of iOS.

declarations.name: TopBarStyle
declarations.description:
`PantrixTopBar`'s geometry, and the icon `PantrixBackButton` draws.

`titleInset` keeps the title clear of an edge that has nothing beside it; next to a navigation icon or the actions the title is `titleGap` away from them. The bar is taller than `height` only where what it holds needs it. The heights and the room in the bar follow the density; where the title stands and which icon goes back do not. A top bar's colours are not part of its style: they are the theme's, and `TopBarColors` where a bar has its own.

parameters.name: height
parameters.description: How tall the bar is, under the insets it keeps clear: 54dp on Android and iOS, 56dp on desktop and the web.

parameters.name: expandedHeight
parameters.description: How tall a bar with a collapsing title is before it collapses: `height`, and under it the band that holds the title in a large type. 106dp on Android and iOS, 104dp on desktop and the web: a band of 52dp, and of 48dp on desktop and the web. A band is taller only where its lines need it, and a style that sets this no higher than `height` has no band: its bar is of one height, with a state or without.

parameters.name: horizontalPadding
parameters.description: The room between the bar's edges and the navigation icon and the actions: 8dp.

parameters.name: titleInset
parameters.description: How far the title stands from the bar's start edge where there is no navigation icon, and from its end edge where there are no actions: 16dp. The title is never nearer an edge than `horizontalPadding`.

parameters.name: titleGap
parameters.description: The room between the navigation icon and the title, and between the title and the actions: 8dp.

parameters.name: titleAlignment
parameters.description: Where the title stands: in the middle on iOS, at the start elsewhere.

parameters.name: backIcon
parameters.description: What a `PantrixBackButton` draws: a chevron on iOS, an arrow elsewhere.

declarations.name: TopBarColors
declarations.description:
What a `PantrixTopBar` is painted with, for a bar that does not take the theme's colours: a colour that is set is used, and one that is left out stays the theme's.

```
// A bar in the brand's own colour, written in what the theme pairs with it.
PantrixTopBar(title = title, colors = TopBarColors(container = PantrixTheme.colors.primary.color))
```

A `container` given here that is one of the theme's role colours brings the colour the theme pairs with it for what the bar holds, unless `content` is given too. A fill no role has does not: what reads on it is the caller's to give.

parameters.name: container
parameters.description: The bar's fill, which runs behind the insets the bar keeps clear. The theme's `surface`.

parameters.name: content
parameters.description: The title, the subtitle, and the icons of the navigation icon and the actions that give no colour of their own. On the theme's own fill the title is the theme's `textPrimary`, the subtitle its `textSecondary`, and an icon its own default.

parameters.name: divider
parameters.description: The line along the bar's bottom edge while content is scrolled under it. The theme's `divider` on the theme's own grounds. On a fill, where that line would not read, a share of `content`: the edge a subtle button has.

declarations.name: TwoPaneOrientation
declarations.signature: enum class TwoPaneOrientation
declarations.description: Which way two panes stand: beside each other, or one above the other.

entries.name: SideBySide
entries.description: The first pane at the start, the second at the end: a list and what is chosen in it.

entries.name: Stacked
entries.description: The first pane above, the second below: what is looked at, and the controls under it.

declarations.name: PaneSize
declarations.signature: sealed interface PaneSize
declarations.description: How much of the room the first pane takes, where no fold says where the panes meet. The second pane takes the rest, past the gap.

members.name: Fraction
members.signature: data class Fraction(public val fraction: Float) : PaneSize
members.description: A share of the room the panes have between them, the gap left out: `0.5f` is half each.

parameters.name: fraction
parameters.description: The first pane's share, from 0 to 1.

members.name: Fixed
members.signature: data class Fixed(public val size: Dp) : PaneSize
members.description: A size of its own: a list as wide as 360dp, whatever the window. A room smaller than it and the gap gives the first pane all there is.

parameters.name: size
parameters.description: The first pane's width beside the second, or its height above it.

declarations.name: PantrixTwoPane
declarations.signature:
@Composable
fun PantrixTwoPane(
    first: @Composable () -> Unit,
    second: @Composable () -> Unit,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    orientation: TwoPaneOrientation = TwoPaneOrientation.SideBySide,
    firstSize: PaneSize = PaneSize.Fraction(0.5f),
    gap: Dp = PantrixTheme.layout.gutter,
    tagKey: String? = null
)
declarations.description:
Two panes in one room: beside each other or one above the other, split at the window's fold where one divides the room.

- **Where they meet.** A fold that divides the room the way the panes stand, upright for panes beside each other and lying across for panes one above the other, is where they meet: each pane is on one side of it, and the strip the system asks to keep clear around it, the fold's `clearance`, is the gap. Elsewhere `firstSize` says how much the first pane takes and `gap` stands between them.

- **Which fold.** The fold is the window's where it crosses this room, so a pair of panes in part of a window splits at the fold only where the fold runs through it. A foldable held like a book splits panes beside each other; one on a table, panes one above the other.

- **Reading direction.** Beside each other, the first pane is at the start: on the right where the language is read from right to left. A fold stays where it is on the screen, and the first pane is on its start side.

- **Room.** The panes take the whole room across: beside each other, as tall as the room, or as tall as the taller of them where the room's height is not bounded. Along the split the room is to be bounded.

- **Both, always.** The two panes are always shown. A layout that shows one where there is no room for two asks the window first: `PantrixTheme.window.paneCount()`.

- **Automation.** The pair is tagged `TwoPane_<tagKey>`.

parameters.name: first
parameters.description: the first pane: at the start beside the second, or above it.

parameters.name: second
parameters.description: the second pane.

parameters.name: modifier
parameters.description: the room the two panes have.

parameters.name: orientation
parameters.description: which way the panes stand.

parameters.name: firstSize
parameters.description: how much the first pane takes where no fold divides the room: half by default.

parameters.name: gap
parameters.description: the room between the panes where no fold divides it: the layout's gutter by default.

parameters.name: tagKey
parameters.description: the key of the pair's automation tag.

declarations.name: PantrixCarousel
declarations.signature:
@Composable
fun PantrixCarousel(
    pageCount: Int,
    currentPage: Int,
    onPageChange: (page: Int) -> Unit,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    contentDescription: String? = null,
    swipeEnabled: Boolean = true,
    loop: Boolean = false,
    autoAdvanceMillis: Int = 0,
    style: CarouselStyle? = null,
    colors: CarouselColors? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null,
    page: @Composable (index: Int) -> Unit
)
declarations.description:
Slides one beside another, one of them on screen: pictures, cards, the steps of an introduction. A swipe turns them; what is under them says where the carousel is, and turns them for a reader with no finger on the screen.

Which slide is on screen is the screen's state: the carousel shows `currentPage` and goes to another when that changes, turning there, or at once where the theme's motion is reduced. A swipe turns the slides by itself and tells `onPageChange` where it ended; a press on a button or a dot, and an arrow key, ask `onPageChange` for a slide and turn nothing by themselves. A caller that keeps a slide the reader swiped away from is asked once, and the carousel stays where the reader left it until `currentPage` changes. The carousel keeps no slide of its own beyond that: one that comes back to the screen is on `currentPage`.

Under the slides a dot stands for each of them; a style counts the slides instead, or shows nothing. With a pointer, a press on a dot asks for its slide. Under a finger a dot is too small a thing to touch, and the dots are one thing to press, as large as the platform's touch target: a press before their middle asks for the slide before, and one after it for the slide after. Where the reader has no touch, two buttons turn the slides back and on: a press while the carousel is turning goes on from the slide it is heading for, so two quick presses turn two slides. The slides take the keyboard's focus as one stop: the arrow keys turn them, mirrored where the reading runs from the right, and Home and End go to the first and the last. A button at the end it turns to cannot be pressed, and the focus it had goes to the slides; so does the focus of what is in a slide that an arrow turns away. Of what is in the slides, Tab stops at what is in the one on screen alone.

With `loop` the slides go round: the last goes on to the first and the first back to the last, by a swipe, a button or an arrow, and neither button is ever at an end.

With `autoAdvanceMillis` the carousel turns by itself: so long after it came to a slide, it asks `onPageChange` for the slide after, and for the first after the last. It waits while the reader holds a slide, while a pointer is over the carousel and while the keyboard's focus is in it. Beside the dots it has a button that stops it and lets it turn again, and that button is the reader's last word: stopped, the carousel turns only when it is turned, and let to turn again it does so with the focus on that button. Where the theme's motion is reduced the carousel does not turn by itself at all, and has no such button.

A screen reader is told the carousel's name, where it is given one, and where the carousel is whenever that changes, as "Slide 2 of 5" in the theme's language; a carousel that is turning by itself does not break in at every turn, and where it is can be read when the reader asks. On iOS the carousel is a group without a name: a screen reader there reads a group's own name after what the group holds.

The slides are as tall as the carousel is told to be, less what is under them, and a slide lower than that stands at their top. Told nothing, as on a page that scrolls, the carousel is as tall as the slide on screen, and on the way from a slide to a taller or a lower one as tall as the way between the two is far gone. A slide is as wide as the carousel, less the style's `peek` at each side. A style puts the dots and the buttons over the slides instead, as on a gallery of pictures, where they take no room of their own.

parameters.name: pageCount
parameters.description: how many slides there are.

parameters.name: currentPage
parameters.description: the slide on screen, counted from zero, as a pager's is. One past either end is the nearest slide. A `PantrixPagination` counts its pages from one, as it writes them: its page is this and one.

parameters.name: onPageChange
parameters.description: told the slide a swipe ended on, and the slide a button, a dot or a key asks for, or the carousel itself when it turns by itself.

parameters.name: modifier
parameters.description: applied to the carousel: the slides and what is under them.

parameters.name: contentDescription
parameters.description: what the carousel holds, for a screen reader: "Featured products".

parameters.name: swipeEnabled
parameters.description: whether a swipe turns the slides. An introduction that goes on by its own button turns it off.

parameters.name: loop
parameters.description: whether the slides go round, the last on to the first. A carousel of one slide has nowhere to go.

parameters.name: autoAdvanceMillis
parameters.description: how long the carousel stays on a slide before it turns to the next by itself, or 0, the default, for a carousel that is turned by its reader alone. Long enough to read a slide in: five seconds or more.

parameters.name: style
parameters.description: this call's own style: over every enclosing one and under the density. Only the fields it sets change, on every platform.

parameters.name: colors
parameters.description: this call's own colours for what is under the slides. Only the ones it sets change.

parameters.name: tagKey
parameters.description: a locale-independent key for automation: the carousel's tag is `Carousel_<tagKey>`, and its parts are named inside it: `Carousel_<tagKey>.Slides_view`, which takes the keyboard's focus, `.Page_<index>`, `.Control_previous`, `.Control_next`, `.Control_pause` and `.Indicator_position`. Where the slides go round and a slide's neighbours show, a carousel of two slides has the same slide at both sides, twice under one tag.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: a slide, by its index.

declarations.name: CarouselIndicator
declarations.signature: enum class CarouselIndicator
declarations.description: What says where a carousel is, under its slides.

entries.name: Dots
entries.description: A dot for each slide, the current one in the brand's colour. A press on a dot asks for its slide. More slides than a row of dots tells at a glance, more than ten, are counted instead, as `Count` counts them.

entries.name: Count
entries.description: The slide's number and how many there are, as `3 / 12`.

entries.name: None
entries.description: Nothing. The slides say where they are themselves, or what the caller puts beside them does.

declarations.name: CarouselControls
declarations.signature: enum class CarouselControls
declarations.description: Where a carousel shows its two buttons, which turn it back a slide and on a slide.

entries.name: Always
entries.description: On every platform.

entries.name: WithoutTouch
entries.description: Where the platform is not used by touch, as `PantrixTheme.platform.isTouch` says: with a mouse, which has no swipe, the buttons are how the slides are turned. It goes by the pointer the screen is used with and not by what the screen can do: a laptop with a touch screen shows them.

entries.name: Never
entries.description: Nowhere: the slides are turned by a swipe, by the arrow keys, and by what the caller puts beside them.

declarations.name: CarouselPlacement
declarations.signature: enum class CarouselPlacement
declarations.description: Where what says where a carousel is, and its buttons, stand.

entries.name: Below
entries.description: Under the slides, in a row of their own.

entries.name: Overlaid
entries.description: Over the slides, as on a gallery of pictures: the two buttons at the slides' sides, half way up, and what says where the carousel is at their foot. Each stands on a fill of the carousel's own, so that it reads on whatever the slide shows, and takes no room of its own: the carousel is as tall as its slides.

declarations.name: CarouselStyle
declarations.description: `PantrixCarousel`'s geometry and what it shows under its slides. It is the same on every platform: the buttons come and go with the pointer the reader has, not with the platform. The rooms follow the density; a dot does not.

parameters.name: pageSpacing
parameters.description: Between two slides, seen while one gives way to the next and beside a slide whose neighbours `peek`.

parameters.name: peek
parameters.description: How much room is kept at each side of the current slide, in which its neighbours show.

parameters.name: indicatorSize
parameters.description: A dot of the indicator.

parameters.name: indicatorGap
parameters.description: Between two dots.

parameters.name: indicatorSpacing
parameters.description: Between the slides and what is under them. Where that stands over the slides, between it and the slides' edges.

parameters.name: indicator
parameters.description: What says where the carousel is.

parameters.name: controls
parameters.description: Where the two buttons are shown.

parameters.name: placement
parameters.description: Whether those stand under the slides or over them.

declarations.name: CarouselColors
declarations.description:
What a `PantrixCarousel` is painted with under its slides, for a carousel that does not take the theme's colours: a colour that is set is used, and one that is left out stays the theme's. The slides are the caller's own.

```
PantrixCarousel(…, colors = CarouselColors(indicator = PantrixTheme.colors.success.color))
```

A carousel has no fill of its own and stands on what is behind it. On a fill, which says what is written on it, the current dot and the buttons are written in that, and the other dots in a share of it: the brand's colour and the theme's border are colours for the theme's own grounds. So is the theme's disabled colour: a button at the end it would turn past is drawn in that on the theme's grounds, and in a share of the buttons' colour on a fill and where the buttons are given a colour.

Over the slides, where a style puts them, the dots and the buttons do have a fill of their own, `overlay`, and are written in what reads on it, as on any other fill.

parameters.name: indicator
parameters.description: The dot of the current slide. The primary role's `color`.

parameters.name: indicatorTrack
parameters.description: The dots of the other slides. The theme's `borderStrong`, which is told from a ground as a control's own mark is.

parameters.name: control
parameters.description: The buttons. The theme's `onSurface`, an icon's colour.

parameters.name: overlay
parameters.description: The fill behind the dots and behind each button where they stand over the slides. The theme's `onSurface`, the tone opposite the theme's grounds, thinned so that the slide shows through it. One of the theme's role colours given here brings the colour the theme pairs with it for what is written on it.

declarations.id: com.pantrixui.components.data.codeblock.PantrixCodeBlock(String, Modifier, List<CodeToken>, String?, String?, ImageVector?, Boolean, Int, Boolean, Boolean, Boolean, ((copied: Boolean) -> Unit)?, (@Composable () -> Unit)?, CodeBlockStyle?, CodeBlockColors?, String?, (@Composable RowScope.() -> Unit)?, TextStyle?)
declarations.name: PantrixCodeBlock
declarations.signature:
@Composable
fun PantrixCodeBlock(
    code: String,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    tokens: List<CodeToken> = emptyList(),
    title: String? = null,
    language: String? = null,
    icon: ImageVector? = null,
    lineNumbers: Boolean = false,
    firstLineNumber: Int = 1,
    softWrap: Boolean = false,
    selectable: Boolean = true,
    copyable: Boolean = true,
    onCopy: ((copied: Boolean) -> Unit)? = null,
    trailing: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null,
    style: CodeBlockStyle? = null,
    colors: CodeBlockColors? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null,
    leading: (@Composable RowScope.() -> Unit)? = null,
    textStyle: TextStyle? = null
)
declarations.description:
Code set out to be read: in the theme's code type, a line to a line, each run of it in the colour of what it is, and ready to be copied.

The block does not know the language it shows. What colours the code are the `tokens` its caller gives: the runs of the text and what each is, as whatever read the code found them. Code given none is written in one colour.

A header stands over the code while there is something to say in it: a `title`, which is a file's name most often, the `language`, an `icon`, what the screen puts in `trailing`. The button that copies stands at its end; a block that has nothing else to put there has no header, and the button stands in a strip of its own over the code. That button copies all of the code, whatever part of it is on the screen, and shows a tick for a moment after. What is on the screen can be selected too, and copied a part at a time.

A line too long for the block is not broken: the code scrolls sideways, under line numbers that stay where they are. A line of code broken where the room ends loses what its indent says. With `softWrap` a line goes on under itself all the same, for a narrow screen where the words matter more than the columns.

The block fills the width it is given. Given a height, it scrolls inside it under a header that stays, and only the lines on the screen are built. With no height, in a page that scrolls, it is as tall as its lines where it has no more than three hundred; longer code is no taller there than the window, and scrolls in it. Where it scrolls, a bar at its edge shows how far, and a mouse can drag it.

Where a pointer leads and there is something to scroll, the lines are a stop for Tab: with the focus on them the arrow keys scroll by a line and, sideways, by a step; Page Up and Page Down by a screen of lines; Home and End go to the first line and to the last. A screen reader reads the code a line at a time, and passes the line numbers.

Code is written from left to right in every language, and so are its lines here. The header is laid out as the app is.

```
PantrixCodeBlock(code = snippet, language = "Kotlin", tagKey = "usage")
```

parameters.name: code
parameters.description: the code. Its lines end at a line feed, at a carriage return, or at the two together, and the break that ends the text starts no line.

parameters.name: modifier
parameters.description: the block's modifier. A height given here is the room the code scrolls in.

parameters.name: tokens
parameters.description: the runs of `code` that have a colour, placed by the letters of the whole text. None by default.

parameters.name: title
parameters.description: what the header says first: a file's name, or what the code is. A title too long for the header is cut short.

parameters.name: language
parameters.description: the language's name, written after the title in the header, as it is to be read: `Kotlin`, `TS`. The block keeps no list of languages.

parameters.name: icon
parameters.description: an icon before the title.

parameters.name: lineNumbers
parameters.description: whether each line carries its number before the code.

parameters.name: firstLineNumber
parameters.description: the number of the first line. A part taken out of a file starts where it started there.

parameters.name: softWrap
parameters.description: whether a line too long for the block goes on under itself. By default no line does, and the code scrolls sideways.

parameters.name: selectable
parameters.description: whether the code can be selected, by a pointer drawn over it or a finger held on it, and copied by the system's own means. What is copied so is what the lines on the screen show, without their numbers and without what is said about them. Code that scrolls in its own height has built the lines on its screen and no others, and "select all" there selects those. The button copies all of it.

parameters.name: copyable
parameters.description: whether the block has the button that copies the code.

parameters.name: onCopy
parameters.description: called after that button was pressed, with whether the code got to the clipboard: a screen that says so in its own way listens here. The button itself shows a tick for a moment and tells a screen reader, unless the system shows every copy itself (`PantrixClipboard.traits`): there nothing more is needed.

parameters.name: trailing
parameters.description: what the screen puts at the header's end, before the button that copies: a count, a button of its own. It is drawn in the block's text colour.

parameters.name: style
parameters.description: this call's own style: over every enclosing one and under the density. Only the fields it sets change, on every platform.

parameters.name: colors
parameters.description: this block's own colours, where they are not the theme's: the ones set here, with the theme's for the rest.

parameters.name: tagKey
parameters.description: the block's automation key: the block is `CodeBlock_<tagKey>`, a line of it `CodeBlock_<tagKey>.Line_<number>`, the message under a line `CodeBlock_<tagKey>.Note_<number>`, the lines' window where a keyboard scrolls it `CodeBlock_<tagKey>.Lines_window`, and the button that copies `CodeBlock_<tagKey>.Button_copy`. A press on that button is reported as a `CodeBlock` `copy` event with whether the code got there. Nothing of the code is reported.

parameters.name: leading
parameters.description: what the screen puts at the header's start, before the icon and the title, written in the header's colour: the tabs of one file in two forms, as a page of documentation shows a setup for two repositories.

parameters.name: textStyle
parameters.description: what the code is set in: the theme's `code` where it is not given, a smaller one on a phone's page.

declarations.id: com.pantrixui.components.data.codeblock.PantrixCodeBlock(List<CodeLine>, Modifier, String?, String?, ImageVector?, Boolean, Int, Boolean, Boolean, Boolean, ((copied: Boolean) -> Unit)?, (@Composable () -> Unit)?, CodeBlockStyle?, CodeBlockColors?, String?, (@Composable RowScope.() -> Unit)?, TextStyle?)
declarations.name: PantrixCodeBlock
declarations.signature:
@Composable
fun PantrixCodeBlock(
    lines: List<CodeLine>,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    title: String? = null,
    language: String? = null,
    icon: ImageVector? = null,
    lineNumbers: Boolean = false,
    firstLineNumber: Int = 1,
    softWrap: Boolean = false,
    selectable: Boolean = true,
    copyable: Boolean = true,
    onCopy: ((copied: Boolean) -> Unit)? = null,
    trailing: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null,
    style: CodeBlockStyle? = null,
    colors: CodeBlockColors? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null,
    leading: (@Composable RowScope.() -> Unit)? = null,
    textStyle: TextStyle? = null
)
declarations.description:
`PantrixCodeBlock` given its lines one by one, each with what is said about it: a band behind a line that is to be looked at, the lines that were added and taken out, a finding with its message under the line it is about.

`codeLines` makes the lines of a text, to be marked from there.

```
val lines = remember(source, finding) {
    codeLines(source).mapIndexed { index, line ->
        if (index == finding.line) line.copy(mark = CodeMark(CodeTone.Danger, message = finding.message)) else line
    }
}
PantrixCodeBlock(lines = lines, title = "AuthRepository.kt", lineNumbers = true, tagKey = "review")
```

A line with a mark is drawn on the soft fill of its tone's role, and written in the one colour the theme pairs with that fill; a bar in the role's colour runs down its left edge. A mark's message stands under its line, after the tone's icon, in the app's own reading direction, and does not scroll sideways with the code.

parameters.name: lines
parameters.description: the lines, in their order. The button copies their texts, a line to a line.

parameters.name: modifier
parameters.description: the block's modifier. A height given here is the room the code scrolls in.

parameters.name: title
parameters.description: what the header says first: a file's name, or what the code is.

parameters.name: language
parameters.description: the language's name, written after the title in the header, as it is to be read.

parameters.name: icon
parameters.description: an icon before the title.

parameters.name: lineNumbers
parameters.description: whether each line carries its number before the code.

parameters.name: firstLineNumber
parameters.description: the number of the first line. A part taken out of a file starts where it started there.

parameters.name: softWrap
parameters.description: whether a line too long for the block goes on under itself.

parameters.name: selectable
parameters.description: whether the code can be selected and copied by the system's own means.

parameters.name: copyable
parameters.description: whether the block has the button that copies the code.

parameters.name: onCopy
parameters.description: called after that button was pressed, with whether the code got to the clipboard.

parameters.name: trailing
parameters.description: what the screen puts at the header's end, before the button that copies.

parameters.name: style
parameters.description: this call's own style: over every enclosing one and under the density. Only the fields it sets change, on every platform.

parameters.name: colors
parameters.description: this block's own colours, where they are not the theme's: the ones set here, with the theme's for the rest.

parameters.name: tagKey
parameters.description: the block's automation key, as the other overload has it.

parameters.name: leading
parameters.description: what the screen puts at the header's start, before the icon and the title: the tabs of a file in two forms, written in the header's colour.

parameters.name: textStyle
parameters.description: what the code is set in: the theme's `code` where it is not given.

declarations.name: CodeBlockStyle
declarations.description:
`PantrixCodeBlock`'s geometry: the room around its lines, its header, the room before the code where the lines are numbered, and the edge.

The lines stand close, as lines of code do: nothing in them is pressed, and they need no room for a finger. A line of the theme's code type is 20dp tall; Android leaves 2dp over and under its words, iOS 1dp, and the desktop and the web none.

The corners are the card's on each platform: medium on Android, large on iOS, small on desktop and the web.

The paddings, the header's height and the gap follow the density, since they are the room around the words. The icons' size, the widths of the edge and of a mark's bar, and the shape do not.

parameters.name: shape
parameters.description: The corners of the block: a step of the brand's shape scale, or a fixed shape.

parameters.name: horizontalPadding
parameters.description: The room between the block's sides and what it holds: the header's words, the lines, a message under a line. A mark's band is drawn across it, to the sides.

parameters.name: verticalPadding
parameters.description: The room over the first line and under the last, and under a message. A message has half of it over its words.

parameters.name: linePadding
parameters.description: The room over and under the words of each line.

parameters.name: headerHeight
parameters.description: The least the header is tall. It grows with what stands in it. A block that has nothing in its header but the button that copies has no header: the button's strip is as tall as the button.

parameters.name: gutterGap
parameters.description: Between the line numbers and the code, where the lines are numbered.

parameters.name: iconSize
parameters.description: The width and height of the header's icon, of the icon of the button that copies, and of the one before a message.

parameters.name: borderWidth
parameters.description: The width of the edge around the block, and of the line under its header where `headerLineWidth` is not set. Zero draws none.

parameters.name: barWidth
parameters.description: The width of the bar down the left edge of a line with a mark. Zero draws none.

parameters.name: headerLineWidth
parameters.description: The width of the line under the header: `borderWidth` where it is not set, so that a block without an edge can still have its header ruled off. Zero draws none.

parameters.name: headerHorizontalPadding
parameters.description: The room between the block's sides and what its header holds: `horizontalPadding` where it is not set. Tabs at the header's start stand nearer the side than the lines do.

declarations.name: CodeBlockColors
declarations.description:
What a `PantrixCodeBlock` is painted with, for a block that does not take the theme's colours: a colour that is set is used, and one that is left out stays the theme's.

```
// No fill and no edge of its own, in a card that has both:
PantrixCodeBlock(
    code = snippet,
    colors = CodeBlockColors(container = Color.Transparent, border = Color.Transparent)
)
```

On the theme's own grounds each kind of token has a colour of its own, from the theme's roles. On another fill those colours are not known to read. A `container` that is one of the theme's role colours, and a transparent one on a fill that gives what stands on it a colour, write all the code in the one colour that reads there; a fill the theme does not have writes it in the theme's text colour. Each colour given here is used wherever the block stands.

A line with a mark is drawn on the soft fill of its tone's role, and all of it is written in the one colour the theme pairs with that fill, as a toned row of a table is: the colours of the kinds are for the theme's grounds, and are not known to read on a role's fill. A comment is still slanted there.

parameters.name: container
parameters.description: The fill behind the header and the lines: the theme's `surface`. `Color.Transparent` leaves what is behind the block to show.

parameters.name: text
parameters.description: What no token colours, and the header's title. The theme's `textPrimary`.

parameters.name: comment
parameters.description: A comment, which is slanted too. The theme's `textSecondary`.

parameters.name: keyword
parameters.description: A word of the language. The theme's primary role.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: The name of a type. The theme's info role.

parameters.name: string
parameters.description: A string. The theme's success role.

parameters.name: number
parameters.description: A number. The theme's warning role.

parameters.name: punctuation
parameters.description: Brackets, commas and semicolons. The theme's `textSecondary`.

parameters.name: annotation
parameters.description: A name that says something about what follows it. The theme's danger role.

parameters.name: lineNumber
parameters.description: The line numbers, the header's language and its icon, the icon of the button that copies, and the scroll bars. The theme's `textSecondary`.

parameters.name: border
parameters.description: The edge around the block and the line under its header. The theme's `divider` on the theme's own grounds, and on a fill, where that line would not read, a share of what is written there.

declarations.name: CodeTokenKind
declarations.signature: enum class CodeTokenKind
declarations.description:
What a run of code is, which is what it is coloured by.

There are as many kinds as the theme has colours to tell them apart with: a kind that could only be drawn as its neighbour is would say that two different things are one. A reader of a language that knows more folds the rest in: an operator is `Punctuation`, a property is `Plain`, an escape inside a string is a part of the `StringLiteral`.

entries.name: Plain
entries.description: What no other kind claims: names, the room between words. A token of it takes a colour off what is under it.

entries.name: Comment
entries.description: A comment. It is slanted as well as coloured.

entries.name: Keyword
entries.description: A word of the language: `fun`, `val`, `return`.

entries.name: Type
entries.description: The name of a type.

entries.name: StringLiteral
entries.description: A string or a character, with its quotes.

entries.name: Number
entries.description: A number.

entries.name: Punctuation
entries.description: Brackets, commas, semicolons: what holds the code together and says nothing itself.

entries.name: Annotation
entries.description: A name that says something about what follows it: `@Composable`, `@Override`, a decorator, an attribute.

declarations.name: CodeToken
declarations.description:
One coloured run of a text of code: the letters from `start` up to `end`, and what they are.

Its place counts the letters of the text it is given with: of the whole text for `codeLines`, which then cuts a run that goes over several lines into one for each, and of the line itself for a `CodeLine`. Where two runs lie over the same letters the later one colours them. What reaches past the text's end is cut there, and a run that holds nothing colours nothing.

parameters.name: start
parameters.description: The place of the run's first letter, counted from nought.

parameters.name: end
parameters.description: The place after its last letter.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: What the run is.

declarations.name: CodeTone
declarations.signature: enum class CodeTone
declarations.description:
What a mark on a line of code means: the role of the theme its band and its bar are drawn in.

A tint says nothing to someone who cannot see it. What a mark means stands in its message, as words.

entries.name: Primary
entries.description: The brand's colour: the line someone was sent to, the one a step of a guide is about.

entries.name: Info
entries.description: Something worth knowing that is neither good nor bad.

entries.name: Success
entries.description: Something that is well: a line that was added, a check that passed.

entries.name: Warning
entries.description: Something to look at before it becomes a problem.

entries.name: Danger
entries.description: Something that is wrong: a finding, a failure, a line that was taken out.

entries.name: Neutral
entries.description: Set apart without a judgement in it.

declarations.name: CodeMark
declarations.description:
What is said about a line of code: a band behind the line in the soft fill of the `tone`'s role, a bar down its left edge in the role's colour and, with a `message`, the message under the line.

```
// The line someone was sent to:
CodeMark(CodeTone.Primary)
// A finding, with what reported it:
CodeMark(CodeTone.Danger, message = "This may be null here.", source = "kotlin:S2259")
```

parameters.name: tone
parameters.description: What the mark means.

parameters.name: message

declarations.name: PantrixDataTable
declarations.signature:
@Composable
fun <T> PantrixDataTable(
    rows: List<T>,
    columns: List<DataTableColumn<T>>,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    rowKey: ((row: T) -> String)? = null,
    rowLabel: ((row: T) -> String)? = null,
    rowEnabled: ((row: T) -> Boolean)? = null,
    rowTone: ((row: T) -> DataTableTone?)? = null,
    sort: List<DataTableSort> = emptyList(),
    onSortChange: ((List<DataTableSort>) -> Unit)? = null,
    multiSort: Boolean = false,
    selected: Set<String> = emptySet(),
    onSelectionChange: ((Set<String>) -> Unit)? = null,
    selection: DataTableSelection = DataTableSelection.Multiple,
    expanded: Set<String> = emptySet(),
    onExpandedChange: ((Set<String>) -> Unit)? = null,
    expansion: DataTableExpansion = DataTableExpansion.Multiple,
    rowDetail: (@Composable (row: T) -> Unit)? = null,
    onRowClick: ((row: T) -> Unit)? = null,
    loading: Boolean = false,
    loadingRows: Int = 5,
    empty: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null,
    toolbar: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null,
    footer: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null,
    listContent: (@Composable (row: T) -> Unit)? = null,
    variant: DataTableVariant = DataTableVariant.Plain,
    striped: Boolean = false,
    layout: DataTableLayout = DataTableLayout.Auto,
    headerTextStyle: TextStyle = PantrixTheme.typography.label.copy(fontWeight = FontWeight.SemiBold),
    state: DataTableState = rememberDataTableState(),
    style: DataTableStyle? = null,
    colors: DataTableColors? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null
)
declarations.description:
Rows of records in columns: a header that orders them, boxes that choose them, rows that open, columns that stay in place while the others scroll, and a list of records where there is no room for a table.

```
var sort by remember { mutableStateOf(listOf(DataTableSort("total", descending = true))) }
var chosen by remember { mutableStateOf(emptySet<String>()) }
val columns = remember {
    listOf(
        DataTableColumn.text<Order>(key = "customer", header = customer, sortable = true) { it.customer },
        DataTableColumn.text(key = "total", header = total, alignment = Alignment.End, sortable = true) { it.total }
    )
}
PantrixDataTable(
    rows = remember(orders, sort) { orders.sortedWith(sort.comparator(columns)) },
    columns = columns,
    rowKey = { it.id },
    sort = sort,
    onSortChange = { sort = it },
    selected = chosen,
    onSelectionChange = { chosen = it },
    tagKey = "orders"
)
```

**The rows are the caller's.** The table shows `rows` in the order they are given and changes nothing by itself: a press on a header asks for an order with `onSortChange`, a box for a choice with `onSelectionChange`, a chevron for a row to be opened with `onExpandedChange`. That is what lets one table show rows a screen holds and orders itself, with comparator, and rows a server orders and sends a page at a time. The rows given are the page: the box in the header chooses those, and keeps what was chosen on other pages.

**Columns.** A `DataTableColumn` says how wide it is, or shares what is left. Where the columns do not fit at their least widths the table scrolls sideways: by a drag, by a wheel, by the bar under the rows where a pointer leads, and by the keyboard, which brings the cell with the focus into view. A column pinned to an edge stays there while the others pass under it. The end of a resizable column's header is dragged with a pointer, and moved with the arrow keys once Tab has come to it. Which columns there are, and in which order, is the list itself: a screen that lets its reader hide a column or move one gives the table another list.

**Height.** A table told no height is as tall as its rows and builds them all: that is for a page of rows, in a screen that scrolls, and its header goes up with the page as the rows do. A table told a height keeps its header in place, scrolls its rows under it and builds only the ones in view, so that it holds thousands: a table whose header is to stay is told a height. A height it may not pass is a height too: a table laid straight in a window, with nothing around it that scrolls, is no taller than the window, and one that shares a column with other things is given `Modifier.weight`, as a lazy list is.

**State.** Where the rows are scrolled to, how far the columns are and the widths they were dragged to are kept in a `DataTableState`, which a screen holds itself to read them, to keep them and to scroll to a column.

**Narrow.** A table of `DataTableLayout.Auto` narrower than the style's `compactWidth` is a list of records: each row a block, a column's name before each of its values. The boxes, the chevrons and the order stay: the names of the columns that sort stand in a strip over the list, each the button it is in the header. Where the names do not fit, the strip scrolls sideways, fades towards the end it goes on past, and shows the name of the column the records are ordered by. A column that is not in the list has no name there.

**Keyboard and screen readers.** Tab goes through the headers that sort, the boxes, the chevrons, the rows that can be pressed and whatever the cells hold, and the arrow keys move the focus to the nearest of them that way. A cell that holds nothing to press is no stop: this is a table to read and to act on, and not a grid of cells to walk. Where a pointer leads, the rows' window is a stop itself while the table scrolls, so that a table of plain values is scrolled by the keyboard too: by the arrows, Page Up and Page Down, Home and End. A header says that it is one, as a heading, and how its column is ordered; a box says which row it chooses where `rowLabel` names the rows, and a cell which row and column it is in.

parameters.name: rows
parameters.description: the rows, in the order they are shown.

parameters.name: columns
parameters.description: the columns, in the order they are shown. No two of them have one key. Keep the list in a `remember`: a table given its columns anew at every composition lays every row out again.

parameters.name: modifier
parameters.description: the table's modifier. The table is as wide as the room it is given.

parameters.name: rowKey
parameters.description: what tells a row from the others, the same while the row is the same: what `selected` and `expanded` hold, and the row's automation key. Rows that are chosen or opened need one. Without it a row is known by its place.

parameters.name: rowLabel
parameters.description: what a screen reader calls a row by: `Select Ada Lovelace` in place of twenty boxes that all say `Select row`.

parameters.name: rowEnabled
parameters.description: whether a row can be chosen and pressed. One that cannot is drawn fainter, its box is closed, and the box in the header neither chooses it nor lets it go. Its chevron opens it all the same, and what its cells hold stays the caller's to close. A table whose every row is closed is given `{ false }`.

parameters.name: rowTone
parameters.description: what a row means, or null for a row like the others: the row lies on the soft fill of the tone's role, over any stripe, and what it shows is written in the colour the theme pairs with that fill.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: the order the rows are in: the columns it goes by, the first one first. It is drawn in the headers.

parameters.name: onSortChange
parameters.description: called with the order a press on a sortable column's header asks for: smallest first, then largest first, then no order. Null leaves the headers as names.

parameters.name: multiSort
parameters.description: whether a press adds its column to the order, to settle the rows the columns before it hold equal, in place of ordering by that column alone.

parameters.name: selected
parameters.description: the keys of the rows that are chosen.

parameters.name: onSelectionChange
parameters.description: called with the keys that are to be chosen after a box was pressed. Null leaves the table without boxes.

parameters.name: selection
parameters.description: whether many rows are chosen or one.

parameters.name: expanded
parameters.description: the keys of the rows that are open.

parameters.name: onExpandedChange
parameters.description: called with the keys that are to be open after a chevron was pressed. Null leaves the rows without chevrons: the rows named in `expanded` are open all the same.

parameters.name: expansion
parameters.description: whether many rows are open at a time or one. Where it is one, a chevron that opens a row asks for that row alone, and the row that was open closes; the rows named in `expanded` are open as they are given.

parameters.name: rowDetail
parameters.description: what an open row shows under itself, as wide as the table.

parameters.name: onRowClick
parameters.description: called with a row that was pressed. It makes every row a button.

parameters.name: loading
parameters.description: whether the rows are still on their way: blocks stand in their place, in the table's columns.

parameters.name: loadingRows
parameters.description: how many rows of blocks stand there.

parameters.name: empty
parameters.description: what a table without rows shows in their place, in place of the theme's words for it.

parameters.name: toolbar
parameters.description: what stands over the header inside the table's edge: a title, a search field, what is done with the chosen rows.

parameters.name: footer
parameters.description: what stands under the rows inside the table's edge: a `PantrixPagination`, a count.

parameters.name: listContent
parameters.description: what a record of the list shows, in place of its columns' names and values.

parameters.name: variant
parameters.description: how much is drawn around the rows.

parameters.name: striped
parameters.description: whether every other row is laid on a faint fill, to keep the eye on its line.

parameters.name: layout
parameters.description: whether this is a table, a list, or whichever its width has room for.

parameters.name: headerTextStyle
parameters.description: what the columns' names are written in: the control label's type, a little heavier. A table whose headers are small capitals set apart gives that type here, and writes its headers in capitals.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: where the rows and the columns are scrolled to and the widths the columns were dragged to.

parameters.name: style
parameters.description: this call's own style: over every enclosing one and under the density. Only the fields it sets change, on every platform.

parameters.name: colors
parameters.description: this table's own colours, where they are not the theme's: the ones set here, with the theme's for the rest.

parameters.name: tagKey
parameters.description: the table's automation key: the table is `DataTable_<tagKey>`, and in it a header is `Header_<column>`, a row `Row_<row>`, a cell `Cell_<row>/<column>`, a row's box `Select_<row>`, its chevron `Toggle_<row>` and what it opens `Detail_<row>`. A press is reported as a `DataTable` event: `sort`, `select`, `selectAll`, `expand`, `collapse` and `open`.

declarations.name: DataTablePin
declarations.signature: enum class DataTablePin
declarations.description: Where a column of a `PantrixDataTable` stands while the others scroll sideways.

entries.name: None
entries.description: With the others: it scrolls sideways where the columns do not fit the table.

entries.name: Start

declarations.name: DataTableColumn
declarations.description:
One column of a `PantrixDataTable`: its header, how wide it is, and what a row shows in it.

```
DataTableColumn(key = "state", header = stringResource(Res.string.state), width = 120.dp) { order ->
    PantrixBadge(text = order.state.label)
}
```

A column of plain text is written shorter with `DataTableColumn.text`, which cuts a long text with an ellipsis and orders the rows by it.

**Width.** A column given a `width` is that wide. One given none shares what the fixed columns leave, by its `weight`, and is no narrower than `minWidth`. Where the columns do not fit the table at their least widths, they keep those and the table scrolls sideways.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: What tells this column from the others, the same in every language: what a `DataTableSort` names, and the column's automation key. No two columns of a table have one key.

parameters.name: header
parameters.description: The column's name, written once over the rows and before each value in the list a narrow table becomes. It is written as given: a header is a word of a language before it is a style, and the table does not turn it to capitals.

parameters.name: width
parameters.description: A fixed width, or `Dp.Unspecified` for a share of what is left.

parameters.name: weight
parameters.description: This column's share of what the fixed columns leave, where `width` is unspecified.

parameters.name: minWidth
parameters.description: The least width of a column that shares, or `Dp.Unspecified` for the style's `columnMinWidth`.

parameters.name: alignment
parameters.description: Where the header and what a row shows stand in the column. Numbers end at its end, so that their digits line up.

parameters.name: sortable
parameters.description: Whether a press on the header asks for the rows in this column's order. A column with a `comparator` is sortable without it. The header of a column that sorts keeps the place of the order's arrow beside its name, whether the rows are in its order or not: a `width` that just fits the name cuts it.

parameters.name: comparator
parameters.description: How two rows compare by this column, smallest first, for a screen that holds all its rows and orders them itself with comparator. A table whose order is made elsewhere, as by a server, names none.

parameters.name: pin
parameters.description: Whether the column stays at an edge while the others scroll sideways.

parameters.name: resizable
parameters.description: Whether the column's width can be dragged at the end of its header with a pointer. The table keeps the width it was dragged to.

parameters.name: showInList
parameters.description: Whether the column is in the list a narrow table becomes: one of a record's lines, and, where it sorts, one of the names over the list that order it. A column that is there for the table's shape, as a row's actions are, is left out. So is one that a record drawn its own way does not show: it sorts in the table, and the list is not ordered by what it does not show.

parameters.name: tone
parameters.description: What the column's header is tinted with, or null for a header like the others: the soft fill of one of the theme's roles behind the column's name, which is written in the colour the theme pairs with it. It marks the header alone. What the rows show under it is `cell`'s to colour.

parameters.name: cell
parameters.description: What a row shows in this column.
