declarations.name: DataTableSort
declarations.description: Which column the rows of a `PantrixDataTable` are in the order of, and which way round.

parameters.name: columnKey
parameters.description: The `DataTableColumn.key` of the column.

parameters.name: descending
parameters.description: Whether the largest comes first. Smallest first unless set.

declarations.name: comparator
declarations.signature: fun <T> List<DataTableSort>.comparator(columns: List<DataTableColumn<T>>): Comparator<T>
declarations.description:
How two rows compare in this order: by the first column named, and where that says they are equal by the next. Each column compares by its own `DataTableColumn.comparator`, turned round where the order is descending; a column that has none, or that is not among `columns`, says nothing. With no order at all every two rows are equal, and a sort that keeps equal rows as they were, as `sortedWith` does, leaves the list as it is.

```
PantrixDataTable(rows = remember(orders, sort) { orders.sortedWith(sort.comparator(columns)) }, …)
```

declarations.name: DataTableState
declarations.signature: class DataTableState(public val listState: LazyListState = LazyListState())
declarations.description:
What a `PantrixDataTable` holds from one composition to the next, for a screen that reads it, keeps it or changes it: where the rows are scrolled to, how far the columns are scrolled sideways, and the widths the columns were given by a drag.

```
val table = rememberDataTableState()
val scope = rememberCoroutineScope()
PantrixDataTable(rows = orders, columns = columns, state = table)
PantrixButton(text = total, onClick = { scope.launch { table.animateScrollToColumn("total") } })
PantrixButton(text = reset, onClick = { table.columnWidths = emptyMap() })
```

One state is one table's: two tables given the same one would scroll each other's columns.

parameters.name: listState
parameters.description: The state of the list the rows scroll in, where the table is told a height.

members.name: columnWidths
members.signature: var columnWidths: Map<String, Dp> by mutableStateOf(emptyMap())
members.description: The widths columns were given after the table laid them out, by their keys: by a drag at the end of a resizable column's header, by the arrow keys there, or by the screen itself, which may write them. A width kept from the last visit goes in here, and an empty map gives every column back the width the table makes it. A column that is not named is as wide as the table makes it.

members.name: columnScroll
members.description: How far the columns are scrolled from their start, in pixels: nought at rest. Their start is at the right where the table is read from there.

members.name: columnScrollRange
members.description: How far the columns can be scrolled, in pixels: nought while every column fits the table.

members.name: scrollColumnsBy
members.description: Scrolls the columns `pixels` further from their start at once, or back towards it by a negative distance, no further than their two ends. Returns how far they went.

members.name: animateScrollColumnsBy
members.description: Scrolls the columns as `scrollColumnsBy` does, with the motion a wheel's turn has.

parameters.name: pixels
parameters.description: how far the columns scroll, in pixels: further from their start, or back towards it where it is less than nought.

members.name: scrollToColumn
members.description: Brings the column with `columnKey` into view at once, by the shorter way, and no further than it has to go. Nothing happens for a column that is in view already, one that is pinned, or one the table does not have.

members.name: animateScrollToColumn
members.description: Brings the column with `columnKey` into view as `scrollToColumn` does, with a motion.

companion.name: saver
companion.description: Keeps how far the columns are scrolled and the widths they were given, for a state that is to come back as it was: `rememberSaveable(saver = DataTableState.saver(listState)) { DataTableState(listState) }`. Where the rows are is `listState`'s own to keep.

declarations.name: rememberDataTableState
declarations.signature:
@Composable
fun rememberDataTableState(listState: LazyListState = rememberLazyListState()): DataTableState
declarations.description: A `DataTableState` that is kept over what a saved state is kept over: a turn of the screen, a visit to another screen and back.

parameters.name: listState
parameters.description: the state of the list the rows scroll in, for a screen that holds that one itself.

declarations.name: DataTableVariant
declarations.signature: enum class DataTableVariant
declarations.description: How much a `PantrixDataTable` draws around its rows.

entries.name: Plain
entries.description: A line between one row and the next, and nothing around the table: for a table inside a card or on a page.

entries.name: Bordered
entries.description: One edge around the whole table, in the style's shape, with a line between the rows inside it.

entries.name: Grid
entries.description: That edge, and a line between the columns as well: for a dense report the eye reads down as much as along.

declarations.name: DataTableLayout
declarations.signature: enum class DataTableLayout
declarations.description: Whether a `PantrixDataTable` is drawn as a table or as a list of records.

entries.name: Auto
entries.description: A table where there is room for one, and a list where the table itself is narrower than the style's `compactWidth`: what a table of six columns has to become on a phone.

entries.name: Table
entries.description: Always a table, however narrow its place: its columns keep their least widths and scroll sideways.

entries.name: List
entries.description: Always a list: each record a block of its own, a column's header before each of its values.

declarations.name: DataTableSelection
declarations.signature: enum class DataTableSelection
declarations.description: How many rows of a `PantrixDataTable` can be chosen at a time.

entries.name: Multiple
entries.description: Any number of rows, each by a checkbox of its own, and all of them at once by the checkbox in the header.

entries.name: Single
entries.description: One row, by a radio button: choosing another lets the first go.

declarations.name: DataTableExpansion
declarations.signature: enum class DataTableExpansion
declarations.description: How many rows of a `PantrixDataTable` can be open at a time.

entries.name: Multiple
entries.description: Any number of rows: a row stays open until its own chevron closes it.

entries.name: Single
entries.description: One row: opening another closes the one that was open.

declarations.name: DataTableExpander
declarations.signature: enum class DataTableExpander
declarations.description: Where the button that opens a row of a `PantrixDataTable` stands.

entries.name: Start
entries.description: Before the first column, after the box that chooses the row.

entries.name: End
entries.description: After the last column, at the row's end, where a list's row has its chevron. It stays there while the columns scroll.

declarations.name: DataTableTone
declarations.signature: enum class DataTableTone
declarations.description:
What a row of a `PantrixDataTable` means, or the header of a column: drawn as the soft fill of one of the theme's roles, written in the colour the theme pairs with it.

A tint says nothing to someone who cannot see it: what it means stands in the row as words too.

entries.name: Info
entries.description: Something worth knowing that is neither good nor bad.

entries.name: Success
entries.description: Something that worked or is well.

entries.name: Warning
entries.description: Something to look at before it becomes a problem.

entries.name: Danger
entries.description: Something that failed, or is overdue.

entries.name: Neutral
entries.description: Set apart without a judgement in it: a row of totals, a column of another kind.

declarations.name: DataTableStyle
declarations.description:
`PantrixDataTable`'s geometry: how tall a header and a row are at the least, the room a cell has around what it shows, and the edge.

On Android the rows are Material's data table rows, 52dp under a header of 56dp with 16dp at a cell's sides. On iOS there is no table to follow, and a row is a list's row of 44pt, the least a finger is given there. Desktop and the web are tighter, for a pointer: a table read with a mouse shows half as many rows again.

The heights, and the room in a cell, follow the density: a table is where a compact screen earns its name. The sort arrow's size, the line's width, the shape and the widths the layout goes by do not.

parameters.name: shape
parameters.description: The corners of the edge around the table in `DataTableVariant.Bordered` and `DataTableVariant.Grid`: a step of the brand's shape scale, or a fixed shape.

parameters.name: headerMinHeight
parameters.description: The least height of the header. A header's name on two lines makes it taller.

parameters.name: rowMinHeight
parameters.description: The least height of a row. What a cell shows makes its row taller, and a row that holds a control is no lower than the platform's touch target.

parameters.name: cellPadding
parameters.description: The room between a cell's sides and what it shows.

parameters.name: cellVerticalPadding
parameters.description: The room over and under what a cell shows, where that needs more than the least height.

parameters.name: columnMinWidth
parameters.description: The least width of a column that shares the table's width and names no least of its own. The columns keep it where the table is too narrow for them, and the table scrolls sideways.

parameters.name: sortIconSize
parameters.description: The width and height of the arrow beside the header of the column the rows are in the order of.

parameters.name: borderWidth
parameters.description: The width of the lines between the rows and the columns, and of the edge. Zero draws none.

parameters.name: compactWidth
parameters.description: Narrower than this, a table of `DataTableLayout.Auto` is drawn as a list of records.

parameters.name: expander
parameters.description: Where the button that opens a row stands: at the row's end on every platform, as a list's chevron does. Null leaves it as it is.

declarations.name: DataTableColors
declarations.description:
What a `PantrixDataTable` is painted with, for a table that does not take the theme's colours: a colour that is set is used, and one that is left out stays the theme's.

```
// The grey band a report's header usually has, written in what the theme pairs with it.
PantrixDataTable(…, colors = DataTableColors(headerContainer = PantrixTheme.colors.neutral.container))
```

A `container` or a `headerContainer` given here that is one of the theme's role colours brings the colour the theme pairs with it, unless `content` or `headerContent` is given too. A fill no role has does not: what reads on it is the caller's to give.

parameters.name: container
parameters.description: The fill behind the whole table. None unless given: a table stands on what is behind it, a card's surface or a page.

parameters.name: content
parameters.description: What a cell is given for what it shows, where that gives no colour of its own, and what a row's own marks are drawn in: the chevron that opens it, the mark of a pointer over it. The theme's `textPrimary`, or on a fill that is not the table's, the colour that fill gives what stands on it.

parameters.name: headerContainer
parameters.description: The fill behind the header. None unless given.

parameters.name: headerContent
parameters.description: The headers' names and the sort arrow. The theme's `textSecondary` on the theme's own grounds, the colour paired with `headerContainer` where that is a role's, and `content` elsewhere.

parameters.name: stripe
parameters.description: The fill behind every other row of a striped table: a faint share of `content` unless given.

parameters.name: selected
parameters.description: The fill behind a chosen row: a faint share of the theme's `primary` on the theme's own grounds, and of `content` on a fill.

parameters.name: divider
parameters.description: The lines between the rows and the columns, and the edge. The theme's `divider` on the theme's own grounds. On a fill, where that line would not read, a share of `content`: the edge a subtle button has.

declarations.id: com.pantrixui.components.data.jsonview.PantrixJsonView(String, Modifier, Int, String, Boolean, Boolean, Boolean, Boolean, ((copied: Boolean) -> Unit)?, JsonViewStyle?, JsonViewColors?, String?)
declarations.name: PantrixJsonView
declarations.signature:
@Composable
fun PantrixJsonView(
    json: String,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    expandedDepth: Int = Int.MAX_VALUE,
    search: String = "",
    softWrap: Boolean = true,
    lineNumbers: Boolean = false,
    selectable: Boolean = true,
    copyable: Boolean = true,
    onCopy: ((copied: Boolean) -> Unit)? = null,
    style: JsonViewStyle? = null,
    colors: JsonViewColors? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null
)
declarations.description:
A JSON text set out to be read: one value to a line, each level set in from the one that holds it, each kind of value in a colour of its own, and every object and array folding away behind its first line.

What an open document shows is the document: the names and the strings in their quotes, the brackets and the commas, as a pretty-printer writes them. A number is shown as the text wrote it, to its last digit. An object or an array that is folded is one line, its brackets around an ellipsis and, after them, how many things it holds. A thin line runs down from an open one, under its chevron, past everything it holds.

This view keeps what is open by itself: everything down to `expandedDepth` at first, and from then on what its reader folds and unfolds, which stays as the reader left it while the text changes under it and while a search comes and goes. A screen that opens the document from a button of its own, or keeps what was open somewhere, holds that state itself, with the overload that takes `expanded`.

The document is one stop for Tab, as a tree is: the focus comes to the line it was on last, or to the first line on the screen where that one was scrolled away, and the keys walk from there, over the lines a value starts on: the bracket that closes a value says nothing of its own, and is passed. Down and up go to the line after and the line before, Home and End to the first and the last, however far in the document that is. The right arrow unfolds a folded line and, on an open one, goes in to the first thing it holds; the left arrow folds an open line and, on any other, goes out to the line that opened what holds it. A line that folds is a button: a press, Enter and Space fold and unfold it. A screen reader is offered what a press does, is told whether the line is open, and hears its name, how many things a folded one holds and how deep it is, in the theme's words.

`search` marks what it looks for wherever a name or a value has it, opens the values that hold some of it, and brings the first of it on the screen where the view scrolls. `lineNumbers` counts the lines as the open document has them: a folded value keeps the number it opens with, and the line after it goes on from where the folded lines would have ended.

The text can be taken away. A button in the view's corner copies the whole document as an open view writes it, and what is on the screen can be selected and copied a part at a time.

The view fills the width it is given, and a line too long for it goes on under itself; with `softWrap` off no line does, and the document scrolls sideways. Given a height, it scrolls inside it, and only the lines on the screen are built: that is how a document of thousands of lines is shown. With no height, in a page that scrolls, it is as tall as the lines it shows where the document, all open, has no more than three hundred; a longer document is no taller there than the window, and scrolls in it. Where it scrolls, a bar at its edge shows how far, and a mouse can drag it.

A document is written from left to right in every language, as code is. A text that is not JSON is shown as it is, under a line that says where the reading stopped.

```
PantrixJsonView(json = response.body, tagKey = "response")
```

parameters.name: json
parameters.description: the JSON text, as RFC 8259 writes it. It is read again only when it changes: a megabyte takes a phone some tenths of a second.

parameters.name: modifier
parameters.description: the view's modifier. A height given here is the room the document scrolls in.

parameters.name: expandedDepth
parameters.description: how many levels are open at first: `1` shows the text's own value with everything in it folded, `2` opens those too, and every level is open by default. Giving another depth starts again from it.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: what is looked for in the names and the values, in capitals or in small letters. Nothing by default, which marks nothing. It is looked for as it is given, in the lines as they are written: a name and a string in their quotes, and no space taken off its ends. The whole document is looked through each time it changes: for a text of megabytes, give it when the reader stops typing.

parameters.name: softWrap
parameters.description: whether a line too long for the view goes on under itself. False keeps every value on one line and lets the document scroll sideways.

parameters.name: lineNumbers
parameters.description: whether each line carries its number in the open document, before everything else of it.

parameters.name: selectable
parameters.description: whether what the lines say can be selected, by a pointer drawn over it or a finger held on it, and copied by the system's own means. What is copied so is what the lines show, a line to a line: without the room they are set in by, and with a folded value as it is folded. A view that scrolls in its own height has built the lines on its screen and no others, and "select all" there selects those. The button copies the document itself.

parameters.name: copyable
parameters.description: whether the view has the button that copies the document.

parameters.name: onCopy
parameters.description: called after that button was pressed, with whether the document got to the clipboard: a screen that says so in its own way listens here. The button itself shows a tick for a moment and tells a screen reader, unless the system shows every copy itself (`PantrixClipboard.traits`): there nothing more is needed.

parameters.name: style
parameters.description: this call's own style: over every enclosing one and under the density. Only the fields it sets change, on every platform.

parameters.name: colors
parameters.description: this view's own colours, where they are not the theme's: the ones set here, with the theme's for the rest.

parameters.name: tagKey
parameters.description: the view's automation key: the view is `JsonView_<tagKey>`, a line in it `JsonView_<tagKey>.Row_<path>` with the path as it is written (`Row_/user/tags/0`, and `Row_root` for the text's own value), the line that closes an open one `JsonView_<tagKey>.End_<path>`, the line over a text that is not JSON `JsonView_<tagKey>.Note_fault`, and the button that copies `JsonView_<tagKey>.Button_copy`. Only two members of one name share a path, and so a tag. A press is reported as a `JsonView` event: `expand` and `collapse` with the line's level, and `copy` with whether it got there. Nothing of the document is reported.

declarations.id: com.pantrixui.components.data.jsonview.PantrixJsonView(String, Set<String>, (Set<String>) -> Unit, Modifier, String, Boolean, Boolean, Boolean, Boolean, ((copied: Boolean) -> Unit)?, JsonViewStyle?, JsonViewColors?, String?)
declarations.name: PantrixJsonView
declarations.signature:
@Composable
fun PantrixJsonView(
    json: String,
    expanded: Set<String>,
    onExpandedChange: (Set<String>) -> Unit,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    search: String = "",
    softWrap: Boolean = true,
    lineNumbers: Boolean = false,
    selectable: Boolean = true,
    copyable: Boolean = true,
    onCopy: ((copied: Boolean) -> Unit)? = null,
    style: JsonViewStyle? = null,
    colors: JsonViewColors? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null
)
declarations.description:
`PantrixJsonView` with what is open held by the caller, as an accordion's sections are: give `expanded` and act on `onExpandedChange`. That is what lets a screen open everything from a button of its own, unfold the way to a value a search found, or keep what was open across a visit to another screen.

What a `search` finds is marked here too, and a folded value that holds some of it is marked whole; opening it is the caller's to do, with the paths `jsonViewSearchPaths` gives.

```
var open by remember(json) { mutableStateOf(jsonViewPaths(json, depth = 1)) }
PantrixJsonView(json = json, expanded = open, onExpandedChange = { open = it }, tagKey = "settings")
```

parameters.name: json
parameters.description: the JSON text, as RFC 8259 writes it. It is read again only when it changes.

parameters.name: expanded
parameters.description: the paths of the objects and arrays that are open, as `jsonViewPaths` writes them: the empty string for the text's own value, `/user` for its member `user`, `/user/tags/0` for the first of that one's `tags`. A path that leads to nothing that folds changes nothing.

parameters.name: onExpandedChange
parameters.description: called with the paths that are to be open after a line was pressed: `expanded` with the line's path added or taken out. The view changes nothing by itself.

parameters.name: modifier
parameters.description: the view's modifier. A height given here is the room the document scrolls in.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: what is looked for in the names and the values, in capitals or in small letters.

parameters.name: softWrap
parameters.description: whether a line too long for the view goes on under itself.

parameters.name: lineNumbers
parameters.description: whether each line carries its number in the open document.

parameters.name: selectable
parameters.description: whether what the lines say can be selected and copied by the system's own means.

parameters.name: copyable
parameters.description: whether the view has the button that copies the document.

parameters.name: onCopy
parameters.description: called after that button was pressed, with whether the document got to the clipboard.

parameters.name: style
parameters.description: this call's own style: over every enclosing one and under the density. Only the fields it sets change, on every platform.

parameters.name: colors
parameters.description: this view's own colours, where they are not the theme's: the ones set here, with the theme's for the rest.

parameters.name: tagKey
parameters.description: the view's automation key, as the other overload has it.

declarations.name: jsonViewPaths
declarations.signature:
fun jsonViewPaths(
    json: String,
    depth: Int = Int.MAX_VALUE
): Set<String>
declarations.description:
The paths of the objects and arrays of `json` that a `PantrixJsonView` can fold, down to `depth` levels: what its `expanded` is given to open a document so far.

A path is a JSON Pointer (RFC 6901): the names and the places that lead to a value from the text's own, each after a slash. The text's own value is the empty string, its member `user` is `/user`, and the first of that one's `tags` is `/user/tags/0`. A slash in a name is written `~1` and a tilde `~0`. An object or an array that holds nothing has nothing to fold, and its path is not among them.

```
var open by remember(json) { mutableStateOf(jsonViewPaths(json, depth = 1)) }
PantrixJsonView(json = json, expanded = open, onExpandedChange = { open = it })
// Everything open, from a button of the screen's own:
open = jsonViewPaths(json)
```

The text is read each time this is called: keep what it gives while the text is the same, as the `remember` above does.
declarations.returns: the paths, in the order the text writes them.

parameters.name: json
parameters.description: the text. One that is not JSON has no paths.

parameters.name: depth
parameters.description: how many levels are counted: `1` is the text's own value alone, `2` that one and what it holds, and every level by default. Zero and less count none.

declarations.name: jsonViewSearchPaths
declarations.signature:
fun jsonViewSearchPaths(
    json: String,
    search: String,
    language: String = ""
): Set<String>
declarations.description:
The paths of the objects and arrays of `json` that hold something `search` looks for, in a name or in a value, however deep inside them: what a `PantrixJsonView`'s `expanded` is given, or has added to it, to show everything that was found.

```
val found = remember(json, query) { jsonViewSearchPaths(json, query) }
PantrixJsonView(
    json = json,
    expanded = open + found,
    onExpandedChange = { open = it },
    search = query
)
```

The text is read each time this is called: keep what it gives while the text and the search are the same.
declarations.returns: the paths of the values that are to be open, as `jsonViewPaths` writes a path. A value is among them for what is inside it, not for its own name: the line that carries its name is in what holds it.

parameters.name: json
parameters.description: the text. One that is not JSON has no paths.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: what is looked for, in capitals or in small letters. A search of nothing finds nothing.

parameters.name: language
parameters.description: the language whose small letters the search compares, the theme's `locale.language` as the view does: in Turkish and Azerbaijani a dotless ı is I's small letter, so "i" finds "İstanbul" and not "Irmak".

declarations.name: JsonViewStyle
declarations.description:
`PantrixJsonView`'s geometry: the room around its lines, how far a level is set in, and the edge.

The lines are a document's and not a list's rows: they stand close, as lines of code do. Under a finger, on Android, on iOS and on the web, whose browser may be a touch screen's, a line has 4dp over and under its words, which makes it 28dp tall in the theme's code type; on the desktop it has 2dp, for a pointer. A level is set in by two letters of that type on the desktop and on the web, and by a letter and a half on a phone, where a line is short.

The corners are the card's on each platform: medium on Android, large on iOS, small on desktop and the web.

The paddings, the indent and the gap follow the density, since they are the room around the words. The chevron's size, the widths of the edge and of the guides, and the shape do not.

parameters.name: shape
parameters.description: The corners of the view: a step of the brand's shape scale, or a fixed shape.

parameters.name: horizontalPadding
parameters.description: The room between the view's sides and its lines. A pointer's mark and a press are drawn across it, to the sides.

parameters.name: verticalPadding
parameters.description: The room over the first line and under the last.

parameters.name: linePadding
parameters.description: The room over and under the words of each line.

parameters.name: indent
parameters.description: How far each level is set in from the one that holds it. Where lines go on under themselves, a line is set in by no more than half the room it has, however deep it is.

parameters.name: chevronSize
parameters.description: The width and height of the chevron before a line that folds.

parameters.name: chevronGap
parameters.description: Between that chevron and the line's words. Every line leaves the chevron's room, so that the names of one level start under one another.

parameters.name: borderWidth
parameters.description: The width of the edge around the view. Zero draws none.

parameters.name: guideWidth
parameters.description: The width of the lines that run down from an open object or array, under its chevron, past everything it holds: what tells one level from the next where the indent is narrow. Zero draws none.

declarations.name: JsonViewColors
declarations.description:
What a `PantrixJsonView` is painted with, for a view that does not take the theme's colours: a colour that is set is used, and one that is left out stays the theme's.

```
// No fill and no edge of its own, in a card that has both:
PantrixJsonView(
    json = response,
    colors = JsonViewColors(container = Color.Transparent, border = Color.Transparent)
)
```

On the theme's own grounds each kind of value has a colour of its own, from the theme's roles, so that a number is told from a string that holds digits before its quotes are read. On another fill those colours are not known to read. A `container` that is one of the theme's role colours, and a transparent one on a fill that gives what stands on it a colour, write the whole document in the one colour that reads there; a fill the theme does not have writes it in the theme's text colour. Each colour given here is used wherever the view stands.

parameters.name: container
parameters.description: The fill behind the lines: the theme's `surface`. `Color.Transparent` leaves what is behind the view to show.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: A member's name. A pointer's mark and a press on a line that folds are drawn in it too. The theme's `textPrimary`.

parameters.name: string
parameters.description: A string. The theme's success role.

parameters.name: number
parameters.description: A number. The theme's warning role.

parameters.name: literal
parameters.description: `true`, `false` and `null`. The theme's primary role.

parameters.name: punctuation
parameters.description: The brackets, the colons and the commas, the ellipsis of what is folded and how many things it holds, the chevron before a line that folds, and a text that is not JSON. The theme's `textSecondary`.

parameters.name: border
parameters.description: The edge around the view. The theme's `divider` on the theme's own grounds, and on a fill, where that line would not read, a share of what is written there.

parameters.name: guide
parameters.description: The lines that run down from an open object or array. The theme's `divider` on the theme's own grounds, and on a fill a share of what is written there. That is what `border` is too where it is given nothing, but the two are apart: a colour given to `border` does not change the guides.

parameters.name: match
parameters.description: What is laid behind the letters a search found. The theme's warning role softened, written in what the theme pairs with it; on a fill a share of what is written there, under letters that keep their colour. A colour given here that is one of the theme's role colours brings its pair too.

declarations.name: ListItemDivider
declarations.signature: enum class ListItemDivider
declarations.description: The line a `PantrixListItem` draws under itself, which parts it from the row under it.

entries.name: None
entries.description: No line: the rows are parted by their room, or by what the list draws between them.

entries.name: Full
entries.description: A line under the whole row, from one side to the other.

entries.name: Inset
entries.description: A line under the row from where its text starts, past what leads it, as iOS's lists draw theirs: the rows' avatars or icons stand in an unbroken column.

declarations.name: ListItemStyle
declarations.description:
`PantrixListItem`'s geometry and type: how tall a row of one, two and three lines is at the least, the room around and between what it holds, the corners of its fill and the types it writes in.

Each platform has its own list: Material 3's rows on Android (56, 72 and 88dp, 16dp in from the sides, the title in the body type), iOS's on iOS (44, 60 and 76), and denser rows where a pointer leads, 36, 52 and 68 on the desktop and 40, 56 and 72 on the web, their titles in the label type. A row is taller where what it holds needs more, as a larger type does. A fill on a phone runs to the row's edges; on the desktop and the web it has round corners.

The heights and the room follow the density. The corners, the chevron and the types do not.

parameters.name: oneLineHeight
parameters.description: The least height of a row of its title alone.

parameters.name: twoLineHeight
parameters.description: The least height of a row of a title and one other line: an overline or a supporting text.

parameters.name: threeLineHeight
parameters.description: The least height of a row of a title, an overline and a supporting text.

parameters.name: horizontalPadding
parameters.description: The room between the row's sides and what it holds.

parameters.name: verticalPadding
parameters.description: The room over and under what the row holds, where it is taller than the least height.

parameters.name: gap
parameters.description: The room between what leads the row, its text and what ends it.

parameters.name: shape
parameters.description: The corners of the row's fill: none on Android and iOS, small on the desktop and the web.

parameters.name: chevronSize
parameters.description: The width and height of the chevron at the end of a row that leads on.

parameters.name: headlineRole
parameters.description: The type the title is set in: the body on Android and iOS, the label on the desktop and the web.

parameters.name: supportingRole
parameters.description: The type the supporting text and the trailing text are set in: the label on Android and iOS, the footnote on the desktop and the web.

declarations.name: ListItemColors
declarations.description:
What a `PantrixListItem` is painted with, where it is not the theme's: a colour that is set is used, and one that is left out stays the theme's.

```
PantrixListItem(
    headline = message.from,
    supportingText = message.subject,
    selected = message.id == open,
    onClick = { open = message.id },
    colors = ListItemColors(selectedContainer = brand.container, selectedContent = brand.onContainer)
)
```

A row has no fill of its own unless `container` is given: it stands on what holds it, and is written in what is written there, the theme's text on the theme's grounds and the colour a fill around it gives on one.

parameters.name: container
parameters.description: The row's own fill: none, by default.

parameters.name: content
parameters.description: The title and the trailing text: the theme's primary text on its grounds, what reads on a fill.

parameters.name: supportingContent
parameters.description: The overline, the supporting text and the chevron: the theme's secondary text on its grounds, and on a fill `content`.

parameters.name: selectedContainer
parameters.description: The fill of a selected row: the primary role's `container`.

parameters.name: selectedContent
parameters.description: What a selected row is written in: what the theme pairs with `selectedContainer`.

parameters.name: divider
parameters.description: The line under a row that draws one: the theme's divider on its grounds, a share of `content` on a fill.

declarations.name: PantrixPageJump
declarations.signature:
@Composable
fun PantrixPageJump(
    pageCount: Int,
    onPageChange: (page: Int) -> Unit,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    label: String = PantrixTheme.strings.goToPage,
    enabled: Boolean = true,
    tagKey: String? = null
)
declarations.description:
Goes to a page of a long list by its number: the words "Go to page" and, beside them, a short field the number is typed in.

It stands beside a `PantrixPagination` in a table's foot, for a list of more pages than a reader steps through. Enter, or the action of a keyboard on the screen, asks for the page that was typed, with `onPageChange`, and empties the field for the next number. The field keeps the focus, so that a second page is typed without another press. A number that is no page's is taken as the nearest page: nought is the first page, and a number past the last is the last. An empty field asks for nothing.

The field takes digits alone: the Western ones and the ones the theme's language writes its numbers with. A sign that is neither is dropped as it is typed, and out of a text that is pasted. It takes no more digits than the last page's number has, so a number is never longer than the field: typing stops there, and a number pasted with more digits is not put in, as a text field turns down a paste that does not fit. On a phone it brings up a keyboard of numbers whose action is "go" (`numberKeyboardOptions`): on an iPhone the one of numbers and punctuation, since the number pad there has no key for an action.

The field is as wide as the last page's number needs, in the widest of the digits, and a digit more: a few digits, and not a text field's width. It is no narrower than the platform's touch target, or than it is tall. The words stand before it, where the row starts: at the right in a language that is read from the right. They are for the eye. A screen reader is given one control, the field, which is named by the words. The row is one line, as tall as the field. In a place wider than itself it starts where the place does. In one too narrow for it the words give way and the field does not.

parameters.name: pageCount
parameters.description: how many pages there are: the last page a number is taken as, and how many digits the field holds. A count under one is taken as one, as `PantrixPagination` takes it.

parameters.name: onPageChange
parameters.description: told the page that was asked for, by its number, counted from one.

parameters.name: modifier
parameters.description: applied to the row.

parameters.name: label
parameters.description: the words before the field, and the field's name for a screen reader: the theme's "Go to page" unless given.

parameters.name: enabled
parameters.description: whether a number can be typed: a row that cannot be used has its words in the disabled text colour and a field that is disabled, which takes no focus and says so.

parameters.name: tagKey
parameters.description: a locale-independent key for automation: the row's tag is `PageJump_<tagKey>` and its words are `PageJump_<tagKey>.Text_label`. The field in it has the key `<tagKey>_page_jump`, and is tagged as a text field is: `TextField_<tagKey>_page_jump`. A key too long for a tag is cut, and `_page_jump` is kept whole. A page that is asked for is reported as `PageJump`, with the page and never with what was typed. That the field took the focus is reported as `PageJump` too, with the row's tag: the row is one component, and reports under one name.

declarations.name: DefaultPageSizes
declarations.signature: val DefaultPageSizes: List<Int>
declarations.description: The sizes a `PantrixPageSize` offers where it is given none of its own: ten, twenty-five, fifty and a hundred rows to a page.

declarations.name: PantrixPageSize
declarations.signature:
@Composable
fun PantrixPageSize(
    pageSize: Int,
    onPageSizeChange: (pageSize: Int) -> Unit,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    pageSizes: List<Int> = DefaultPageSizes,
    label: String = PantrixTheme.strings.perPage,
    enabled: Boolean = true,
    tagKey: String? = null
)
declarations.description:
Chooses how many rows a page of a list shows: the words "Per page" and, beside them, a select of sizes.

It stands beside a `PantrixPagination` in a table's foot. What is chosen is its caller's and not the control's: it is given `pageSize` and asks for another with `onPageSizeChange`. Choosing the size that is chosen already asks for nothing. A `pageSize` that is none of `pageSizes`, as one kept from an earlier visit may be, is shown as the choice all the same, and is listed with the sizes, before the first of them that is larger.

The sizes are written in the digits of the theme's language. The words stand before the select, where the row starts: at the right in a language that is read from the right. They are for the eye. A screen reader is given one control, the select, which is named by the words, and not a text and after it a control without a name.

The select is as wide as the longest of its sizes needs, in its box and in the rows of its list, so that the row stands still as the choice changes and no size is cut in the list. The row is one line, as tall as the select, and as wide as its words and its select. In a place wider than itself it starts where the place does. In one too narrow for it the words give way and the select does not.

parameters.name: pageSize
parameters.description: how many rows a page shows now.

parameters.name: onPageSizeChange
parameters.description: told the size that was chosen, where it is another than `pageSize`. The select shows it once `pageSize` says so.

parameters.name: modifier
parameters.description: applied to the row.

parameters.name: pageSizes
parameters.description: the sizes to choose from, in the order they are listed: `DefaultPageSizes` unless given. A size given twice is listed once. There is one at the least, and each is a row or more: a list that is empty or holds a number under one is refused.

parameters.name: label
parameters.description: the words before the select, and the select's name for a screen reader: the theme's "Per page" unless given.

parameters.name: enabled
parameters.description: whether a size can be chosen: a row that cannot be used has its words in the disabled text colour and a select that is disabled, which takes no focus and says so.

parameters.name: tagKey
parameters.description: a locale-independent key for automation: the row's tag is `PageSize_<tagKey>` and its words are `PageSize_<tagKey>.Text_label`. The select in it has the key `<tagKey>_page_size`, and is tagged as a select is: `Select_<tagKey>_page_size`, its list `SelectList_<tagKey>_page_size`, and a size in the list `Select_<tagKey>_page_size.SelectOption_<size>`. A key too long for a tag is cut, and `_page_size` is kept whole. A choice is reported as `PageSize`, with the size. That the list of sizes opened is reported as `PageSize` too, with the row's tag: the row is one component, and reports under one name.

declarations.name: PantrixPagination
declarations.signature:
@Composable
fun PantrixPagination(
    page: Int,
    pageCount: Int,
    onPageChange: (page: Int) -> Unit,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    siblingCount: Int = 1,
    boundaryCount: Int = 1,
    firstAndLast: Boolean = false,
    enabled: Boolean = true,
    textStyle: TextStyle = PantrixTheme.typography.label,
    style: PaginationStyle? = null,
    colors: PaginationColors? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null
)
declarations.description:
Moves between the pages of a long list or a table.

A row of numbers has previous, the first and the last `boundaryCount` pages, `siblingCount` pages on each side of the page on screen with the pages between folded into gaps, and next. It has as many items whichever page is on screen, each in the same room, so the row stands still as the page moves; only a number of three digits or more makes its own item wider.

The row fits itself to the room it is given, and not to the platform or the window. Where the numbers do not fit as they are asked for, it shows fewer pages beside the page on screen, as many as fit, and then fewer at its ends, down to one. Where no row of numbers fits it is laid out as previous, "Page 3 of 10" and next: the same row on a phone held upright and in a table's narrow foot, and the row of numbers again where there is room. The room is asked for the row as it is on its widest page, so the row is the same on every page. `PaginationStyle.layout` asks for the short row everywhere: a theme that gives it to its phones has what a row laid out by the platform has. In a place narrower than its buttons the short row is drawn smaller, and keeps both whole.

A page's number is a button a screen reader calls by what it opens, "Page 4". The page on screen is no button and offers no press: it is said to be the current page. It keeps the focus a keyboard put on it, and is a stop for Tab, so that the row is entered where it is. A button that has taken the row to its end can no longer be pressed, and gives its focus to the page on screen, or to a button of the other side in the short row. A row that stops being `enabled` while a keyboard is on one of its items leaves the focus there, on an item that does nothing, until the row can be pressed again. The gaps say nothing. The row is one group, named a pagination in the theme's language; on iOS it is a group without a name, where a screen reader reads a group's own name after what the group holds.

Numbers are written in the digits of the theme's language. The row is as wide as its items and one line, as tall as the platform's touch target at the least. In a place wider than itself it starts where the place does. What starts there is its first button, the room a press on it has: the arrow stands in the middle of that room, a little inside the edge a text over the row starts at, as an icon does in any button. Drawn at that edge, the button's fill, its ring and half of what a finger presses would lie outside the row.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: the page on screen, counted from one, as it is written on the row: a pager's or a carousel's index counts from nought, and is this less one. A number outside the pages is taken as the nearest page.

parameters.name: pageCount
parameters.description: how many pages there are. A list with nothing in it has one page, an empty one: a count under one is taken as one.

parameters.name: onPageChange
parameters.description: told the page that was asked for, by its number or by a button. The row shows it once `page` says so.

parameters.name: modifier
parameters.description: applied to the row.

parameters.name: siblingCount
parameters.description: in a row of numbers, how many pages are shown on each side of the page on screen where there is room for them: none or more. More than there are pages is all of them.

parameters.name: boundaryCount
parameters.description: in a row of numbers, how many pages are always shown at each end where there is room for them: none or more.

parameters.name: firstAndLast
parameters.description: whether the row has, outside previous and next, the two buttons that go to the first page and to the last.

parameters.name: enabled
parameters.description: whether the row can be pressed: one that cannot is drawn in the theme's disabled colours.

parameters.name: textStyle
parameters.description: the type the numbers and the words are set in: the theme's `label` unless given. An item that is made larger by the style is not written larger by itself.

parameters.name: style
parameters.description: this call's own style: over every enclosing one and under the density. Only the fields it sets change, on every platform.

parameters.name: colors
parameters.description: this call's own colours. Only the ones it sets change; the rest stay the theme's.

parameters.name: tagKey
parameters.description: a locale-independent key for automation: the row's tag is `Pagination_<tagKey>`, and its parts are named inside it, `Pagination_<tagKey>.Page_<number>`, `Pagination_<tagKey>.Step_previous`, `Pagination_<tagKey>.Step_next`, `Pagination_<tagKey>.Step_first`, `Pagination_<tagKey>.Step_last`, and `Pagination_<tagKey>.Text_position` for the words of a row without numbers.

declarations.name: PaginationLayout
declarations.signature: enum class PaginationLayout
declarations.description: How a `PantrixPagination` lays out its pages.

entries.name: Numbered
entries.description: Previous, the pages by their numbers with the far ones folded into gaps, and next: where people jump between pages. A row too narrow for it is laid out as `Compact`.

entries.name: Compact
entries.description: Previous, "Page 3 of 10", and next: where people step from one page to the one after it.

declarations.name: PaginationStyle
declarations.description:
`PantrixPagination`'s layout and geometry.

Each item, a page's number, previous and next, is `itemSize` square at the least, in `itemShape`, and `itemGap` from the one beside it; around it the platform's touch target is kept free. The gap follows the density; the items do not.

parameters.name: layout
parameters.description: How the pages are laid out: by their numbers on every platform, in a row that has the room.

parameters.name: itemSize
parameters.description: A page's number, previous and next: 40dp on Android, 36dp on iOS, 32dp on desktop and the web. A number too long for it makes its item wider. The icons in previous and next are half of it and 4dp.

parameters.name: itemShape
parameters.description: The corners of an item, of its fill where it is the page on screen and of its ring: round on Android and iOS, small on desktop and the web.

parameters.name: itemGap
parameters.description: Between two neighbours of the row.

declarations.name: PaginationColors
declarations.description:
What a `PantrixPagination` is painted with, for a row that does not take the theme's colours: a colour that is set is used, and one that is left out stays the theme's.

```
PantrixPagination(…, colors = PaginationColors(selectedContainer = PantrixTheme.colors.success.container))
```

A row has no fill of its own and stands on what is behind it. On a fill, which says what is written on it, all of the row is written in that: the theme's texts and its brand's fill are colours for the theme's own grounds. The page on screen is told there by a fill that is a share of the same colour.

parameters.name: content
parameters.description: The numbers of the pages that are not on screen, and the words of a row that has no room for numbers. The theme's `textPrimary`.

parameters.name: control
parameters.description: Previous and next, and the marks that stand for the pages folded away. The theme's `textSecondary`.

parameters.name: selectedContainer
parameters.description: The fill of the page on screen. The primary role's `container`.

parameters.name: selectedContent
parameters.description: The number of the page on screen: what the theme pairs with `selectedContainer`, which is the primary role's `onContainer` on the fill the row has by itself. The theme has no pair for a fill that is none of its roles' and writes on it as on the row's own: give such a fill its number too.

declarations.name: TagTone
declarations.signature: enum class TagTone
declarations.description:
What a tag means: one of the theme's colour roles, so a brand changes every tag at once.

The tone chooses the role, and `TagVariant` how much of it the tag wears. A tone says nothing by itself: a screen reader hears the tag's words and not its colour, so what the colour means has to be in the words.

entries.name: Primary
entries.description: The brand's colour: the tag that matters most in a row of them.

entries.name: Info
entries.description: Something worth knowing that is neither good nor bad: a type, a channel.

entries.name: Success
entries.description: Something that worked or is well: paid, in stock, passing.

entries.name: Warning
entries.description: Something to look at before it becomes a problem: expiring, low stock.

entries.name: Danger
entries.description: Something that failed or cannot be undone: overdue, rejected.

entries.name: Neutral
entries.description: A category with no judgement in it: a topic, a version. The default.

declarations.name: TagVariant
declarations.signature: enum class TagVariant
declarations.description: How much of the page a tag takes: its weight, not its meaning.

entries.name: Soft
entries.description: The role's pale fill, written in the colour the theme pairs with it. The default: read without shouting.

entries.name: Solid
entries.description: The role's full colour, written in its pair: for the one state a row is about.

entries.name: Outline
entries.description: No fill, and an edge and the words in the role's full colour: for a page that has colour in it already. On a fill that is not the theme's ground, the edge and the words are what is written there.

declarations.name: PantrixTag
declarations.signature:
@Composable
fun PantrixTag(
    text: String,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    tone: TagTone = TagTone.Neutral,
    variant: TagVariant = TagVariant.Soft,
    icon: ImageVector? = null,
    dot: Boolean = false,
    contentDescription: String? = null,
    style: TagStyle? = null,
    colors: TagColors? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null,
    textStyle: TextStyle = PantrixTheme.typography.footnote
)
declarations.description:
A short label on a piece of data: a status, a category, a version.

A tag is read, not pressed. Something that is pressed, removed or chosen is a chip, and a count or a dot on another element is a badge. Since nothing presses it, a tag takes no focus, has no touch target and is lower than a chip on every platform: it stands inside a row without taking it over.

The words carry the meaning, not the colour: "Overdue" in the danger tone says the same to someone who cannot see that it is red. A tag whose words are a colour's name has nothing to say.

The words are one line, set in `textStyle`, the theme's footnote type unless given, and are cut where the room ends. A larger type makes the tag taller. An `icon` or a `dot` stands before them, at the start of the line, which is the right in a right-to-left layout. A screen reader hears the tag as one thing, its words, or `contentDescription` in their place.

```
PantrixTag(text = stringResource(Res.string.overdue), tone = TagTone.Danger, dot = true, tagKey = "state")
```

parameters.name: text
parameters.description: what the tag says: a word or two.

parameters.name: modifier
parameters.description: the tag's modifier.

parameters.name: tone
parameters.description: the colour role the tag is drawn in.

parameters.name: variant
parameters.description: how much of the role the tag wears.

parameters.name: icon
parameters.description: drawn before the words, in their colour. It says nothing to a screen reader.

parameters.name: dot
parameters.description: whether a small disc in the role's full colour stands before the words, where there is no `icon`: a status a row is in.

parameters.name: contentDescription
parameters.description: what a screen reader says for the tag in place of its words, or null for the words.

parameters.name: style
parameters.description: this call's own style: over every enclosing one and under the density. Only the fields it sets change, on every platform.

parameters.name: colors
parameters.description: this tag's own colours, in place of its tone's: the ones it sets, with the tone's for the rest.

parameters.name: tagKey
parameters.description: the tag's automation key: it is `Tag_<tagKey>`, and is tagged only when given one.

parameters.name: textStyle
parameters.description: the type the words are set in: the theme's `footnote` unless given. Their colour is the tag's.

declarations.name: TagStyle
declarations.description:
`PantrixTag`'s geometry: a label small enough to stand inside a row without taking it over.

A tag is lower than a chip on every platform, as a chip is pressed and a tag is read: 24dp on Android and 22 on iOS, on desktop and on the web. Its corners part it from a chip too, except on iOS, whose own labels are round at the ends as its chips are.

The height and the room around the words follow the density. The icon, the dot, the edge and the corners do not.

parameters.name: shape
parameters.description: The tag's corners: a step of the brand's shape scale, or a fixed shape.

parameters.name: height
parameters.description: The least height of a tag. A larger type makes it taller.

parameters.name: horizontalPadding
parameters.description: The room between the tag's sides and what it holds.

parameters.name: iconPadding
parameters.description: Between the icon or the dot and the words.

parameters.name: iconSize
parameters.description: The width and height of the icon.

parameters.name: borderWidth
parameters.description: The width of the edge of `TagVariant.Outline`, and of an edge given in `TagColors`.

parameters.name: dotSize
parameters.description: The width and height of the dot.

declarations.name: TagColors
declarations.description:
What a `PantrixTag` is painted with, in place of its tone's colours: a colour that is set is used, and one that is left out stays the tone's.

```
// A campaign's own colours, which no role of the theme has.
PantrixTag(text = campaign.name, colors = TagColors(container = campaign.color, content = campaign.onColor))
```

A `container` given here that is one of the theme's role colours brings the colour the theme pairs with it for the words, the icon and the dot, unless those are given too. A fill no role has does not: what reads on it is the caller's to give.

parameters.name: container
parameters.description: The tag's fill. The role's `container` in `TagVariant.Soft`, its `color` in `TagVariant.Solid`, and none in `TagVariant.Outline`.

parameters.name: content
parameters.description: The words and the icon: the colour that reads on `container`. The role's `onContainer` in `TagVariant.Soft`, its `onColor` in `TagVariant.Solid`, and its `color` in `TagVariant.Outline`, which reads on the theme's grounds. An outlined tag on a fill that is not the theme's ground is written in what is written there.

parameters.name: border
parameters.description: The tag's edge: that of `TagVariant.Outline`, in `content`. A tag of another variant has one where it is given here.

parameters.name: dot
parameters.description: The dot: the role's `color`, and on the role's full colour its `onColor`. On a fill that is not the theme's ground, an outlined tag's dot is in `content`.

declarations.name: TreeSelection
declarations.signature: enum class TreeSelection
declarations.description: How the rows of a `PantrixTreeView` are chosen.

entries.name: None
entries.description: None is chosen: a press on a row opens its branch or closes it.

entries.name: Single
entries.description: One row at a time: a press chooses it and lets go of the one chosen before.

entries.name: Checkbox
entries.description: Any number of rows, each by a checkbox: a branch checks everything under it, and shows a dash where only some of what is under it is checked.

declarations.name: TreeNode
declarations.description:
One node of a `PantrixTreeView`, and the nodes under it.

```
TreeNode(
    key = "src",
    label = "src",
    icon = PantrixIcons.Folder,
    children = listOf(TreeNode(key = "src/main.kt", label = "main.kt", trailing = "4 KB"))
)
```

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: What tells this node from every other one in the tree: what the tree's `expanded` and `selected` hold for it. It is the same in every language, so a translated screen opens and chooses the same nodes, and no two nodes of a tree have one key.

parameters.name: label
parameters.description: What the row says, and the node's name for a screen reader.

parameters.name: children
parameters.description: The nodes under this one, in the order they are shown. A node with none is a leaf, unless `hasChildren` says that its children are still to come.

parameters.name: icon
parameters.description: Drawn before the label, or null for none: a folder, a file's kind. A screen reader passes over it.

parameters.name: trailing
parameters.description: A short text at the row's end, or null for none: how many things the node holds, how large a file is. It is read with the label.

parameters.name: enabled
parameters.description: Whether the node can be chosen or checked. One that cannot is written in the disabled text's colour, and its branch still opens and closes.

parameters.name: hasChildren
parameters.description: Whether the node is a branch: its twisty is drawn and it opens, even while `children` is still empty, for a tree that loads a level when it is opened.

parameters.name: tagKey
parameters.description: The row's automation key, the same in every language, where it is to be another than `key`: the row is `Node_<tagKey>`, inside the tag of a tree that has a key, as `TreeView_files.Node_src`.

declarations.name: PantrixTreeView
declarations.signature:
@Composable
fun PantrixTreeView(
    nodes: List<TreeNode>,
    expanded: Set<String>,
    onExpandedChange: (Set<String>) -> Unit,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    selection: TreeSelection = TreeSelection.None,
    selected: Set<String> = emptySet(),
    onSelectionChange: ((Set<String>) -> Unit)? = null,
    loading: Set<String> = emptySet(),
    filter: String = "",
    guides: Boolean = false,
    style: TreeViewStyle? = null,
    colors: TreeViewColors? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null
)
declarations.description:
A hierarchy whose branches open and close: folders and files, categories, a document's headings.

Which branches are open is the caller's state, as an accordion's sections are: give `expanded` and act on `onExpandedChange`. So is which rows are chosen: give `selected` and act on `onSelectionChange`. That is what lets a screen open the branch a link points at, keep the tree as it was left across a rotation, or close it all from a button of its own.

**Choosing.** With `TreeSelection.None` a press on a row opens its branch or closes it. With `TreeSelection.Single` a press chooses the row, and with `TreeSelection.Checkbox` it checks the row's checkbox; the twisty at the row's start is then a press of its own that opens and closes the branch. A branch's checkbox checks everything under it that can be checked, or where all of that is checked, clears it; a branch whose children are not all checked shows a dash, and one all of whose children are is checked itself. What `onSelectionChange` is given in that mode is every node that is checked, branches and all. A node that is not `enabled` cannot be chosen or checked, and its branch still opens and closes.

**Loading a level at a time.** A node whose `hasChildren` is true and whose `children` are still empty has a twisty, and opening it is what tells the caller to load them. While its key is in `loading`, a spinner stands in its twisty's place.

**Filtering.** While `filter` holds more than spaces, the tree shows the nodes whose labels hold it, in the theme's language, with the letters that hold it marked, and the branches they stand in, which open while the filter is given: the reader may close one again. Under a node that holds it the tree shows everything, as its own branches are open. A tree in which nothing holds it shows no row; what to say then is the caller's.

**With the keyboard** the tree is one stop for Tab, the row the focus was on last, or else the chosen one or the first. The arrows down and up go from row to row, Home and End to the first and the last; the arrow that points away from where lines start opens a branch, and on an open one goes to its first child, and the other closes an open branch, and on any other row goes to the branch it stands in. A letter goes to the next row whose label starts with it, and `*` opens every branch beside the row. Enter and Space press the row.

**To a screen reader** a row is its label, what stands at its end, how many children a closed branch has and how deep the row stands, all in the theme's words. It is offered what pressing it does, to choose it, to check it, or to open or close it, and a branch says whether it is open: by that action on Android, and in the theme's words elsewhere. The rows are read in the order they stand, whatever their depth does to their bounds.

**Its size.** The tree is as wide as the room it is given and as tall as its open rows, and does not scroll: it stands in a page that does. Every open row is composed, so a tree of many thousands of open rows wants a list of its own. A branch's children come and go with the theme's motion.

```
var open by remember { mutableStateOf(setOf("src")) }
var chosen by remember { mutableStateOf(emptySet<String>()) }
PantrixTreeView(
    nodes = files,
    expanded = open,
    onExpandedChange = { open = it },
    selection = TreeSelection.Single,
    selected = chosen,
    onSelectionChange = { chosen = it },
    tagKey = "files"
)
```

parameters.name: nodes
parameters.description: the nodes at the top of the tree, in the order they are shown. No two nodes of the tree have one key.

parameters.name: expanded
parameters.description: the keys of the branches that are open.

parameters.name: onExpandedChange
parameters.description: called with the keys that are to be open after a branch was opened or closed. The tree changes nothing by itself.

parameters.name: modifier
parameters.description: the tree's modifier. The tree is as wide as the room it is given and as tall as its open rows.

parameters.name: selection
parameters.description: how rows are chosen: not at all, one at a time, or by checkboxes.

parameters.name: selected
parameters.description: the keys of the chosen rows, or of the checked ones.

parameters.name: onSelectionChange
parameters.description: called with the keys that are to be chosen, or checked, after a press. `null` leaves the rows as `selected` has them, and a press on a row opens its branch or closes it.

parameters.name: loading
parameters.description: the keys of the branches whose children are being loaded: a spinner stands in their twisty's place.

parameters.name: filter
parameters.description: what the rows' labels are to hold for the rows to be shown, or nothing for all of them.

parameters.name: guides
parameters.description: whether a faint line runs down from each open branch's twisty along what it holds.

parameters.name: style
parameters.description: this call's own style: over every enclosing one and under the density. Only the fields it sets change, on every platform.

parameters.name: colors
parameters.description: this tree's own colours, where they are not the theme's: the ones set here, with the theme's for the rest.

parameters.name: tagKey
parameters.description: the tree's automation key: the tree is `TreeView_<tagKey>`, a row in it `TreeView_<tagKey>.Node_<key>` and its twisty `TreeView_<tagKey>.Twisty_<key>`. What a press does is reported as a `TreeView` event: `expand`, `collapse`, `select`, `check` and `uncheck`, with the node's key.

declarations.name: TreeViewStyle
declarations.description:
`PantrixTreeView`'s geometry: how tall a row is, how far each level steps in, and how large the twisty is.

A row is a row of the platform's own list, which is what a tree is made of: 48dp on Android and 44pt on iOS, which are the least a finger is given there, and 32dp on desktop and the web, the least a pointer is given. A row is never lower than the platform's touch target, and a desktop or a web page used by touch gives it a finger's.

The row's height, the gap and the padding follow the density, as the room around the words. The indent, the icon's size, the guides' width and the shape do not.

parameters.name: shape
parameters.description: The corners of a chosen row's fill: a step of the brand's shape scale, or a fixed shape.

parameters.name: rowHeight
parameters.description: The least height of a row. A larger type makes it taller.

parameters.name: indent
parameters.description: How far a level steps in from the one it stands under.

parameters.name: iconSize
parameters.description: The width and height of the twisty, of a node's own icon and of the spinner of a branch that loads.

parameters.name: gap
parameters.description: Between the twisty, the checkbox, the icon, the label and what stands at the row's end.

parameters.name: horizontalPadding
parameters.description: The room between a row's sides and what it holds.

parameters.name: guideWidth
parameters.description: The width of the lines that run down from an open branch where the tree draws them.

declarations.name: TreeViewColors
declarations.description:
What a `PantrixTreeView` is painted with, for a tree that does not take the theme's colours: a colour that is set is used, and one that is left out stays the theme's.

```
// The chosen row in the success role, the rest as the theme has it.
PantrixTreeView(…, colors = TreeViewColors(selectedContainer = PantrixTheme.colors.success.container))
```

A `container` given here that is one of the theme's role colours brings the colour the theme pairs with it for the rows, unless `content` is given too, and a `selectedContainer` brings its pair for the chosen row, unless `selectedContent` is given. A fill no role has does not: what reads on it is the caller's to give.

parameters.name: container
parameters.description: The fill behind the rows. None: the tree stands on what is behind it.

parameters.name: content
parameters.description: A row's label and its icon. The theme's `textPrimary`, or on a fill that is not the tree's, the colour that fill gives what stands on it. The twisty and what stands at a row's end are the theme's `textSecondary` on the theme's own grounds, and this colour elsewhere and where it is given.

parameters.name: selectedContainer
parameters.description: The fill behind the chosen row. The primary role's `container`.

parameters.name: selectedContent
parameters.description: The chosen row's label, icon and twisty: the colour that reads on `selectedContainer`. The primary role's `onContainer`.

parameters.name: guide
parameters.description: The lines that run down from an open branch. The theme's `divider` on the theme's own grounds. On a fill, where that line would not read, a share of `content`.

parameters.name: match
parameters.description: What is laid behind the letters a filter found. The theme's warning role softened, written in what the theme pairs with it; on a fill a share of what is written there, under letters that keep their colour. A row that cannot be chosen lays a share of it under letters that keep the row's faint colour.

declarations.name: DateFieldOrder
declarations.signature: enum class DateFieldOrder
declarations.description: The order a date field takes a day's parts in.

entries.name: DayMonthYear
entries.description: The day, the month, then the year: `18.10.2026`.

entries.name: MonthDayYear
entries.description: The month, the day, then the year: `10/18/2026`.

entries.name: YearMonthDay
entries.description: The year, the month, then the day: `2026-10-18`, as ISO 8601 writes a day.

declarations.name: DateFieldFormat
declarations.description:
How a date field takes a day: the order of its parts, and the mark that stands between them. The day and the month are two digits each and the year four, whatever the order, so a whole day is eight digits.

Only the digits are typed: the field puts the mark in itself as each part is filled, and a press on Backspace after it takes the digit before it away. The order is the field's setting and not a word, so it is no part of the strings pack: what the pack gives a field is the letters its pattern is written in, "DD", "MM" and "YYYY".

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: the order the parts are typed and shown in.

parameters.name: separator
parameters.description: what stands between the parts on the screen: a mark, never a letter, a digit or a space.

companion.name: DayMonthYearDots
companion.description: `18.10.2026`: Turkish, German, Russian, Polish and the Nordic languages but Swedish.

companion.name: DayMonthYearSlashes
companion.description: `18/10/2026`: British English, French, Spanish, Italian, Portuguese, Greek and Arabic.

companion.name: MonthDayYearSlashes
companion.description: `10/18/2026`: American English.

companion.name: Iso
companion.description: `2026-10-18`: ISO 8601, and Swedish and Lithuanian.

companion.name: of
companion.description: The format `locale`'s language writes a day in with digits, and for English its region: the United States and an English with no region name the month first, Canada writes ISO 8601, and the rest of the English speaking world the day first. A language Pantrix knows no order for is given ISO 8601, which reads the same everywhere.

declarations.name: DatePickerPresentation
declarations.signature: enum class DatePickerPresentation
declarations.description: What a date control opens what it shows in, a field's calendar or an elastic date picker's panels: the same on every platform. A sheet and a dialog stand over a scrim, and none of them has a title over what it holds.

entries.name: Popover
entries.description: A popover beside the part that was pressed: under a field's box, or beside a part of an elastic date picker.

entries.name: Sheet
entries.description: A sheet from the window's edge, with no title over what it holds.

entries.name: Dialog
entries.description: A dialog in the middle of the window, over a scrim, as wide as what it holds and with no title over it.

entries.name: Adaptive
entries.description: A sheet in a narrow window, the `Compact` width class, within the thumb's reach on a phone, and a popover in every wider one. The window is the one the control's overlay is shown over, and it is asked as the picker opens: one that is open stays as it is when the window changes.

declarations.name: DateTextFieldState
declarations.signature: class DateTextFieldState(initial: PantrixDate? = null)
declarations.description:
What a date field holds, for a caller that keeps it itself: the digits typed into it so far, and the day they make.

`date` is the day the field takes: null while the field is empty, while what is typed is no whole day, names no day of the calendar, or is a day the field does not take. Setting it writes the day into the field, which shows it as its format writes it; setting it to null empties the field. A state the field is not drawing at the time keeps the day, and the field writes it once it is drawn.

Create it with `rememberDateTextFieldState`, which keeps it across a configuration change and a process that is brought back.

parameters.name: initial
parameters.description: the day the field starts with, or null for an empty one.

members.name: date
members.description: The day the field takes, or null: see the class.

members.name: text
members.description: The digits typed so far, without the marks the field shows between the parts: `1810` for `18.10.`. It tells a field that is half typed from an empty one, where `date` is null for both.

members.name: clear
members.description: Empties the field: no digit is left, and no day.
