declarations.description:
A filled text field for a day: the day is typed in digits, or chosen from a calendar that a button at the box's end opens. It is `PantrixDateTextField` in a filled box.

It is drawn as `PantrixFilledTextField` is, the label inside the box where it rests in the text's place while the field is empty and without the focus, and the pattern shows once the label has moved up. It takes digits alone: the `format`'s mark comes in by itself as each part of the day is whole, so `18102026` shows as `18.10.2026` in Turkish and `10182026` as `10/18/2026` in American English. A phone shows its keyboard of digits. While the box is empty it shows the pattern, `GG.AA.YYYY` in Turkish and `MM/DD/YYYY` in American English, which a screen reader is told as the order of the parts. A day pasted written out is read as it is written, in the `format`'s order and else with the year first as ISO 8601 has it: `2026-10-18` pasted in Turkish shows as `18.10.2026`, and a year of two digits is the one of the hundred years around `today` that ends in them.

`onValueChange` is told the day the field holds each time it changes: a whole day the calendar takes, as it is typed or chosen, and null while the field is empty, half typed, or holds digits that make no day or a day it does not take. The field keeps what is typed itself, so a half-typed day stays on the screen while `value` is null. A `value` that is a day other than the field's is written in, and a null `value` empties a field that holds a day.

The field writes its own error under the box where what is typed is wrong: digits that make no whole day, once the user has left the field; a day the calendar has not, the 31st of February; a day before `minDate` or after `maxDate`; and a day `isDateEnabled` turns down. An `error` of the caller's comes first, its `supportingText` the message.

The calendar opens by its button, by Alt and ↓, and in a `readOnly` field by a press on the box, by Enter or by Space too: a read-only field takes a day from the calendar alone. It opens in what `presentation` says, the same on every platform. A day pressed in it is the field's at once and closes it; Escape and a press outside close it and change nothing. Opened by the keyboard, the focus goes to its chosen day, or to today, and comes back to the field as it closes.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: the day the field shows, or null.

parameters.name: onValueChange
parameters.description: told the field's day each time the user changes it: a day, or null for none.

parameters.name: modifier
parameters.description: the modifier of the whole field: its label, its box and what is under it.

parameters.name: enabled
parameters.description: whether the field can be used. One that cannot takes no focus and opens no calendar.

parameters.name: readOnly
parameters.description: whether the day can only be chosen from the calendar, and not typed.

parameters.name: label
parameters.description: what the field is for, inside the box: the field's name for a screen reader, and its calendar's.

parameters.name: placeholder
parameters.description: shown in the box while it is empty, in the place of the pattern the field shows by itself.

parameters.name: supportingText
parameters.description: help under the box. With `error` it is the message that says what to put right; without it, the field's own error takes its place while there is one.

parameters.name: error
parameters.description: whether the caller finds the day wrong, as a day already taken: the field is drawn in error, and `supportingText` is the message.

parameters.name: leadingIcon
parameters.description: what stands before the text. A slot does not size what is put in it.

parameters.name: showClearButton
parameters.description: shows a button that empties the field, while it can be typed into and is not empty.

parameters.name: minDate
parameters.description: the first day the field takes, or null for no first. Not after `maxDate`.

parameters.name: maxDate
parameters.description: the last day the field takes, or null for no last.

parameters.name: isDateEnabled
parameters.description: whether the field takes a day between the two, or null for every day: a weekday, a day not yet booked.

parameters.name: firstDayOfWeek
parameters.description: the day the calendar's weeks start on, 1 for Monday to 7 for Sunday as ISO 8601 numbers them, or null for the language's.

parameters.name: today
parameters.description: the day the calendar marks as today: by default the one the screen's clock shows (`rememberToday`), which turns at midnight.

parameters.name: format
parameters.defaultNote: `of`: The role of the theme this tone is drawn in.
parameters.description: the order the parts are typed in and the mark between them: the theme's language's and region's by default.

parameters.name: presentation
parameters.description: what the calendar opens in: by default a sheet in a narrow window and a popover under the box in a wider one, chosen as it opens; or always a popover, a sheet or a dialog.

parameters.name: style
parameters.description: this call's own style of the field: over every enclosing one and under the density.

parameters.name: colors
parameters.description: this call's own colours of the field, in place of the theme's roles.

parameters.name: pickerStyle
parameters.description: this call's own style of the calendar.

parameters.name: pickerColors
parameters.description: this call's own colours of the calendar.

parameters.name: contentDescription
parameters.description: what a screen reader says for the field where it has no `label`.

parameters.name: tagKey
parameters.description: the field's automation key: the field is `DateFilledTextField_<tagKey>`, its button `DateFilledTextFieldCalendar_<tagKey>`, its clear button `DateFilledTextFieldClear_<tagKey>` and its calendar `DatePicker_<tagKey>`. The field reports that the calendar opened and that a day was chosen in it, and never the day.

parameters.name: interactionSource
parameters.description: the field's interactions, hoisted: its focus, its hover and its presses.

declarations.description:
A calendar to choose a day from, a month at a time: the month's title between the arrows that turn it, the days of the week over its columns, and its days.

The calendar is the choice itself, and stands where it is put: in the page, or in a `PantrixPopover`, a `PantrixDialog` or a `PantrixSheet` that a button or a field opens. It paints no ground of its own and holds nothing of the choice: `selected` is the caller's, and a press on a day hands it to `onSelect`. What it keeps is the month on show, which starts at the chosen day's, or today's, and goes to the chosen day's month when the caller chooses one that is not on show.

The days a calendar cannot take are drawn faint and cannot be chosen: those before `minDate` and after `maxDate`, which the arrows do not turn to either, and those between that `isDateEnabled` leaves out, a weekend, a day that is full. Pressing the title shows the years in place of the days, and choosing one turns the calendar to the same month of that year.

The calendar is one stop for Tab, on the chosen day, today or the month's first, and its keys walk the days as a calendar's do: the arrows a day or a week, Page Up and Page Down a month, with Shift a year, Home and End the week's first and last day; Enter and Space choose. A screen reader hears each day in full, with the day of the week, and is told politely when the month changes.

Days are `PantrixDate`s, with no library of dates: docs/guide/date-time/DATE_TIME_GUIDE.md turns them into an app's own.

```
var due by remember { mutableStateOf<PantrixDate?>(null) }
PantrixDatePicker(
    selected = due,
    onSelect = { due = it },
    minDate = PantrixDate.today(),
    tagKey = "due"
)
```

parameters.description: the chosen day, or null while none is.

parameters.name: onSelect

parameters.name: modifier

Given a width, as `Modifier.fillMaxWidth()` gives it the width of a sheet, it fills it: its columns grow as far as `DatePickerStyle.maxCellWidth`, and past that it stands in the middle.

parameters.name: maxDate
parameters.description: the last day that can be chosen, or null for none so late.

parameters.name: isDateEnabled
parameters.description: whether a day between them can be chosen, or null where every one can.

parameters.name: firstDayOfWeek
parameters.description: the day the weeks start on, as ISO 8601 numbers the days: 1 is Monday and 7 is Sunday. Null is the language's, `PantrixLocale.firstDayOfWeek`: Sunday in English, Monday in Turkish, Saturday in Arabic.

parameters.name: enabled
parameters.description: whether a day can be chosen at all. A calendar that takes no choice is drawn faint.

parameters.name: today
parameters.description: the day marked as today: by default the one the screen's clock shows (`rememberToday`), which turns at midnight. A test gives a day of its own.

A calendar to choose a stretch of days from: a stay, a leave, the days a report is of. It is the calendar that chooses a day, pressed twice: its first press chooses the first day of the stretch and its second the last.

The second press ends the stretch on its day, or on the first day again for a stretch of one day, and `onRangeSelect` is handed the stretch; one before the first day starts the stretch again from there. declarations.name: DatePickerStyle
declarations.description:
`PantrixDatePicker`'s geometry: the room of a day, the round mark a chosen day is drawn in, and the room around the month.

A day's room is as wide as a column of the week and as tall as a row of it, and the days touch: a press anywhere in the room is the day's. On a phone it is the platform's least touch target, 48dp on Android and 44pt on iOS, so that a month is seven targets wide, 360dp across on Android as a Material calendar is. Under a pointer it is 36dp. A place too narrow for the month makes every day's room narrower, and its mark with it, by the same share. A calendar given more width than that, as a sheet gives it with `Modifier.fillMaxWidth()`, widens its columns to fill it, up to `maxCellWidth`, and stands in the middle of what is left; its rows and its marks keep their size.

The room around the month and the gap under its title follow the density; a day's room, its widest and its mark do not, as a touch target does not.

parameters.name: cellSize
parameters.description: The width and the height of a day's room: the column and the row. The title and the year's rooms are as tall.

parameters.name: daySize
parameters.description: The width and the height of the round mark a chosen day, today and the day under a pointer are drawn in, in the middle of its room. A stretch of days is a band as tall.

parameters.name: padding
parameters.description: The room between the calendar's edge and what it holds.

parameters.name: gap
parameters.description: Between the title and the days of the week over the month.

parameters.name: maxCellWidth
parameters.description: The widest a column grows to where the calendar is given more width than seven days' rooms: half as wide again as `cellSize`.

declarations.name: DatePickerColors
declarations.description:
What a `PantrixDatePicker` is painted with, in place of the theme's colours: a colour that is set is used, and one that is left out stays the theme's.

A `selectedContainer` given here that is one of the theme's role colours brings the colour the theme pairs with it for the chosen day's number, unless `selectedContent` is given too, and a `rangeContainer` brings its pair for the days of a stretch, unless `rangeContent` is given. A fill no role has does not: what reads on it is the caller's to give.

The calendar paints no ground of its own: it stands on what is under it, a popover's, a dialog's, a sheet's or a page's, and its words are the theme's for its grounds.

parameters.name: content
parameters.description: The days' numbers, the title and the arrows. The theme's `textPrimary`.

parameters.name: weekday
parameters.description: The days of the week over the columns. The theme's `textSecondary`.

parameters.name: selectedContainer
parameters.description: The round mark of a chosen day, and of a stretch's first and last. The primary role's `color`.

parameters.name: selectedContent
parameters.description: The number on it. The primary role's `onColor`, or the colour a role's fill given as `selectedContainer` gives what stands on it.

parameters.name: rangeContainer
parameters.description: The band under the days between a stretch's first and last. The primary role's `container`. While the last is being chosen under a pointer, the band to the day under it is drawn in half of it.

parameters.name: rangeContent
parameters.description: The numbers on the band. The primary role's `onContainer`.

parameters.name: today
parameters.description: The ring around today, and its number. The primary role's `color`.

parameters.name: hover
parameters.description: The round mark under a pointer: which day a press would choose. A share of `content`.

parameters.name: disabled
parameters.description: The numbers of the days that cannot be chosen, and everything of a calendar that takes no choice. The theme's `textDisabled`.

declarations.description:
A text field for a day: the day is typed in digits, or chosen from a calendar that a button at the box's end opens.

It is drawn as `PantrixTextField` is, the label above the box, and takes digits alone: the `format`'s mark comes in by itself as each part of the day is whole, so `18102026` shows as `18.10.2026` in Turkish and `10182026` as `10/18/2026` in American English. A phone shows its keyboard of digits. While the box is empty it shows the pattern, `GG.AA.YYYY` in Turkish and `MM/DD/YYYY` in American English, which a screen reader is told as the order of the parts. A day pasted written out is read as it is written, in the `format`'s order and else with the year first as ISO 8601 has it: `2026-10-18` pasted in Turkish shows as `18.10.2026`, and a year of two digits is the one of the hundred years around `today` that ends in them.

`onValueChange` is told the day the field holds each time it changes: a whole day the calendar takes, as it is typed or chosen, and null while the field is empty, half typed, or holds digits that make no day or a day it does not take. The field keeps what is typed itself, so a half-typed day stays on the screen while `value` is null. A `value` that is a day other than the field's is written in, and a null `value` empties a field that holds a day.

The field writes its own error under the box where what is typed is wrong: digits that make no whole day, once the user has left the field; a day the calendar has not, the 31st of February; a day before `minDate` or after `maxDate`; and a day `isDateEnabled` turns down. An `error` of the caller's comes first, its `supportingText` the message.

The calendar opens by its button, by Alt and ↓, and in a `readOnly` field by a press on the box, by Enter or by Space too: a read-only field takes a day from the calendar alone. It opens in what `presentation` says, the same on every platform. A day pressed in it is the field's at once and closes it; Escape and a press outside close it and change nothing. Opened by the keyboard, the focus goes to its chosen day, or to today, and comes back to the field as it closes.

declarations.description:
A range of time that can move with the clock, as a dashboard is filtered by: "the last 15 minutes" is still the last 15 minutes at the next refresh. Elastic UI's `EuiSuperDatePicker`, built again on Pantrix.

A field holds the range and a button beside it refreshes it or takes an edit. Every part opens a panel, a popover by default, or a sheet or a dialog where `presentation` asks for one, on every platform alike:

- **The quick menu's button**, the calendar at the field's start, opens the last or the next amount of a unit, ‹ and › to move the range by its own length, the ranges `commonlyUsed` offers by name, and those `recentlyUsed` holds. A choice there is handed over at once.

- **The range's name**, "Last 15 minutes" or "Today", stands in the field while the range has one. A press on it shows the two ends, start → end, and opens the start's panel.

- **An end** opens its tabs: a moment on a calendar, with the times of the day by the half hour and the moment to type; an amount of time from now, with the moment it falls on and a switch that rounds it; or now itself. Moving to a tab makes the end what that tab shows. An edit waits: the field is painted in the success colour with a mark at its end, and the button beside it says Update, which hands the range over. An end before the start paints the field in the danger colour, and Update takes nothing. With `updateButton` `None` each edit is handed over at once. Apply at the end of the moment's field on the calendar's and the relative tab takes the edit and closes the panel, and the button of now's tab makes the end now and does the same.

- **Refresh** reads the range again where no edit waits: `onRefresh` where it is given, and `onRangeChange` with the same range where not.

A press outside an open popover goes on to what it lands on, as in Elastic UI: one press on the other end opens that end's panel, one on Update takes the edit, and one on the open end's button closes its panel. A sheet and a dialog stand over a scrim, and a press on it closes them alone.

The panels are set close, as Elastic UI's are: an end's popover is as wide as its calendar and the times beside it, the quick menu's 400dp, and the text fields, selects, tabs and buttons in them are 8 lower than a form's, 40dp on Android, 36pt on iOS and 32dp on the desktop and the web.

The range is the caller's: a new `range` drops an edit that waits. Where the field has less room than its words and its button need, the button beside it is its icon alone.

```
val lastQuarterHour = PantrixTimeRange(PantrixTimePoint.Relative(-15, PantrixTimeUnit.Minutes), PantrixTimePoint.Now)
var range by remember { mutableStateOf(lastQuarterHour) }
PantrixElasticDatePicker(range = range, onRangeChange = { range = it }, recentlyUsed = rememberRecentRanges())
```

declarations.description:
A filled text field for a time of day: the time is typed in digits, or chosen from a time picker that a button at the box's end opens. It is `PantrixTimeTextField` in a filled box.

It is drawn as `PantrixFilledTextField` is, the label inside the box where it rests in the text's place while the field is empty and without the focus, and the pattern shows once the label has moved up. It takes digits alone, four at most: the colon comes in by itself once the hour is whole, so `1430` shows as `14:30`, and a first digit that cannot start an hour is an hour of one digit, so `930` shows as `09:30`. A phone shows its keyboard of digits. While the box is empty it shows the pattern, `SS:DD` in Turkish and `HH:MM` in English, which a screen reader is told as the order of the parts. A time pasted written out is read as it is written: `14:30`, `14.30`, `1430`, or `2:30 PM` with a half of the day; a second written after the minute is let go.

By a clock of twelve hours, `is24Hour` false, the hours are typed 01 to 12 and the half of the day stands in the box beside them, as a button: a press on it, or Space while it holds the focus, turns it, and A and P typed in the field set it.

`onValueChange` is told the time the field holds each time it changes: a whole time the field takes, as it is typed or chosen, and null while the field is empty, half typed, or holds digits that make no time or a time it does not take. The field keeps what is typed itself, so a half-typed time stays on the screen while `value` is null. A `value` that is a time other than the field's is written in, and a null `value` empties a field that holds a time. A `value`'s second is kept while its hour and minute are not typed over; a time typed has none.

The field writes its own error under the box where what is typed is wrong: digits that make no whole time, once the user has left the field; a time the clock has not, 25 o'clock; and a time before `minTime` or after `maxTime`. An `error` of the caller's comes first, its `supportingText` the message.

The picker opens by its button, by Alt and ↓, and in a `readOnly` field by a press on the box, by Enter or by Space too: a read-only field takes a time from the picker alone. It opens in what `presentation` says, the same on every platform. A value pressed in it is the field's at once and leaves it open, so that the minute can be chosen after the hour; Enter on a value, Escape and a press outside close it. Opened by the keyboard, the focus goes to its chosen hour, or to the hour it is now, and comes back to the field as it closes.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: the time the field shows, or null.

parameters.name: onValueChange

parameters.name: presentation

parameters.name: style

declarations.signature:
@Composable
fun PantrixTimePicker(
    selected: PantrixTime?,
    onSelect: (PantrixTime) -> Unit,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    minTime: PantrixTime? = null,
    maxTime: PantrixTime? = null,
    minuteStep: Int = 1,
    is24Hour: Boolean = true,
    enabled: Boolean = true,
    style: TimePickerStyle? = null,
    colors: TimePickerColors? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null
)
declarations.description:
A time of day to choose from columns: the hours, the minutes, and by a clock of twelve hours the half of the day, each a column of five rows that scrolls through the rest, the chosen value filled in the middle of it.

`is24Hour` gives it its shape: by twenty-four hours, two columns, the hours 00 to 23 and the minutes, that choose `22:00`; by twelve, the hours 12 to 11, the minutes and a third column of the half of the day, that choose `10:00 PM`. It is twenty-four hours in every language unless the call asks for twelve.

The picker is the choice itself, and stands where it is put: in the page, or in a `PantrixPopover`, a `PantrixDialog` or a `PantrixSheet` that a button or a field opens. It paints no ground of its own and holds nothing of the choice: `selected` is the caller's, and a press on a value hands `onSelect` the whole time it makes, the other columns kept as they are. With nothing chosen, an hour comes with its first minute, and a minute with the first hour the picker takes. A time it shows that is to be taken only on a press of OK is the caller's draft.

The values a picker cannot take are drawn faint and cannot be pressed: the minutes before `minTime` and after `maxTime`, and the hours none of whose minutes are between them. The minutes are `minuteStep` apart.

Each column is one stop for Tab, on its chosen value, and its keys choose as they walk: the arrows the value below and above, Home and End the first and the last, Page Down and Page Up six hours or fifteen minutes on, and typed digits the value they write, `1` then `4` the fourteenth hour; the arrows across go to the column beside. A screen reader hears each column by its name and each value as a button, and is told politely the time a press or a key chose.

Times are `PantrixTime`s, with no library of dates: docs/guide/date-time/DATE_TIME_GUIDE.md turns them into an app's own, and a day and a time into a moment.

```
var at by remember { mutableStateOf<PantrixTime?>(null) }
PantrixTimePicker(
    selected = at,
    onSelect = { at = it },
    minuteStep = 15,
    tagKey = "at"
)
```

parameters.name: selected
parameters.description: the chosen time, or null while none is. Its seconds are kept in every time a press makes of it.

parameters.name: onSelect
parameters.description: handed the time a press or a key chose: one the picker takes.

parameters.name: modifier
parameters.description: the picker's modifier. The picker is as wide as its columns; given more room, it stands in the middle of it.

parameters.name: minTime
parameters.description: the first time that can be chosen, or null for none so early: its hour and minute.

parameters.name: maxTime
parameters.description: the last time that can be chosen, or null for none so late. Where it comes before `minTime`, the times that can be chosen run past midnight, from `minTime` to `maxTime` of the next day: a night's. By a clock of 24 hours the column of the hours then starts at `minTime`'s, so that the night's hours stand together: 22, 23, 00.

parameters.name: minuteStep
parameters.description: how far apart the minutes in their column are, 1 to 60: 15 offers the hour's first, a quarter past, half past and a quarter to. A chosen minute between them is shown all the same.

parameters.name: is24Hour
parameters.description: whether the hours are counted by twenty-four, and so the picker's shape: two columns that choose `22:00`; or by twelve, with a third column of the half of the day, `10:00 PM`. Twenty-four by default, in every language. Either way the time chosen is a `PantrixTime` of twenty-four hours; a screen writes it by the same clock with `PantrixStrings.time(hour, minute, is24Hour = …)`.

parameters.name: enabled
parameters.description: whether a time can be chosen at all. A picker that takes no choice is drawn faint.

parameters.name: style
parameters.description: this call's own style: over every enclosing one and under the density. Only the fields it sets change, on every platform.

parameters.name: colors
parameters.description: this picker's own colours: the ones it sets, with the theme's for the rest.

parameters.name: tagKey
parameters.description: the picker's automation key: it is `TimePicker_<tagKey>`, and its values are `TimePicker_<tagKey>.Hour_14`, `.Minute_30` and `.Period_pm`.

declarations.name: TimePickerStyle
declarations.description:
`PantrixTimePicker`'s geometry: the room of a value in a column, the pill a chosen value is drawn in, how wide a column is, and the room around the columns.

A value's room is as wide as its column and as tall as a row, and the rows touch: a press anywhere in the room is the value's. On a phone a row is the platform's least touch target, 48dp on Android and 44pt on iOS, as a calendar's day is; under a pointer it is 36dp. A column shows five rows and scrolls through the rest.

The room around the columns and the gap under their names follow the density; a row, its pill and a column's width do not, as a touch target does not.

parameters.name: cellSize
parameters.description: The height of a value's room: a row.

parameters.name: markHeight
parameters.description: The height of the pill a chosen value and the value under a pointer are drawn in, in the middle of its room. It is most of the column wide.

parameters.name: columnWidth
parameters.description: The width of a column of values.

parameters.name: padding
parameters.description: The room between the picker's edge and its columns.

parameters.name: gap
parameters.description: Between the columns' names and their values.

declarations.name: TimePickerColors
declarations.description:
What a `PantrixTimePicker` is painted with, in place of the theme's colours: a colour that is set is used, and one that is left out stays the theme's.

A `selectedContainer` given here that is one of the theme's role colours brings the colour the theme pairs with it for the chosen value's number, unless `selectedContent` is given too. A fill no role has does not: what reads on it is the caller's to give.

The picker paints no ground of its own: it stands on what is under it, a popover's, a dialog's, a sheet's or a page's.

parameters.name: content
parameters.description: The values' numbers and the mark between the hours and the minutes. The theme's `textPrimary`.

parameters.name: heading
parameters.description: The columns' names over them. The theme's `textSecondary`.

parameters.name: selectedContainer
parameters.description: The pill of a chosen value. The primary role's `color`.

parameters.name: selectedContent
parameters.description: The number on it. The primary role's `onColor`, or the colour a role's fill given as `selectedContainer` gives what stands on it.

parameters.name: hover
parameters.description: The pill under a pointer: which value a press would choose. A share of `content`.

parameters.name: disabled
parameters.description: The values that cannot be chosen, and everything of a picker that takes no choice. The theme's `textDisabled`.

declarations.description:
A text field for a time of day: the time is typed in digits, or chosen from a time picker that a button at the box's end opens.

It is drawn as `PantrixTextField` is, the label above the box, and takes digits alone, four at most: the colon comes in by itself once the hour is whole, so `1430` shows as `14:30`, and a first digit that cannot start an hour is an hour of one digit, so `930` shows as `09:30`. A phone shows its keyboard of digits. While the box is empty it shows the pattern, `SS:DD` in Turkish and `HH:MM` in English, which a screen reader is told as the order of the parts. A time pasted written out is read as it is written: `14:30`, `14.30`, `1430`, or `2:30 PM` with a half of the day; a second written after the minute is let go.

By a clock of twelve hours, `is24Hour` false, the hours are typed 01 to 12 and the half of the day stands in the box beside them, as a button: a press on it, or Space while it holds the focus, turns it, and A and P typed in the field set it.

`onValueChange` is told the time the field holds each time it changes: a whole time the field takes, as it is typed or chosen, and null while the field is empty, half typed, or holds digits that make no time or a time it does not take. The field keeps what is typed itself, so a half-typed time stays on the screen while `value` is null. A `value` that is a time other than the field's is written in, and a null `value` empties a field that holds a time. A `value`'s second is kept while its hour and minute are not typed over; a time typed has none.

The field writes its own error under the box where what is typed is wrong: digits that make no whole time, once the user has left the field; a time the clock has not, 25 o'clock; and a time before `minTime` or after `maxTime`. An `error` of the caller's comes first, its `supportingText` the message.

The picker opens by its button, by Alt and ↓, and in a `readOnly` field by a press on the box, by Enter or by Space too: a read-only field takes a time from the picker alone. It opens in what `presentation` says, the same on every platform. A value pressed in it is the field's at once and leaves it open, so that the minute can be chosen after the hour; Enter on a value, Escape and a press outside close it. Opened by the keyboard, the focus goes to its chosen hour, or to the hour it is now, and comes back to the field as it closes.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: the time the field shows, or null.

parameters.name: onValueChange
parameters.description: told the field's time each time the user changes it: a time, or null for none.

parameters.name: modifier
parameters.description: the modifier of the whole field: its label, its box and what is under it.

parameters.name: enabled
parameters.description: whether the field can be used. One that cannot takes no focus and opens no picker.

parameters.name: readOnly
parameters.description: whether the time can only be chosen from the picker, and not typed.

parameters.name: label
parameters.description: what the field is for, written above the box: the field's name for a screen reader, and its picker's.

parameters.name: placeholder
parameters.description: shown in the box while it is empty, in the place of the pattern the field shows by itself.

parameters.name: supportingText
parameters.description: help under the box. With `error` it is the message that says what to put right; without it, the field's own error takes its place while there is one.

parameters.name: error
parameters.description: whether the caller finds the time wrong, as a time already booked: the field is drawn in error, and `supportingText` is the message.

parameters.name: leadingIcon
parameters.description: what stands before the text. A slot does not size what is put in it.

parameters.name: showClearButton
parameters.description: shows a button that empties the field, while it can be typed into and is not empty.

parameters.name: minTime
parameters.description: the first time the field takes, or null for no first. Where it is after `maxTime`, the times run past midnight, as a night's do.

parameters.name: maxTime
parameters.description: the last time the field takes, or null for no last.

parameters.name: minuteStep
parameters.description: how many minutes apart the picker's minutes are, 1 to 60. A minute typed between them is taken.

parameters.name: is24Hour
parameters.description: whether the field and its picker count the hours of a day, 00 to 23, or by a clock of twelve hours.

parameters.name: presentation
parameters.description: what the picker opens in: by default a sheet in a narrow window and a popover under the box in a wider one, chosen as it opens; or always a popover, a sheet or a dialog.

parameters.name: style
parameters.description: this call's own style of the field: over every enclosing one and under the density.

parameters.name: colors
parameters.description: this call's own colours of the field, in place of the theme's roles.

parameters.name: pickerStyle
parameters.description: this call's own style of the picker.

parameters.name: pickerColors
parameters.description: this call's own colours of the picker.

parameters.name: contentDescription
parameters.description: what a screen reader says for the field where it has no `label`.

parameters.name: tagKey
parameters.description: the field's automation key: the field is `TimeTextField_<tagKey>`, its button `TimeTextFieldClock_<tagKey>`, its half of the day `TimeTextFieldPeriod_<tagKey>`, its clear button `TimeTextFieldClear_<tagKey>` and its picker `TimePicker_<tagKey>`. The field reports that the picker opened and that a value was chosen in it, and never the time.

parameters.name: interactionSource
parameters.description: the field's interactions, hoisted: its focus, its hover and its presses.

Text that gets smaller to stay in view: an amount, a title or a name that is read whole in the room it has.

The text is as large as its `style` says while it fits. A text too long for its room is set in a smaller size, the largest in which all of it is in view: no wider than the width it is given, no taller than the height, and on no more than `maxLines` lines. It is one line unless told. With more lines the text wraps first, and is set smaller when its lines run out. At `minFontSize` it stops shrinking, and what still does not fit is cut as `overflow` says.

It needs a room to fit: a width from its parent or its `modifier`, and a height too where it may take any number of lines. A text that is offered all the width there is has room for any line, and is never set smaller.

The lines of a text that is set smaller are as much closer: the style's line height follows the size. So do the sizes its spans give in em, and one given in sp is kept. In everything else it is `PantrixText`: the theme's type, the colour of where it sits, and what a screen reader is told of it. The size is found while the text is laid out, so the first frame shows it fitted, and so does every frame in which its room gets narrower, wider or lower. A room that only gets taller is followed a frame later.

parameters.name: text
parameters.description: the text.

parameters.name: modifier
parameters.description: the text's modifier: `fillMaxWidth()`, a `weight` or a size gives it the room it is fitted to.

parameters.name: style
parameters.description: the style of the text at its largest: a role of the theme's typography, and the base text unless given, `LocalPantrixTextStyle`, as a `PantrixText`'s is. A style whose size is not in sp has no smaller size to be set in, and its text is not shrunk.

parameters.name: minFontSize
parameters.description: the smallest the text gets: a size in sp, or one in em, which is a share of the style's own. It is the theme's footnote size unless told. At the style's own size or above it the text never shrinks, and at zero it shrinks until it fits, as far as a 256th of the style's size.

parameters.name: color
parameters.description: the text's colour. Unset, it is the style's, or the content colour of where the text sits, or the primary text colour.

parameters.name: textAlign
parameters.description: how the lines are aligned in the text's width.

parameters.name: maxLines
parameters.description: the most lines the text takes: one unless told. `Int.MAX_VALUE` leaves the lines to the height the text is given.

parameters.name: minLines
parameters.description: the least lines the text is tall, at its largest size.

parameters.name: overflow
parameters.description: how a text that does not fit at its smallest size is cut.

parameters.name: softWrap
parameters.description: whether the text wraps where its width ends. A text that does not is fitted to its longest line.

parameters.name: role
parameters.description: what the text is, for a screen reader: prose, a heading, a label or decoration.

parameters.name: selectable
parameters.description: whether the user can select the text and copy it.

parameters.name: onTextLayout
parameters.description: called with the text as it is laid out, in the size it is set in.

parameters.name: tagKey
parameters.description: the text's automation key: the text is `AutoText_<tagKey>`. Without one it has no tag.

declarations.name: AvatarTone
declarations.signature: enum class AvatarTone
declarations.description:
How an avatar is coloured where no picture covers it: one of the theme's colour roles, so a brand changes every avatar at once.

An avatar is filled in every tone, from the role's `color` and `onColor`, as initials on a solid circle are drawn everywhere else. The role's pale `container` is chosen for an area as wide as the screen, and a circle of it 32dp across is lost on a white page.

A tone says nothing by itself: a screen reader hears the avatar's description and not its colour, so what a colour is to mean has to be in the words beside it.

entries.name: Primary
entries.description: The brand's colour: the person using the app.

entries.name: Info
entries.description: A distinction with no judgement in it: a guest, a group, an account that is not a person.

entries.name: Success
entries.description: Someone or something in good standing.

entries.name: Warning
entries.description: Someone or something to look at.

entries.name: Danger
entries.description: Someone or something that failed or is blocked.

entries.name: Neutral
entries.description: No meaning at all: a grey for the initials to sit on. The default.

declarations.name: PantrixAvatar
declarations.signature:
@Composable
fun PantrixAvatar(
    contentDescription: String?,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    initials: String? = null,
    icon: ImageVector? = null,
    tone: AvatarTone = AvatarTone.Neutral,
    colors: AvatarColors? = null,
    style: AvatarStyle? = null,
    size: Dp = PantrixTheme.style(AvatarStyle, style).size,
    tagKey: String? = null,
    image: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null
)
declarations.description:
The picture of a person or a thing: a photograph, the initials of a name, or an icon standing for either.

The avatar draws its `initials`, or its `icon` where it has none, on its `tone`. With neither it is the plain shape in its tone. A picture is drawn over them, so the initials show while it loads and where it fails, and are covered once it is there. A picture with parts that can be seen through shows what is under them: give such a picture alone, without initials or an icon.

Pantrix loads no pictures. `image` is a slot, so an app draws one with whatever it already uses: an image loader, a `PantrixImage` of a resource, a canvas of its own. The slot is as large as the avatar and cut to its shape. A picture that is not square is fitted by its own rule, so ask for `ContentScale.Crop`.

Initials are drawn as they are written. They are not put in upper case: `i` becomes `İ` in Turkish and `I` everywhere else, and an avatar is not the place to get a name wrong. Pass what should be drawn. Two letters of it are kept, without the spaces between them. How a name is shortened is the app's to say, and its language's.

The initials and the icon are a share of the avatar, so one of any size keeps its proportions, whether the size is given as `size` or by `modifier`. The initials keep that share at every font scale: an avatar does not grow with the text around it, and letters that grew would leave it.

With a `contentDescription` the avatar is announced as an image by that name. Without one it is hidden from screen readers, which is right beside a name they already read. The initials are never read out: they are what the description shortens. An avatar is drawn and not pressed. One that opens a profile goes inside what takes the press, a button or a list's row.

parameters.name: contentDescription
parameters.description: what a screen reader says for the avatar, usually the name it stands for, or null to hide the avatar from it.

parameters.name: modifier
parameters.description: the avatar's modifier. A size given here goes over `size`.

parameters.name: initials
parameters.description: the letters to draw, usually one or two. More than two are cut, and none leaves the `icon`.

parameters.name: icon
parameters.description: what is drawn where there are no initials: a person, a group, a company.

parameters.name: tone
parameters.description: the colour under the initials or the icon, and theirs. A picture covers it.

parameters.name: colors
parameters.description: this avatar's own colours, in place of its tone's: the ones it sets, with the tone's for the rest.

parameters.name: style
parameters.description: this call's own style: over every enclosing one and under the density. Only the fields it sets change, on every platform.

parameters.name: size
parameters.description: the avatar's width and height: the style's unless given.

parameters.name: tagKey
parameters.description: the avatar's automation key: it is `Avatar_<tagKey>`, and is tagged only when given one.

parameters.name: image
parameters.description: a picture that fills the avatar, over the initials or the icon. What it says of itself is not read: the avatar's description stands for both.

declarations.name: AvatarStyle
declarations.description:
`PantrixAvatar`'s geometry: how large it is, what its corners are, and how much of it the initials or the icon take.

An avatar is a circle on every platform, 40dp across on Android and iOS, as Material 3 has it beside a list's row, and 32dp on the desktop and the web, where a row is shorter. The initials are four tenths of it and the icon six: an icon fills its box less than a capital letter fills its line, and at these shares the two look alike.

The two shares are fractions of the avatar and not sizes of their own, so an avatar given a size, a large one at the top of a profile or a small one in a comment, keeps its proportions without a second style.

None of the four follows the density: an avatar is a row's identity, and a denser row does not make it smaller.

parameters.name: size
parameters.description: The avatar's width and height.

parameters.name: shape
parameters.description: The avatar's corners: the round end of the brand's shape scale, a circle, unless a brand or a theme asks for a step of it or a shape of its own.

parameters.name: initialsScale
parameters.description: The height the initials are set in, as a fraction of the avatar's shorter side.

parameters.name: iconScale
parameters.description: The icon's width and height, as a fraction of the avatar's shorter side.

declarations.name: AvatarColors
declarations.description:
What `PantrixAvatar` is painted with, for an avatar that does not take its tone's colours: a colour that is set is used, and one that is left out stays the tone's.

```
PantrixAvatar(
    contentDescription = team.name,
    initials = team.initials,
    colors = AvatarColors(container = team.color, content = team.onColor)
)
```

A fill given here that is one of the theme's own colours brings the colour the theme pairs with it for what is drawn on it, unless that is given too. A fill no role has does not: what reads on it is the caller's to give.

parameters.name: container
parameters.description: The fill under the initials or the icon, which a picture covers. The `color` of the tone's role.

parameters.name: content
parameters.description: The initials or the icon: the colour that reads on `container`. The `onColor` of the tone's role.

declarations.name: BadgeTone
declarations.signature: enum class BadgeTone
declarations.description:
How a badge is coloured: one of the theme's colour roles, so a brand changes every badge at once.

A badge is filled in every tone, from the role's `color` and `onColor`. It is a mark a few millimetres across with no room to be subtle: on the role's pale `container` a number reads as a stray digit and not as a badge, and a dot has nothing on it to hold a contrast with at all.

entries.name: Primary
entries.description: The brand's colour: a count that is good news, or one to notice without alarm.

entries.name: Info
entries.description: Something worth knowing: a count of items, a new entry.

entries.name: Success
entries.description: Something that worked or is well: a finished job, someone who is online.

entries.name: Warning
entries.description: Something to look at before it becomes a problem.

entries.name: Danger
entries.description: Something that needs attention: unread messages, failures. The default, as each platform's own badge is.

entries.name: Neutral
entries.description: A count with no urgency at all.

declarations.name: BadgeOverlap
declarations.signature: enum class BadgeOverlap
declarations.description: How a badge lies on what it is the badge of, in a `PantrixBadgedBox`.

entries.name: Rectangular
entries.description: On the box around it: its corner or its edge. For an icon, a label, a picture with corners. The default.

entries.name: Circular
entries.description: On the circle inside that box. For a round avatar, whose own edge is well inside the corners of its box: a badge on the corner would hang beside it and not on it.

declarations.name: PantrixBadge
declarations.signature:
@Composable
fun PantrixBadge(
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    count: Int? = null,
    maxCount: Int = 99,
    tone: BadgeTone = BadgeTone.Danger,
    colors: BadgeColors? = null,
    style: BadgeStyle? = null,
    contentDescription: String? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null
)
declarations.description:
A count or a status dot, usually put on another element with `PantrixBadgedBox`.

Without a `count` the badge is a dot. With one it is a pill that grows with its number, and a circle around one digit. Above `maxCount` it reads that number and a plus, `99+` by default, and stops growing. Zero is drawn as `0`: taking a badge away when there is nothing to count is the caller's to do. A count below zero is drawn as `0` too: a number a server got wrong is no reason to bring an app down.

The number is set in the theme's caption type and grows with the font scale, and the pill with it. It is always at least as wide as it is tall.

Without a `contentDescription` the badge is hidden from screen readers. A lone "3" read out after an icon says nothing, so what the badge sits on should say it, "Inbox, 3 unread", and a badge says something of its own only where it stands alone. A badge is not pressed, and has no touch target.

parameters.name: modifier
parameters.description: the badge's modifier.

parameters.name: count
parameters.description: the number to show, or null for a dot.

parameters.name: maxCount
parameters.description: the largest number that is written out. It has to be positive.

parameters.name: tone
parameters.description: the colour role the badge is filled from.

parameters.name: colors
parameters.description: this badge's own colours, in place of its tone's: the ones it sets, with the tone's for the rest.

parameters.name: style
parameters.description: this call's own style: over every enclosing one and under the density. Only the fields it sets change, on every platform.

parameters.name: contentDescription
parameters.description: what a screen reader says for the badge, or null to hide the badge from it.

parameters.name: tagKey
parameters.description: the badge's automation key: it is `Badge_<tagKey>`, and is tagged only when given one.

declarations.name: PantrixBadgedBox
declarations.signature:
@Composable
fun PantrixBadgedBox(
    badge: @Composable () -> Unit,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    alignment: Alignment = Alignment.TopEnd,
    overlap: BadgeOverlap = BadgeOverlap.Rectangular,
    content: @Composable () -> Unit
)
declarations.description:
Puts `badge` on `content`, with its middle on a corner of it, and takes no room for it.

The box is as large as `content`. The badge hangs over its edge and pushes nothing aside, so a badge that comes and goes moves nothing around it. A parent that clips cuts what hangs over. The badge is as large as its number, whatever it sits on, and a baseline of `content` is the box's, so a badged label lines up with the text beside it. A badge wider than it is tall has its round end on the corner and grows away from the content, as the badge of a tab does on each platform: three digits cover no more of an icon than one.

`alignment` says which corner, or which edge: the top corner where lines end by default, which is the top left in a right-to-left layout. `overlap` says what the corners are corners of. Put the box around the icon itself: the corner of something larger, such as a button with its touch target, is far from what is drawn.

parameters.name: badge
parameters.description: what is put on the content: usually a `PantrixBadge`. Nothing, where there is nothing to show.

parameters.name: modifier
parameters.description: the box's modifier.

parameters.name: alignment
parameters.description: where on `content` the middle of the badge is.

parameters.name: overlap
parameters.description: whether that is on the box around `content`, or on the circle in it.

parameters.name: content
parameters.description: what the badge belongs to.

declarations.name: BadgeStyle
declarations.description:
`PantrixBadge`'s geometry: a dot where there is nothing to count, and otherwise a pill that grows with its number.

The pill is 16dp tall and the dot 6dp across, as Material 3 has its large and its small badge, and a little larger on iOS, after the badge of its tab bar. The pill is as wide as it is tall at the least on every platform, so one digit sits in a circle.

The pill's height, its least width and its padding follow the density, since they are the room around the number. The dot does not: it is a mark, and a mark that shrank with a denser screen would be harder to see where there is more to look at.

parameters.name: dotSize
parameters.description: The dot's width and height.

parameters.name: height
parameters.description: The pill's height. A number set larger than it has room for, at a large font scale, makes the pill taller.

parameters.name: minWidth
parameters.description: The pill's least width. The pill is never narrower than it is tall, whatever this says.

parameters.name: horizontalPadding
parameters.description: The room on each side of the number, which is what makes the pill wider than it is tall as the number grows.

declarations.name: BadgeColors
declarations.description:
What `PantrixBadge` is painted with, for a badge that does not take its tone's colours: a colour that is set is used, and one that is left out stays the tone's.

```
PantrixBadge(count = offers, colors = BadgeColors(container = brand, content = onBrand))
```

A fill given here that is one of the theme's own colours brings the colour the theme pairs with it for what is drawn on it, unless that is given too. A fill no role has does not: what reads on it is the caller's to give.

parameters.name: container
parameters.description: The badge's fill, and the whole of a dot. The `color` of the tone's role.

parameters.name: content
parameters.description: The number: the colour that reads on `container`. The `onColor` of the tone's role.

declarations.id: com.pantrixui.components.elements.button.PantrixButton(String, () -> Unit, Modifier, ButtonVariant, ButtonSize, Boolean, Boolean, Boolean, (@Composable () -> Unit)?, (@Composable () -> Unit)?, ButtonStyle?, Shape, ButtonColors, String?, FormState?, String?, MutableInteractionSource?)
declarations.name: PantrixButton
declarations.signature:
@Composable
fun PantrixButton(
    text: String,
    onClick: () -> Unit,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    variant: ButtonVariant = ButtonVariant.Solid,
    size: ButtonSize = ButtonSize.Medium,
    enabled: Boolean = true,
    loading: Boolean = false,
    fullWidth: Boolean = false,
    leadingIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null,
    trailingIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null,
    style: ButtonStyle? = null,
    shape: Shape = PantrixTheme.style(key = ButtonStyle, override = style).shape.toShape(),
    colors: ButtonColors = variant.colors(),
    contentDescription: String? = null,
    form: FormState? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null,
    interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null
)
declarations.description:
A button with a text label, the form most buttons take.

`variant` picks the colours and `size` the height, padding and label type. `style` overrides the theme's `ButtonStyle` for this button alone: its shape, pressed scale and per-size geometry. The height is the least the button is tall: where a reader's larger type makes the label taller than that, the button grows with it. A pointer over the button lays a light cover of its content colour on it, and a press a stronger one, so that a mouse shows what a click would press.

`loading` shows a spinner in place of `leadingIcon` and stops clicks, as a submitting `form` does. Given a `form`, a click validates it first: while a field is invalid, `onClick` is not called, and that field takes focus with an error haptic.

`contentDescription` is read in place of `text`, and not after it: give one only where the label alone does not say what the button does, as a "+" does not.

parameters.name: modifier
parameters.description: the button's modifier.

parameters.name: enabled
parameters.description: whether the button can be pressed: one that cannot is drawn in the disabled colours and does nothing.

parameters.name: fullWidth
parameters.description: true stretches the button across the width it is given, its content in the middle.

parameters.name: trailingIcon
parameters.description: what stands after the label: an arrow, or a count.

parameters.name: shape
parameters.description: the button's corners: by default the resolved style's. Given here, it wins over `style`'s.

parameters.name: colors
parameters.description: this call's own colours, in place of `variant`'s.

parameters.name: tagKey
parameters.description: the button's automation key: the button is `Button_<tagKey>`, and without one a key of where it is called. Visible text is never the key.

parameters.name: interactionSource
parameters.description: the button's interactions, hoisted: its focus, its hover and its presses. It keeps a source of its own when this is null.

declarations.id: com.pantrixui.components.elements.button.PantrixButton(() -> Unit, String, Modifier, ButtonVariant, ButtonSize, Boolean, Boolean, Boolean, ButtonStyle?, Shape, ButtonColors, FormState?, String?, MutableInteractionSource?, @Composable RowScope.() -> Unit)
declarations.name: PantrixButton
declarations.signature:
@Composable
fun PantrixButton(
    onClick: () -> Unit,
    contentDescription: String,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    variant: ButtonVariant = ButtonVariant.Solid,
    size: ButtonSize = ButtonSize.Medium,
    enabled: Boolean = true,
    loading: Boolean = false,
    fullWidth: Boolean = false,
    style: ButtonStyle? = null,
    shape: Shape = PantrixTheme.style(ButtonStyle, style).shape.toShape(),
    colors: ButtonColors = variant.colors(),
    form: FormState? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null,
    interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null,
    content: @Composable RowScope.() -> Unit
)
declarations.description:
Slot form, for content a string cannot express.

`contentDescription` is required here rather than optional, because without the text parameter there is nothing left for a screen reader to fall back on. It is all a screen reader hears of the button: what is in `content` is drawn, and not read after it. `style` is the text form's.

parameters.name: onClick
parameters.description: what a press does. Given a `form`, it is called once the form is valid.

parameters.name: modifier
parameters.description: the button's modifier.

parameters.name: variant
parameters.description: the button's prominence, and the colours that come with it.

parameters.name: size
parameters.description: the button's height, its padding and the type its label is set in.

parameters.name: enabled
parameters.description: whether the button can be pressed: one that cannot is drawn in the disabled colours and does nothing.

parameters.name: loading
parameters.description: whether the button takes no press while what it began is under way, and tells a screen reader it is loading. What `content` shows meanwhile is the caller's.

parameters.name: fullWidth
parameters.description: true stretches the button across the width it is given, its content in the middle.

parameters.name: shape
parameters.description: the button's corners: by default the resolved style's. Given here, it wins over `style`'s.

parameters.name: colors
parameters.description: this call's own colours, in place of `variant`'s.

parameters.name: form
parameters.description: the form the button submits: a press validates it first, and the button takes no press while it is submitting.

parameters.name: tagKey
parameters.description: the button's automation key: the button is `Button_<tagKey>`, and without one a key of where it is called. Visible text is never the key.

parameters.name: interactionSource
parameters.description: the button's interactions, hoisted: its focus, its hover and its presses. It keeps a source of its own when this is null.

declarations.name: ButtonVariant
declarations.signature: enum class ButtonVariant
declarations.description:
How prominent a button is.

Four of them are a ladder rather than a menu, each one quieter than the one above it: `Solid` is filled in the role's colour, `Soft` in the role's pale container, `Outline` has no fill and an edge, and `Text` has neither. Reading them in that order, which is not the order they are declared in, is how to pick one: go down until the button stops competing with what is around it.

`Subtle` stands on `Soft`'s rung: the same pale fill, with a faint edge in its content colour that keeps the button's shape where the fill alone barely parts from the background.

`Destructive` is not a rung. It says what the button *does*, which is why it is the only variant that changes the colour role, and why it sits at the bottom out of the ladder's reach.

entries.name: Solid
entries.description: The one primary action on a screen. The default.

entries.name: Outline
entries.description: Secondary on a busy surface, where a filled shape would compete.

entries.name: Soft
entries.description: Secondary, still clearly a button: a pale fill in the role's container colour.

entries.name: Subtle
entries.description: `Soft` with a faint edge, so the shape still shows where the pale fill alone would fade into what is around it.

entries.name: Text
entries.description: Tertiary: toolbar actions, "cancel". No surface at all.

entries.name: Destructive
entries.description: Destructive and irreversible. Never the only action in a dialog.

declarations.name: ButtonSize
declarations.signature: enum class ButtonSize
declarations.description:
Five heights, stepping by 8dp from 24 to 56.

`Medium` is the default and the one to reach for. The two ends are for the places a default would be wrong rather than for a general sense of scale: `ExtraSmall` inside a dense table row or beside a field, `ExtraLarge` as the single action a phone screen is built around.

entries.name: ExtraSmall
entries.description: 24dp tall: inside a dense table row, or beside a field.

entries.name: Small
entries.description: 32dp tall.

entries.name: Medium
entries.description: 40dp tall: the default, and the one to reach for.

entries.name: Large
entries.description: 48dp tall.

entries.name: ExtraLarge
entries.description: 56dp tall: the single action a phone screen is built around.

declarations.name: ButtonColors
declarations.description: What a button is painted with. `ButtonVariant.colors` gives a variant's in `primary`, and `PantrixColor.buttonColors` the same prominences in any role.

parameters.name: container
parameters.description: The fill; transparent for an outline or a text button.

parameters.name: content
parameters.description: The label's and the icon's colour.

parameters.name: border

declarations.description:
The variant's colours, from the theme's `primary` role, and `danger` for `ButtonVariant.Destructive`. The default `colors` of `PantrixButton`; `ButtonColors` of your own override it for one button.

`ButtonVariant.Outline` and `ButtonVariant.Text` have no fill of their own. On a fill that says what is written on it, a top bar of the brand's colour, they are written as it is, their edge too, where the theme's `primary` would hardly be told from the fill. On the theme's own grounds they keep `primary`.

declarations.name: buttonColors
declarations.signature: fun PantrixColor.buttonColors(variant: ButtonVariant = ButtonVariant.Solid): ButtonColors
declarations.description:
The same prominences, drawn from any role instead of from `primary`.

`ButtonVariant.Destructive.colors()` stays the way to say "this deletes something", and it keeps its own meaning: a variant is what the button *is*. This is only what it is *painted with*, for a button that carries a status — "Mark as paid" in `success`, "Retry" in `warning` — so `ButtonVariant.Destructive` here paints exactly like `ButtonVariant.Solid` rather than quietly ignoring the role it was handed.

`ButtonVariant.Subtle` is `ButtonVariant.Soft` with an edge here too, and the edge is all that tells the two apart. It is drawn in the role's own colour at full strength, where the default draws `primary.onContainer` at 30%.

```
PantrixButton(
    text = stringResource(Res.string.mark_paid),
    onClick = onMarkPaid,
    colors = PantrixTheme.colors.success.buttonColors(),
    tagKey = "mark_paid"
)
```

declarations.name: PantrixButtonGroup
declarations.signature:
@Composable
fun PantrixButtonGroup(
    buttons: List<GroupButton>,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    variant: ButtonVariant = ButtonVariant.Outline,
    size: ButtonSize = ButtonSize.Medium,
    orientation: Orientation = Orientation.Horizontal,
    attached: Boolean = true,
    equalWidth: Boolean = false,
    enabled: Boolean = true,
    style: ButtonGroupStyle? = null,
    shape: Shape = PantrixTheme.style(ButtonGroupStyle, style).shape.toShape(),
    colors: ButtonColors = variant.colors(),
    tagKey: String? = null
)
declarations.description:
A group of buttons: a few actions of the same rank, drawn as one control or set apart at one distance.

Attached, which it is unless told otherwise, the buttons touch: the group has one shape, of which each button keeps the corners at its own end, one edge around it where its colours have one, and a line between each two buttons. Apart, they are the same buttons a gap from each other, each with its own shape and edge, as the actions under a dialog are.

Each button is a button like any other: it is one stop for Tab, says its own name and role to a screen reader, shows its own focus ring, and reports its own press, as a `Button` or an `IconButton` event. The group reports nothing and chooses nothing: no button stays selected. For a choice of one among several, where one stays chosen, use a segment button, which says which one is.

In a row the buttons are as wide as what they say. In a room too narrow for that the short ones stay whole and the long ones share what is left; with `equalWidth` they all share the width the group is given. In a column they are all as wide as the widest of them.

An attached group keeps the platform's touch target around itself, and each of its buttons is at least as long as that along the group: beside its neighbours, a button has no room of its own to be reached in.

parameters.name: buttons
parameters.description: the buttons, in order. An empty list draws nothing.

parameters.name: modifier
parameters.description: the group's modifier, outside the touch target an attached group reserves.

parameters.name: variant
parameters.description: the variant of every button that has none of its own.

parameters.name: size
parameters.description: the size of every button, so that they line up.

parameters.name: orientation
parameters.description: `Orientation.Horizontal` for a row, `Orientation.Vertical` for a column of actions.

parameters.name: attached
parameters.description: true draws the buttons as one control. False sets them the style's gap apart.

parameters.name: equalWidth
parameters.description: true gives every button of a row the same share of the width the group is given; in a room without an end, the width of the widest. A column's buttons are as wide as each other whatever this says.

parameters.name: enabled
parameters.description: false disables every button.

parameters.name: style
parameters.description: this call's own style: over every enclosing one and under the density. Only the fields it sets change, on every platform. The buttons keep the button's own style for their sizes.

parameters.name: shape
parameters.description: the group's shape: attached, the shape of the whole group; apart, of each button.

parameters.name: colors
parameters.description: what the buttons are painted with, each one that has neither colours nor a variant of its own. Attached, the border's colour is the group's one edge, and the colour of the lines between the buttons.

parameters.name: tagKey
parameters.description: the group's automation key: the group is `ButtonGroup_<tagKey>`, and its buttons are named inside it, `ButtonGroup_<tagKey>.Button_<key>`, so that two groups with the same actions are told apart.

declarations.name: ButtonGroupStyle
declarations.description:
`PantrixButtonGroup`'s geometry: the shape of the group, the line between two buttons that are attached, and the room between two that are not.

The shape is the button's own on every platform, so that a group and a button beside it have the same corners: a pill on Android, on desktop and on the web, a rounded rectangle on iOS. Attached, it is the shape of the whole group, and each button keeps the corners at its own end of it. Apart, every button has it whole.

Only the gap follows the density, since it is the room between the buttons. The line and the shape do not.

parameters.name: shape
parameters.description: The group's shape: a step of the brand's shape scale, or a fixed shape.

parameters.name: dividerWidth
parameters.description: The width of the line between two attached buttons.

parameters.name: gap
parameters.description: The room between two buttons that are not attached.

declarations.signature:
@Composable
fun PantrixCheckbox(
    checked: Boolean,
    onCheckedChange: ((Boolean) -> Unit)?,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    enabled: Boolean = true,
    label: String? = null,
    supportingText: String? = null,
    error: Boolean = false,
    style: CheckboxStyle? = null,
    colors: CheckboxColors? = null,
    contentDescription: String? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null,
    interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null,
    controlPosition: ControlPosition = ControlPosition.Start
)
declarations.description:
A checkbox: a box that is checked or not, and the label it is the box of.

The box, the label and the supporting text are one target. A press anywhere on them toggles the box, since on a phone the words are most of what a finger can hit, and a screen reader hears one checkbox, named by its label, that says whether it is checked. The box stands on the label's first line, however many lines the label and the supporting text run to. The row takes the platform's touch target, small as the box is.

Without `onCheckedChange` the checkbox is read-only: it takes no press and no focus, and still says its name and its state. `error` turns the box and the supporting text to the danger role and is announced. Checking and unchecking draw the tick on and off while the fill fades in and out: at once under reduced motion.

parameters.name: checked
parameters.description: whether the box is checked.

parameters.name: onCheckedChange
parameters.description: called with the value the user asks for, the opposite of `checked`. The checkbox changes nothing by itself: it is checked when `checked` says so. Null makes it read-only.

parameters.name: modifier
parameters.description: the row's modifier.

parameters.name: enabled
parameters.description: whether the checkbox can be toggled. One that cannot is drawn in the disabled colours and says so.

parameters.name: label
parameters.description: the text beside the box: part of the target, and the checkbox's name for a screen reader.

parameters.name: supportingText
parameters.description: help under the label, in a smaller type: the message, while `error` is true.

parameters.name: error
parameters.description: whether the value is wrong: the box and the supporting text turn to the danger role, and a screen reader is told the input is invalid.

parameters.name: style
parameters.description: this call's own style: over every enclosing one and under the density. Only the fields it sets change, on every platform.

parameters.name: colors
parameters.description: this checkbox's own colours: the ones it sets, with the theme's for the rest. A disabled box and one in error keep the theme's.

parameters.name: contentDescription
parameters.description: what a screen reader says for the checkbox: its name where it has no `label`, as in a table's row, or in place of the label.

parameters.name: tagKey
parameters.description: the checkbox's automation key: the row is `Checkbox_<tagKey>`. A toggle is reported as a `Checkbox` event that carries the state the box had, and never its label.

parameters.name: interactionSource
parameters.description: the checkbox's interactions, hoisted. It keeps a source of its own when this is null.

parameters.name: controlPosition
parameters.description: where the box stands: before the label, as a list of choices has it, or after it. After it, the box is at the end of the width the row is given, `Modifier.fillMaxWidth()` lining it up with the others, or right after the label where the row is given none; the label wraps in what the box leaves.

It is an overload of its own and not a parameter of the controlled form, so that a value and a field cannot both be given.

declarations.name: CheckboxStyle
declarations.description:
`PantrixCheckbox`'s box: its size, its corners and its edge.

The box is a square with the small step of the shape scale for its corners, 4dp by default, on every platform. It is 18dp, as Material 3 has it, and 22dp on iOS. iOS has no checkbox of its own, and its box is not round there either: a circle is a radio button, and an empty one would say that only one of the boxes can be chosen.

None of the three follows the density: a box, its corners and its edge are not air. The space between the box and its label does, since it comes from the theme's spacing. A checkbox's colours are not part of its style: they come from its state, and from `CheckboxColors` where a checkbox has its own.

parameters.name: size
parameters.description: The box's width and height, its edge included.

parameters.name: shape
parameters.description: The box's corners: a step of the brand's shape scale, so a brand with square corners has square boxes.

parameters.name: strokeWidth
parameters.description: How thick the box's edge is, and the tick's and the dash's line.

declarations.name: CheckboxColors
declarations.description:
What `PantrixCheckbox` is painted with, for a checkbox that does not take the theme's: a colour that is set is used, and one that is left out stays the theme's role. A product gives the colours it changes and no others:

```
PantrixCheckbox(
    checked = accepted,
    onCheckedChange = { accepted = it },
    label = stringResource(Res.string.accept_terms),
    colors = CheckboxColors(checked = brand, checkmark = onBrand)
)
```

They are the colours of a checkbox that can be toggled and is not in error. A disabled one is drawn in the theme's disabled roles and one in error in its danger role, whatever is given here, so that both look the same across a product.

A fill given here that is one of the theme's own colours brings the colour the theme pairs with it for what is drawn on it, unless that is given too. A fill no role has does not: what reads on it is the caller's to give.

parameters.name: checked
parameters.description: The box's fill when it is checked or indeterminate. The theme's `primary`.

parameters.name: checkmark
parameters.description: The tick and the dash on the fill: the colour that reads on `checked`. The primary role's `onColor`.

parameters.name: border
parameters.description: The box's edge when it is not checked. The theme's `borderStrong`: an empty box is nothing but its edge.

declarations.description:
A chip: a compact action, or an item the user put in and can take out again, such as a recipient, a tag or an applied filter.

It is as tall as its style says and as wide as its icon, its label and its remove button need, with the platform's touch target reserved around it. A label too long for the room the chip is given ends in an ellipsis, and the remove button stays whole beside it. A label set larger than the chip, at a large font scale, makes the chip taller. In a chip made wider than it needs, the icon and the label are in the middle, as a button's are, and the remove button is at the end.

With `onClick` the chip is a button, named by its label. Without, it only shows a value: one item for a screen reader, which takes no press and no focus, and keeps its remove button when `onRemove` is given.

`onRemove` puts a remove button at the chip's end: a target of its own, as tall as the chip, that a screen reader hears with the label, "Remove Kotlin", so that the buttons of a row can be told apart. The chip does not take itself out: the callback does.

parameters.name: label
parameters.description: the chip's text, and its name for a screen reader.

parameters.name: onClick
parameters.description: called when the chip is pressed. Null makes a chip that only shows a value.

parameters.name: modifier
parameters.description: the chip's modifier, outside the touch target it reserves.

parameters.name: leadingIcon
parameters.description: an icon before the label, in the style's icon size.

parameters.name: onRemove
parameters.description: called when the remove button is pressed. Null leaves the button out.

parameters.name: enabled
parameters.description: whether the chip and its remove button can be pressed. A chip that cannot is drawn in the disabled colours and says so.

parameters.name: style
parameters.description: this call's own style: over every enclosing one and under the density. Only the fields it sets change, on every platform.

parameters.name: colors
parameters.description: this chip's own colours: the ones it sets, with the theme's for the rest. A disabled chip keeps the theme's.

parameters.name: tagKey
parameters.description: the chip's automation key: the chip is `Chip_<tagKey>` and its remove button `ChipRemove_<tagKey>`. A press is reported as a `Chip` event, `click` or `remove`, which never carries the label.

parameters.name: interactionSource
parameters.description: the chip's interactions, hoisted. It keeps a source of its own when this is null, and the remove button always has its own.

parameters.name: colors

declarations.name: ChipStyle
declarations.description:
`PantrixChip`'s geometry.

An icon stands nearer the chip's edge than text does: on a side that has one, `iconPadding` is the room to the edge in place of `horizontalPadding`. It is Material 3's rule, kept on every platform.

On Android the numbers are Material 3's: 32dp tall with corners of 8dp, the medium step of the shape scale. iOS has no chip of its own; it takes the height of a small button, so the two line up in a row, and the pill a Pantrix control has. Desktop and the web are a step tighter, for a pointer.

An icon goes by the buttons': a small button's 20dp on Android and on iOS, where the chip is as tall as one, and 18dp in the chip of 30dp that the desktop and the web have. On every platform that is the largest the chip has room for: the remove button's focus ring goes around the cross, inside the chip, and in high contrast it reaches 6dp past it.

The height and the two paddings follow the density, since they are the room around the label. The icon's size, the edge's width and the shape do not.

parameters.name: shape
parameters.description: The chip's shape: a step of the brand's shape scale, or a fixed shape.

parameters.name: height
parameters.description: The chip's height. A label set larger than it has room for, at a large font scale, makes the chip taller.

parameters.name: horizontalPadding

declarations.name: ChipColors

What `PantrixChip` is painted with, for a chip that does not take the theme's: a colour that is set is used, and one that is left out stays the theme's role. A product gives the colours it changes and no others:

```

    selected = inStock,
    onSelectedChange = { inStock = it },
    colors = ChipColors(selectedContainer = brand, selectedContent = onBrand)
)
```

They are the colours of a chip that can be pressed. A disabled one is drawn in the theme's disabled roles whatever is given here, so that a disabled chip looks the same across a product.

A fill given here that is one of the theme's own colours brings the colour the theme pairs with it for what is drawn on it, unless that is given too. A fill no role has does not: what reads on it is the caller's to give.
