declarations.name: PantrixFileDrop
declarations.signature:
@Composable
fun PantrixFileDrop(
    onFiles: (List<PantrixFile>) -> Unit,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    accept: List<PantrixFileType> = listOf(PantrixFileType.Any),
    multiple: Boolean = false,
    maxSize: Long? = null,
    onRejected: (List<RejectedFile>) -> Unit = {},
    label: String? = null,
    supportingText: String? = null,
    enabled: Boolean = true,
    error: Boolean = false,
    picker: FilePicker = rememberFilePicker(),
    interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null,
    style: FileDropStyle? = null,
    colors: FileDropColors? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null
)
declarations.description:
Somewhere to give the app a file: a zone with a dashed edge that opens the platform's picker when it is pressed, and takes the files dropped on it from the platform's files, another app or another window.

The press is the way in on every platform, and the only one where nothing is dragged in: a phone, a keyboard, a screen reader. The zone says so in its words, which put the drop first under a pointer, on the desktop and the web, and the picker first on a phone. Where only pictures are taken (`PantrixFileType.Images`), Android and iOS open their photo picker.

What is chosen or dropped is screened before the app is handed it: a file of a kind not in `accept`, one larger than `maxSize`, and, where only one is taken, every one after the first go to `onRejected` with the reason, and the rest to `onFiles`. The zone keeps nothing: what was taken is the app's to list, with `PantrixFileItem`s under the zone, and what was not is the app's to say, in `supportingText` with `error`. A screen reader is told politely how many files the zone took and how many it did not.

Nothing is read here: a `PantrixFile` reads its bytes when the app asks it to, which a large file should be read for off the screen's work, and sent where it goes as it is read.

```
PantrixFileDrop(
    onFiles = { files -> attachments += files },
    accept = listOf(PantrixFileType.Pdf),
    multiple = true,
    maxSize = 10_000_000,
    onRejected = { refused = it },
    supportingText = stringResource(Res.string.pdf_up_to_10_mb),
    tagKey = "attachments"
)
```

parameters.name: onFiles
parameters.description: handed the files the zone took, at least one, in the order they came.

parameters.name: modifier
parameters.description: the zone's modifier, with its supporting text. The zone fills the width it is given.

parameters.name: accept
parameters.description: the kinds of file the zone takes. The picker shows only these, where the platform's can filter.

parameters.name: multiple
parameters.description: whether the zone takes more than one file at a time.

parameters.name: maxSize
parameters.description: the most bytes a file the zone takes may have, or null for any size.

parameters.name: onRejected
parameters.description: handed the files the zone did not take, each with why, at least one.

parameters.name: label
parameters.description: what the zone says first, in place of the platform's words.

parameters.name: supportingText
parameters.description: a line under the zone: what it takes and how large, or what was wrong.

parameters.name: enabled
parameters.description: whether the zone takes anything: a press or a drop. A zone that does not is drawn faint.

parameters.name: error
parameters.description: whether the zone shows that what it was given was not right: its edge and its supporting text in the danger colour. A screen reader hears the supporting text as the error.

parameters.name: picker
parameters.description: what a press opens: the platform's own picker, or a test's.

parameters.name: interactionSource
parameters.description: the zone's interactions: its press, its hover and its focus.

parameters.name: style
parameters.description: this call's own style: over every enclosing one and under the density. Only the fields it sets change, on every platform.

parameters.name: colors
parameters.description: this zone's own colours: the ones it sets, with the theme's for the rest.

parameters.name: tagKey
parameters.description: the zone's automation key: it is `FileDrop_<tagKey>`.

declarations.name: FileDropStyle
declarations.description:
`PantrixFileDrop`'s geometry: the zone, its dashed edge and what stands in it.

No platform has a drop zone of its own. The zone is tall enough to be a target from across a screen, taller on a phone, where a thumb presses it, than under a pointer; its corners are a card's, and its edge is dashed: a solid edge reads as a card, a dashed one as a place to put something.

The least height, the room inside, the gaps and the dashes' gaps follow the density. The edge's width, the dashes' length, the corners and the icon do not.

parameters.name: shape
parameters.description: The zone's corners: a step of the brand's shape scale, or a fixed shape.

parameters.name: minHeight
parameters.description: The least height of the zone. A larger type makes it taller.

parameters.name: padding
parameters.description: The room between the zone's edge and what stands in it.

parameters.name: borderWidth
parameters.description: The width of the dashed edge.

parameters.name: dashLength
parameters.description: The length of each of the edge's dashes.

parameters.name: dashGap
parameters.description: The room between two dashes.

parameters.name: iconSize
parameters.description: The width and height of the icon over the zone's words.

parameters.name: gap
parameters.description: Between the icon and the words, and between the two lines of words.

declarations.name: FileDropColors
declarations.description:
What a `PantrixFileDrop` is painted with, in place of the theme's colours: a colour that is set is used, and one that is left out stays the theme's.

A `container` given here that is one of the theme's role colours brings the colour the theme pairs with it for what is written in the zone, unless `content` is given too, and an `overContainer` brings its pair for the zone something is dragged over, unless `overContent` is given. A fill no role has does not: what reads on it is the caller's to give.

parameters.name: container
parameters.description: The zone's fill. The theme's `surface`.

parameters.name: content
parameters.description: The zone's first line and its icon. The theme's `textPrimary`, or the colour a role's fill given as `container` gives what stands on it.

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: The second line, the press that opens the picker, as a link is. The primary role's `color` on the theme's own grounds, and `content` on another fill.

parameters.name: border
parameters.description: The dashed edge. The theme's `border`, `borderHover` under a pointer, on its own grounds; a share of `content` on another fill, as a line on a fill is.

parameters.name: overContainer
parameters.description: The zone's fill while something is dragged over it. The primary role's `container`.

parameters.name: overContent
parameters.description: What is written in it then. The primary role's `onContainer`.

parameters.name: overBorder
parameters.description: The edge then. The primary role's `color`.

parameters.name: error
parameters.description: The edge and the supporting text of a zone that shows an error. The danger role's `color`.

parameters.name: supporting
parameters.description: The supporting text under the zone. The theme's `textSecondary`.

declarations.name: FileItemStyle
declarations.description:
`PantrixFileItem`'s geometry: a row for a file the app took, with its icon, its name and size, and the button that takes it away.

The row is a list's row: as tall as one on each platform, 56dp on a phone, where a thumb presses its button, and 44dp under a pointer. Its corners and its edge are a card's, a step lower than the zone's on a phone.

The least height, the room inside, the gap and the progress bar's height follow the density. The edge's width, the corners and the icon do not.

parameters.name: shape
parameters.description: The row's corners.

parameters.name: minHeight
parameters.description: The least height of the row. A larger type, a progress bar or an error makes it taller.

parameters.name: horizontalPadding
parameters.description: The room between the row's sides and what it holds.

parameters.name: verticalPadding
parameters.description: The room above and below what it holds.

parameters.name: borderWidth
parameters.description: The width of the row's edge.

parameters.name: iconSize
parameters.description: The width and height of the file's icon.

parameters.name: gap
parameters.description: Between the icon, the words and the button, and between the words and the progress bar.

parameters.name: progressHeight
parameters.description: The height of the progress bar under the words.

declarations.name: PantrixFileItem
declarations.signature:
@Composable
fun PantrixFileItem(
    name: String,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    size: Long? = null,
    onRemove: (() -> Unit)? = null,
    progress: Float? = null,
    error: String? = null,
    icon: ImageVector = PantrixIcons.File,
    enabled: Boolean = true,
    style: FileItemStyle? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null
)
declarations.description:
A file the app took, in a row: its icon, its name, its size or what went wrong with it, how far it is sent, and the button that takes it away. The rows stand under a `PantrixFileDrop`, each for a file the app keeps.

A long name is cut in its middle, so that its start and its extension both show: `Quarterly rep….pdf`. The size is written as the language writes one, `1,2 MB` in Turkish; an `error` stands in its place, in the danger colour, and the row's edge turns that colour too. A `progress` draws a bar under the words, filled from the start of the reading direction, and a screen reader hears it as one.

A screen reader hears the row as one thing, its name and its size or error, and the button apart from it, named for what it removes: `Remove report.pdf`.

```
PantrixFileItem(name = file.name, size = file.size, onRemove = { attachments -= file }, progress = sent[file])
```

declarations.name: FormField
declarations.signature: class FormField<T>
declarations.description:
One field in a form: its value, its rules, and whether it is currently in error.

`id` doubles as the component's automation tag, so a form-bound component needs no `tagKey` — the field already carries a stable, locale-independent name.

`@Stable` for the same reason as `FormState`: `value`, `error` and `touched` are snapshot state, and `isAttached` is bookkeeping that composition never reads.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The field's name in its form, and the automation tag of the component bound to it.

members.name: value
members.signature:
var value: T by mutableStateOf(initial)
    internal set
members.description: What the field holds now: its first value until the user gives another, and that value again after a reset.

members.name: error
members.signature:
var error: String? by mutableStateOf(null)
    private set
members.description:
The message to show, or null.

Stays null until the field has been `touched` or the form has been submitted. Showing "Required" the instant a form opens tells the user they have done something wrong before they have done anything at all.

members.name: touched
members.signature:
var touched: Boolean by mutableStateOf(false)
    internal set
members.description: True once the user has interacted with this field.

members.name: focusRequester
members.description: What the field is focused by: the component bound to it attaches it, and a submit that finds the field in error moves the focus there.

members.name: onValueChange
members.description: Called by components on change. Re-validates only once the field has been touched.

parameters.name: newValue
parameters.description: the value the user has given the field.

members.name: onFocusLost
members.description: Called by components on blur. Marks touched and validates, which is the usual moment to show an error.

members.name: validate
members.description: Runs every rule and publishes the first failure. Returns true when the field is valid.

members.name: isValid
members.description: Whether the field would pass, without publishing an error the user has not earned yet.

members.name: reset
members.description: Puts the field back as it was before the user touched it: `newValue` as its value, and no error.

declarations.name: FormState
declarations.signature: class FormState
declarations.description:
A form's fields and its submission lifecycle.

Holds three things components would otherwise each reinvent, differently: which field to focus when validation fails, whether a submission is in flight, and what Enter does.

`@Stable` is a claim the compiler cannot prove but the class honours: everything a composable reads is snapshot state, and the one plain field — the submit handler — is never read during composition. Without it the compiler reports the class unstable, and the compiler-metrics gate rejects every component that takes a `form`.

members.name: fields
members.description: The form's fields, in the order they were declared: the first one in error takes the focus on a submit.

members.name: isSubmitting
members.signature:
var isSubmitting: Boolean by mutableStateOf(false)
    private set
members.description:
True while `submit` is running.

`PantrixButton(form = ...)` reads this for its loading state, so a form cannot be submitted twice by an impatient second tap — the disabled state comes from the same source of truth as the spinner rather than from a separate flag someone has to remember to set.

members.name: isValid
members.description: Whether every field currently passes, without marking anything touched.

members.name: validateAll
members.description:
Validates everything and marks every field touched, so errors become visible.

Touching on submit is what makes "press submit on an empty form" show all the errors at once rather than one per attempt.

members.name: focusFirstError
members.description:
Moves focus to the first field in error. Returns false when there is nothing to focus.

Scrolling a long form to the problem is the difference between a fixable error and a user staring at a submit button that does nothing. Skips fields whose component is not currently composed — requesting focus on a detached FocusRequester throws.

members.name: submit
members.description:
Validates, then runs `block` if everything passed.

Owns `isSubmitting` around the call so the flag cannot be left stuck on by an early return or an exception — the single most common bug in hand-written form submission.

members.name: reset
members.description: Starts the form over. Every field on screen goes back to its initial value, untouched and without an error, and is still validated. Fields that have left the screen are forgotten; one that comes back registers again.

members.name: requestSubmit
members.description: Invoked when a field reports that Enter was pressed.

Declares a field.

Remembered by `id`, so the value survives recomposition but a genuinely different field — a different row of a dynamic list — gets its own state.

Points Enter at a submit action.

The last registration wins, which matches what a user expects on a form with both "Save" and "Save and add another": Enter triggers the primary action, and the primary action is the one declared last in the footer.

A validation rule. Returns the error message, or null when the value is acceptable.

Rules carry their own message rather than an error code because the message has to be translated by whoever wrote the form — the library cannot know that a field called `code` wants "Enter the 6-digit code" rather than "Invalid input".

declarations.name: PantrixLink
declarations.signature:
@Composable
fun PantrixLink(
    text: String,
    onClick: () -> Unit,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    style: TextStyle = LocalPantrixTextStyle.current,
    color: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    enabled: Boolean = true,
    tagKey: String? = null,
    underline: LinkUnderline = LinkUnderline.Always
)
declarations.description:
A link on its own that runs `onClick`: `text` underlined in the primary colour, in a row as tall as the platform's minimum touch target, so that a touch above or under the text reaches it. The click is reported to the theme's analytics as a `Link` `click` event. When it is not `enabled`, it keeps its underline, in the disabled text colour, so that it still reads as a link, and does nothing.

`color` is the link's own colour where it is not the theme's `primary`: its text, and the tint under a pointer and a press. A disabled link keeps the theme's disabled text colour whatever is given. `style` is the base text unless given, `LocalPantrixTextStyle`, the type a `PantrixText` has by itself: a link beside a text is as large as the text.

parameters.name: modifier
parameters.description: the link's modifier.

parameters.name: tagKey
parameters.description: the link's automation key: the link is `Link_<tagKey>`, and without one a key of where it is called. Visible text is never the key.

parameters.name: underline
parameters.description: when the link is underlined: always unless told; `OnHover` for a link that stands apart from any sentence, underlined under a pointer and the keyboard's focus, and always where the platform is used by touch.

A link on its own that opens `url` with the platform's `UriHandler`: in the browser, or the app that handles the address.

Everything else is the other `PantrixLink`'s. The `click` event says the link is external, never which address it opens.

An address that nothing on the device can open is let go, as Compose lets go of its own text's links (`TextLinkScope`): the press does nothing, and the app goes on.

parameters.name: text
parameters.description: what the link says.

parameters.name: modifier
parameters.description: the link's modifier.

parameters.name: style
parameters.description: the link's type: `LocalPantrixTextStyle` unless given, so that a link beside a text is as large as the text.

parameters.name: color
parameters.description: the link's own colour, where it is not the theme's `primary`.

parameters.name: enabled
parameters.description: whether the link can be pressed: one that cannot keeps its underline, in the disabled text colour.

parameters.name: tagKey

parameters.name: underline
parameters.description: when the link is underlined, as the other `PantrixLink` has it.

declarations.name: LinkUnderline
declarations.signature: enum class LinkUnderline
declarations.description:
When a link is underlined: what tells it from the text around it besides its colour.

A link inside a sentence is underlined always: told apart by colour alone, it is lost on whoever cannot tell the two colours apart (WCAG 1.4.1). A link that stands apart, in a row of links or a breadcrumb's trail, is told apart by where it is, and may be underlined only under a pointer or the keyboard's focus. Where the platform is used by touch there is neither to show it, and it is underlined always.

entries.name: Always
entries.description: Underlined always: the default, and what a link in a sentence needs.

entries.name: OnHover
entries.description: Underlined under a pointer and while it holds the keyboard's focus, and always where the platform is used by touch: for a link that stands apart from any sentence.

declarations.name: PantrixRadioButton
declarations.signature:
@Composable
fun PantrixRadioButton(
    selected: Boolean,
    onClick: (() -> Unit)?,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    enabled: Boolean = true,
    label: String? = null,
    supportingText: String? = null,
    error: Boolean = false,
    style: RadioStyle? = null,
    colors: RadioColors? = null,
    contentDescription: String? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null,
    interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null,
    controlPosition: ControlPosition = ControlPosition.Start
)
declarations.description:
A radio button: a ring that is selected or not, and the label it is the ring of. One of several, of which one is chosen.

It is almost always used through `PantrixRadioGroup`, which lays the options out, moves the selection with the arrow keys and binds it to a form's field. On its own it is for options in a layout a group cannot make, such as a card for each: wrap them in `Modifier.selectableGroup()`, so that a screen reader hears them as one choice.

The ring, the label and the supporting text are one target. A press anywhere on them asks for the option, since on a phone the words are most of what a finger can hit, and a screen reader hears one radio button, named by its label, that says whether it is selected. The ring stands on the label's first line, however many lines the label and the supporting text run to. The row takes the platform's touch target, small as the ring is.

Without `onClick` the radio button is read-only: it takes no press and no focus, and still says its name and whether it is selected. `error` turns the ring and the supporting text to the danger role and is announced. Selecting grows the dot and turns the ring to the primary role's colour together, and unselecting takes both back: at once under reduced motion.

parameters.name: selected
parameters.description: whether this is the option chosen.

parameters.name: onClick
parameters.description: called when the user presses the radio button, selected already or not. The radio button changes nothing by itself: it is selected when `selected` says so. Null makes it read-only.

parameters.name: modifier
parameters.description: the row's modifier.

parameters.name: enabled
parameters.description: whether the radio button can be selected. One that cannot is drawn in the disabled colours and says so.

parameters.name: label
parameters.description: the text beside the ring: part of the target, and the radio button's name for a screen reader.

parameters.name: supportingText
parameters.description: help under the label, in a smaller type: the message, while `error` is true.

parameters.name: error
parameters.description: whether the choice is wrong or missing: the ring and the supporting text turn to the danger role, and a screen reader is told the input is invalid.

parameters.name: style
parameters.description: this call's own style: over every enclosing one and under the density. Only the fields it sets change, on every platform.

parameters.name: colors
parameters.description: this radio button's own colours: the ones it sets, with the theme's for the rest. A disabled ring and one in error keep the theme's.

parameters.name: contentDescription
parameters.description: what a screen reader says for the radio button: its name where it has no `label`, as in a card that is the option, or in place of the label.

parameters.name: tagKey
parameters.description: the radio button's automation key: the row is `RadioButton_<tagKey>`. A press is reported as a `RadioButton` event, and never by its label.

parameters.name: interactionSource
parameters.description: the radio button's interactions, hoisted. It keeps a source of its own when this is null.

parameters.name: controlPosition
parameters.description: where the ring stands: before the label, as a list of choices has it, or after it. After it, the ring is at the end of the width the row is given, `Modifier.fillMaxWidth()` lining it up with the others, or right after the label where the row is given none; the label wraps in what the ring leaves.

declarations.name: RadioOption
declarations.description: One option of `PantrixRadioGroup`: the value it stands for, its label, and a key for automation.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: What the group gives to its `onSelect` when the option is chosen, and compares with its `selected` by `==`.

parameters.name: label
parameters.description: The visible text, and the option's name for a screen reader.

parameters.name: supportingText
parameters.description: Written under the label in a smaller type, to say what the option is: a price, how long a delivery takes. It is part of the option's target and of what a screen reader says for it, and keeps its colour when the group is in error.

parameters.name: enabled
parameters.description: Whether the option can be selected. A press does nothing on one that cannot, and the arrow keys skip it.

parameters.name: tagKey
parameters.description: The option's automation key, the same in every language: the option is `RadioButton_<tagKey>`, or `RadioButton_<index>` without one, inside the tag of a group that has a key: `RadioGroup_plan.RadioButton_pro`.

declarations.id: com.pantrixui.components.elements.radiobutton.PantrixRadioGroup(List<RadioOption<T>>, T?, (T) -> Unit, Modifier, Orientation, Boolean, String?, String?, Boolean, RadioStyle?, RadioColors?, String?, ControlPosition)
declarations.name: PantrixRadioGroup
declarations.signature:
@Composable
fun <T> PantrixRadioGroup(
    options: List<RadioOption<T>>,
    selected: T?,
    onSelect: (T) -> Unit,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    orientation: Orientation = Orientation.Vertical,
    enabled: Boolean = true,
    label: String? = null,
    supportingText: String? = null,
    error: Boolean = false,
    style: RadioStyle? = null,
    colors: RadioColors? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null,
    controlPosition: ControlPosition = ControlPosition.Start
)
declarations.description:
A group of radio buttons: a choice of one among `options`, under a label, with help or an error's message below.

The options stand one under another, or side by side with `Orientation.Horizontal`: as many on a line as the width takes, and the rest on the next. Each is a `PantrixRadioButton`, with the ring on the first line of its label.

The group is one stop for Tab, on the selected option, as the radio group pattern of WAI-ARIA has it: the first option that can be selected, while none is. The arrow keys choose the next and the previous option, left and right the other way round in a right-to-left layout, wrapping around and skipping an option that is disabled. They choose and do not only move: while an option has the focus, the focus goes with the selection, whoever makes it, so that the option a screen reader is on is the one chosen. A press on an option takes the focus to it, where a press can.

For a screen reader each option is a radio button that says whether it is selected, in one group named by `label`. `error` is announced by the group, once, and turns every ring and the group's message to the danger role.

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: the options, in order.

parameters.name: selected
parameters.description: the value of the selected option. Null, or a value no option has, selects none.

parameters.name: onSelect
parameters.description: called with the value of the option the user chose, by a press or by the keys. The group selects nothing by itself: an option is selected when `selected` says so. A press on the option that is selected asks again, and an arrow key only ever asks for another option.

parameters.name: modifier
parameters.description: the group's modifier.

parameters.name: orientation
parameters.description: `Orientation.Vertical` for one option under another, `Orientation.Horizontal` for side by side.

parameters.name: enabled
parameters.description: false disables every option, and writes the label and the supporting text in the disabled text colour.

parameters.name: label
parameters.description: what the choice is, written over the options: the group's name for a screen reader.

parameters.name: supportingText
parameters.description: help under the options, in a smaller type: the message, while `error` is true.

parameters.name: error
parameters.description: whether the choice is wrong or missing: the rings and the supporting text turn to the danger role, and a screen reader is told the input is invalid.

parameters.name: style
parameters.description: this call's own style, the one every option is drawn with: over every enclosing one and under the density. Only the fields it sets change, on every platform.

parameters.name: colors
parameters.description: the colours every option is drawn in, where they are not the theme's: the ones set here, with the theme's for the rest. A disabled option and a group in error keep the theme's.

parameters.name: tagKey
parameters.description: the group's automation key: the group is `RadioGroup_<tagKey>`, and its options are named inside it, `RadioGroup_<tagKey>.RadioButton_<key>`, so that two groups with the same options are told apart. A choice is reported once, as a `RadioGroup` event that carries the option's index, and never its value or its label.

parameters.name: controlPosition
parameters.description: where each option's ring stands: before its label, or after it. After it, one under another, every option spans the group and the rings line up at its end; side by side, each ring follows its label.

declarations.id: com.pantrixui.components.elements.radiobutton.PantrixRadioGroup(FormField<T>, List<RadioOption<T>>, Modifier, Orientation, Boolean, String?, String?, RadioStyle?, RadioColors?, ControlPosition)
declarations.name: PantrixRadioGroup
declarations.signature:
@Composable
fun <T> PantrixRadioGroup(
    field: FormField<T>,
    options: List<RadioOption<T>>,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    orientation: Orientation = Orientation.Vertical,
    enabled: Boolean = true,
    label: String? = null,
    supportingText: String? = null,
    style: RadioStyle? = null,
    colors: RadioColors? = null,
    controlPosition: ControlPosition = ControlPosition.Start
)
declarations.description:
A radio group bound to a form's field: its selection, its error and its name come from `field`.

A choice changes the field and marks it touched, so a rule's message shows after the first choice, or when the form is submitted, and not on a form nobody has touched. While the field is in error the message takes the place of `supportingText`, rather than standing beside it. The field's id is the group's automation key, `RadioGroup_<id>`, with its options inside it, and the form can send the focus here when it is submitted with this field in error: it goes to the group's one stop.

A choice that has to be made is a field of a nullable value that starts at null, with `Rules.required`. Its options are options of the value itself: a `RadioOption<String>` is an option of a `FormField<String?>`.

It is an overload of its own and not a parameter of the controlled form, so that a selection and a field cannot both be given.

parameters.name: field
parameters.description: the field the group shows and changes.

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: the options, in order.

parameters.name: modifier
parameters.description: the group's modifier.

parameters.name: orientation
parameters.description: `Orientation.Vertical` for one option under another, `Orientation.Horizontal` for side by side.

parameters.name: enabled
parameters.description: false disables every option.

parameters.name: label
parameters.description: what the choice is, written over the options: the group's name for a screen reader.

parameters.name: supportingText
parameters.description: help under the options, while the field has no error to show there.

parameters.name: style
parameters.description: this call's own style, the one every option is drawn with: over every enclosing one and under the density. Only the fields it sets change, on every platform.

parameters.name: colors
parameters.description: the colours every option is drawn in, where they are not the theme's: the ones set here, with the theme's for the rest. A disabled option and a group in error keep the theme's.

parameters.name: controlPosition
parameters.description: where each option's ring stands: before its label, or after it. After it, one under another, every option spans the group and the rings line up at its end; side by side, each ring follows its label.

declarations.name: RadioStyle
declarations.description:
`PantrixRadioButton`'s ring and the dot in it: how large each is, and how thick the ring.

The ring is 20dp around a 10dp dot, as Material 3 has it, and 22dp around a 12dp dot on iOS, where a checkbox is 22dp too. iOS has no radio button of its own: it marks the one chosen row of a list with a tick. Pantrix draws the same ring on every platform, so that a choice of one looks like one wherever it is made.

None of the three follows the density: a ring, its dot and its line are not air. The space between the ring and its label does, since it comes from the theme's spacing. A radio button's colours are not part of its style: they come from its state, and from `RadioColors` where a radio button has its own.

parameters.name: size
parameters.description: The ring's width and height, its line included.

parameters.name: dotSize
parameters.description: The width and height of the dot in a selected ring.

parameters.name: strokeWidth
parameters.description: How thick the ring's line is.

declarations.name: RadioColors
declarations.description:
What `PantrixRadioButton` and the options of `PantrixRadioGroup` are painted with, for ones that do not take the theme's: a colour that is set is used, and one that is left out stays the theme's role.

```
PantrixRadioGroup(
    options = plans,
    selected = plan,
    onSelect = { plan = it },
    colors = RadioColors(selected = brand)
)
```

They are the colours of a radio button that can be selected and is not in error. A disabled one is drawn in the theme's disabled role and one in error in its danger role, whatever is given here.

parameters.name: selected
parameters.description: The ring and the dot of the option that is chosen. The theme's `primary`.

parameters.name: unselected
parameters.description: The ring of an option that is not. The theme's `borderStrong`: an empty ring is nothing but its line.

declarations.name: pantrixVerticalScroll
declarations.description:
Scrolls this content up and down by `state`, as `Modifier.verticalScroll` does, with Pantrix's scroll bar along its side: a page of text, a form, a settings screen that is taller than its window.

The bar is the one Pantrix's own views of documents draw. Its thumb is as long as the share of the content on the screen, and stands where that share is. Where the reader has a pointer it is there while there is something to scroll, darker under the pointer, and a mouse can drag it; under a finger it shows while the content moves and fades after, since a finger scrolls the content itself. It stands at the end of the content, at the left where the layout is read from the right, and is drawn over the content rather than beside it: the content keeps its width.

The scroll and the bar come together, so that the bar stands over the window the content scrolls in, not on the content that scrolls under it:

```
val scroll = rememberScrollState()
Column(Modifier.fillMaxSize().pantrixVerticalScroll(scroll)) {
    Article()
}
```

A lazy list scrolls by itself, and takes its bar with `pantrixScrollBar`.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: how far the content is scrolled, as `rememberScrollState()` gives it.

parameters.name: enabled
parameters.description: whether a drag, the wheel and the bar scroll the content: the bar is drawn either way, while there is something to scroll.

parameters.name: color

declarations.name: PantrixSegmentButton
declarations.signature:
@Composable
fun <T> PantrixSegmentButton(
    options: List<SegmentOption<T>>,
    selected: T?,
    onSelect: (T) -> Unit,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    enabled: Boolean = true,
    fullWidth: Boolean = true,
    style: SegmentButtonStyle? = null,
    colors: SegmentButtonColors? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null,
    labelStyle: TextStyle = PantrixTheme.typography.label
)
declarations.description:
A segment button: a small set of choices side by side in one control, one of them chosen.

It is a radio group drawn as one control. A screen reader hears a group of radio buttons, one of them selected, and a choice changes what is on the screen around it at once: a list's order, a chart's span, a map's layer. A pill slides to the chosen segment, and its label takes the primary colour. Choosing the segment that is chosen already does nothing.

The control is one stop for Tab, on the chosen segment. The arrow keys choose the next or the previous segment, the other way round in a right-to-left layout, round from the last to the first, and skip a segment that cannot be chosen. A press takes the focus to the control where a press can.

The track is as tall as the style says, with the platform's touch target reserved around it. A label set larger than the track, at a large font scale, makes it taller. Use it for two to five choices of a word or two: for more, or for longer ones, a radio group; for actions rather than a choice, buttons.

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: the choices, in order. An empty list draws nothing.

parameters.name: selected
parameters.description: the value of the chosen segment, compared with each option's by `==`. A value no option has, null among them, chooses none: no segment is selected and no pill is drawn.

parameters.name: onSelect
parameters.description: called with the value of the segment the user chose, by a press or by a key, when it is not the chosen one already. The control chooses nothing by itself: a segment is chosen when `selected` says so.

parameters.name: modifier
parameters.description: the control's modifier, outside the touch target it reserves.

parameters.name: enabled
parameters.description: false disables every segment. The pill stays where it is, so that the choice can still be read.

parameters.name: fullWidth
parameters.description: true spans the control across the width it is given, each segment taking an equal share, so that the segments stay where they are whatever their labels say in another language. False makes each segment as wide as its label; in a room too narrow for that, the short labels stay whole and the long ones share what is left.

parameters.name: style
parameters.description: this call's own style: over every enclosing one and under the density. Only the fields it sets change, on every platform.

parameters.name: colors
parameters.description: this control's own colours: the ones it sets, with the theme's for the rest. A disabled control's track and a segment that cannot be chosen keep the theme's.

parameters.name: tagKey
parameters.description: the control's automation key: the control is `SegmentButton_<tagKey>`, and its segments are named inside it, `SegmentButton_<tagKey>.Segment_<key>`, so that two controls with the same options are told apart. A choice is reported as a `SegmentButton` event, `select`, which carries the segment's key, or its place without one, and never its label.

parameters.name: labelStyle
parameters.description: the type the labels are set in: the theme's `label` unless given. A label set larger than the track makes it taller, as a large font scale does.

declarations.name: SegmentButtonStyle
declarations.description:
`PantrixSegmentButton`'s geometry: the track, the pill that slides inside it, and the room each segment gives its label.

The pill has no shape of its own: it is the track's shape with each corner smaller by `trackPadding`, so the two curve around the same centres on every brand's shape scale. A pill as round as the track would look rounder than the room it is in.

On Android the control is Material 3's segmented button: 40dp tall, a pill throughout. On iOS it is `UISegmentedControl`: 32pt tall, a rounded rectangle with the pill close to its edge. The desktop's is lower, 30dp, for a pointer, and the web's 34dp.

An icon goes by the buttons': 20dp on Android, where the pill is as tall as a small button, and 18dp in the lower pills of the other platforms, between a small button's icon and an extra small one's.

The height, the two paddings and the gap follow the density, since they are the room around the labels. The icon's size and the shape do not.

parameters.name: shape
parameters.description: The track's shape: a step of the brand's shape scale, or a fixed shape.

parameters.name: height
parameters.description: The track's height. A label set larger than it has room for, at a large font scale, makes the track taller.

parameters.name: trackPadding
parameters.description: The room between the track's edge and the pill.

parameters.name: segmentPadding
parameters.description: The room on each side of a segment's label.

parameters.name: iconGap
parameters.description: Between a segment's icon and its label.

parameters.name: iconSize
parameters.description: The width and height of a segment's icon.

declarations.name: SegmentButtonColors
declarations.description:
What `PantrixSegmentButton` is painted with, for a control that does not take the theme's: a colour that is set is used, and one that is left out stays the theme's role.

```
PantrixSegmentButton(
    options = sorts,
    selected = sort,
    onSelect = { sort = it },
    colors = SegmentButtonColors(pill = brand, selectedContent = onBrand)
)
```

They are the colours of segments that can be chosen. A disabled control's track and a segment that cannot be chosen are drawn in the theme's disabled roles whatever is given here; the pill keeps its colour, so that the choice can still be read.

A fill given here that is one of the theme's own colours brings the colour the theme pairs with it for what is drawn on it, unless that is given too. A fill no role has does not: what reads on it is the caller's to give.

parameters.name: track
parameters.description: The track the segments stand on. The neutral role's `container`.

parameters.name: pill
parameters.description: The pill under the chosen segment. The theme's `surface`.

parameters.name: selectedContent
parameters.description: The label and the icon of the chosen segment: the colour that reads on `pill`. The theme's `primary`.

parameters.name: unselectedContent
parameters.description: The label and the icon of the other segments: the colour that reads on `track`. The theme's `textSecondary`.

declarations.name: ControlPosition

declarations.description: Where a checkbox's box, a radio button's ring or a switch's track stands against its label: before it, as a list of choices has it, or after it, at the end of the row, as a settings screen has a switch.

entries.name: Start
entries.description: Before the label, at the row's start: at the left, or at the right where the layout is read from the right.

entries.name: End
entries.description: After the label: at the end of the width the row is given, or right after the label where it is given none. The label and its help wrap in what the control leaves, and never push it on.

declarations.name: PantrixSwitchButton
declarations.signature:
@Composable
fun PantrixSwitchButton(
    checked: Boolean,
    onCheckedChange: ((Boolean) -> Unit)?,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    enabled: Boolean = true,
    label: String? = null,
    supportingText: String? = null,
    error: Boolean = false,
    style: SwitchStyle? = null,
    colors: SwitchColors? = null,
    contentDescription: String? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null,
    interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null,
    labelStyle: TextStyle = PantrixTheme.typography.label,
    controlPosition: ControlPosition = ControlPosition.Start
)
declarations.description:
A switch: a setting that is on or off and takes effect at once, and the label it is the switch of.

The track, the label and the supporting text are one target. A press anywhere on them turns the switch, since on a phone the words are most of what a finger can hit, and a screen reader hears one switch, named by its label, that says whether it is on. The track stands on the label's first line, however many lines the label and the supporting text run to. The row takes the platform's touch target, small as the track is.

The thumb can be dragged as well. Let go past the middle of the track, it turns the switch on, and short of the middle it turns it off: a thumb let go on the side it started from settles back and nothing is reported. The drag runs with the reading direction, so right to left the on end is the left one, the end a press sends the thumb to. A press, a key and a drag change the switch in one way, with one haptic and one event.

The thumb slides, and the track turns to the primary role's colour with it, wherever the thumb is: under a finger that drags it too. Both happen at once under reduced motion.

Without `onCheckedChange` the switch is read-only: it takes no press, no drag and no focus, and still says its name and its state. `error` turns the supporting text to the danger role and is announced. The switch itself keeps its colours: a switch is a setting, and an answer that can be wrong belongs to a checkbox.

parameters.name: checked
parameters.description: whether the switch is on.

parameters.name: onCheckedChange
parameters.description: called with the value the user asks for, the opposite of `checked`. The switch changes nothing by itself: it is on when `checked` says so. Null makes it read-only.

parameters.name: modifier
parameters.description: the row's modifier.

parameters.name: enabled
parameters.description: whether the switch can be turned. One that cannot is drawn in the disabled colours and says so.

parameters.name: label
parameters.description: the text beside the track: part of the target, and the switch's name for a screen reader.

parameters.name: supportingText
parameters.description: help under the label, in a smaller type: the message, while `error` is true.

parameters.name: error
parameters.description: whether the value is wrong: the supporting text turns to the danger role, and a screen reader is told the input is invalid.

parameters.name: style
parameters.description: this call's own style: over every enclosing one and under the density. Only the fields it sets change, on every platform.

parameters.name: colors
parameters.description: this switch's own colours: the ones it sets, with the theme's for the rest. A disabled switch keeps the theme's.

parameters.name: contentDescription
parameters.description: what a screen reader says for the switch: its name where it has no `label`, as in a row of the app's own that has the words elsewhere, or in place of the label.

parameters.name: tagKey
parameters.description: the switch's automation key: the row is `SwitchButton_<tagKey>`. A change is reported as a `SwitchButton` event that carries the new value, and never its label.

parameters.name: interactionSource
parameters.description: the switch's interactions, hoisted: its presses, its drags and its focus. It keeps a source of its own when this is null.

parameters.name: labelStyle
parameters.description: the type the label is set in: the theme's `label` unless given. The track stands on its first line at any size. A colour in it is the label's while the switch is enabled; a disabled switch writes it in the disabled colour.

parameters.name: controlPosition
parameters.description: where the track stands: before the label, or after it, as a settings screen has it. After it, the track is at the end of the width the row is given, `Modifier.fillMaxWidth()` lining it up with the others, or right after the label where the row is given none; the label wraps in what the track leaves.

A switch bound to a form's field: its value, its error and its name come from `field`.

A change sets the field and marks it touched, so a rule's message shows after the first change, or when the form is submitted, and not on a form nobody has touched. While the field is in error the message takes the place of `supportingText`, rather than standing beside it. The field's id is the switch's automation key, `SwitchButton_<id>`, and the form can send the focus here when it is submitted with this field in error.

It is an overload of its own and not a parameter of the controlled form, so that a value and a field cannot both be given.

parameters.name: field
parameters.description: the field the switch shows and changes.

parameters.name: modifier
parameters.description: the row's modifier.

parameters.name: enabled
parameters.description: whether the switch can be turned.

parameters.name: label
parameters.description: the text beside the track: part of the target, and the switch's name for a screen reader.

parameters.name: supportingText
parameters.description: help under the label, while the field has no error to show there.

parameters.name: style
parameters.description: this call's own style: over every enclosing one and under the density. Only the fields it sets change, on every platform.

parameters.name: colors
parameters.description: this switch's own colours: the ones it sets, with the theme's for the rest. A disabled switch keeps the theme's.

parameters.name: contentDescription
parameters.description: what a screen reader says for the switch where it has no `label`, or in place of it.

parameters.name: labelStyle
parameters.description: the type the label is set in: the theme's `label` unless given.

parameters.name: controlPosition
parameters.description: where the track stands: before the label, or after it, as a settings screen has it. After it, the track is at the end of the width the row is given, `Modifier.fillMaxWidth()` lining it up with the others, or right after the label where the row is given none; the label wraps in what the track leaves.

declarations.name: SwitchStyle
declarations.description:
`PantrixSwitchButton`'s track and its thumb: how large each is, the track's edge, and what the thumb looks like.

The thumb has three sizes. On Material 3 it grows from off to on, and further while it is held: that change is the switch's own motion, so Android's preset has three sizes. iOS's switch never resizes its thumb, and under a pointer a thumb that changes size is noise, so on iOS, the desktop and the web the three are one size. The component never asks which platform it is on.

The thumb sits in the middle of the track's round end, as far from the end as from the sides, at every size: the room around it is what the track's height leaves, and no value of its own.

`strokeWidth` is the edge of a track that is off, in the border colour, which marks where the control is at 3:1 against what it sits on. Material 3 draws one, and so does Windows: Android's preset has Material's, and the desktop's and the web's a thinner one, since their track is smaller. iOS draws none and leaves a pale track with a white thumb and its shadow, which Pantrix keeps there.

None of it follows the density: a track, its thumb and its edge are not air. The space between the track and its label does, since it comes from the theme's spacing. A switch's colours are not part of its style: they come from its state, and from `SwitchColors` where a switch has its own.

parameters.name: trackWidth
parameters.description: The track's width, its edge included.

parameters.name: trackHeight
parameters.description: The track's height, its edge included. The track's ends are as round as it is tall.

parameters.name: thumbSizeOff
parameters.description: The thumb's width and height while the switch is off.

parameters.name: thumbSizeOn
parameters.description: The thumb's width and height while the switch is on.

parameters.name: thumbSizePressed
parameters.description: The thumb's width and height while it is pressed or dragged.

parameters.name: strokeWidth
parameters.description: How thick the edge of a track that is off is. Zero draws none.

parameters.name: thumbAlwaysLight
parameters.description: True keeps the thumb white whatever the theme and the state, as iOS has it. False draws it in the border colour when off and in the colour paired with the track's fill when on, as Material has it. Null is unspecified.

parameters.name: thumbShadow
parameters.description: How far the thumb stands above the track: the size of the shadow under it. Zero draws none.

declarations.name: SwitchColors
declarations.description:
What `PantrixSwitchButton` is painted with, for a switch that does not take the theme's: a colour that is set is used, and one that is left out stays the theme's role.

```
PantrixSwitchButton(
    checked = notifications,
    onCheckedChange = { notifications = it },
    label = stringResource(Res.string.notifications),
    colors = SwitchColors(checkedTrack = brand)
)
```

They are the colours of a switch that can be turned. A disabled one is drawn in the theme's disabled roles whatever is given here. Between off and on the track and the thumb turn from one colour to the other as the thumb moves.

A track given here that is one of the theme's own colours brings the thumb the theme pairs with it, unless the thumb is given too or the style keeps it light. A track no role has does not: the thumb on it is the caller's to give.

parameters.name: checkedTrack
parameters.description: The track's fill when the switch is on. The theme's `primary`.

parameters.name: checkedThumb
parameters.description: The thumb when the switch is on: the colour that stands out on `checkedTrack`. The primary role's `onColor`, or white where the style keeps the thumb light.

parameters.name: uncheckedTrack
parameters.description: The track's fill when the switch is off. A tint of the theme's `borderStrong`.

parameters.name: uncheckedThumb
parameters.description: The thumb when the switch is off: the colour that stands out on `uncheckedTrack`. The theme's `borderStrong`, or white where the style keeps the thumb light.

parameters.name: border
parameters.description: The edge of a track that is off, where the style draws one. The theme's `borderStrong`: a switch that is off is seen by its edge and its thumb.

declarations.name: TextRole
declarations.signature: sealed interface TextRole
declarations.description:
What a piece of text *is*, which decides how a screen reader treats it.

A visual style is not a substitute: text styled like a heading but not marked as one is invisible to the heading-navigation every screen reader user relies on to skim a page.

members.name: Paragraph
members.description: Ordinary prose.

members.name: Heading
members.signature: data class Heading(val level: Int) : TextRole
members.description: A heading at `level` (1 = page title). Enables heading navigation.

parameters.name: level
parameters.description: The heading's depth: 1 for the page's title, 2 for its sections, and so on down.

members.name: Label
members.description: Names a control or a value.

members.name: Decorative
members.description:
Purely visual — hidden from assistive technology.

For text already announced by something else: the letter inside an avatar whose content description is the person's full name. Its words are left out of the semantics tree, so a parent heard as one does not read them with its own: a test finds it by its tag.

declarations.description:
A text field whose text gets smaller to stay in view: an amount, a card's number, a short note, anything that is read whole.

The text is as large as its style says while it fits. A text too long for the box is set in a smaller size, as small as it takes to fit, and grows back as it is shortened. The box does not grow wider with its text: its width is its style's least or the one its caller gave it. At `minFontSize` the text stops shrinking and scrolls, as the text of any field does.

The field holds one line unless told: a line that is fitted to the box's width, in a box that keeps its height. With `lineLimits` of several lines the text wraps, and the box grows with it from the least of its lines to the most, as a text field's does. From there the box keeps its height and the text is set smaller, its lines as much closer, so that all of it stays in the box.

A height the field is given comes before its lines. The box fills what the label and the supporting text leave of it, and the text is fitted to that: it is set smaller where the height holds fewer lines than the field may take, and keeps its size for as many lines as a taller one holds. One line is set smaller in a box too low for it.

What is fitted is the text as it is shown: after an output transformation, and with what the keyboard is still composing. It is the text's size that changes, and nothing is drawn smaller than it is laid out: the caret, a selection and its handles are those of the size the text is in, and that size is what a test reads from the text's layout. The placeholder is set as the text would be, in a smaller size where it is too long. A box whose size changes has its text fitted again a frame later. A text that is too long for its box when the field is first shown is drawn a frame later too, fitted, and is never seen in a size too large.

It is the label, the box and the supporting text of `PantrixTextField`, and takes that component's `style` and `colors`: a product that restyles its text fields restyles this one with them. It is built on a `TextFieldState`, and has an overload that takes a `value` and an `onValueChange`, and one for a form's field.

parameters.name: readOnly

parameters.name: placeholder

parameters.name: supportingText

It looks, measures and shrinks its text as the field on a `TextFieldState` does, and underneath it is Foundation's text field of a value and a callback. declarations.description: What a text area does with an edit that takes its text past its `maxLength`: takes it and shows that the text is too long, or turns it down.

entries.name: Allow
entries.description: The edit is taken, and the field shows that the text is too long: the count says in words how far past the limit it is, and the border and the count turn to the error's colour. declarations.description:
A filled text field whose text shrinks to fit, and whose text is a `String` its caller holds: `value` is what it shows, and `onValueChange` is asked for every change the user makes.

It looks, measures and shrinks its text as the field on a `TextFieldState` does, and underneath it is Foundation's text field of a value and a callback. The text the callback is given has to come back as `value` by the next frame, or the field shows the old text again and the caret jumps: keep the text in state that the callback writes at once, and take the `TextFieldState` overload when the text lives in a flow. declarations.description:
A secure text field whose label is inside its box: a password, a PIN or a card's security code in the filled box of `PantrixFilledTextField`.

What is typed is drawn as dots, and cannot be cut, copied or dragged out of the field. The platform is told that the field holds a password, and while the text is hidden it is given the dots for the text: a screen reader reads no password out, and a password manager still fills the field and saves it. The field holds one line.

A button at the box's end shows the text and hides it again. With a keyboard it is a Tab stop of its own, after the field, and the keyboard's `Next` goes past it to the next field. A press on it with a pointer leaves the caret where it is. That the text was shown is not saved: it is hidden again when the field is made anew, as it is after the screen turns.

The label rests where the text will be, and moves up to its own line above the text when the field takes the focus or holds a text. The box is filled and has no outline at rest, and is outlined with the focus and in error. It is that filled box around the secure text field that `PantrixSecureTextField` is underneath, and takes the filled text field's `style` and `colors`: the two filled fields are restyled together, and the two secure fields can stand in for each other. It is built on a `TextFieldState`, and has an overload for a form's field: the text is read from the state, where it is used or as it changes.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: the text and the selection. Create it with `remember { TextFieldState() }`, or keep it in a view model: `rememberTextFieldState()` puts what is typed into the saved state, which the platform holds after the app's process has gone and may write to its disk. A remembered state goes when the screen is made anew, as it is after the screen turns, and the field is empty again. Read what was typed from it: `state.text` where the text is used, or `snapshotFlow { state.text.toString() }` to follow it as it changes.

parameters.name: modifier
parameters.description: the modifier of the whole field: its box and what is under it. `fillMaxWidth()` makes the box as wide as its parent.

parameters.name: enabled
parameters.description: whether the field can be typed into. One that cannot takes no focus, is drawn without its fill in the disabled colours, has no button to show its text and says so.

parameters.name: readOnly
parameters.description: whether the text can only be read: it can still be focused, and shown by the button.

parameters.name: label
parameters.description: what the field is for, written inside the box: the field's name for a screen reader. Without one the text stands in the middle of the box, and the `placeholder` shows whenever the field is empty.

parameters.name: placeholder
parameters.description: shown where the text goes while the field is empty and its label is out of the way: while it has the focus, or always where it has no label.

parameters.name: supportingText
parameters.description: help under the box, in a smaller type. With `error` it is the message that says what to put right, which a screen reader announces as the error.

parameters.name: error
parameters.description: whether the text is wrong: the box is outlined in the danger role's colour, the supporting text and the caret turn to it, and a screen reader is told.

parameters.name: leadingIcon
parameters.description: what stands before the label and the text, in the secondary text colour. A slot does not size what is put in it: `PantrixIcon(size = PantrixTheme.style(FilledTextFieldStyle).iconSize)` is the platform's size.

parameters.name: trailingIcon
parameters.description: what stands after the text, after the clear button and the button that shows the text.

parameters.name: showClearButton
parameters.description: shows a button that empties the field, while the field can be typed into and is not empty. It leaves the caret in the field, and is no stop for Tab.

parameters.name: showRevealButton
parameters.description: shows the button that shows the text and hides it again, while the field is enabled. Without it the text stays as `textObfuscationMode` draws it: for a text that is never to be shown, and for a caller that shows it another way.

parameters.name: maxLength
parameters.description: the most characters the user can enter, counted as `String.length` counts them. An edit that would pass the limit is turned down whole. Text set in code is not cut, and the user can still make it shorter. It has to be positive.

parameters.name: showCharacterCount
parameters.description: shows `count/maxLength` under the box while `maxLength` is set.

parameters.name: textObfuscationMode
parameters.description: how the text is drawn while it is hidden. `TextObfuscationMode.System` does as the platform does: on Android the last character typed shows for a moment where the system's own setting says so, and nowhere else does anything show. `Hidden` shows nothing on any platform, and `RevealLastTyped` the last character for a moment on every one.

parameters.name: textObfuscationCharacter
parameters.description: what is drawn in place of a hidden character.

parameters.name: keyboardOptions
parameters.description: the keyboard's type, its capitals, its corrections and its action key. What these leave unset is a password's, the password keyboard and no corrections, so that naming an action does not bring back a keyboard that learns what is typed. `KeyboardType.NumberPassword` is a PIN's.

parameters.name: onKeyboardAction
parameters.description: called for the keyboard's action key, for the action `keyboardOptions` names. Null keeps what the platform does.

parameters.name: inputTransformation
parameters.description: what is done to the text as the user types it. With `maxLength`, it comes first and the limit applies to what it lets through.

parameters.name: contentType
parameters.description: what the field holds, for the platform to fill it in. Left out, the field holds `ContentType.Password`, as Foundation's secure field says for itself: `ContentType.NewPassword` is one that is being chosen.

parameters.name: style
parameters.description: this call's own style: over every enclosing one and under the density. Only the fields it sets change, on every platform.

parameters.name: colors
parameters.description: this call's own colours, in place of the theme's roles: the ones it sets are used, and the rest stay the theme's. A disabled field has no fill and is drawn in the theme's disabled text colour whatever is given.

parameters.name: contentDescription
parameters.description: what a screen reader says for the field: its name where it has no `label`. A `placeholder` that says the same is then left to the eye.

parameters.name: tagKey
parameters.description: the field's automation key: the field is `FilledSecureTextField_<tagKey>`, its clear button `FilledSecureTextFieldClear_<tagKey>` and the button that shows its text `FilledSecureTextFieldReveal_<tagKey>`. The field reports that it took the focus, that it was cleared and that its text was shown or hidden, and never its text.

parameters.name: interactionSource
parameters.description: the field's interactions, hoisted: its focus, its hover and its presses. It keeps a source of its own when this is null.

declarations.description:
A filled text area: a field for text of several lines, a comment, a message or a note, on a filled box that grows with what is typed and then scrolls, with its label inside the box, and help or an error's message below it and a count of its characters.

The label rests in the place of the first line while the field is empty and without the focus, and rises above the text as the field takes the focus or holds text, as a filled text field's does.

The box is `minLines` lines tall while it is empty and grows a line at a time with its text, up to `maxLines`. Past them the text scrolls in the box, and a thin bar at the box's end shows how far. Where the platform is used with a pointer, a handle in the box's bottom corner drags it taller or shorter, and the box then keeps the height it was left at whatever its text, down to its least lines.

Enter starts a new line on every keyboard: a software keyboard always shows its key for one, and never an action in its place. A text that is sent takes `onSubmit`, which Ctrl and Enter, or Cmd and Enter, call from a hardware keyboard; a screen gives it a button as well, since a software keyboard has no such keys. Tab moves the focus on, and does not type a tab, which would leave a keyboard no way forward out of the field.

A `maxLength` is soft unless told otherwise: the text may pass it, and the count then says how far past it the text is, in words, with the border in the error's colour. A paste that does not fit is kept whole, for the user to cut where they choose. `TextLimit.Block` turns an edit past the limit down instead, as a text field's limit does.

On iOS a field of several lines has no key that puts the keyboard away: `Modifier.clearFocusOnTap()` on the screen puts it away when the user taps outside the field.

It is the box and the supporting text of `PantrixFilledTextField`, and takes that component's `style` and `colors`: a product that restyles its filled text fields restyles its filled text areas with them. It is built on a `TextFieldState`, and has an overload that takes a `value` and an `onValueChange`, and one for a form's field.

A filled text field bound to a form's field: its text, its error and its name come from `field`.

The field's value and the text on screen stay in step both ways: typing changes the field, and a change made to the field in code, such as a reset, replaces the text. When the focus leaves, the field is marked touched and checked, which is when an error first shows. While the field is in error its message takes the place of `supportingText`. The field's id is the automation key, `FilledTextField_<id>`, and the form can send the focus here when it is submitted with this field in error.

parameters.name: field
parameters.description: the field the text field shows and changes.

parameters.name: modifier

parameters.name: form
parameters.description: given, the keyboard's action key submits the form through the button registered with it. An action of `Next` or `Previous` moves the focus as it always does. A field of one line that names no action gets `ImeAction.Done`, since the default action never reaches a handler. A field of several lines is left alone: there Enter starts a new line. An `onKeyboardAction` of the caller's own takes the place of the submit.

parameters.name: enabled
parameters.description: whether the field can be typed into.

parameters.name: readOnly
parameters.description: whether the text can only be read.

parameters.name: label

parameters.name: placeholder

parameters.name: supportingText

parameters.name: leadingIcon

parameters.name: trailingIcon

parameters.name: showClearButton

parameters.name: onKeyboardAction
parameters.description: called for the keyboard's action key, in place of the form's submit.

parameters.name: inputTransformation
parameters.description: what is done to the text as the user types it.

parameters.name: outputTransformation
parameters.description: how the text is shown, without changing it.

parameters.name: contentType
parameters.description: what the field holds, for the platform to fill it in.

declarations.name: FilledTextFieldStyle
declarations.description:
`PantrixFilledTextField`'s box: its shape, how tall and how wide it is at the least, the room around what it holds, its icons and its outline.

The box holds two lines between its paddings: the label's, in the footnote role, and the text's under it, in its `textRole`. `height` is a minimum: a field of several lines, or a large font scale, makes the box taller and never cuts the text. Each preset's `verticalPadding` leaves those two lines of its height, at every density, so a field of one line is exactly as tall as its style says.

An icon sits in a slot of `iconSize + 2 × iconPadding`, flush with the box's edge, and the label and the text beside a slot start `horizontalPadding − iconPadding` from it.

parameters.name: shape
parameters.description: The box's shape. A fully round one, `ShapeRole.Full`, is a pill only while the field holds one line: a field of several lines takes `ShapeRole.Large` instead, since a capsule's curve runs into the first line of its text.

parameters.name: height
parameters.description: The least the box is tall.

parameters.name: minWidth
parameters.description: The least the box is wide, which keeps an empty field from growing as the user types into it.

parameters.name: horizontalPadding
parameters.description: The room between the box's edge and its label and text, where no icon is.

parameters.name: verticalPadding
parameters.description: The room above the label's line and below the last line of the text.

parameters.name: iconPadding
parameters.description: The room around an icon in its slot.

parameters.name: iconSize
parameters.description: The size an icon in a slot should take. A slot does not size what is put in it.

parameters.name: borderWidth
parameters.description: How thick the outline is that the box takes with the focus, in error and under a pointer. At rest it has none.

parameters.name: textRole
parameters.description: The role of the type scale the text is typed in, the label rests in and the placeholder is set in: the body's, 16sp, on Android and iOS, as Material 3 types a field, and the label's, 14sp, on the desktop and the web, as a page under a pointer does.

declarations.name: FilledTextFieldColors
declarations.description:
What `PantrixFilledTextField` is painted with, for a field that does not take the theme's: a colour that is set is used, and one that is left out stays the theme's role. A product gives the colours it changes and no others:

```
PantrixFilledTextField(
    state = state,
    label = stringResource(Res.string.iban),
    colors = FilledTextFieldColors(focusedOutline = brand, cursor = brand)
)
```

They are the colours of an enabled field, read-only or not. A disabled one has no fill and is drawn in the theme's disabled text colour whatever is given here, so that a disabled field looks the same across a product.

parameters.name: container
parameters.description: The box's fill at rest. The theme's neutral container.

parameters.name: focusedContainer
parameters.description: The box's fill under an outline: with the focus, and in error. The theme's `surface`.

parameters.name: hoveredOutline
parameters.description: The outline under a pointer. The theme's `borderHover`.

parameters.name: focusedOutline
parameters.description: The outline while the field has the focus. The theme's `primary`.

parameters.name: error
parameters.description: What says the text is wrong: the outline, the message under the box, the caret, and the count once it is past its limit. The theme's `danger`.

parameters.name: text
parameters.description: The typed text. The theme's `textPrimary`.

parameters.name: label
parameters.description: The label, at rest in the text's place and on its own line above the text. The theme's `textSecondary`.

parameters.name: placeholder
parameters.description: The placeholder. The theme's `textSecondary`.

parameters.name: supportingText
parameters.description: The help under the box, and the count. The theme's `textSecondary`.

parameters.name: icon
parameters.description: What an icon in a slot is drawn in unless it sets a tint of its own, and the clear button's cross. The theme's `textSecondary`.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The caret, and with it the handles and the highlight of a selection. The theme's `primary`.

parameters.name: scrollBar
parameters.description: The bar that shows how far the text of a box of several lines is scrolled. The theme's `borderStrong`: it is a mark on the box's fill, and a box's soft edge would not be seen there.
