declarations.description:
A text field for what is not to be read over a shoulder: a password, a PIN, a card's security code.

What is typed is drawn as dots, and cannot be cut, copied or dragged out of the field. The platform is told that the field holds a password, and while the text is hidden it is given the dots for the text: a screen reader reads no password out, and a password manager still fills the field and saves it. The field holds one line.

A button at the box's end shows the text and hides it again. With a keyboard it is a Tab stop of its own, after the field, and the keyboard's `Next` goes past it to the next field. A press on it with a pointer leaves the caret where it is. That the text was shown is not saved: it is hidden again when the field is made anew, as it is after the screen turns.

It is the label, the box and the supporting text of `PantrixTextField` around Foundation's secure text field, and takes that component's `style` and `colors`: a product that restyles its text fields restyles its password fields with them. It is built on a `TextFieldState`, and has an overload for a form's field. Foundation's secure field has none of a value and a callback: the text is read from the state, where it is used or as it changes, and a caller that keeps it as a `String` is handed each change that way.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: the text and the selection. Create it with `remember { TextFieldState() }`, or keep it in a view model: `rememberTextFieldState()` puts what is typed into the saved state, which the platform holds after the app's process has gone and may write to its disk. A remembered state goes when the screen is made anew, as it is after the screen turns, and the field is empty again. Read what was typed from it: `state.text` where the text is used, or `snapshotFlow { state.text.toString() }` to follow it as it changes.

parameters.name: modifier
parameters.description: the modifier of the whole field: its label, its box and what is under it. `fillMaxWidth()` makes the box as wide as its parent.

parameters.name: enabled
parameters.description: whether the field can be typed into. One that cannot takes no focus, is drawn in the disabled colours, has no button to show its text and says so.

parameters.name: readOnly
parameters.description: whether the text can only be read: it can still be focused, and shown by the button.

parameters.name: label
parameters.description: what the field is for, written above the box: the field's name for a screen reader.

parameters.name: placeholder
parameters.description: shown in the box while it is empty. It is no label: it goes as soon as the user types.

parameters.name: supportingText
parameters.description: help under the box, in a smaller type. With `error` it is the message that says what to put right, which a screen reader announces as the error.

parameters.name: error
parameters.description: whether the text is wrong: the border, the label, the supporting text and the caret turn to the danger role, and a screen reader is told.

parameters.name: leadingIcon
parameters.description: what stands before the text, in the secondary text colour. A slot does not size what is put in it: `PantrixIcon(size = PantrixTheme.style(TextFieldStyle).iconSize)` is the platform's size.

parameters.name: trailingIcon
parameters.description: what stands after the text, after the clear button and the button that shows the text.

parameters.name: showClearButton
parameters.description: shows a button that empties the field, while the field can be typed into and is not empty. It leaves the caret in the field, and is no stop for Tab.

parameters.name: showRevealButton
parameters.description: shows the button that shows the text and hides it again, while the field is enabled. Without it the text stays as `textObfuscationMode` draws it: for a text that is never to be shown, and for a caller that shows it another way.

parameters.name: maxLength
parameters.description: the most characters the user can enter, counted as `String.length` counts them. An edit that would pass the limit is turned down whole. Text set in code is not cut, and the user can still make it shorter. It has to be positive.

parameters.name: showCharacterCount
parameters.description: shows `count/maxLength` under the box while `maxLength` is set.

parameters.name: textObfuscationMode
parameters.description: how the text is drawn while it is hidden. `TextObfuscationMode.System` does as the platform does: on Android the last character typed shows for a moment where the system's own setting says so, and nowhere else does anything show. `Hidden` shows nothing on any platform, and `RevealLastTyped` the last character for a moment on every one.

parameters.name: textObfuscationCharacter
parameters.description: what is drawn in place of a hidden character.

parameters.name: keyboardOptions
parameters.description: the keyboard's type, its capitals, its corrections and its action key. What these leave unset is a password's, the password keyboard and no corrections, so that naming an action does not bring back a keyboard that learns what is typed. `KeyboardType.NumberPassword` is a PIN's.

parameters.name: onKeyboardAction
parameters.description: called for the keyboard's action key, for the action `keyboardOptions` names. Null keeps what the platform does: `Next` moves the focus on, and `Done` closes the keyboard.

parameters.name: inputTransformation
parameters.description: what is done to the text as the user types it. With `maxLength`, it comes first and the limit applies to what it lets through.

parameters.name: contentType
parameters.description: what the field holds, for the platform to fill it in. Left out, the field holds `ContentType.Password`, as Foundation's secure field says for itself: `ContentType.NewPassword` is one that is being chosen.

parameters.name: style
parameters.description: this call's own style: over every enclosing one and under the density. Only the fields it sets change, on every platform.

parameters.name: colors
parameters.description: this call's own colours, in place of the theme's roles: the ones it sets are used, and the rest stay the theme's. A disabled field is drawn in the theme's disabled colours whatever is given.

parameters.name: contentDescription
parameters.description: what a screen reader says for the field: its name where it has no `label`. A `placeholder` that says the same is then left to the eye.

parameters.name: tagKey
parameters.description: the field's automation key: the field is `SecureTextField_<tagKey>`, its clear button `SecureTextFieldClear_<tagKey>` and the button that shows its text `SecureTextFieldReveal_<tagKey>`. The field reports that it took the focus, that it was cleared and that its text was shown or hidden, and never its text.

parameters.name: interactionSource
parameters.description: the field's interactions, hoisted: its focus, its hover and its presses. It keeps a source of its own when this is null.

declarations.description:
A text area: a field for text of several lines, a comment, a message or a note, that grows with what is typed and then scrolls, under a label, with help or an error's message below it and a count of its characters.

The box is `minLines` lines tall while it is empty and grows a line at a time with its text, up to `maxLines`. Past them the text scrolls in the box, and a thin bar at the box's end shows how far. Where the platform is used with a pointer, a handle in the box's bottom corner drags it taller or shorter, and the box then keeps the height it was left at whatever its text, down to its least lines.

Enter starts a new line on every keyboard: a software keyboard always shows its key for one, and never an action in its place. A text that is sent takes `onSubmit`, which Ctrl and Enter, or Cmd and Enter, call from a hardware keyboard; a screen gives it a button as well, since a software keyboard has no such keys. Tab moves the focus on, and does not type a tab, which would leave a keyboard no way forward out of the field.

A `maxLength` is soft unless told otherwise: the text may pass it, and the count then says how far past it the text is, in words, with the border in the error's colour. A paste that does not fit is kept whole, for the user to cut where they choose. `TextLimit.Block` turns an edit past the limit down instead, as a text field's limit does.

On iOS a field of several lines has no key that puts the keyboard away: `Modifier.clearFocusOnTap()` on the screen puts it away when the user taps outside the field.

It is the label, the box and the supporting text of `PantrixTextField`, and takes that component's `style` and `colors`: a product that restyles its text fields restyles its text areas with them. It is built on a `TextFieldState`, and has an overload that takes a `value` and an `onValueChange`, and one for a form's field.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: the text and the selection. Create it with `rememberTextFieldState()`, and read what was typed from it: `state.text` where the text is used, or `snapshotFlow { state.text.toString() }` to follow it as it changes.

parameters.name: modifier
parameters.description: the modifier of the whole field: its label, its box and what is under it. `fillMaxWidth()` makes the box as wide as its parent. A height is the whole field's as well, in place of its lines: the box fills what the label and the supporting text leave of it, and its text scrolls in it. The handle moves the box only within such a height, so a field that is to be dragged is given `heightIn` and not `height`.

parameters.name: enabled
parameters.description: whether the field can be typed into. One that cannot takes no focus, is drawn in the disabled colours, has no handle and says so.

parameters.name: readOnly
parameters.description: whether the text can only be read: it can still be focused, selected, copied, scrolled and dragged taller.

parameters.name: label
parameters.description: what the field is for, written above the box: the field's name for a screen reader.

parameters.name: placeholder
parameters.description: shown in the box while it is empty. It is no label: it goes as soon as the user types.

parameters.name: supportingText
parameters.description: help under the box, in a smaller type. With `error` it is the message that says what to put right, which a screen reader announces as the error.

parameters.name: error

declarations.description:
A text field: one line of text or several that the user types, under a label, with help or an error's message below it, icons at either end, a button that clears it and a count of its characters.

It is built on a `TextFieldState` and not on a value and a callback. The state holds the text, the selection and what the keyboard is still composing together, so the keyboard is never handed a text that has moved on: that is what loses characters and makes the caret jump with some input methods. Code that keeps its text as a `String` has an overload that takes a `value` and an `onValueChange`, and a form's field has one of its own.

The label sits above the box and stays there. A label that never moves never covers the placeholder and stays readable while the user types. The whole field is one target: a press on the label puts the caret in the box.

The border is what shows the focus, in the primary role's colour and thicker, however the focus came: a press shows it as much as Tab does. No ring is drawn around the box as well, which would read as a second border. Under a modal the field keeps the focus, to have it again when the modal closes, and is drawn at rest and without its caret: the modal is where the user is until then.

Each paragraph takes its reading direction from its own first letter, so an e-mail address typed into an Arabic form reads `ada@` and not `@ada`. The text is aligned with the layout, so it stays on the label's side whatever script it is in.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: the text and the selection. Create it with `rememberTextFieldState()`, and read what was typed from it: `state.text` where the text is used, or `snapshotFlow { state.text.toString() }` to follow it as it changes.

parameters.name: modifier
parameters.description: the modifier of the whole field: its label, its box and what is under it. `fillMaxWidth()` makes the box as wide as its parent. A height is the whole field's as well: the box fills what the label and the supporting text leave of it, with one line in its middle and several from its top, and a text too long for the box scrolls in it.

parameters.name: enabled
parameters.description: whether the field can be typed into. One that cannot takes no focus, is drawn in the disabled colours and says so.

parameters.name: readOnly
parameters.description: whether the text can only be read: it can still be focused, selected and copied.

parameters.name: label
parameters.description: what the field is for, written above the box: the field's name for a screen reader.

parameters.name: placeholder
parameters.description: shown in the box while it is empty. It is no label: it goes as soon as the user types.

parameters.name: supportingText
parameters.description: help under the box, in a smaller type. With `error` it is the message that says what to put right, which a screen reader announces as the error.

parameters.name: error
parameters.description: whether the text is wrong: the border, the label, the supporting text and the caret turn to the danger role, and a screen reader is told.

parameters.name: leadingIcon
parameters.description: what stands before the text, in the secondary text colour. A slot does not size what is put in it: `PantrixIcon(size = PantrixTheme.style(TextFieldStyle).iconSize)` is the platform's size.

parameters.name: trailingIcon
parameters.description: what stands after the text, and after the clear button.

parameters.name: showClearButton
parameters.description: shows a button that empties the field, while the field can be typed into and is not empty. It leaves the caret in the field. It is no stop for Tab, since a stop after every field doubles the presses through a form, and a screen reader still reaches it as a button.

parameters.name: maxLength
parameters.description: the most characters the user can enter, counted as `String.length` counts them, so that an emoji can count as two. An edit that would pass the limit is turned down whole: typing stops at the limit, and a paste that does not fit is not put in. Text set in code is not cut, and the user can still make it shorter. It has to be positive.

parameters.name: showCharacterCount
parameters.description: shows `count/maxLength` under the box while `maxLength` is set.

parameters.name: lineLimits
parameters.description: one line, or `TextFieldLineLimits.MultiLine`, in which the box grows with its text and Enter starts a new line. Past its most lines the text scrolls, and a thin bar at the box's end shows how far. Its icons and its clear button stand at its first line. Tab moves the focus on from either: a field of several lines does not type a tab, which would leave a keyboard no way forward out of it.

parameters.name: keyboardOptions
parameters.description: the keyboard's type, its capitals, its corrections and its action key. A field of numbers that has an action takes `numberKeyboardOptions(imeAction)`: an iPhone's number pad has no key for one. A field of several lines that names an action loses the key for a new line on Android, whose keyboard shows the action in its place: such a field leaves the action unset, or is a `PantrixTextArea`.

parameters.name: onKeyboardAction
parameters.description: called for the keyboard's action key: the key a software keyboard shows for the action `keyboardOptions` names, and Enter on a hardware keyboard in a field of one line. It is called only for a named action, since the default one never reaches a handler. Null keeps what the platform does: `Next` moves the focus on, and `Done` closes the keyboard.

parameters.name: inputTransformation
parameters.description: what is done to the text as the user types it. With `maxLength`, it comes first and the limit applies to what it lets through.

parameters.name: outputTransformation
parameters.description: how the text is shown, without changing it: a phone number's spaces.

parameters.name: contentType
parameters.description: what the field holds, for the platform to fill it in: `ContentType.EmailAddress` and the like.

parameters.name: style
parameters.description: this call's own style: over every enclosing one and under the density. Only the fields it sets change, on every platform.

parameters.name: colors
parameters.description: this call's own colours, in place of the theme's roles: the ones it sets are used, and the rest stay the theme's. A disabled field is drawn in the theme's disabled colours whatever is given.

parameters.name: contentDescription
parameters.description: what a screen reader says for the field: its name where it has no `label`, as a search field has none. A `placeholder` that says the same is then left to the eye, so that the field is not named twice while it is empty.

parameters.name: tagKey
parameters.description: the field's automation key: the field is `TextField_<tagKey>`, and its clear button `TextFieldClear_<tagKey>`. The field reports that it took the focus and that it was cleared, and never its text.

parameters.name: interactionSource
parameters.description: the field's interactions, hoisted: its focus, its hover and its presses. It keeps a source of its own when this is null.

parameters.description: the field's interactions, hoisted: its focus, its hover and its presses. It keeps a source of its own when this is null.

declarations.id: com.pantrixui.components.inputs.textfield.PantrixTextField(FormField<String>, Modifier, FormState?, Boolean, Boolean, String?, String?, String?, (@Composable () -> Unit)?, (@Composable () -> Unit)?, Boolean, Int?, Boolean, TextFieldLineLimits, KeyboardOptions, KeyboardActionHandler?, InputTransformation?, OutputTransformation?, ContentType?, TextFieldStyle?, TextFieldColors?, String?, MutableInteractionSource?)
declarations.name: PantrixTextField
declarations.signature:
@Composable
fun PantrixTextField(
    field: FormField<String>,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    form: FormState? = null,
    enabled: Boolean = true,
    readOnly: Boolean = false,
    label: String? = null,
    placeholder: String? = null,
    supportingText: String? = null,
    leadingIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null,
    trailingIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null,
    showClearButton: Boolean = false,
    maxLength: Int? = null,
    showCharacterCount: Boolean = true,
    lineLimits: TextFieldLineLimits = TextFieldLineLimits.SingleLine,
    keyboardOptions: KeyboardOptions = KeyboardOptions.Default,
    onKeyboardAction: KeyboardActionHandler? = null,
    inputTransformation: InputTransformation? = null,
    outputTransformation: OutputTransformation? = null,
    contentType: ContentType? = null,
    style: TextFieldStyle? = null,
    colors: TextFieldColors? = null,
    contentDescription: String? = null,
    interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null
)
declarations.description:
A text field bound to a form's field: its text, its error and its name come from `field`.

The field's value and the text on screen stay in step both ways: typing changes the field, and a change made to the field in code, such as a reset, replaces the text. When the focus leaves, the field is marked touched and checked, which is when an error first shows. While the field is in error its message takes the place of `supportingText`, rather than standing beside it. The field's id is the automation key, `TextField_<id>`, and the form can send the focus here when it is submitted with this field in error.

It is an overload of its own and not a parameter of the state's form, so that a state and a field cannot both be given.

parameters.name: field
parameters.description: the field the text field shows and changes.

parameters.name: modifier
parameters.description: the modifier of the whole field.

parameters.name: form
parameters.description: given, the keyboard's action key submits the form through the button registered with it: the form is checked, and then submitted or the focus sent to its first field in error. An action of `Next` or `Previous` moves the focus as it always does. A field of one line that names no action gets `ImeAction.Done`, since the default action never reaches a handler and Enter would submit nothing. A field of several lines is left alone: there Enter starts a new line. An `onKeyboardAction` of the caller's own takes the place of the submit.

parameters.name: enabled
parameters.description: whether the field can be typed into.

parameters.name: readOnly
parameters.description: whether the text can only be read.

parameters.name: label
parameters.description: what the field is for, written above the box: the field's name for a screen reader.

parameters.name: placeholder
parameters.description: shown in the box while it is empty.

parameters.name: supportingText
parameters.description: help under the box, while the field has no error to show there.

parameters.name: leadingIcon
parameters.description: what stands before the text.

parameters.name: trailingIcon
parameters.description: what stands after the text, and after the clear button.

parameters.name: showClearButton
parameters.description: shows a button that empties the field, while it can be typed into and is not empty.

parameters.name: maxLength
parameters.description: the most characters the user can enter. It has to be positive.

parameters.name: showCharacterCount
parameters.description: shows `count/maxLength` under the box while `maxLength` is set.

parameters.name: lineLimits
parameters.description: one line, or `TextFieldLineLimits.MultiLine`. Tab moves the focus on from either.

parameters.name: keyboardOptions
parameters.description: the keyboard's type, its capitals, its corrections and its action key.

parameters.name: onKeyboardAction
parameters.description: called for the keyboard's action key, in place of the form's submit.

parameters.name: inputTransformation
parameters.description: what is done to the text as the user types it.

parameters.name: outputTransformation
parameters.description: how the text is shown, without changing it.

parameters.name: contentType
parameters.description: what the field holds, for the platform to fill it in.

parameters.name: style
parameters.description: this call's own style: over every enclosing one and under the density. Only the fields it sets change, on every platform.

parameters.name: colors
parameters.description: this call's own colours, in place of the theme's roles: the ones it sets are used, and the rest stay the theme's. A disabled field is drawn in the theme's disabled colours whatever is given.

parameters.name: contentDescription
parameters.description: what a screen reader says for the field where it has no `label`.

parameters.name: interactionSource
parameters.description: the field's interactions, hoisted. It keeps a source of its own when this is null.

declarations.name: TextFieldStyle
declarations.description:
`PantrixTextField`'s box: its shape, how tall and how wide it is at the least, the room around its text, its icons and its border.

`height` is the box alone. The label sits above the box and not inside it, so one height serves a field with a label and one without. It is a minimum: a field of several lines, or a large font scale, makes the box taller and never cuts the text. Each preset's `verticalPadding` leaves at least the body's line of its height, at every density, so a field of one line is exactly as tall as its style says.

An icon sits in a slot of `iconSize + 2 × iconPadding`, flush with the box's edge, and the text beside a slot starts `horizontalPadding − iconPadding` from it. On Android that is a 44dp slot with the icon 10dp from the edge and the text 48dp from it.

The box has the medium step of the shape scale for its corners on every platform.

parameters.name: shape
parameters.description: The box's shape. A fully round one, `ShapeRole.Full`, is a pill only while the field holds one line: a field of several lines takes `ShapeRole.Large` instead, since a capsule's curve runs into the first line of its text.

parameters.name: height
parameters.description: The least the box is tall.

parameters.name: minWidth
parameters.description: The least the box is wide, which keeps an empty field from growing as the user types into it.

parameters.name: horizontalPadding
parameters.description: The room between the box's edge and its text, where no icon is.

parameters.name: verticalPadding
parameters.description: The room above the first line of the text and below the last.

parameters.name: iconPadding
parameters.description: The room around an icon in its slot.

parameters.name: iconSize
parameters.description: The size an icon in a slot should take. A slot does not size what is put in it.

parameters.name: borderWidth
parameters.description: How thick the box's border is.

parameters.name: focusedBorderWidth
parameters.description: How thick the border is while the field has the focus: the border is what shows it.

parameters.name: textRole
parameters.description: The role of the type scale the text is typed in, and its placeholder set in: the body's, 16sp, on Android and iOS, as Material 3 and iOS type a field, and the label's, 14sp, on the desktop and the web, as a page under a pointer does. A select's box and the fields made on this style take it as well.

declarations.name: TextFieldColors
declarations.description:
What `PantrixTextField` is painted with, for a field that does not take the theme's: a colour that is set is used, and one that is left out stays the theme's role. A product gives the colours it changes and no others:

```
PantrixTextField(
    state = state,
    label = stringResource(Res.string.email),
    colors = TextFieldColors(focusedBorder = brand, cursor = brand)
)
```

They are the colours of an enabled field, read-only or not. A disabled one is drawn in the theme's disabled roles whatever is given here, so that a disabled field looks the same across a product.

parameters.name: container
parameters.description: The box's fill. The theme's `surface`.

parameters.name: border
parameters.description: The box's border at rest. The theme's `border`.

parameters.name: hoveredBorder
parameters.description: The border under a pointer. The theme's `borderHover`, a notch stronger than `border`.

parameters.name: focusedBorder
parameters.description: The border while the field has the focus. The theme's `primary`.

parameters.name: error
parameters.description: What says the text is wrong: the border, the label, the message under the box, the caret, and the count once it is past its limit. The theme's `danger`.

parameters.name: text
parameters.description: The typed text. The theme's `textPrimary`.

parameters.name: label
parameters.description: The label above the box. Left out, it is drawn as any text is where the field stands, since it is outside the box on whatever the field is put on: in `textPrimary` on the theme's own ground, and in the content colour of a fill.

parameters.name: placeholder
parameters.description: The placeholder. The theme's `textSecondary`.

parameters.name: supportingText
parameters.description: The help under the box, and the count. The theme's `textSecondary`.

parameters.name: icon
parameters.description: What an icon in a slot is drawn in unless it sets a tint of its own, and the clear button's cross. The theme's `textSecondary`.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The caret, and with it the handles and the highlight of a selection. The theme's `primary`.

parameters.name: scrollBar
parameters.description: The bar that shows how far the text of a box of several lines is scrolled. The theme's `borderStrong`: it is a mark beside the text, and the box's soft edge would not be seen there.

declarations.name: BreadcrumbItem
declarations.description: One page of a `PantrixBreadcrumb`'s trail.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: What the trail's `onSelect` reports when the page is pressed. It is the same in every language, so a translated screen still knows which page was asked for.

parameters.name: label
parameters.description: The page's name, as it is written and as a screen reader says it.

parameters.name: icon
parameters.description: A picture of the page before its name, as a house before the first page of a trail.

parameters.name: iconOnly
parameters.description: Whether the page is shown by its `icon` alone. Its `label` is then what a screen reader says of it, and what the menu of folded pages writes beside the icon. A page without an icon is written whatever this says.

parameters.name: tagKey
parameters.description: The page's automation key, the same in every language, where it is to be another than `key`: the page is `Item_<tagKey>`, inside the tag of a trail that has a key, as `Breadcrumb_docs.Item_components`.

declarations.name: PantrixBreadcrumb
declarations.signature:
@Composable
fun PantrixBreadcrumb(
    items: List<BreadcrumbItem>,
    onSelect: (key: String) -> Unit,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    maxItems: Int = Int.MAX_VALUE,
    textStyle: TextStyle = PantrixTheme.typography.label,
    style: BreadcrumbStyle? = null,
    colors: BreadcrumbColors? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null
)
declarations.description:
The trail of pages above the one on screen, each a link back to it, ending in the page on screen.

The pages above are links, underlined and announced as links; the last one is the page on screen, a text whose state a screen reader says is the current page. A page may have an icon before its name, or in its place: a page shown by its icon alone is a button named by the page. The marks between the pages point the way the trail is read, and say nothing to a screen reader. The row is one group, named a breadcrumb in the theme's language. On iOS it is a group without a name: a screen reader there reads a group's own name after what the group holds, as one more thing at the trail's end.

A trail is one line, as tall as the platform's touch target at the least, and as wide as its pages: it starts where the text under it starts. It never wraps. Where the row is too narrow for all of it, the pages after the first fold away, as few of them as it takes, into a button that opens them as a menu: the trail keeps its first page, where it began, and its last ones, where it is. Where the first page and the last do not fit beside that button either, the longest names are cut to one width, and a short one keeps all of its own.

`maxItems` folds a trail that would fit, too: a row never shows more pages than that. A page chosen in the menu is reported as one pressed in the row is.

parameters.name: items
parameters.description: the trail from its top, ending in the page on screen.

parameters.name: onSelect
parameters.description: told the key of a page that is pressed, in the row or in the menu: never the last one's, which is where the app is.

parameters.name: modifier
parameters.description: applied to the row.

parameters.name: maxItems
parameters.description: the most pages the row shows, whatever room it has: at least two.

parameters.name: textStyle
parameters.description: the type the pages are set in: the theme's `label` unless given.

parameters.name: style
parameters.description: this call's own style: over every enclosing one and under the density. Only the fields it sets change, on every platform.

parameters.name: colors
parameters.description: this call's own colours. Only the ones it sets change; the rest stay the theme's.

parameters.name: tagKey
parameters.description: a locale-independent key for automation: the row's tag is `Breadcrumb_<tagKey>`, and its pages and the button that shows the folded ones are named inside it, `Breadcrumb_<tagKey>.Item_<page's key>` and `Breadcrumb_<tagKey>.More_pages`. The menu is `Menu_<tagKey>_more`, with a row for each folded page.

declarations.name: BreadcrumbStyle
declarations.description: `PantrixBreadcrumb`'s geometry: the room between a page and the mark beside it, how large that mark is, and how large a page's own icon is. It is the same on every platform: a trail of pages is a line of text, with 16dp marks and icons 4dp from the words. The room follows the density; the mark and the icon do not.

parameters.name: itemGap
parameters.description: Between a page's name and the mark that parts it from the next, and between a page's icon and its name.

parameters.name: separatorSize
parameters.description: The mark between two pages, and the button that stands for the pages a trail has folded.

parameters.name: iconSize
parameters.description: A page's own icon, before its name or in its place.

parameters.name: minHeight
parameters.description: The least height of the trail's row: the platform's touch target where it is not set, so that nothing else lies under a touch beside a page. A lower one fits a trail to a line of text over a page's title; a touch beside a page still reaches it, as the theme gives a small target its room for a touch without room in the layout.

parameters.name: linkUnderline
parameters.description: When the pages above the one on screen are underlined: `Always` where it is not set. A trail stands apart from any sentence, and its marks tell its links from the page on screen as well: `LinkUnderline.OnHover` underlines them under a pointer and the keyboard's focus, and always under a finger.

declarations.name: BreadcrumbColors
declarations.description:
What a `PantrixBreadcrumb` is painted with, for a trail that does not take the theme's colours: a colour that is set is used, and one that is left out stays the theme's.

```
PantrixBreadcrumb(…, colors = BreadcrumbColors(link = PantrixTheme.colors.success.color))
```

A trail has no fill of its own and stands on what is behind it. On a fill, which says what is written on it, all of the trail is written in that: the theme's link, its texts and its marks are colours for the theme's own grounds. A link is told from the page on screen by its underline there.

parameters.name: link
parameters.description: The pages above the one on screen, which are links, and their icons. The primary role's `color`.

parameters.name: current
parameters.description: The page on screen, the trail's last, and its icon. The theme's `textPrimary`.

parameters.name: separator
parameters.description: The marks between two pages, and the button that shows the pages a long trail has folded away. The theme's `textSecondary`.

declarations.name: NavigationIndicator
declarations.signature: enum class NavigationIndicator
declarations.description: What marks the destination the app is at, in a navigation bar or a navigation rail.

entries.name: Pill
entries.description: A pill behind the destination's icon, in the primary role's container: every platform's own bar and rail.

entries.name: None
entries.description: No shape: the destination's icon and its label are in the brand's colour, as a tab bar's are on iOS. A style that asks for it gets it; no platform's own bar or rail does.

declarations.name: NavigationColors
declarations.description:
What a navigation bar or a navigation rail is painted with, where it does not take the theme's colours: a colour that is set is used, and one that is left out stays the theme's. The two take the same colours, so a screen that shows one or the other by the window's width paints both with one set.

```
// The current destination in the success role, the rest as the theme has it.
val colors = NavigationColors(selectedContainer = PantrixTheme.colors.success.container)
PantrixNavigationBar(…, colors = colors)
```

A `container` given here that is one of the theme's role colours brings the colour the theme pairs with it for the destinations, unless `content` is given too, and a `selectedContainer` brings its pair for the icon on it, unless `selectedContent` is given. A fill no role has does not: what reads on it is the caller's to give.

The current destination is marked with a pill, or by colour alone where the style says so, and each has its own colours here: `selectedContainer` and `selectedContent` are the pill and what is on it, and `selectedTint` the colour where there is no pill. Giving the one changes nothing where the other is drawn.

parameters.name: container
parameters.description: The fill, which runs behind the insets that are kept clear. The theme's `surface`.

parameters.name: content
parameters.description: What is written on the fill: the label of the destination the app is at, under its pill, and the icons and labels of the others. On the theme's own fill the first is the theme's `textPrimary` and the others its `textSecondary`. On a fill of the caller's, and where this is given, all of them are this colour, and where no pill marks the current destination, the others are a share of it.

parameters.name: selectedContainer
parameters.description: The pill behind the current destination's icon, where the style draws one. The primary role's `container`.

parameters.name: selectedContent
parameters.description: The current destination's icon on its pill: the colour that reads on `selectedContainer`. The primary role's `onContainer`.

parameters.name: selectedTint
parameters.description: The current destination's icon and its label where the style draws no pill, and colour alone marks it: a colour that reads on `container`. The primary role's `color` on the theme's own fill where no `content` is given, and `content` where it is given or on a fill of the caller's, where nothing says that the brand's colour reads.

parameters.name: divider
parameters.description: The hairline along a bar's top edge or a rail's end edge, where the style draws one. The theme's `divider` on the theme's own grounds. On a fill, where that line would not read, a share of `content`: the edge a subtle button has.

declarations.name: NavigationBadge
declarations.description:
A badge on a destination of a navigation bar or a navigation rail: a count, or a dot where there is nothing to count.

The badge is on the destination's icon, at the corner where lines end, with its top level with the icon's: it stays inside a bar. It is a `PantrixBadge`, as large as that is and in its colours, on a destination of any state.

A screen reader hears `contentDescription` after the destination's label, as a part of the destination: "Inbox, 3 unread". The badge is over the label, and the destination says the two itself so that the name comes first. A number alone would say nothing of what it counts, so the badge is silent without a description, which is right only where the label says it already. It has no default for that reason: null is a decision.

parameters.name: contentDescription
parameters.description: What a screen reader says of the badge, after the destination's label, or null to say nothing.

parameters.name: count
parameters.description: The number to show, or null for a dot. It is capped as a badge's is: `99+`.

parameters.name: tone
parameters.description: The colour role the badge is filled from.

parameters.name: colors
parameters.description: The badge's own colours, in place of its tone's: the ones it sets, with the tone's for the rest.

declarations.name: NavigationItem
declarations.description: One of the app's top-level destinations: an icon with its label under it. A navigation bar and a navigation rail take the same destinations, so a screen can show one list of them along the bottom of a narrow window and down the side of a wide one.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: What the bar's or the rail's `selected` holds and its `onSelect` reports. It is the same in every language, so a translated screen still knows where it is, and the same destination has the same key wherever it is shown.

parameters.name: label
parameters.description: The visible text under the icon, and the destination's name for a screen reader.

parameters.name: icon
parameters.description: Drawn over the label, in the colour of what the destination is. A screen reader passes over it.

parameters.name: selectedIcon
parameters.description: Drawn in place of `icon` while the app is at this destination, a filled form of it, or null for the same icon.

parameters.name: badge
parameters.description: A count or a dot on the icon, or null for none.

parameters.name: enabled
parameters.description: Whether the destination can be pressed. One that cannot is drawn in the disabled text's colour.

parameters.name: tagKey
parameters.description: The destination's automation key, the same in every language, where it is to be another than `key`: the destination is `Item_<tagKey>`, inside the tag of a bar or a rail that has a key, as `NavigationBar_main.Item_inbox`.

declarations.name: NavigationBarOrientation
declarations.signature: enum class NavigationBarOrientation
declarations.description: Which way a `PantrixNavigationBar` runs.

entries.name: Horizontal
entries.description: Along the bottom of the screen: the destinations side by side, sharing the bar's width.

entries.name: Vertical
entries.description: Upright, in the system's vertical bar: the destinations one above another in a capsule as wide as they are, as the iPhone Duo's outer screen keeps its tabs. `PantrixScaffold` puts it at the bottom of the column there.

declarations.name: PantrixNavigationBar
declarations.signature:
@Composable
fun PantrixNavigationBar(
    items: List<NavigationItem>,
    selected: String?,
    onSelect: (key: String) -> Unit,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    orientation: NavigationBarOrientation = NavigationBarOrientation.Horizontal,
    showLabels: Boolean = orientation == NavigationBarOrientation.Horizontal,
    labelStyle: TextStyle = PantrixTheme.typography.footnote,
    style: NavigationBarStyle? = null,
    colors: NavigationColors? = null,
    insets: PaddingValues = PaddingValues(),
    tagKey: String? = null
)
declarations.description:
The app's top-level destinations along the bottom of the screen, three to five of them, with the one the app is at marked.

Which destination the app is at is the screen's state: the bar is given its key in `selected`, and reports a press in `onSelect`. A press on the current destination is reported too: an app commonly takes that destination back to its top.

The destinations share the bar's width. What marks the current one is the style's `NavigationBarStyle.indicator`: a pill behind its icon, or its colour alone where the style says so. A destination is a tab to a screen reader, which says its label, then what its badge says, and whether it is the one selected.

A `PantrixNavigationRail` takes the same destinations and the same colours: a screen that shows the bar in a narrow window and the rail in a wide one gives both the one list.

In a `PantrixScaffold`'s bottom bar the bar is given the scaffold's `insets`: its fill runs behind the system's navigation bar, and its destinations stay clear of it.

**Upright.** Where the system keeps a vertical bar, the column along the side of the iPhone Duo's outer screen, the bar stands in it as `NavigationBarOrientation.Vertical`: the destinations one above another in a capsule of the bar's fill, under a hairline around it where the style draws one along the top. A `PantrixScaffold` with adaptive navigation says where it is, `ScaffoldNavigationPlacement.VerticalBar`, and puts it at the column's bottom.

**Labels.** Each destination shows its label under its icon unless `showLabels` says not to, which is what an upright bar does unless it is asked: the system's column holds icons. Without its label a destination is named by it for a screen reader, and a tooltip shows it while a pointer rests on the icon, while the keyboard's focus is on it and after a long press: above a bar along the bottom, at the start of an upright one.

parameters.name: items
parameters.description: the destinations, in order: three to five of them is what a bar is made for, though nothing counts them.

parameters.name: selected
parameters.description: the key of the destination the app is at, or null where it is at none of them.

parameters.name: onSelect
parameters.description: told the key of a destination that is pressed, the current one's too.

parameters.name: modifier
parameters.description: applied to the bar.

parameters.name: orientation
parameters.description: which way the bar runs: along the bottom, or upright in the system's vertical bar.

parameters.name: showLabels
parameters.description: whether each destination shows its label under its icon: along the bottom it does unless told not to, upright it does not unless told to.

parameters.name: labelStyle
parameters.description: the type the labels are set in: the theme's `footnote` unless given. Their colour is the bar's.

parameters.name: style
parameters.description: this call's own style: over every enclosing one and under the density. Only the fields it sets change, on every platform.

parameters.name: colors
parameters.description: this call's own colours. Only the ones it sets change; the rest stay the theme's.

parameters.name: insets
parameters.description: the room the bar keeps clear along the bottom edge and at its sides, with its fill behind it: what a scaffold gives its bottom bar. An upright bar keeps it clear around its capsule, with nothing behind it.

parameters.name: tagKey
parameters.description: a locale-independent key for automation: the bar's tag is `NavigationBar_<tagKey>`, and its destinations are named inside it, `NavigationBar_<tagKey>.Item_<destination's key>`.

declarations.name: NavigationBarStyle
declarations.description:
`PantrixNavigationBar`'s geometry, and how it marks the destination the app is at.

The bar is the same on every platform: 64dp tall under a hairline, with a pill of 56dp by 28dp behind the current destination's icon, a 20dp icon and 4dp over the label. A pill, a gap and a line of a label leave 8dp over and under them. Android's own bar is 80dp with a larger pill, and a tab bar on iOS 49pt with no pill; neither is the preset here, and a style of the app's can ask for either.

The pill's room takes the press and the focus ring, where a pill is drawn and where none is. The height and the gap follow the density; the pill and the icon do not.

Upright, in the system's vertical bar, a destination is as tall as a touch and its pill 40dp wide, so that the capsule of icons is 48dp across, as UIKit's tab bar is in that column. A badge that reaches further widens the capsule as far as it reaches: it stays inside.

parameters.name: height
parameters.description: How tall the bar is, over the insets it keeps clear. A destination is never lower than the platform's touch target, and grows with a larger type.

parameters.name: indicatorWidth
parameters.description: How wide the pill behind the current destination's icon is, and the room a press is drawn in.

parameters.name: indicatorHeight
parameters.description: How tall that pill is.

parameters.name: iconSize
parameters.description: A destination's icon.

parameters.name: labelGap
parameters.description: Between the pill's room and the label under it.

parameters.name: indicator
parameters.description: What marks the current destination.

parameters.name: divider
parameters.description: Whether a hairline runs along the bar's top edge, inside its height; upright, around its capsule.

parameters.name: uprightIndicatorWidth
parameters.description: How wide the pill is in an upright bar, and the room a press is drawn in there. A destination there is as wide as its pill and its label.

declarations.name: PantrixNavigationRail
declarations.signature:
@Composable
fun PantrixNavigationRail(
    items: List<NavigationItem>,
    selected: String?,
    onSelect: (key: String) -> Unit,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    labelStyle: TextStyle = PantrixTheme.typography.footnote,
    style: NavigationRailStyle? = null,
    colors: NavigationColors? = null,
    header: (@Composable ColumnScope.() -> Unit)? = null,
    insets: PaddingValues = PaddingValues(),
    tagKey: String? = null
)
declarations.description:
The app's top-level destinations down the start edge of a wide window, with the one the app is at marked: the navigation bar's place on a tablet, an open foldable or a desktop window.

It takes a bar's destinations and is told where the app is as a bar is: the key of the current destination in `selected`, and a press reported in `onSelect`, the current destination's too. A screen that shows a bar in a narrow window and a rail in a wide one gives both the one list, and the one set of colours.

The destinations stand one under another from the top, under an optional `header`: a button that opens a menu, or the screen's main action. Where they are taller than the rail they scroll, and the header stays. A destination is a tab to a screen reader, which says its label, then what its badge says, and whether it is the one selected.

The rail is as tall as the room it is given, which has to have an end: a scaffold's side bar has. There it is given the scaffold's `insets`: its fill runs behind the system's bars, and what it holds stays clear of them.

parameters.name: items
parameters.description: the destinations, in order: three to seven of them is what a rail is made for, though nothing counts them.

parameters.name: selected
parameters.description: the key of the destination the app is at, or null where it is at none of them.

parameters.name: onSelect
parameters.description: told the key of a destination that is pressed, the current one's too.

parameters.name: modifier
parameters.description: applied to the rail.

parameters.name: labelStyle
parameters.description: the type the labels are set in: the theme's `footnote` unless given. Their colour is the rail's.

parameters.name: style
parameters.description: this call's own style: over every enclosing one and under the density. Only the fields it sets change, on every platform.

parameters.name: colors
parameters.description: this call's own colours. Only the ones it sets change; the rest stay the theme's.

parameters.name: header
parameters.description: over the destinations, in the middle of the rail's width. A text or an icon in it that names no colour of its own has its own default on the theme's fill, and what is written on the rail on a fill of the caller's.

parameters.name: insets
parameters.description: the room the rail keeps clear at its top, its bottom and its start, with its fill behind it: what a scaffold gives its side bar.

parameters.name: tagKey
parameters.description: a locale-independent key for automation: the rail's tag is `NavigationRail_<tagKey>`, and its destinations are named inside it, `NavigationRail_<tagKey>.Item_<destination's key>`.

declarations.name: NavigationRailStyle
declarations.description:
`PantrixNavigationRail`'s geometry, and how it marks the destination the app is at.

The rail is the same on every platform, and its destinations are a navigation bar's: 80dp wide beside a hairline, with a pill of 56dp by 28dp behind the current destination's icon, a 20dp icon and 4dp over the label. The destinations stand one under another from the top, 56dp tall each and 4dp apart, under a header 8dp over them.

The pill's room takes the press and the focus ring, where a pill is drawn and where none is. The width, the heights and the gaps follow the density; the pill and the icon do not.

parameters.name: width
parameters.description: How wide the rail is, beside the insets it keeps clear.

parameters.name: indicatorWidth
parameters.description: How wide the pill behind the current destination's icon is, and the room a press is drawn in.

parameters.name: indicatorHeight
parameters.description: How tall that pill is.

parameters.name: iconSize
parameters.description: A destination's icon.

parameters.name: labelGap
parameters.description: Between the pill's room and the label under it.

parameters.name: itemMinHeight
parameters.description: The least a destination is tall. It is never lower than the platform's touch target, and grows with a larger type.

parameters.name: itemSpacing
parameters.description: Between one destination and the next.

parameters.name: headerGap
parameters.description: Between the header and the first destination.

parameters.name: verticalPadding
parameters.description: Over the header, or the first destination, and under the last.

parameters.name: indicator
parameters.description: What marks the current destination.

parameters.name: divider
parameters.description: Whether a hairline runs along the rail's end edge, inside its width.

declarations.name: PantrixSidebar
declarations.signature:
@Composable
fun PantrixSidebar(
    groups: List<SidebarGroup>,
    selected: String?,
    onSelect: (String) -> Unit,
    expanded: Set<String>,
    onExpandedChange: (Set<String>) -> Unit,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    collapsed: Boolean = false,
    adaptive: Boolean = true,
    flyout: SidebarFlyout = SidebarFlyout.Popup,
    singleExpanded: Boolean = true,
    style: SidebarStyle? = null,
    colors: SidebarColors? = null,
    header: (@Composable SidebarSlotScope.() -> Unit)? = null,
    footerItems: List<SidebarItem> = emptyList(),
    footer: (@Composable SidebarSlotScope.() -> Unit)? = null,
    insets: PaddingValues = PaddingValues(),
    tagKey: String? = null,
    textStyle: TextStyle = PantrixTheme.typography.label,
    titleTextStyle: TextStyle = PantrixTheme.typography.caption.copy(fontWeight = FontWeight.Bold)
)
declarations.description:
The column of destinations down the side of an app, with the sections of the app it holds.

A sidebar is two levels deep and no more: sections, and the destinations inside them. A section opens and closes in place, and by default opening one closes whichever was open (`singleExpanded`), so a sidebar of six sections stays the height of six rows and not of everything the app can show. The rows between the header and the pinned destinations scroll when there are more than fit.

`collapsed`, it is a rail of icons. A destination's icon then carries its name, which a tooltip shows, and a section opens what it holds beside the rail (`flyout`): a card, as a pointer rests on the section and at a press where there is no pointer, or a column of its own that moves the page over. Either goes once a destination in it is chosen, and it is where a row's `SidebarItem.detail` is written. A top-level row without an icon is drawn as a chevron on the rail: give every one an icon.

By default the sidebar takes the rail by itself where its column would crowd the page (`adaptive`): an unfolded foldable, a tablet held upright and a narrow window get the rail, a wide window the column. The header and the footer are told which it is, through `SidebarSlotScope.collapsed`.

Which destination is current and which sections are open are both the caller's state: navigation belongs to the app, and a sidebar that kept its own would fight the back button, a deep link and a restored process.

```
var where by rememberSaveable { mutableStateOf("crashes") }
var open by rememberSaveable { mutableStateOf(setOf("quality")) }
PantrixScaffold(
    sideBar = { insets ->
        PantrixSidebar(
            groups = groups,
            selected = where,
            onSelect = { where = it },
            expanded = open,
            onExpandedChange = { open = it },
            insets = insets,
            tagKey = "main"
        )
    }
) { padding -> Page(where, padding) }
```

The current destination is told three ways: its fill, a label a step heavier than the others, and its selected state for a screen reader. The section that holds it is written heavier too, and on the rail it has the fill and the bar on the rail's edge: a closed section still says where the app is. A section says to a screen reader whether it is open, and a closed one composes nothing of what it holds. A row is never lower than the platform's touch target, and grows with a larger type. Rows that do not fit scroll, with Pantrix's scroll bar along the sidebar's end where the reader has a pointer.

parameters.name: groups
parameters.description: the rows, in groups, in order. A line is drawn between one group and the next.

parameters.name: selected
parameters.description: the key of the destination the app is showing, or null where it shows none of them.

parameters.name: onSelect
parameters.description: called with the key of a destination that was pressed. The sidebar changes nothing by itself.

parameters.name: expanded
parameters.description: the keys of the sections that are open in the column. The rail opens a section beside itself and keeps which by itself: nothing of it is the app's to restore.

parameters.name: onExpandedChange
parameters.description: called with the keys that are to be open after a section of the column was pressed.

parameters.name: modifier
parameters.description: the sidebar's modifier. The sidebar is as wide as its style says, and wider by the `insets` at its sides, and as tall as the room it is given: its rows take what the header, the pinned destinations and the footer leave, and scroll inside it. Where the room has no end, inside a page that scrolls, it needs a height of its own.

parameters.name: collapsed
parameters.description: whether the sidebar is drawn as its rail, at any width. The shape changes at once, and the sidebar's width follows it over the theme's motion, the page beside it moving with it.

parameters.name: adaptive
parameters.description: whether the sidebar takes the rail by itself where the column would crowd the page: where the width it is offered, less the column's, is under the window's expanded breakpoint, 840dp unless the window's breakpoints say otherwise, below which a page has no room for two panes. False leaves the shape to `collapsed` alone: for a sidebar in a drawer, which covers the page and crowds nothing, or for an app that lets its user pin the column. It measures what it is offered, so it cannot be asked its intrinsic size: turn it off under a parent that is sized by `IntrinsicSize`.

parameters.name: flyout
parameters.description: what a section of the rail opens: `SidebarFlyout.Popup`, a card beside the section, or `SidebarFlyout.Panel`, a column beside the rail that moves the page over. The column opens its sections in place either way.

parameters.name: singleExpanded
parameters.description: whether opening a section of the column closes whichever was open.

parameters.name: style
parameters.description: this call's own style: over every enclosing one and under the density. Only the fields it sets change, on every platform.

parameters.name: colors
parameters.description: this sidebar's own colours, where they are not the theme's: the ones set here, with the theme's for the rest. What a rail's section opens is drawn in them too.

parameters.name: header
parameters.description: what stands above the rows and does not scroll: the app's mark, a workspace switcher. A line sets it off. It lays itself out for the width it has, by `SidebarSlotScope.collapsed`.

parameters.name: footerItems
parameters.description: destinations pinned under the rows, below a line: settings, help. They are no sections: one that has children is refused.

parameters.name: footer
parameters.description: what stands at the very bottom and does not scroll, below `footerItems` and a line: an account, a plan. It lays itself out for the width it has, as the header does.

parameters.name: insets
parameters.description: the room the sidebar keeps clear at its edges while its fill runs behind it: what a scaffold gives its side bar, so that the rows stand clear of the system bars.

parameters.name: tagKey
parameters.description: the sidebar's automation key: the sidebar is `Sidebar_<tagKey>`, a destination in it `Sidebar_<tagKey>.Item_<key>` wherever it is shown, and a section `Sidebar_<tagKey>.Section_<key>`; what a rail's section opens is `Sidebar_<tagKey>.Flyout_<key>` or `Sidebar_<tagKey>.Panel_<key>`. A press is reported as a `Sidebar` event: `select` with the destination's key and whether the sidebar was its rail, `expand` and `collapse` with the section's.

parameters.name: textStyle
parameters.description: the type a row's name is set in, in the column, in a section's and in what a rail's section opens: the theme's `label` unless given. The current destination and the section that holds it are set a step heavier than it. A colour in it is not a row's, which is the row's state's.

parameters.name: titleTextStyle
parameters.description: the type a group's title is set in, in capitals: the theme's `caption`, bold, unless given. It is written in the sidebar's quiet colour whatever colour it holds.

declarations.name: SidebarFlyout
declarations.signature: enum class SidebarFlyout
declarations.description: What a section of a collapsed `PantrixSidebar`, its rail, opens to show its destinations.

entries.name: Popup
entries.description: A card beside the section, as tall as what it holds. Where there is a pointer it is up while the pointer rests on the section or on the card, so that moving down the rail reads each section in turn; a press without a pointer, a finger's, the keyboard's or a screen reader's, opens it with the keyboard in it, until it is dismissed.

entries.name: Panel
entries.description: The section's destinations in a column of their own against the rail, the column's width and the rail's height: a part of the sidebar, which is wider by it, so that the page beside it moves over and is not covered. It opens at a press, and not as a pointer passes. Choosing a destination, pressing the section again and Escape close it, and pressing another section shows that one's.

declarations.name: SidebarSlotScope
declarations.signature: interface SidebarSlotScope : ColumnScope
declarations.description:
What a sidebar's header and its footer are laid out in: a column as wide as the sidebar, which knows the shape the sidebar is drawn in.

A header lays itself out for the width it has, a mark alone on the rail and the mark with a name beside it in the column, and a footer does the same with an avatar.

members.name: collapsed
members.description: Whether the sidebar is drawn as its rail: because the caller said so, or because an adaptive sidebar took the rail by itself.

declarations.name: SidebarItem
declarations.description: One row of a `PantrixSidebar`: a destination, or a section with the destinations inside it.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: What the sidebar's `selected` holds and its `onSelect` reports, and what its `expanded` holds for a section. It is the same in every language, so a translated screen still knows where it is.

parameters.name: label
parameters.description: The visible text, and the row's name for a screen reader.

parameters.name: icon
parameters.description: Drawn before the label, in the label's colour, or null for none. A screen reader passes over it.

parameters.name: children
parameters.description: The destinations inside this row. A row that has any is a section and no destination itself: a press opens and closes it. A sidebar is two levels and no more, so a child's own children are not drawn.

parameters.name: detail
parameters.description: A number or a state beside the label, "87 open", "48.2M requests", or null for none. It is drawn in what a rail's section opens, where there is room for it. The column is a list of places to go, and a run of figures down its side would read as data.

parameters.name: enabled
parameters.description: Whether the row can be pressed. One that cannot is written in the disabled text's colour. A section that cannot be pressed stays open or closed as the sidebar's `expanded` has it, and each destination inside it follows its own.

parameters.name: tagKey
parameters.description: The row's automation key, the same in every language, where it is to be another than `key`: a destination is `Item_<tagKey>` and a section `Section_<tagKey>`, inside the tag of a sidebar that has a key, as `Sidebar_main.Item_crashes`.

declarations.name: SidebarGroup
declarations.description:
A run of a `PantrixSidebar`'s rows, with a line between it and the next, or its `title` over it.

Groups are how a sidebar says which destinations belong together, what the app is above and what it measures below. A group without a title is set apart by a line alone, and a sidebar of one such group draws no line at all. A group with a title opens with it, in small capitals in the quiet colour, as a documentation's "Getting started" and "Guides" do; a rail has no room for words, and draws the line there instead.

parameters.name: items
parameters.description: The group's rows, in order.

parameters.name: title
parameters.description: What the group is called, over its rows in the column, or null for a line alone. It is written in capitals by the rules of the theme's language, and a screen reader hears it as a heading.

constructors.description: A group of `items`, in the order they are given, without a title.

declarations.name: SidebarStyle
declarations.description:
`PantrixSidebar`'s geometry: its width as a column and as a rail, its rows at both levels, and the line that says a section's destinations are inside it.

The column's width is the same on every platform: what a sidebar holds is the same, and one that changed its width would move the app's whole layout with it. The rows and the room in them follow the density; the widths, the icons, the indent, the corners, the line and the mark do not. A sidebar's colours are not part of its style: they are the theme's, and `SidebarColors` where a sidebar has its own.

parameters.name: width
parameters.description: How wide the sidebar is as a column, and how wide the column a rail's section opens beside it: 248dp.

parameters.name: collapsedWidth
parameters.description: How wide the sidebar is as a rail of icons: 76dp on Android and iOS, 68dp on desktop, 72dp on the web.

parameters.name: rowHeight
parameters.description: The least height of a top-level row, a destination's or a section's: 44dp on Android and iOS, 36dp on desktop, 40dp on the web. A row is never lower than the platform's touch target.

parameters.name: childRowHeight
parameters.description: The least height of a destination inside a section: 40dp on Android and iOS, 32dp on desktop, 36dp on the web. It is never lower than the platform's touch target either.

parameters.name: shape
parameters.description: The corners of a row's fill: medium on Android and iOS, small on desktop and the web.

parameters.name: horizontalPadding
parameters.description: The room between the sidebar's edge and a row's fill, and again between the fill's edge and what the row holds: 12dp on Android and iOS, 10dp on desktop and the web.

parameters.name: iconSize
parameters.description: A row's icon, and a section's chevron: 20dp on Android and iOS, 18dp on desktop and the web.

parameters.name: collapsedIconSize
parameters.description: A row's icon on the rail, where the icon is the row: 24dp on Android and iOS, 22dp on desktop and the web.

parameters.name: iconGap
parameters.description: The room between a row's icon and its label: 12dp on Android and iOS, 10dp on desktop and the web.

parameters.name: childIndent
parameters.description: How far a destination inside a section starts in from where its section does: 32dp on Android and iOS, 28dp on desktop and the web.

parameters.name: guideWidth
parameters.description: How thick the line down an open section's destinations is: 1dp.

parameters.name: markerSize
parameters.description: How thick the bar on the rail's edge is, beside the row the app is at: 4dp.

declarations.name: SidebarColors
declarations.description:
What a `PantrixSidebar` is painted with, for a sidebar that does not take the theme's colours: a colour that is set is used, and one that is left out stays the theme's.

```
// The current destination in the success role, the rest as the theme has it.
PantrixSidebar(…, colors = SidebarColors(selectedContainer = PantrixTheme.colors.success.container))
```

A `container` given here that is one of the theme's role colours brings the colour the theme pairs with it for the rows, unless `content` is given too, and a `selectedContainer` brings its pair for the current destination, unless `selectedContent` is given. A fill no role has does not: what reads on it is the caller's to give.

parameters.name: container
parameters.description: The sidebar's fill. The theme's `surface`.

parameters.name: content
parameters.description: A section's icon and name, and what the header and the footer hold where they give no colour of their own. The theme's `textPrimary`. A destination that is not the current one, and a section's chevron, are the theme's `textSecondary` on the theme's own fill, and this colour on a fill of the caller's.

parameters.name: selectedContainer
parameters.description: The fill behind the current destination. The primary role's `container`.

parameters.name: selectedContent
parameters.description: The current destination's icon and label: the colour that reads on `selectedContainer`. The primary role's `onContainer`.

parameters.name: divider
parameters.description: The lines between the header, the groups, the pinned destinations and the footer, the line down an open section's destinations, and the edge of what a rail's section opens. The theme's `divider` on the theme's own grounds. On a fill, where that line would not read, a share of `content`: the edge a subtle button has.

parameters.name: marker
parameters.description: The bar on the rail's edge beside the row the app is at. The primary role's `color` on the theme's own fill, and `content` on a fill of the caller's.

declarations.name: PantrixCommandPalette
declarations.signature:
@Composable
fun PantrixCommandPalette(
    visible: Boolean,
    onDismissRequest: () -> Unit,
    commands: List<PantrixCommand>,
    onRun: (PantrixCommand) -> Unit,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    placeholder: String? = null,
    emptyText: String? = null,
    style: CommandPaletteStyle? = null,
    colors: CommandPaletteColors? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null
)
declarations.description:
Every command of the app, found by its name and run from the keyboard: what Cmd+K or Ctrl+K opens.

The palette is modal, as a dialog is: a scrim over the app, the focus inside, and back, Escape and a click on the scrim asking to close. Whether it is shown is the caller's: give `visible`, and act on `onDismissRequest` and on `onRun`, which is where the palette is closed before the command does its work. It stands at the top of the window, where its field stays while the list under it grows and shrinks.

**Finding.** The field takes the focus as the palette opens, on a phone too, and keeps it while the list is walked. With nothing typed every command is listed, under its group. What is typed narrows the list to the commands whose label, group or keywords hold each word of it, compared in the theme's language; inside a group those whose label starts with it come first, and the letters found are marked. Each time it opens the field is empty.

**Running.** One command is highlighted, at first the first that can be run. The arrows down and up move the highlight over the commands that can be run and stop at the ends, Page Down and Page Up a page at a time, and the pointer moves it to the row it passes over. Enter, the keyboard's action and a press on a row run the command. A command that is not `enabled` is listed, faint, and is not run.

**Shortcuts.** A command's `PantrixCommand.shortcut` is written at its row's end as the system writes it. The palette opens by a shortcut of the app's, and the commands run by theirs, with `commandShortcuts` on the window's root.

**To a screen reader** the palette is announced by the theme's name for a list of commands. The highlighted row is selected, the groups are headings, and as what is typed narrows the list, the number of commands left is said.

```
var open by rememberSaveable { mutableStateOf(false) }
Box(Modifier.shortcutRoot().onShortcut(PantrixShortcut(Key.K, command = true)) { open = true }) {
    …
    PantrixCommandPalette(
        visible = open,
        onDismissRequest = { open = false },
        commands = commands,
        onRun = { command ->
            open = false
            run(command.key)
        },
        tagKey = "commands"
    )
}
```

parameters.name: visible
parameters.description: whether the palette is shown. It never hides itself.

parameters.name: onDismissRequest
parameters.description: called for back, Escape and a click on the scrim.

parameters.name: commands
parameters.description: every command, in the order they are listed under their groups. No two have one key.

parameters.name: onRun
parameters.description: called with the command run, by Enter, the keyboard's action or a press. Close the palette here.

parameters.name: modifier
parameters.description: the panel's modifier.

parameters.name: placeholder
parameters.description: what the empty field shows, or null for the theme's words for searching commands.

parameters.name: emptyText
parameters.description: what stands in the list's place while nothing matches, or null for the theme's words for it.

parameters.name: style
parameters.description: this call's own style: over every enclosing one and under the density. Only the fields it sets change, on every platform.

parameters.name: colors
parameters.description: this palette's own colours, where they are not the theme's: the ones set here, with the theme's for the rest.

parameters.name: tagKey
parameters.description: the palette's automation key: the panel is `CommandPalette_<tagKey>`, its field `CommandPalette_<tagKey>.TextField_query` and a command's row `CommandPalette_<tagKey>.Command_<key>`. What is done is reported as a `CommandPalette` event: `open`, `dismiss` with `via` (`back` or `scrim`), and `run` with the command's key and `via` (`key` or `click`). What is typed is never reported.

declarations.name: CommandPaletteStyle
declarations.description:
`PantrixCommandPalette`'s geometry: the panel, where it stands, and the rows of its list.

No platform has a command palette of its own. The panel is a dialog's, its corners and its shadow as the platform's dialog has them, and the rows are the platform's list rows: 48dp on Android, 44pt on iOS and 36dp under a pointer. A row is never lower than the platform's touch target.

The panel stands at the top of the window, where a field that is typed in stays while the list under it grows and shrinks: below the margin on a phone, and lower on a desktop and the web, by `topSpace`.

The room, the rows' height and the gaps follow the density. The panel's size, its corners, its shadow and the icons do not.

parameters.name: shape
parameters.description: The panel's corners: a step of the brand's shape scale, or a fixed shape.

parameters.name: maxWidth
parameters.description: The widest the panel grows in a wide window.

parameters.name: maxHeight
parameters.description: The tallest the panel grows in a tall window. A narrower window, and the keyboard, make it less.

parameters.name: elevation
parameters.description: The panel's shadow. iOS sets a panel apart by the dimming alone.

parameters.name: margin
parameters.description: The least room between the panel and the window's safe area.

parameters.name: topSpace
parameters.description: The room above the panel, past `margin`.

parameters.name: itemHeight
parameters.description: The least height of a command's row. A larger type makes it taller.

parameters.name: itemHorizontalPadding
parameters.description: The room between a row's sides and what it holds, and a heading's.

parameters.name: iconSize
parameters.description: The width and height of a command's icon.

parameters.name: iconGap
parameters.description: Between a command's icon, its label and its shortcut.

declarations.name: CommandPaletteColors
declarations.description:
What a `PantrixCommandPalette` is painted with, in place of the theme's colours: a colour that is set is used, and one that is left out stays the theme's.

A `container` given here that is one of the theme's role colours brings the colour the theme pairs with it for what is written on the panel, unless `content` is given too, and a `highlightedContainer` brings its pair for the highlighted row, unless `highlightedContent` is given. A fill no role has does not: what reads on it is the caller's to give.

parameters.name: container
parameters.description: The panel's fill. The theme's `surface`.

parameters.name: content
parameters.description: A command's label and its icon, and what is typed. The theme's `textPrimary`, or the colour a role's fill given as `container` gives what stands on it.

parameters.name: highlightedContainer
parameters.description: The fill behind the command Enter runs. The primary role's `container`.

parameters.name: highlightedContent
parameters.description: That command's label, icon and shortcut: the colour that reads on `highlightedContainer`. The primary role's `onContainer`.

parameters.name: heading
parameters.description: A group's heading, a shortcut and what stands in the list's place when nothing matches. The theme's `textSecondary` on the theme's own grounds, and `content` on another fill.

parameters.name: scrim
parameters.description: The dimming laid over the app behind the palette, with its own alpha. The theme's `scrim`.

declarations.name: commandShortcuts
declarations.signature:
fun Modifier.commandShortcuts(
    commands: List<PantrixCommand>,
    onRun: (PantrixCommand) -> Unit
): Modifier
declarations.description:
Runs each command of `commands` that has a shortcut by that shortcut, by `onRun`, while the focus is on this node or inside it: the one list of commands is what the palette shows and what the keyboard runs.

A command that is not `enabled` lets its keys through. Of two commands with one shortcut, the first one runs. Put it on a window's root with `shortcutRoot`, which holds the focus while nothing else does, so that the shortcuts are heard then too:

```
Box(Modifier.shortcutRoot().commandShortcuts(commands, onRun = { run(it.key) })) { … }
```

While a palette or another modal of Pantrix's is open, the keys are its own, and these shortcuts are not heard.

parameters.name: commands
parameters.description: the commands, as the palette is given them.

parameters.name: onRun
parameters.description: called with the command whose shortcut was pressed.

declarations.name: PantrixCommand
declarations.description:
One command of a `PantrixCommandPalette`: what the user reads, where it is listed, and what else finds it.

```
PantrixCommand(
    key = "rename",
    label = stringResource(Res.string.rename),
    group = stringResource(Res.string.file),
    shortcut = PantrixShortcut(Key.R, command = true)
)
```

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: the command's own key, the same in every language: what `PantrixCommandPalette`'s `onRun` and its `run` event are given, and its row's automation key unless `tagKey` is given. No two commands of a palette have one key.

parameters.name: label
parameters.description: what the command does, as the user reads it.

parameters.name: group
parameters.description: the heading the command is listed under, or null for one listed under none.

parameters.name: icon
parameters.description: drawn before the label.

parameters.name: shortcut
