parameters.description: the keys that run the same thing, written at the row's end as the system writes them. Binding them is `Modifier.commandShortcuts`'s.

parameters.name: keywords
parameters.description: other words that find the command: what another app calls it, a word a user types for it.

parameters.name: enabled
parameters.description: whether the command can be run now. One that cannot is listed, faint, and the arrows pass it by.

parameters.name: tagKey
parameters.description: the row's automation key, where it is not `key`.

parameters.name: supportingText
parameters.description: a second line under the label, smaller and quieter: what the command opens or where it leads. A screen reader hears it after the label, and a search finds the command by it, as by a keyword.

declarations.name: OverlayPresentation
declarations.signature: enum class OverlayPresentation
declarations.description:
How an overlay that belongs to a control is shown: beside the control, or as a sheet from the bottom of the window.

A popover beside what was pressed suits a window with room around the control, and a pointer. On a phone the same overlay is small under a finger and hides the screen's middle; a sheet from the bottom edge is within the thumb's reach and as wide as the window.

entries.name: Adaptive
entries.description: A sheet in a narrow window, the `Compact` width class, and a popover in every wider one. The window is the one the overlay is shown over, not the room of a pane it was opened in, and it is asked as the overlay opens: one that is open stays as it is when the window changes, and the next one is shown by the window as it is then.

entries.name: Popover
entries.description: A popover beside the control, in every window.

entries.name: Sheet
entries.description: A sheet from the bottom edge of the window, in every window.

declarations.name: PantrixDialog
declarations.signature:
@Composable
fun PantrixDialog(
    visible: Boolean,
    onDismissRequest: () -> Unit,
    title: String? = null,
    actions: @Composable RowScope.() -> Unit,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    message: String? = null,
    icon: ImageVector? = null,
    dismissible: Boolean = true,
    style: DialogStyle? = null,
    colors: DialogColors? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null,
    content: (@Composable ColumnScope.() -> Unit)? = null
)
declarations.description:
A decision or a message that stops the app until the user deals with it.

The dialog sits in the middle of the window, above a scrim, and is modal on every platform: nothing behind it takes a click, Tab never leaves it, and on Android TalkBack stays inside it. It is shown while `visible` is true and enters and leaves with the theme's motion; it never hides itself. Back, Escape and a click on the scrim call `onDismissRequest` unless `dismissible` is false. The actions the caller puts in `actions` call only their own `onClick`: an action that ends the dialog sets `visible` to false there.

A keyboard user starts on the first control, usually the first action, so put the safe choice first: "Cancel" before "Delete". The title is announced when the dialog appears and is its heading. A dialog without one, a `title` that is null or blank, has nothing in its place: what it holds starts at the top.

**Close it to see it leave.** A dialog that has closed composes nothing, so leaving it in the tree with `visible = false` is free, and it leaves with the theme's motion. An open one that is taken out of the composition is gone without it, and that is all it costs: its window is composed at the root of the window around it, so a layout that throws its content away while it measures closes no layer that is still being measured.

It looks the same on every platform; what differs is in `DialogStyle`: the corners, the widths and the shadow. A dialog of a title, a message and actions is as wide as its widest part, between the style's two widths: a short question is narrow, and a long message wraps at the widest. A dialog that holds `content` is as wide as it may be, so that a field or a list in it has room.

parameters.name: visible
parameters.description: whether the dialog is shown. It enters and leaves with the theme's motion.

parameters.name: onDismissRequest
parameters.description: called for back, Escape and a click on the scrim while `dismissible`. The dialog stays until `visible` is false.

parameters.name: title
parameters.description: what the dialog is about, as a short question or statement: "Delete this file?". Null or blank for none: no line is kept for it, and a screen reader announces no name when the dialog appears.

parameters.name: actions
parameters.description: end-aligned buttons, which wrap onto another line when they do not fit. They keep their own test tags.

parameters.name: modifier
parameters.description: applied to the dialog itself. The margin it keeps to the window is no part of it.

parameters.name: message
parameters.description: the explanation under the title. It scrolls with `content` when the window is short.

parameters.name: icon
parameters.description: a decorative icon above the title, which then centres.

parameters.name: dismissible
parameters.description: whether back, Escape and a click on the scrim ask to close. Turn it off only when the user must choose one of `actions`.

parameters.name: style
parameters.description: this call's own style: over every enclosing one and under the density. Only the fields it sets change, on every platform.

parameters.name: colors
parameters.description: this call's own colours. Only the ones it sets change; the rest stay the theme's.

parameters.name: tagKey
parameters.description: a locale-independent key for automation: the dialog's tag is `Dialog_<tagKey>`, on the dialog as it is drawn.

parameters.name: content
parameters.description: anything else the dialog holds, under the message: a form field, a list of choices.

declarations.name: DialogStyle
declarations.description:
`PantrixDialog`'s geometry.

The padding and the gaps between the title, the message and the actions come from the theme's spacing, so they follow density, and so do the narrowest width and the margin. The widest width, the corners, the shadow and the icon do not. A dialog's colours are not part of its style: they are the theme's, and `DialogColors` where a call has its own.

parameters.name: shape
parameters.description: The dialog's corners: large on Android and iOS, medium on desktop and the web.

parameters.name: minWidth
parameters.description: The narrowest the dialog gets, however short its title, its message and its actions are.

parameters.name: maxWidth
parameters.description: The widest the dialog gets: longer text wraps. A dialog that holds content of the caller's is this wide.

parameters.name: margin
parameters.description: Kept clear between the dialog and the window's edges, so the scrim still shows around it in a small window. A window narrower than `minWidth` and two margins gives the dialog what is left.

parameters.name: elevation
parameters.description: How high the dialog floats over the scrim, which is how large its shadow is. None on iOS.

parameters.name: iconSize
parameters.description: The size of the icon above the title.

declarations.name: DialogColors
declarations.description:
What a `PantrixDialog` is painted with, for a call that does not take the theme's colours: a colour that is set is used, and one that is left out stays the theme's.

```
PantrixDialog(…, colors = DialogColors(icon = PantrixTheme.colors.danger.color))
```

A `container` given here that is one of the theme's role colours brings the colour the theme pairs with it for the title, the message and the icon, unless those are given too. A fill no role has does not: what reads on it is the caller's to give.

parameters.name: container
parameters.description: The dialog's fill. The theme's `surface`.

parameters.name: title
parameters.description: The title. The theme's `textPrimary`.

parameters.name: message
parameters.description: The message under the title. The theme's `textSecondary`.

parameters.name: icon
parameters.description: The icon above the title. The primary role's `color`.

parameters.name: scrim
parameters.description: The dimming laid over the app behind the dialog, with its own alpha. The theme's `scrim`.

declarations.name: PantrixDiagnosticsInspector
declarations.signature:
@Composable
fun PantrixDiagnosticsInspector(
    findings: PantrixFindings,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    alignment: Alignment = Alignment.BottomEnd,
    tagKey: String? = null,
    content: @Composable () -> Unit
)
declarations.description:
Shows over an app what its theme's diagnostics have found: a button with the number of findings, and on its press a sheet that lists them, each with its check, where it was found and what puts it right. A finding chosen in the list is outlined where its node stands, until the screen is next pressed. While nothing has been found, nothing is shown.

It holds the app's screen: `content` is laid out as it would be without it, and gets every press, the one that takes an outline away among them. A release build leaves it out, as it leaves the diagnostics off.

parameters.name: findings
parameters.description: what the theme's diagnostics have found: the `diagnostics` of the theme around `content`.

parameters.name: modifier
parameters.description: applied to the box that holds `content` and the inspector over it.

parameters.name: alignment
parameters.description: where the button stands over `content`.

parameters.name: tagKey
parameters.description: a locale-independent key for automation: the inspector's tag is `DiagnosticsInspector_<tagKey>`, and its button's, its list's and its findings' are made from the key.

parameters.name: content
parameters.description: the app's screen.

declarations.name: PantrixMenu
declarations.signature:
@Composable
fun PantrixMenu(
    visible: Boolean,
    onDismissRequest: () -> Unit,
    anchor: @Composable () -> Unit,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    side: PopoverSide = PopoverSide.Bottom,
    alignment: PopoverAlignment = PopoverAlignment.Start,
    style: MenuStyle? = null,
    colors: MenuColors? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null,
    presentation: OverlayPresentation = OverlayPresentation.Adaptive,
    content: @Composable ColumnScope.() -> Unit
)
declarations.description:
A list of actions for one element, in a panel beside it: what a "more" button opens, or the actions of a row.

It is anchored, not modal: nothing is dimmed, the app stays in view around it, and the panel follows its anchor as the content moves. It sits on `side` of the anchor, lined up as `alignment` says, while the window has room for it there, and takes the opposite side otherwise, never closer than the style's margin to the edges of the window, its system bars or the keyboard. It is as wide as its longest row, between the style's narrowest and widest, and more rows than fit its tallest height scroll.

The menu never hides itself. A press outside it, Escape and back call `onDismissRequest`, and so does the choosing of a row, before the row's own `onClick`: a row says what it does and nothing about the menu. The caller sets `visible` to false. The first press outside only asks to close: what is under it is not pressed.

Opened by the keyboard it takes the focus on its first row. The arrows walk the rows and go round from the last to the first, Home and End go to the first and the last, and Tab walks them as well, the rows being the only stops in the panel. Enter and the space bar choose the row, and Escape closes the menu. Opened by a touch or a click no row shows the focus, and the first of those keys brings the keyboard into use: an arrow down or Home on the first row, an arrow up or End on the last. Once the menu has closed the focus is on the anchor, on the control that opened it. While it is shown the app under it shows no focus, as under a dialog.

It looks the same on every platform; what differs is in `MenuStyle`: the corners, the widths, the shadow and the rows' height.

**In a narrow window it is a sheet** (`presentation`): on a phone a panel beside a button is small under a finger, and a sheet from the bottom edge is within the thumb's reach. The rows are as wide as the sheet and as tall as the platform's touch target, there is no title, and a drag down or a press on the scrim closes it as anything outside the panel does. A destructive row keeps its colour; a shortcut is not written where the platform is used by touch, which has no keys to press. The keyboard walks the rows as in the panel.

parameters.name: visible
parameters.description: whether the menu is shown. It enters and leaves with the theme's motion.

parameters.name: onDismissRequest
parameters.description: called for a press outside, Escape, back and a row that is chosen. The menu stays until `visible` is false.

parameters.name: anchor
parameters.description: the control the menu belongs to, laid out where this is called and as that place asks: usually the button that opens it.

parameters.name: modifier
parameters.description: applied to the panel, inside its layer. Not to the anchor.

parameters.name: side
parameters.description: the side of the anchor the panel prefers. `PopoverSide.Start` and `PopoverSide.End` follow the layout direction.

parameters.name: alignment
parameters.description: how the panel lines up with the anchor along that side: from its start edge unless told otherwise, as a menu hangs from what opened it.

parameters.name: style
parameters.description: this call's own style, which its rows are drawn with too: over every enclosing one and under the density. Only the fields it sets change, on every platform.

parameters.name: colors
parameters.description: this call's own colours, its rows' among them. Only the ones it sets change; the rest stay the theme's.

parameters.name: tagKey
parameters.description: a locale-independent key for automation: the panel's tag is `Menu_<tagKey>`, and its rows are named inside it, `Menu_<tagKey>.MenuItem_<row's key>`. A menu shown as a sheet has the same tags, on the sheet.

parameters.name: presentation
parameters.description: how the menu is shown: a sheet in a narrow window and a panel beside its anchor in a wider one, by default; always the panel, or always the sheet. Chosen as the menu opens, it stays until it has closed.

parameters.name: content
parameters.description: the rows: `PantrixMenuItem`s, with a `PantrixDivider` between groups of them. Given no colour, that line is told by the rows' colour on a fill, as the panel's hairline is.

declarations.name: PantrixMenuItem
declarations.signature:
@Composable
fun PantrixMenuItem(
    text: String,
    onClick: () -> Unit,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    icon: ImageVector? = null,
    shortcut: String? = null,
    enabled: Boolean = true,
    destructive: Boolean = false,
    tagKey: String? = null,
    selected: Boolean = false,
    supportingText: String? = null,
    supportingTextStyle: TextStyle = PantrixTheme.typography.footnote
)
declarations.description:
One action in a `PantrixMenu`: a label, an optional icon before it and an optional shortcut after it. Among rows that each choose one thing, a language or an order, the one in effect is `selected`, with a check at its end.

Choosing it asks the menu to close and then calls `onClick`. It is at least as tall as the style's row and as the platform's touch target, and its label is cut at one line where the panel is at its widest.

parameters.name: text
parameters.description: what the action does, in a word or two.

parameters.name: onClick
parameters.description: called when the row is chosen, after the menu has been asked to close.

parameters.name: modifier
parameters.description: applied to the row.

parameters.name: icon
parameters.description: drawn before the label, at the style's icon size and in the label's colour. A picture of what the label says: a screen reader is told the label alone.

parameters.name: shortcut
parameters.description: the keys that do the same thing, such as "Ctrl+K", after the label. It is shown and read out, never bound: binding the keys is the app's.

parameters.name: enabled
parameters.description: whether the row can be chosen. One that cannot takes no press and no focus, and reports nothing.

parameters.name: destructive
parameters.description: draws the label and the icon in the menu's destructive colour, for an action that deletes or cannot be undone.

parameters.name: tagKey
parameters.description: a locale-independent key for automation: the row's tag is `MenuItem_<tagKey>`, inside the tag of a menu that has a key of its own.

parameters.name: selected
parameters.description: whether the row is the choice in effect among rows that each choose one thing: a check stands at its end, in the label's colour, and a screen reader is told it is selected.

parameters.name: supportingText
parameters.description: a second line under the label, smaller and in the shortcut's quieter colour: what the choice leads to, as a language's address under its name. The row grows to hold it, and a screen reader hears it after the label. It is cut at two lines.

parameters.name: supportingTextStyle
parameters.description: the type `supportingText` is set in: the theme's `footnote` unless given. Its colour stays the row's, quieter than the label and the disabled colour on a row that cannot be chosen.

declarations.name: MenuStyle
declarations.description:
`PantrixMenu`'s geometry: the panel it draws, how far that sits from its anchor and from the edges of the window, and the rows in it.

The air follows density: the gap, the margin, the padding above the first row and below the last, a row's height and the padding and the gap inside it, and the narrowest width. The widest width, the tallest height, the corners, the shadow and the icon do not. A row is never shorter than the platform's touch target, whatever the density. A menu's colours are not part of its style: they are the theme's, and `MenuColors` where a call has its own.

parameters.name: shape
parameters.description: The panel's corners: medium on Android and iOS, small on desktop and the web.

parameters.name: minWidth
parameters.description: The narrowest the panel gets, however short its labels.

parameters.name: maxWidth
parameters.description: The widest the panel gets: a longer label is cut short.

parameters.name: maxHeight
parameters.description: The tallest the panel gets: more rows than fit scroll.

parameters.name: elevation
parameters.description: How high the panel floats over the app, which is how large its shadow is.

parameters.name: gap
parameters.description: Between the anchor and the panel.

parameters.name: margin
parameters.description: Kept clear between the panel and the edges of the window, and of what covers the window there: a system bar, a cutout, the keyboard.

parameters.name: verticalPadding
parameters.description: Above the first row and below the last.

parameters.name: itemHeight
parameters.description: The least a row is tall, where the platform's touch target is not taller.

parameters.name: itemHorizontalPadding
parameters.description: Inside a row, before its icon and after its shortcut.

parameters.name: iconSize
parameters.description: A row's icon.

parameters.name: iconGap
parameters.description: Between a row's icon and its label, and between its label and its shortcut.

declarations.name: MenuColors
declarations.description:
What a `PantrixMenu` is painted with, for a call that does not take the theme's colours: a colour that is set is used, and one that is left out stays the theme's.

```
PantrixMenu(…, colors = MenuColors(container = PantrixTheme.colors.primary.container))
```

A `container` given here that is one of the theme's role colours brings the colour the theme pairs with it for the rows, unless `content` is given too. A fill no role has does not: what reads on it is the caller's to give, and so is a `destructive` colour that reads on it.

parameters.name: container
parameters.description: The panel's fill. The theme's `surface`.

parameters.name: content
parameters.description: A row's label and icon. The theme's `textPrimary`. A row's shortcut is the theme's `textSecondary` on the theme's own grounds, and this colour on a fill of the caller's.

parameters.name: destructive
parameters.description: The label and icon of a row that deletes or cannot be undone. The theme's `danger` colour.

parameters.name: border
parameters.description: The hairline around the panel, which tells it from a surface of its own colour under it, as in the dark theme, where a shadow shows little. The theme's `divider` on the theme's own grounds. On a fill, where that line would not read, a share of `content`: the edge a subtle button has. A transparent colour draws none.

declarations.name: ModalPosition
declarations.signature: enum class ModalPosition
declarations.description: Where `PantrixModal`'s content sits in the window, which also says how it enters and leaves.

entries.name: Center
entries.description: In the middle of the window's safe area, fading and growing in, as a dialog does.

entries.name: Top
entries.description: Near the top of the window's safe area, in the middle across, fading and growing in: a search or a palette, whose field stays where it is while what is under it grows and shrinks.

declarations.name: PantrixModal
declarations.signature:
@Composable
fun PantrixModal(
    visible: Boolean,
    onDismissRequest: () -> Unit,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    position: ModalPosition = ModalPosition.Center,
    margin: PaddingValues = PaddingValues(PantrixTheme.spacing.xl),
    paneTitle: String? = null,
    dismissOnScrimClick: Boolean = true,
    dismissOnBack: Boolean = true,
    scrimColor: Color = PantrixTheme.colors.scrim,
    tagKey: String? = null,
    content: @Composable () -> Unit
)

parameters.name: visible
parameters.description: whether the modal is shown. Set to false, the content leaves with its motion, and then nothing is composed.

parameters.name: onDismissRequest
parameters.description: called when the user asks to close the modal: back, Escape, or a press on the scrim.

parameters.name: modifier
parameters.description: applied to the content, inside `margin`: the node it tags is the content as it is drawn, and a press anywhere on it is the content's, never the scrim's.

parameters.name: position
parameters.description: where the content sits: in the middle of the window, or near its top.

parameters.name: margin
parameters.description: the room kept between the content and the window's safe area, side by side. It is part of the scrim: a press in it, right beside the content, dismisses as one anywhere else on the scrim does. None, with content that fills what it is given, makes the content the whole safe area, as an editor on a phone is.

parameters.name: paneTitle
parameters.description: what a screen reader announces as the modal appears: what it is, in a word or two.

parameters.name: dismissOnScrimClick
parameters.description: whether a press on the scrim asks to dismiss. Where it does not, the scrim is a fill a screen reader passes over.

parameters.name: dismissOnBack
parameters.description: whether back and Escape ask to dismiss.

parameters.name: scrimColor
parameters.description: what is drawn over the app while the modal is shown, fading with the content: the theme's scrim unless given. The theme's background makes the modal a page of its own, the window's bars and all.

parameters.name: tagKey
parameters.description: the modal's automation key: the content is `Modal_<tagKey>`. A dismissal is reported as a `Modal` event, `dismiss`, which says whether it came by the scrim or by back.

parameters.name: content
parameters.description: what the modal shows, drawn by the app.

declarations.id: com.pantrixui.components.overlay.multiselect.PantrixMultiSelect(List<SelectOption<T>>, Set<T>, (Set<T>) -> Unit, Modifier, Boolean, String?, String?, String?, Boolean, String?, Boolean, String?, SelectStyle?, TextFieldStyle?, SelectColors?, TextFieldColors?, String?, String?, MutableInteractionSource?, OverlayPresentation)
declarations.name: PantrixMultiSelect
declarations.signature:
@Composable
fun <T> PantrixMultiSelect(
    options: List<SelectOption<T>>,
    selected: Set<T>,
    onSelectionChange: (Set<T>) -> Unit,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    enabled: Boolean = true,
    label: String? = null,
    placeholder: String? = null,
    supportingText: String? = null,
    error: Boolean = false,
    valueText: String? = null,
    searchable: Boolean = false,
    searchPlaceholder: String? = null,
    style: SelectStyle? = null,
    fieldStyle: TextFieldStyle? = null,
    colors: SelectColors? = null,
    fieldColors: TextFieldColors? = null,
    contentDescription: String? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null,
    interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null,
    presentation: OverlayPresentation = OverlayPresentation.Popover
)
declarations.description:
Several choices out of a list the control opens: the projects a page is narrowed to, the days a shop is open.

It is a `PantrixSelect` whose list takes several choices. The box is a text field's, with a chevron at its end and a field's label, placeholder, error and supporting text, and the list opens under it, as wide as the box. Every option is a check box: a press ticks it or clears it, and the list stays open for the next. A press outside the list, Escape and back close it. What is chosen is its caller's and not the control's: it is given `selected` and asks for another set with `onSelectionChange`.

The box shows the labels of what is chosen, in the options' order with a comma between them and cut at one line, or `valueText` where a caller would rather say it another way: a count, or one word for all of them. With nothing chosen it shows its placeholder. Asked how wide it would be, as `Modifier.width(IntrinsicSize.Max)` asks, it answers as a `PantrixSelect` does, with what the longest of its options needs, whatever is chosen.

The keyboard is a select's. Opened by the keyboard the list takes the focus on the first chosen option, or on its first; the arrows walk the options and go round, Home and End go to the first and the last, and Enter and the space bar tick or clear. With `searchable` the list has a field that narrows the options, at its edge nearest the box: at its top under the box, at its foot where the list opens above it. The focus stays in that field, and the keyboard's action ticks or clears the marked option.

It shares a select's style and colours, `SelectStyle` and `SelectColors`, and a text field's for its box: a product that restyles its selects restyles these with them.

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: the choices, in the order they are shown. With none, the list says so.

parameters.name: selected
parameters.description: the values that are chosen now: every option whose value is among them is ticked.

parameters.name: onSelectionChange
parameters.description: asked for another set, with the whole of it: the one before with the pressed option's value put in or taken out.

parameters.name: modifier
parameters.description: the modifier of the whole field: its label, its box and what is under it.

parameters.name: enabled
parameters.description: whether the list can be opened. One that cannot be takes no focus, is drawn in the disabled colours and says so.

parameters.name: label
parameters.description: what the choice is, written above the box: the field's name for a screen reader, and what its list is announced as.

parameters.name: placeholder
parameters.description: shown in the box while nothing is chosen.

parameters.name: supportingText
parameters.description: help under the box. With `error` it is the message that says what to put right, which a screen reader announces as the error.

parameters.name: error
parameters.description: whether the choice is wrong: the border, the label and the supporting text turn to the danger role, and a screen reader is told.

parameters.name: valueText
parameters.description: what the box shows while something is chosen, in place of the chosen labels.

parameters.name: searchable
parameters.description: whether the list has a field to search its options by.

parameters.name: searchPlaceholder
parameters.description: what the search field shows while it is empty, and what it is called. The theme's word for a search where it is null.

parameters.name: style
parameters.description: this call's own `SelectStyle`, the one its list is drawn with: over every enclosing one and under the density. Only the fields it sets change, on every platform.

parameters.name: fieldStyle
parameters.description: this call's own `TextFieldStyle`, the one its box is drawn with: over every enclosing one and under the density. Only the fields it sets change, on every platform.

parameters.name: colors
parameters.description: its list's own colours, in place of the theme's roles: the ones it sets are used, and the rest stay the theme's. The check boxes are the theme's.

parameters.name: fieldColors
parameters.description: its box's own colours, as a text field takes them. A disabled one is drawn in the theme's disabled colours whatever is given.

parameters.name: contentDescription
parameters.description: what a screen reader says for the field: its name where it has no `label`.

parameters.name: tagKey
parameters.description: the field's automation key: the field is `MultiSelect_<tagKey>`, its list `MultiSelectList_<tagKey>`, the list's search field `MultiSelectSearch_<tagKey>`, and its options are named inside it, `MultiSelect_<tagKey>.MultiSelectOption_<option's key>`. It reports that its list opened and that an option was ticked or cleared, by the option's key and never by its label.

parameters.name: interactionSource
parameters.description: the field's interactions, hoisted: its focus, its hover and its presses. It keeps a source of its own when this is null.

parameters.name: presentation
parameters.description: how the list is shown: under the field, by default; as a sheet from the bottom of the window, its title the field's label; or the one in a narrow window and the other in a wider one. Chosen as the list opens, it stays until the list has closed.

declarations.id: com.pantrixui.components.overlay.multiselect.PantrixMultiSelect(FormField<Set<T>>, List<SelectOption<T>>, Modifier, Boolean, String?, String?, String?, String?, Boolean, String?, SelectStyle?, TextFieldStyle?, SelectColors?, TextFieldColors?, String?, MutableInteractionSource?, OverlayPresentation)
declarations.name: PantrixMultiSelect
declarations.signature:
@Composable
fun <T> PantrixMultiSelect(
    field: FormField<Set<T>>,
    options: List<SelectOption<T>>,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    enabled: Boolean = true,
    label: String? = null,
    placeholder: String? = null,
    supportingText: String? = null,
    valueText: String? = null,
    searchable: Boolean = false,
    searchPlaceholder: String? = null,
    style: SelectStyle? = null,
    fieldStyle: TextFieldStyle? = null,
    colors: SelectColors? = null,
    fieldColors: TextFieldColors? = null,
    contentDescription: String? = null,
    interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null,

@Composable
fun PantrixPopover(
    visible: Boolean,
    onDismissRequest: () -> Unit,
    anchor: @Composable () -> Unit,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    side: PopoverSide = PopoverSide.Bottom,
    alignment: PopoverAlignment = PopoverAlignment.Center,
    title: String? = null,
    dismissible: Boolean = true,
    style: PopoverStyle? = null,

    content: @Composable ColumnScope.() -> Unit

declarations.description:
A layer beside an element, holding more about it than the element itself can show: what a status means, what a field expects, a few controls for one row.

It is anchored, not modal: nothing is dimmed, the app stays in view around it, and the popover follows its anchor as the content moves. It sits on `side` of the anchor while the window has room for it there and on the opposite side otherwise, lined up as `alignment` says, and never closer than the style's margin to the edges of the window, its system bars or the keyboard. It is no larger than that room either: what it holds wraps, and scrolls under the title.

The popover never hides itself. A press outside it, Escape and back call `onDismissRequest` unless `dismissible` is false, and the caller sets `visible` to false. The first press outside only asks to close: what is under it is not pressed, so a press on the anchor closes the popover and does not open it again. Once it is told to close it is in no one's way: a press while it fades is the app's.

Opened by the keyboard it takes the focus: its first control does, or the popover itself where it holds none, and then the arrows, Page Up and Page Down, the space bar, Home and End scroll what it holds. Opened by a touch or a click it leaves the focus where it was, and takes it once the keyboard comes into use. Tab stays inside it, and once it has closed the focus is on the anchor: on the control that opened it. While it is shown the app under it shows no focus, as under a dialog.

**Close it to see it leave.** A popover that has closed composes nothing but its anchor, so leaving it in the tree with `visible = false` is free, and it leaves with the theme's motion. An open one that is taken out of the composition is gone without it, and that is all it costs: its layer is composed at the root of its window, so a layout that throws its content away while it measures, such as a `BoxWithConstraints` that changes branch, closes no layer that the window is still measuring.

It looks the same on every platform; what differs is in `PopoverStyle`: the corners, the widths and the shadow.

parameters.name: visible
parameters.description: whether the popover is shown. It enters and leaves with the theme's motion.

parameters.name: onDismissRequest
parameters.description: called for a press outside, Escape and back while `dismissible`. The popover stays until `visible` is false.

parameters.name: anchor
parameters.description: what the popover is placed beside: the control that opens it, laid out where this is called and as that place asks. The popover is placed against its layout box, the room of its touch target included.

parameters.name: modifier
parameters.description: applied to the popover itself, inside its layer. Not to the anchor.

parameters.name: side
parameters.description: the side of the anchor the popover prefers. `PopoverSide.Start` and `PopoverSide.End` follow the layout direction.

parameters.name: alignment
parameters.description: how the popover lines up with the anchor along that side.

parameters.name: title
parameters.description: a heading at the top of the popover, which stays in view while what is under it scrolls, and what a screen reader announces as the popover appears. Give one to a popover of more than a line.

parameters.name: dismissible
parameters.description: whether a press outside, Escape, back and a screen reader's dismiss action ask to close. Turn it off only for a popover that something in `content` closes.

parameters.name: style
parameters.description: this call's own style: over every enclosing one and under the density. Only the fields it sets change, on every platform.

parameters.name: colors
parameters.description: this call's own colours. Only the ones it sets change; the rest stay the theme's.

parameters.name: tagKey
parameters.description: a locale-independent key for automation: the popover's tag is `Popover_<tagKey>`, on the popover as it is drawn, and on the sheet where it is shown as one.

parameters.name: presentation
parameters.description: how the popover is shown: beside its anchor, by default; as a sheet from the bottom of the window, the `title` its heading and `content` under it with the popover's own padding at its sides; or the one in a narrow window and the other in a wider one. Chosen as it opens, it stays until it has closed.

parameters.name: content
parameters.description: what the popover holds, in a column under the title.

`PantrixPopover`'s geometry: how wide and tall it gets, how far it sits from its anchor and how close it comes to the edges of the window.

The widest width, the tallest height, the corners and the shadow do not. A popover's colours are not part of its style: they are the theme's, and `PopoverColors` where a call has its own.

parameters.name: elevation

declarations.name: PopoverColors
declarations.description:
What a `PantrixPopover` is painted with, for a call that does not take the theme's colours: a colour that is set is used, and one that is left out stays the theme's.

```

```

A `container` given here that is one of the theme's role colours brings the colour the theme pairs with it for what the popover holds, and for the title unless a title colour is given too. A fill no role has does not: what reads on it is the caller's to give.

parameters.name: container
parameters.description: The popover's fill. The theme's `surface`.

parameters.name: title
parameters.description: The title. The theme's `textPrimary`.

parameters.name: border
parameters.description: The hairline around the popover, which tells it from a surface of its own colour under it, as in the dark theme, where a shadow shows little. The theme's `divider` on the theme's own grounds. On a fill, where that line would not read, a share of `title`: the edge a subtle button has. A transparent colour draws none.

declarations.description:
One choice out of a list the control opens: a country, a currency, a plan.

It is a text field's box with a chevron at its end, with a field's label, placeholder, error and supporting text, and a list that opens under the box, as wide as the box. What is chosen is its caller's and not the control's: it is given `selected` and asks for another with `onSelect`. A press on the field opens the list, and so do Enter and the space bar while the field has the focus. Choosing an option closes it, and so do a press outside it, Escape and back, which choose nothing. While the list is open the box is drawn as a field with the focus.

By itself the field is as wide as a text field, and its box grows with a choice longer than that. Asked how wide it would be, it answers with what the longest of its options needs, in the box and in a row of the list, with its placeholder and its label: `Modifier.width(IntrinsicSize.Max)` makes a select that is no wider than its options and as wide whichever of them is chosen, as one in a toolbar or in a table's foot is.

The list hangs under the box, over the field's help where it has any, never closer than the style's margin to the edges of the window, its system bars or the keyboard. It opens there where the room holds three of its rows, or all of them where it has fewer, and is as tall as that room at the most, its rows scrolling. With less room than that it opens above the box, and with too little on both sides it lies over the box. Once open it stays on its side while one of its rows has room there: the keyboard, which comes as the list is used, makes it shorter where it is. More options than fit its tallest height scroll, and it opens with the chosen one in view. That option is marked by its row's fill and a tick, and not by a colour alone.

Opened by the keyboard the list takes the focus on the chosen option, or on its first. The arrows walk the options and go round from the last to the first, Home and End go to the first and the last, and Enter and the space bar choose. Opened by a touch or a click no option shows the focus, and the first arrow moves on from the chosen one. Once the list has closed the focus is on the field again.

With `searchable` the list has a field that narrows the options to those whose label holds what is typed, and the list is as short as the options that are left. The field is at the list's edge next to the box, its top, or its bottom where the list is above the box, so that it stays where it is while the list gets shorter. The focus stays in that field: the arrows move a mark among the options that match, and the keyboard's action chooses the marked one, which is the first match as soon as something is typed.

Use it for a list short enough to read, or one worth searching. Two or three choices that should all be in view are a radio group or a segment button, actions are a menu, and several values at once are a `PantrixMultiSelect`.

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: the choices, in the order they are shown. With none, the list says so.

parameters.name: selected
parameters.description: what is chosen now: the first option whose value it equals. A value no option has is nothing chosen, and so is null, unless an option stands for it.

parameters.name: onSelect
parameters.description: asked for another choice, with the option's value. It is asked for the chosen one again too.

parameters.name: modifier
parameters.description: the modifier of the whole field: its label, its box and what is under it. `fillMaxWidth()` fills a form's column, and `width(IntrinsicSize.Max)` is as wide as the options need.

parameters.name: enabled
parameters.description: whether the list can be opened. A select that cannot be takes no focus, is drawn in the disabled colours and says so.

parameters.name: label
parameters.description: what the choice is, written above the box: the field's name for a screen reader, and what its list is announced as.

parameters.name: placeholder
parameters.description: shown in the box while nothing is chosen.

parameters.name: supportingText
parameters.description: help under the box. With `error` it is the message that says what to put right, which a screen reader announces as the error.

parameters.name: error
parameters.description: whether the choice is wrong: the border, the label and the supporting text turn to the danger role, and a screen reader is told.

parameters.name: searchable
parameters.description: whether the list has a field to search its options by.

parameters.name: searchPlaceholder
parameters.description: what the search field shows while it is empty, and what it is called. The theme's word for a search where it is null.

parameters.name: style
parameters.description: this call's own style, the one its list is drawn with: over every enclosing one and under the density. Only the fields it sets change, on every platform.

parameters.name: fieldStyle
parameters.description: this call's own `TextFieldStyle`, the one its box is drawn with: over every enclosing one and under the density. Only the fields it sets change, on every platform.

parameters.name: colors
parameters.description: its list's own colours, in place of the theme's roles: the ones it sets are used, and the rest stay the theme's.

parameters.name: fieldColors
parameters.description: its box's own colours, as a text field takes them. A disabled select is drawn in the theme's disabled colours whatever is given.

parameters.name: contentDescription
parameters.description: what a screen reader says for the field: its name where it has no `label`, as a select in a toolbar has none.

parameters.name: tagKey
parameters.description: the field's automation key: the field is `Select_<tagKey>`, its list `SelectList_<tagKey>`, the list's search field `SelectSearch_<tagKey>`, and its options are named inside it, `Select_<tagKey>.SelectOption_<option's key>`. It reports that its list opened and that an option was chosen, by the option's key and never by its label.

parameters.name: interactionSource
parameters.description: the field's interactions, hoisted: its focus, its hover and its presses. It keeps a source of its own when this is null.

parameters.name: presentation
parameters.description: how the list is shown: under the field, by default; as a sheet from the bottom of the window, its title the field's label; or the one in a narrow window and the other in a wider one. Chosen as the list opens, it stays until the list has closed.

declarations.description:
A panel over the app for a short task that belongs to the current screen: choosing how to sort, where to share, a field or two, a list to pick from, the details of what was pressed.

It lies along the `edge` it is given. Along the bottom edge it is as wide as the window up to the style's `maxWidth` and as tall as what it holds, and a drag moves it. Along the end edge it is a side sheet: as tall as the window and the style's `sideWidth` wide, with a button to close it, and a drag towards the edge closes it. It is modal either way: nothing behind it takes a click, Tab never leaves it, and on Android TalkBack stays inside it. It is shown while `visible` is true and enters and leaves with the theme's motion; it never hides itself. Back, Escape, a click on the scrim, a drag towards its edge and the side sheet's close button call `onDismissRequest` unless `dismissible` is false, and so does a screen reader's dismiss action on a full-screen sheet, which can cover the scrim.

The content spans the sheet's width, so the rows of a list reach its edges; give a form its own horizontal padding. It scrolls under the title when the sheet is too short for it. A long list belongs in a `LazyColumn`, with `scrollContent` off.

**Close it to see it leave.** A sheet that has closed composes nothing, so leaving it in the tree with `visible = false` is free, and it leaves with the theme's motion. An open one that is taken out of the composition is gone without it, and that is all it costs: its window is composed at the root of the window around it, so a layout that throws its content away while it measures closes no layer that is still being measured.

parameters.name: visible
parameters.description: whether the sheet is shown. It enters and leaves with the theme's motion.

parameters.name: onDismissRequest
parameters.description: called for back, Escape, a click on the scrim, a drag towards the edge and the side sheet's close button while `dismissible`. The sheet stays until `visible` is false.

parameters.name: title
parameters.description: what the sheet is for, as a short label: "Sort by". It is announced when the sheet appears and is its heading. Null or blank for none: no line is kept for it, the content starts under the handle, and a screen reader announces no name when the sheet appears. A side sheet's close button still stands at its top.

parameters.name: modifier
parameters.description: applied to the sheet itself. The strip of scrim kept clear beside it is no part of it.

parameters.name: edge
parameters.description: the edge of the window the sheet lies along: the bottom, the end, the start, or by the window's width (`SheetEdge.Adaptive`), full screen from the bottom in a narrow one. `halfOpen`, `fullScreen`, `coverStatusBar` and `overscrollMovesSheet` count for an adaptive sheet where it comes from the bottom.

parameters.name: dismissible
parameters.description: whether back, Escape, a click on the scrim, a drag towards the edge, the side sheet's close button and a screen reader's dismiss action ask to close. Turn it off only when a control in `content` must close the sheet.

parameters.name: halfOpen
parameters.description: whether the sheet first opens half open, its top at the middle of the window, when what it holds is taller than that. A drag up opens it fully, and so does focus moving into it; a drag down from half open closes it. Along the bottom edge only.

parameters.name: fullScreen
parameters.description: whether the fully open sheet is as tall as the window under the status bar however short its content, with no scrim above it. Like every sheet along the bottom edge it reaches the window's bottom edge, under the system's navigation bar, and keeps what it holds above that bar. Along the bottom edge only.

parameters.name: coverStatusBar
parameters.description: whether a `fullScreen` sheet reaches under the status bar too, fully open as tall as the whole window. Its top corners square off as it slides under the bar, its handle and title stay below the bar, and on Android the bar's icons turn to read against the sheet where it is as wide as the window. Along the bottom edge and with `fullScreen` only.

parameters.name: overscrollMovesSheet
parameters.description: whether a drag down on content that is already at its top goes on to move the sheet down: to half open, then closed. Turn it off for a list that should only scroll; the handle and the title still drag the sheet, and a drag up on the content still opens a half-open sheet. Along the bottom edge only.

parameters.name: scrollContent
parameters.description: whether the sheet puts `content` in a scroll area under the title. Turn it off for content that scrolls itself, such as a `LazyColumn`, which cannot sit in a scroll area: `content` then gets the height left under the title, and its scrolling still opens a half-open sheet and moves the sheet down past its top. Give a `LazyColumn` `Modifier.fillMaxWidth()`: a list is only as wide as the rows on screen, and a drag beside them would not scroll it.

parameters.name: style
parameters.description: this call's own style: over every enclosing one and under the density. Only the fields it sets change, on every platform.

parameters.name: colors
parameters.description: this call's own colours. Only the ones it sets change; the rest stay the theme's.

parameters.name: tagKey
parameters.description: a locale-independent key for automation: the sheet's tag is `Sheet_<tagKey>`, on the sheet as it is drawn, and the side sheet's close button is `SheetClose_<tagKey>`.

parameters.name: content
parameters.description: what the sheet holds, under the title.

declarations.name: SheetEdge
declarations.signature: enum class SheetEdge
declarations.description: The edge of the window a `PantrixSheet` lies along.

entries.name: Bottom
entries.description: The bottom edge. The sheet is as wide as the window up to the style's `maxWidth` and as tall as what it holds, and a drag down closes it.

entries.name: End
entries.description: The end edge, the left one in a right-to-left layout. The sheet is as tall as the window and the style's `sideWidth` wide, and a drag towards the edge closes it.

entries.name: Start
entries.description: The start edge, the right one in a right-to-left layout: an app's menu, which a narrow window keeps in a sheet rather than beside its content. The sheet is as tall as the window and the style's `sideWidth` wide, and a drag towards the edge closes it.

entries.name: Adaptive
entries.description: The bottom edge in a narrow window, the `Compact` width class, as a full-screen sheet, and the end edge in every wider one: a form or the details of what was pressed, which fill a phone and stand beside the content on a tablet or a desktop. The window is the one the sheet is shown over, and it is asked as the sheet opens: one that is open stays as it is when the window changes.

declarations.name: SheetStyle
declarations.description:
`PantrixSheet`'s geometry.

The space between the handle, the title and the content comes from the theme's spacing, so it follows density, and so do the margin and the room around the handle. The widths, the corners, the shadow and the handle itself do not. A sheet's colours are not part of its style: they are the theme's, and `SheetColors` where a call has its own.

parameters.name: shape
parameters.description: The corners that face the app: the top two of a sheet along the bottom edge, the start two of one along the end edge. The corners at the window's edge are square. Large on Android and iOS, medium on desktop and the web.

parameters.name: maxWidth
parameters.description: The widest a sheet along the bottom edge gets; in a wider window it stays in the middle of the edge.

parameters.name: sideWidth
parameters.description: How wide a sheet along the end edge is, where the window leaves it that room.

parameters.name: margin
parameters.description: Kept clear between the sheet and the far side of the window, so that the scrim still shows there and a tap on it closes the sheet: above a tall sheet along the bottom edge, beside a sheet along the end edge in a narrow window. It is a target for a tap, so it is each platform's smallest touch target.

parameters.name: elevation
parameters.description: How high the sheet floats over the scrim, which is how large its shadow is. None on iOS.

parameters.name: handleWidth
parameters.description: How long the drag handle is, which a sheet along the bottom edge draws while a drag can move it.

parameters.name: handleHeight
parameters.description: How thick the drag handle is: `handleWidth` is how long it is.

parameters.name: handlePadding
parameters.description: Above and below the handle.

declarations.name: SheetColors
declarations.description:
What a `PantrixSheet` is painted with, for a call that does not take the theme's colours: a colour that is set is used, and one that is left out stays the theme's.

```
PantrixSheet(…, colors = SheetColors(container = PantrixTheme.colors.background))
```

A `container` given here that is one of the theme's role colours brings the colour the theme pairs with it for the title, the handle and the close icon, unless those are given too. A fill no role has does not: what reads on it is the caller's to give.

parameters.name: container
parameters.description: The sheet's fill. The theme's `surface`.

parameters.name: title
parameters.description: The title. The theme's `textPrimary`.

parameters.name: handle
parameters.description: The drag handle of a sheet along the bottom edge, as it is drawn, with its own alpha. The theme's `textSecondary` at 40%: faint, and seen on any surface.

parameters.name: closeIcon
parameters.description: The icon of the close button of a sheet along the end edge. The theme's `onSurface`.

parameters.name: scrim
parameters.description: The dimming laid over the app behind the sheet, with its own alpha. The theme's `scrim`.

declarations.name: SnackbarDuration
declarations.signature: enum class SnackbarDuration
declarations.description: How long a snackbar stays when the user does nothing with it.

entries.name: Short
entries.description: Four seconds, or longer when the platform recommends more time for its user.

entries.name: Long
entries.description: Ten seconds, or longer when the platform recommends more time for its user.

entries.name: UntilDismissed
entries.description: Until the user acts on it or closes it, or the app dismisses it.

declarations.name: SnackbarResult
declarations.signature: enum class SnackbarResult
declarations.description: How a snackbar left.

entries.name: ActionPerformed
entries.description: The user pressed its action.

entries.name: Dismissed
entries.description: Its time ran out, the user closed it, or the app dismissed it.

declarations.name: SnackbarTone
declarations.signature: enum class SnackbarTone
declarations.description:
What a snackbar is telling the user: one of the theme's colour roles, which also decides its icon and how it is announced.

The semantic tones, `Info`, `Success`, `Warning` and `Danger`, reach the user as colour and as an icon, because colour alone fails anyone who cannot see it. `Primary` and `Neutral` carry no meaning of their own, and have no icon.

A snackbar is filled in every tone, from the role's `color` and `onColor` rather than its pale `container`: it floats over the app's own content for a few seconds, and a pale bar would read as one more card on the page. `Primary` takes the brand's `primary` role. `Neutral` takes the `neutral` role, a grey with no hue of its own, which Pantrix's colours keep darker than the page in the light theme and lighter than it in the dark one.

entries.name: Info
entries.description: Something worth knowing that is neither good nor bad.

entries.name: Success
entries.description: Something that worked: saved, sent, uploaded.

entries.name: Warning
entries.description: Something to look at before it becomes a problem.

entries.name: Danger
entries.description: Something that failed. The one tone announced assertively: it interrupts what a screen reader is saying.

entries.name: Primary
entries.description: Something the app wants noticed, in the brand's colour, without an icon: a new version ready to install, a feature to try.

entries.name: Neutral
entries.description: Something the app did: a grey bar, without an icon. The default.

parameters.name: tagKey

declarations.name: PantrixSnackbarState
declarations.signature: class PantrixSnackbarState
declarations.description:
The snackbars an app asks for: one on screen at a time, the others waiting their turn in the order they were asked for.

A `PantrixSnackbarHost` puts them on screen. Keep one state for the part of the app one host covers, usually the whole app, so snackbars from any screen queue behind each other.

members.signature:
var current: SnackbarData? by mutableStateOf(null)
    private set

members.name: show
members.description:
Shows a snackbar once the snackbars asked for before it have left, and returns how it left.

Cancelling the coroutine that called it takes the snackbar away, or drops it before its turn.

parameters.name: message
parameters.description: what happened, in a short sentence: "Conversation archived".

parameters.name: actionLabel
parameters.description: a short verb for the one thing the user can do about it: "Undo".

parameters.name: duration
parameters.description: how long the snackbar stays when nobody acts on it. A snackbar with an action stays until the user acts on it or closes it: a few seconds are too few for some people to reach the action.

parameters.name: closeButton
parameters.description: whether the snackbar has a close button. A snackbar that stays until it is dismissed has one.

parameters.name: tone
parameters.description: what the snackbar is telling the user: its colours, an icon for a semantic tone, and for an error an assertive announcement.

parameters.name: tagKey
parameters.description: the snackbar's automation key: the snackbar is `Snackbar_<tagKey>`, its action `SnackbarAction_<tagKey>` and its close button `SnackbarClose_<tagKey>`.

declarations.name: rememberPantrixSnackbarState
declarations.signature:
@Composable
fun rememberPantrixSnackbarState(): PantrixSnackbarState
declarations.description: A `PantrixSnackbarState` that lives as long as the composition that remembers it.

declarations.name: LocalPantrixSnackbars
declarations.signature: val LocalPantrixSnackbars: ProvidableCompositionLocal<PantrixSnackbarState?>
declarations.description:
The snackbars of the layout around this composable, or null where nothing provides them.

A layout that puts a `PantrixSnackbarHost` over its content provides the host's state here, so a screen inside it shows a snackbar without the state being passed down to it: `LocalPantrixSnackbars.current?.show(...)`, in a coroutine. `PantrixScaffold`, given its `snackbars`, provides them.

declarations.name: PantrixSnackbarHost
declarations.signature:
@Composable
fun PantrixSnackbarHost(
    state: PantrixSnackbarState,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    style: SnackbarStyle? = null,
    colors: SnackbarColors? = null
)
declarations.description:
Puts the snackbars of `state` on screen: short messages about what the app has just done, each with at most one action, in a neutral, primary or semantic tone, one at a time.

Put the host over the app, as the last child of a `Box` that fills the window, so snackbars appear above the content; `PantrixScaffold`, given the state, does that itself, between its bars. The host fills the space it is given and places each snackbar by `SnackbarStyle.placement` inside the window's safe area: in the middle of the bottom edge on Android, at the top on iOS, in the bottom end corner on desktop and the web. A snackbar belongs to the app, not to a dialog or a sheet, and one of those opened over the host covers its snackbars.

Beside an upright fold, a foldable held like a book or a hinge between two screens, a snackbar keeps to a half and never lies across the fold: one in the bottom end corner to the end half, every other one to the start half, in the middle of it or in its corner as it is placed. A snackbar as wide as a phone's window, in a corner too, would reach past the fold otherwise.

A snackbar never takes focus and never blocks the app; a screen reader announces it without interrupting, and one in the `SnackbarTone.Danger` tone assertively. It leaves after its `SnackbarDuration`, which waits while the pointer is over it, focus is inside it or it is being dragged, and then starts again, or when the user presses its action or its close button, swipes it sideways, presses Escape with focus inside it, or uses a screen reader's dismiss action.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: the snackbars to show; `PantrixSnackbarState.show` asks for one.

parameters.name: modifier
parameters.description: the host's modifier. The host fills the space it is given.

parameters.name: style
parameters.description: this call's own style: over every enclosing one and under the density. Only the fields it sets change, on every platform.

parameters.name: colors
parameters.description: the colours of every snackbar this host shows, where they are not their tones': the ones set here, with the tone's for the rest.

declarations.name: SnackbarPlacement
declarations.signature: enum class SnackbarPlacement
declarations.description: Where a `PantrixSnackbarHost` shows its snackbars.

entries.name: Top
entries.description: Along the top edge, in the middle.

entries.name: BottomStart
entries.description: In the bottom corner where lines start: bottom left, and bottom right in a right-to-left layout.

entries.name: BottomCenter
entries.description: Along the bottom edge, in the middle.

entries.name: BottomEnd
entries.description: In the bottom corner where lines end: bottom right, and bottom left in a right-to-left layout. In a wide window it keeps clear of navigation along the start edge, such as a sidebar.

declarations.name: SnackbarStyle
declarations.description:
`PantrixSnackbarHost`'s placement and its snackbars' geometry.

The padding inside a snackbar comes from the theme's spacing, and its height and margin scale with the density as well; the width limit and the elevation do not. A snackbar's colours are not part of its style: they come from its `SnackbarTone`'s colour role, and from `SnackbarColors` where a host has its own.

parameters.name: placement
parameters.description: Where the host shows its snackbars: in the middle of the bottom edge on Android, at the top on iOS, and in the bottom end corner on desktop and the web.

parameters.name: shape
parameters.description: The snackbar's corners: extra small on Android, desktop and the web, large on iOS.

parameters.name: maxWidth
parameters.description: The widest a snackbar gets. In a narrower host it spans the host, less the margin.

parameters.name: minHeight
parameters.description: The height of a snackbar whose message fits on one line.

parameters.name: margin
parameters.description: Kept clear between a snackbar and the host's edges, inside the window's safe area.

parameters.name: elevation
parameters.description: How high the snackbar floats over the app, which is how large its shadow is.

declarations.name: SnackbarColors
declarations.description:
What the snackbars of a `PantrixSnackbarHost` are painted with, for a host that does not take their tones' colours: a colour that is set is used on every snackbar of the host, and one that is left out stays the tone's.

```
PantrixSnackbarHost(snackbars, colors = SnackbarColors(container = brand.color, content = brand.onColor))
```

A tone still gives a snackbar its icon and the way it is announced: only what it is painted in is the host's.

A fill given here that is one of the theme's own colours brings the colour the theme pairs with it for what is drawn on it, unless that is given too. A fill no role has does not: what reads on it is the caller's to give.

parameters.name: container
parameters.description: The snackbar's fill. The `color` of its tone's role.

parameters.name: content
parameters.description: The message, the icon, the action's label and the close button's cross: the colour that reads on `container`. The `onColor` of its tone's role.

declarations.name: PantrixTooltipState
declarations.signature: class PantrixTooltipState
declarations.description:
Whether a `PantrixTooltip` is up, and the handle that brings it up and puts it away.

A tooltip brings itself up when a pointer rests on what it names, when that takes the keyboard's focus and when a press is held on it, and it goes as the pointer or the focus leaves, on a press and on Escape. Every one of those throws this one switch, so `visible` is the whole truth about the tooltip.

A screen that shows one of its own accord, a hint on the first run or a name beside a control it has just changed, holds the state itself and calls `show` and `dismiss`:

```
val hint = rememberPantrixTooltipState()
LaunchedEffect(firstRun) { if (firstRun) hint.show() }
PantrixTooltip(text = stringResource(Res.string.refresh), state = hint, tagKey = "refresh") {
    PantrixIconButton(imageVector = PantrixIcons.Refresh, contentDescription = …, onClick = onRefresh)
}
```

Hold it with `rememberPantrixTooltipState`.

members.name: visible
members.signature:
var visible: Boolean by mutableStateOf(visible)
    private set
members.description: Whether the tooltip is up. A tooltip that is turned off, or whose control is under a dialog or another modal layer, is put away, and this is false then.

members.name: show
members.description: Brings the tooltip up. Showing one that is up changes nothing.

members.name: dismiss
members.description: Puts the tooltip away. Dismissing one that is away changes nothing.

members.name: toggle

@Composable
fun rememberPantrixTooltipState(initiallyVisible: Boolean = false): PantrixTooltipState

declarations.name: PantrixTooltip
declarations.signature:
@Composable
fun PantrixTooltip(
    text: String,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    side: PopoverSide = PopoverSide.Top,
    enabled: Boolean = true,
    state: PantrixTooltipState = rememberPantrixTooltipState(),
    style: TooltipStyle? = null,
    colors: TooltipColors? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null,
    anchor: @Composable () -> Unit
)
declarations.description:
A short label that names the control it is anchored to: an icon button's name, a truncated label in full.

It shows what the control already says. A screen reader reads the control itself and the label is hidden from it: a tooltip is a way of showing a name, not a place for anything new. Give the control the same words, as its `contentDescription` or its text.

It comes up by itself and takes nothing from the app: no focus and no key, and no press but one on the label itself and the one that is held to ask for it. What it names keeps working while it is up, and so does whatever is pressed to put it away.

- **A pointer** brings it up once it has rested on the control for the style's `pointerRestMillis`, and takes it away as it leaves. It may cross onto the label and rest there: the label stays while the pointer is on either. A mouse button on the control puts it away until the pointer has left and come back.

- **The keyboard's focus** brings it up at once, where a focus ring is drawn, and takes it away as it leaves. Escape puts it away while the control keeps the focus.

- **A press that is held**, a finger's long press on the control, brings it up, and it stays until something is pressed: one that left with the finger would never be read. That press asked what the control is and presses nothing as it lifts. A tap is the control's alone and brings nothing up, and a press that travels is the start of a scroll.

`state` is the switch all of these throw, and a screen can throw it too.

It sits on `side` of the control, centred on it, on the opposite side where the window has no room for it, and never closer than the style's margin to the window's edges, its system bars or the keyboard. It is put away while its control is under a dialog, a sheet or an open popover, when its control scrolls out of view, and when the window changes size.

parameters.name: text
parameters.description: what the control is called: a few words, and the ones the control itself says.

parameters.name: modifier
parameters.description: applied to the control's place, the box the control is laid out in where the tooltip is called: an alignment or a weight there places the control, and the label goes with it.

parameters.name: side
parameters.description: the side of the control the tooltip prefers. `PopoverSide.Start` and `PopoverSide.End` follow the layout direction.

parameters.name: enabled
parameters.description: false puts it away and keeps it away, for a control whose name is already in view.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: whether the tooltip is up, and the handle that shows and hides it.

parameters.name: style
parameters.description: this call's own style: over every enclosing one and under the density. Only the fields it sets change, on every platform.

parameters.name: colors
parameters.description: this call's own colours. Only the ones it sets change; the rest stay the theme's.

parameters.name: tagKey
parameters.description: a locale-independent key for automation: the label's tag is `Tooltip_<tagKey>`.

parameters.name: anchor
parameters.description: the control the tooltip names, laid out where this is called and as that place asks. A control that is pressed, a button or an icon, or a text that is only read: one with a long press of its own, a text field or text that can be selected, would have that press taken from it on a touch screen.

declarations.name: TooltipStyle
declarations.description:
`PantrixTooltip`'s geometry: how large the label is, how far it sits from what it names, how close it comes to the edges of the window, and how long a pointer rests on a control before its tooltip appears.

The padding around the text, the gap and the margin follow density. The widest width, the corners, the shadow and the pointer's rest do not. A tooltip's colours are not part of its style: they are the theme's, and `TooltipColors` where a call has its own.

parameters.name: shape
parameters.description: The label's corners.

parameters.name: horizontalPadding
parameters.description: Between the text and the label's start and end edges.

parameters.name: verticalPadding
parameters.description: Between the text and the label's top and bottom edges.

parameters.name: maxWidth
parameters.description: The widest the label gets: longer text wraps.

parameters.name: gap
parameters.description: Between what the tooltip names and the tooltip.

parameters.name: margin
parameters.description: Kept clear between the tooltip and the edges of the window, and of what covers the window there: a system bar, a cutout, the keyboard.

parameters.name: elevation
parameters.description: How high the label floats over the app, which is how large its shadow is.

parameters.name: pointerRestMillis
parameters.description: How long a pointer rests on a control before its tooltip appears, in milliseconds. Keyboard focus shows it at once, and a finger's long press as long as the platform takes one to be: this is the pointer's wait alone. `null` leaves the value of the style underneath in place.

declarations.name: TooltipColors
declarations.description:
What a `PantrixTooltip` is painted with, for a call that does not take the theme's colours: a colour that is set is used, and one that is left out stays the theme's.

```
PantrixTooltip(text = name, colors = TooltipColors(container = PantrixTheme.colors.primary.color)) { … }
```

A `container` given here that is one of the theme's role colours brings the colour the theme pairs with it for the text, unless a `content` colour is given too. A fill no role has does not: what reads on it is the caller's to give.

parameters.name: container
parameters.description: The label's fill. The theme's `onSurface`: the tone opposite the theme's grounds, so that the label stands out over whatever the page shows under it, in the light theme and the dark.

parameters.name: content
parameters.description: The label's text. The theme's `textInverse`, which is what reads on that tone.
