declarations.name: PantrixTestTheme
declarations.signature:
@Composable
fun PantrixTestTheme(
    platform: PlatformType = PlatformType.Android,
    system: OperatingSystem = platform.system,
    dark: Boolean = false,
    locale: PantrixLocale = PantrixLocale.English,
    density: PantrixDensity = PantrixDensity.Comfortable,
    fontScale: Float = 1f,
    window: PantrixWindow? = null,
    findings: PantrixFindings? = null,
    analytics: PantrixAnalytics = PantrixAnalytics.NoOp,
    haptics: PantrixHaptics = PantrixHaptics.NoOp,
    clipboard: TestClipboard? = null,
    filePicker: FilePicker? = null,
    clock: TestClock? = null,
    content: @Composable () -> Unit
)
declarations.description:
Pantrix's theme as a test sees a screen: the same on every machine and in every run, whatever the device under the test. By default the screen is on Android, in the light theme and in English, at the comfortable density and a font scale of one, with motion reduced so that nothing is caught moving; each is a parameter where a test needs another.

The diagnostics are on: what they find goes to `findings`, which `assertNoFindings` reads, or to the log where the test gives no sink. The platform's services are the test's own: `analytics` and `haptics` keep what the screen tells them where the test gives recorders, `clipboard` keeps what it copies, `filePicker` answers its pickers and `clock` is the time it reads. Left out, the clipboard and the picker are the theme's own, so that nothing of the machine's is written to or opened; the clock is the device's. The screen's file saver is always the theme's own, a `TestFileSaver`: a test that reads what was saved gives its own through `LocalFileSaver`, inside the theme.

```
val findings = PantrixFindings()
val analytics = RecordingAnalytics()
setContent { PantrixTestTheme(findings = findings, analytics = analytics) { CheckoutScreen() } }
onPantrixNode("Button", "pay").performClick()
assertEquals(listOf("click"), analytics.eventsOf("Button").map { it.action })
assertNoFindings(findings)
```

parameters.name: platform
parameters.description: the platform the screen is shown as: its touch targets, its focus rings and its own ways.

parameters.name: system
parameters.description: the operating system the screen is typed on, which says whether its shortcuts lead with Command or Control: by default the platform's own, and Windows on the desktop and the web.

parameters.name: dark
parameters.description: whether the theme is the dark one.

parameters.name: locale
parameters.description: the language the screen is in, and with it the direction of its writing.

parameters.name: density
parameters.description: how close together the screen's controls stand.

parameters.name: fontScale
parameters.description: how much larger the system writes than the theme's sizes: `2f` for Android's largest.

parameters.name: window
parameters.description: the window the screen is told it is in, its size and its folds: a phone's, a tablet's, one half of a foldable; null for the one the test draws in.

parameters.name: findings
parameters.description: where the diagnostics' findings are kept; null to write them to the log.

parameters.name: analytics
parameters.description: what the screen's components report to.

parameters.name: haptics
parameters.description: what the screen's components play their feedback with.

parameters.name: clipboard
parameters.description: the clipboard the screen copies to, with the traits it has; null for one of the theme's own.

parameters.name: filePicker
parameters.description: the picker the screen's pickers open, `rememberFilePicker()` and the file drop zones; null for one of the theme's own, which never answers, as a user who closes it.

parameters.name: clock
parameters.description: the time the screen reads: its today, the hour a time picker opens at, a chart's moments; null for the device's.

parameters.name: content
parameters.description: the screen.

declarations.name: onEachPlatform
declarations.signature:
fun ComposeUiTest.onEachPlatform(
    content: @Composable (platform: PlatformType) -> Unit,
    check: ComposeUiTest.(platform: PlatformType) -> Unit
)
declarations.description:
Looks at `content` on each platform in turn, in the one run of the test: `content` is composed anew for each, in the order of `PlatformType`, and `check` follows it.

One run, and not a run for each platform: on the web a run is a promise the test hands back, and a test that starts several from a loop hands back none of them, so that nothing waits for them and what fails in them fails no test.

```
onEachPlatform({ platform -> PantrixTestTheme(platform = platform) { SaveButton() } }) { platform ->
    onPantrixNode("Button", "save").assertTouchTargetOf(platform)
}
```

parameters.name: content
parameters.description: the screen as it is shown on a platform.

parameters.name: check
parameters.description: what is asserted of it there.

declarations.name: RecordingAnalytics
declarations.signature: class RecordingAnalytics : PantrixAnalytics
declarations.description:
Analytics that keep what the screen's components report, in order: what a test reads to see that a press, an open or a choice was told. `PantrixTestTheme` gives them to the screen as its `analytics`.

```
val analytics = RecordingAnalytics()
setContent { PantrixTestTheme(analytics = analytics) { CheckoutScreen() } }
onPantrixNode("Button", "pay").performClick()
assertEquals(listOf("click"), analytics.eventsOf("Button").map { it.action })
```

members.name: events
members.description: Every event reported since these were made or last cleared, in order: a copy, which later events leave alone.

members.name: eventsOf
members.description: The events `component` reported, in order: `eventsOf("Button")`.

members.name: clear
members.description: Forgets every event reported so far.

declarations.name: RecordingHaptics
declarations.signature: class RecordingHaptics : PantrixHaptics
declarations.description: Haptics that keep the feedback the screen's components play, in order, and play none on the device: what a test reads to see that a long press or a choice was felt. `PantrixTestTheme` gives them to the screen as its `haptics`.

members.name: played
members.description: Every feedback played since these were made or last cleared, in order: a copy, which later ones leave alone.

members.name: clear
members.description: Forgets every feedback played so far.

declarations.name: TestClipboard
declarations.description:
A clipboard of the test's own, in the place of the machine's: it keeps what the screen copies, and touches nothing the machine has copied. `PantrixTestTheme` gives it to the screen as Compose's clipboard and `traits` as the platform's, so that a test sees a screen on Android 13, whose system shows a copy itself, by `ClipboardTraits(announcedBySystem = true)`, and in a page served over plain http, which has no clipboard, by `ClipboardTraits(writable = false)`.

```
val clipboard = TestClipboard()
setContent { PantrixTestTheme(clipboard = clipboard) { InviteScreen() } }
onPantrixNode("Button", "copy_link").performClick()
assertEquals("https://example.com/invite/42", clipboard.text())
```

parameters.name: traits
parameters.description: what the clipboard is like, as the screen is told.

members.name: entries
members.description: What was put on the clipboard, in order and in the platform's own type: null where it was cleared.

members.name: texts
members.description: The plain texts put on the clipboard, in order: what the screen copied. On the web a text is read as the browser reads it, which is waited for; an entry that holds no plain text is left out.

members.name: text
members.description: The plain text on the clipboard now, or null while it holds none.

members.name: clear
members.description: Forgets what was put on the clipboard.

declarations.name: TestClock
declarations.description:
A clock of the test's own: it shows the moment the test sets, and moves only when the test moves it. `PantrixTestTheme` gives it to the screen as the screen's clock, at the offset from UTC that `utcOffset` gives: the screen reads its today, the hour a time picker opens at and a chart's moments by it.

It is the time the screen reads, and not the frames of the test: a screen that waits until midnight waits on the test's own clock as well, `mainClock.advanceTimeBy(…)`.

```
val clock = TestClock(Instant.parse("2026-10-17T21:59:00Z")) { 3.hours }
setContent { PantrixTestTheme(clock = clock) { BookingScreen() } }
clock.advanceBy(1.minutes)
mainClock.advanceTimeBy(60_000)
```

parameters.name: now
parameters.description: the moment the clock shows at first.

parameters.name: utcOffset
parameters.description: how far the clock is ahead of UTC at a moment: three hours in Istanbul, less than nought west of Greenwich; by default none, the clock of UTC.

members.name: now
members.description: The moment the clock shows, which the test may set.

members.name: advanceBy
members.description: Moves the clock on by `duration`, or back where `duration` is less than nought.

declarations.name: TestFilePicker
declarations.description:
A file picker of the test's own: it answers a pick with the `files` the test gives it, as a user who chooses them, and keeps what each pick asked for. It answers with the files of the kinds the pick shows and no others, and with the first of them alone where the pick takes one, as the platform's picker lets a user choose; with none of those it does not answer, as a user who closes the picker. `PantrixTestTheme` gives it to the screen in the place of the platform's.

```
val picker = TestFilePicker(listOf(PantrixFile("offer.pdf", bytes)))
setContent { PantrixTestTheme(filePicker = picker) { OfferScreen() } }
onPantrixNode("FileDrop", "offer").performClick()
assertEquals(listOf(PantrixFileType.Pdf), picker.requests.single().accept)
```

parameters.name: files
parameters.description: what a user chooses at a pick, until the test gives others.

members.name: requests
members.description: Every pick asked for since the picker was made, in order: the kinds of file it showed and how many it took.

declarations.name: TestFileSaver

parameters.name: result
parameters.description: what each save answers: saved, unless the test makes the user cancel or the place fail.

members.name: files
members.description: Every file given to be saved since the saver was made, in order.

declarations.name: toPantrixColors
declarations.signature: fun ColorScheme.toPantrixColors(base: PantrixColors = pantrixColorsAsDarkAs(this)): PantrixColors
declarations.description:
Pantrix's colours from this Material scheme: what Pantrix's components are drawn in inside a Material app, so that a screen written with them reads as the app's other screens do.

Each colour Material has a role for comes from the scheme. The brand's role is Material's primary, the neutral one its secondary, and danger its error. The backdrop is the scheme's background and a raised surface its `surfaceContainerLow`, which stands forward of the background as a card does in Material. The text is drawn in the scheme's `onBackground` and `onSurfaceVariant`, and the edges in its `outline` and `outlineVariant`.

What Material has no role for comes from `base`: the success, info and warning roles, the edge under a pointer, the focus ring, the colours of what is disabled, the chart's colours, and how much the scrim dims.

parameters.name: base
parameters.defaultNote: `pantrixColorsAsDarkAs`: Pantrix's own colours as dark as `scheme`: the dark set when its background is.
parameters.description: the Pantrix colours for what the scheme has none of: Pantrix's own by default, as dark as the scheme.

declarations.name: toColorScheme
declarations.signature: fun PantrixColors.toColorScheme(): ColorScheme
declarations.description:
A Material scheme from these Pantrix colours: what Material's components are drawn in inside a Pantrix app, so that a component Pantrix does not have reads as Pantrix's own do.

The brand's role is Material's primary, the neutral role its secondary, the info role its tertiary and danger its error; each of them gives its fixed colours too, from its container. The scheme's surface is the backdrop, as in Material's own schemes, and its containers step from the raised surface towards the text: `surfaceContainerLow` is the surface, and each container after it lays a little more of the text's colour over it. `outline` is the mark of a control, and `outlineVariant` the edge of a box: Material draws an outlined button, a chip and an outlined card in it, so they stand out as clearly as Pantrix's own fields and chips. Material's dividers take that edge too, a step stronger than Pantrix's.

Material's scrim is opaque, and its components dim with it as they need; the one given is these colours' scrim at full strength.

declarations.name: toPantrixShapes
declarations.signature: fun Shapes.toPantrixShapes(base: PantrixShapes = PantrixShapes()): PantrixShapes
declarations.description: Pantrix's corner radii from Material's shape scale, each step from the Material step of its radius: extra small, small, medium and large become `sm`, `md`, `lg` and `xl`, so that Material's own scale, 4, 8, 12 and 16dp, gives Pantrix's own, and a Pantrix component is as round in a Material app as in its own theme. Pantrix's `xs`, less round than any Material step, comes from `base`; Material's extra large, rounder than any Pantrix step, has no Pantrix step. Square and fully round are the same in both.

parameters.name: base
parameters.description: the shapes Material has no step for: Pantrix's own by default.

declarations.name: toMaterialShapes
declarations.signature: fun PantrixShapes.toMaterialShapes(fallback: Shapes = Shapes()): Shapes
declarations.description:
Material's shape scale from Pantrix's corner radii, each step from the Pantrix step of its radius: `sm`, `md`, `lg` and `xl` become extra small, small, medium and large, so that Pantrix's own scale gives Material's own from extra small to large. Material's extra large, rounder than any Pantrix step, takes `xl`, the roundest.

Material takes shapes made of corners only. A Pantrix step of another shape, a brand's own outline, takes `fallback`'s shape for that step.

parameters.name: fallback
parameters.description: the shapes for the steps whose Pantrix shape is not made of corners: Material's own by default.

declarations.name: PantrixThemeFromMaterial
declarations.signature:
@Composable
fun PantrixThemeFromMaterial(content: @Composable () -> Unit)
declarations.description:
A Pantrix theme made of the Material theme around it: inside a Material app, Pantrix's components in `content` take its colours, its type scale and its shapes, so that a screen moved to Pantrix reads as the app's other screens do.

The colours are `toPantrixColors` of the scheme, as dark as it; the type is `toPantrixTypography` over Pantrix's own scale; the shapes are `toPantrixShapes`. Everything else is Pantrix's own, or what a `PantrixTheme` inside gives.

At its root, Pantrix's text style is the one a Material text takes there, the scheme's large body. Its content colour stays Pantrix's own, which on the theme's grounds is already the scheme's text colour: at a Material theme's root Material's own is its default black, which only a Material surface replaces. Inside a Material surface, `PantrixContentFromMaterial` gives Pantrix's content the surface's colour.

Where it is the outermost Pantrix theme, it makes what the system draws follow the scheme's dark rather than the system's: Android's bars' icons, iOS's status bar, keyboard and controls. A Material app that sets them itself gives the other form `followSystemBars = false`.

declarations.name: PantrixThemeFromMaterial
declarations.description: `PantrixThemeFromMaterial`, told whether it sets what the system draws.

parameters.name: followSystemBars
parameters.description: whether this theme, where it is the outermost Pantrix theme, makes what the system draws follow the scheme's dark rather than the system's: Android's bars' icons, iOS's status bar, keyboard and controls. A Material app that sets them itself, or whose bars are coloured, turns it off. docs/guide/system-bars/SYSTEM_BARS_GUIDE.md has the whole of it.

parameters.name: content
parameters.description: what takes the theme: Pantrix's components inside the Material app.

declarations.name: MaterialThemeFromPantrix
declarations.signature:
@Composable
fun MaterialThemeFromPantrix(content: @Composable () -> Unit)
declarations.description:
A Material theme made of the Pantrix theme around it: inside a Pantrix app, Material's components in `content` take its colours, its type scale and its shapes, so that a component Pantrix does not have reads as Pantrix's own do.

The scheme is `toColorScheme` of Pantrix's colours, the type scale `toMaterialTypography` and the shapes `toMaterialShapes`.

At its root, Material's content colour and text style are the ones a Pantrix text would take there: `MaterialContentFromPantrix`.

declarations.name: PantrixContentFromMaterial
declarations.signature:
@Composable
fun PantrixContentFromMaterial(content: @Composable () -> Unit)
declarations.description: Gives Pantrix's text and icons in `content` the colour and the style a Material text takes where this stands: what Pantrix's content inside a Material surface is wrapped in, so that it reads on the surface as Material's does.

declarations.name: MaterialContentFromPantrix
declarations.signature:
@Composable
fun MaterialContentFromPantrix(content: @Composable () -> Unit)
declarations.description: Gives Material's text and icons in `content` the colour and the style a Pantrix text takes where this stands: what Material's content on a Pantrix surface or fill is wrapped in, so that it reads there as Pantrix's does. Where nothing gives Pantrix a content colour, it is the theme's text colour.

declarations.name: toPantrixTypography
declarations.signature: fun Typography.toPantrixTypography(base: PantrixTypography): PantrixTypography
declarations.description:
Pantrix's type scale from this Material one: what Pantrix's text is set in inside a Material app.

Each Pantrix role takes the Material style of its size: display the small display (36 in Material's own scale), headline the medium headline (28), title the large title (22), body the large body (16), label the large label (14), footnote the small body (12) and caption the small label (11). Material has no style of a callout's size: the callout is the large body's face and weight at `base`'s callout size. Nor has it a monospace style: the code is `base`'s.

parameters.name: base
parameters.description: the Pantrix scale the callout's size and the code come from.

declarations.name: toMaterialTypography
declarations.signature: fun PantrixTypography.toMaterialTypography(): Typography
declarations.description:
A Material type scale from this Pantrix one: what Material's text is set in inside a Pantrix app.

Each Material style takes the Pantrix role of its size, and where Pantrix has no role that large, its largest: the three displays are the display, the large and the medium headline the headline, the small headline and the large title the title, the medium title and the large body the body, the small title, the medium body and the large label the label, the small body and the medium label the footnote, and the small label the caption. Material's emphasized styles are its plain ones, as Material's own scale gives them for a scale of an app's.

icons.name: Check
icons.description: Confirmation. Symmetrical in meaning, so it never mirrors.

icons.name: Close
icons.description: Closing or dismissing: a dialog, a sheet, a chip.

icons.name: ChevronDown
icons.description: What opens below: a select's or an accordion's chevron. Never mirrors.

icons.name: ChevronForward
icons.description: Points along the reading direction, so it mirrors in RTL.

icons.name: ChevronBack
icons.description: Points against the reading direction, so it mirrors in RTL: a pagination's previous page.

icons.name: FirstPage
icons.description: Back to where a row of pages starts: `ChevronBack` against a bar, a pagination's first page. Mirrors in RTL.

icons.name: LastPage
icons.description: On to where a row of pages ends: `ChevronForward` against a bar, a pagination's last page. Mirrors in RTL.

icons.name: ArrowBack
icons.description: Back to the previous screen, as Android and the web draw it; mirrors in RTL.

icons.name: ArrowForward
icons.description: On to what comes next, as `ArrowBack` returns: the arrow between a range's two ends. Mirrors in RTL.

icons.name: Calendar
icons.description: A page of a calendar: a date picker's field. Never mirrors.

icons.name: Clock
icons.description: A clock's face, its hands at the hour and a little past it: a time picker's field. A clock turns the same way in every language, so it never mirrors.

icons.name: Refresh
icons.description: Doing it again: a three-quarter turn, clockwise from the right and around to its head at the top right. A turn to the right reads the same in every language, so it never mirrors.

icons.name: ZoomOut
icons.description: Showing more: a lens with a minus in it, which widens a range. A lens is held the same way in every language, so it never mirrors.

icons.name: ZoomIn
icons.description: Showing less: `ZoomOut`'s lens with a plus, which narrows the range. Never mirrors.

icons.name: MoreHorizontal
icons.description: Something folded away: the pages a breadcrumb trail or a pagination leaves out. Never mirrors.

icons.name: Minus
icons.description: Indeterminate or partly selected.

icons.name: Menu
icons.description: The menu a drawer opens: three lines, the mark every platform uses for it.

icons.name: Plus
icons.description: Add. `Minus`'s line with the upright it is missing.

icons.name: Info
icons.description: Information: an "i" in a circle, its dot at the top, the mark `Error` turns upside down.

icons.name: Success
icons.description: Success: a tick in a circle.

icons.name: Warning
icons.description: Warning: an exclamation mark in a triangle, the one status icon with a different outline.

icons.name: Error
icons.description: Error: an exclamation mark in a circle, its dot at the bottom.

icons.name: Inbox
icons.description: A tray with a notch in its rim: an inbox.

icons.name: Star
icons.description: A five-pointed star: something marked as a favourite.

icons.name: Folder
icons.description: A folder.

icons.name: Person
icons.description: A head and shoulders: a person, an account.

icons.name: Search
icons.description: A lens and its handle: a search. A lens is held the same way in every language, so it never mirrors.

icons.name: Download
icons.description: An arrow down onto a line: taking something out of the app as a file. Never mirrors.

icons.name: Upload
icons.description: An arrow up from a line: taking a file into the app. Never mirrors.

icons.name: File
icons.description: A sheet with its upper corner folded: a file. The fold is at the upper right in every language, as a page's is in a file manager, so it never mirrors.

icons.name: Copy
icons.description: Two sheets, one behind the other: copying, of a code block or of a link. The sheet behind shows at the upper left in every language, so it never mirrors.

icons.name: Eye
icons.description: An eye: showing what is hidden, the text of a secure text field. It is the same eye in every language.

icons.name: EyeOff
icons.description: `Eye` with a line through it: hiding the text again. The eye stops short of the line on either side, so that the line is read as one drawn across the eye and not as part of it.

icons.name: Pause
icons.description: Two upright bars: stopping what moves by itself for a while.

icons.name: Play
icons.description: A triangle that points to the right: letting what was stopped move again. A player's button points the same way in every language, so it never mirrors.
